subclassFeature.name: Path of the Titan
entries: {@i Bigger is Better}

There is no denying the might of Jotunheim. Even the smallest of the giants exemplifies the sheer physical power passed down from Aurgelmir, the first giant. Barbarians who follow the Path of the Titan channel the spirits of the jotun through their rage. These otherworldly furies swell the Barbarian's physical form to one that matches the power and might of their rage, causing them to tower over their foes.

subclassFeature.name: Rage of the Giants
entries: Your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} taps into the primal power of giants. Whenever you activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB}, if you are smaller than Large, you can choose to become Large. Your equipment grows to match your new size. If there is not enough room for you to become Large, you do not grow.

While you are Large, your carrying capacity doubles, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your attacks with weapons or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal one additional die of damage (a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} attack deals {@damage 3d6} damage, a {@item Greataxe|XPHB} deals {@damage 2d12}, and so on).

subclassFeature.name: Crushing Steps
entries: As part of your movement, you can move through the space of any creature with a size smaller than you. An enemy whose space you move through must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition and lose the ability to take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Titanic Strikes
entries: When you use your {@classFeature Brutal Strike|Barbarian|XPHB|9|XPHB} feature, the distance the target is pushed by your Forceful Blow is doubled, and the {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of a target struck by your Hamstring Blow is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Rage of the Titans
entries: Whenever you activate your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB}, if you are smaller than Huge, you can choose to become Huge. Your equipment grows to match your new size. If there is not enough room for you to become Huge, you become Large. If there is not enough room for you to become Large, you do not grow.

While you are Huge, your carrying capacity triples, your reach increases by 5 feet, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and your attacks with weapons or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} deal two additional dice of damage (a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} attack deals {@damage 4d6} damage, a {@item Greataxe|XPHB} deals {@damage 3d12}, and so on).

subclassFeature.name: Skald
entries: {@i Provoke, Manipulate, Inspire}

Northlands Bards have passed down skaldic traditions through the ages at their bardic colleges. They use these traditions to entertain in the feasthalls during the long, dark winters; to lift up great leaders and to tear down despots; and to direct the tempers of their Northern kin in productive directions. Skalds are battle-trained to travel with warrior-bands and adventuring groups. Their skills with weapons and words keep them safe while they write the stories of their exploits, sing drinking songs in mead halls, and recite poems of legendary heroes on raider longships.

subclassFeature.name: Poetic Provocation
entries: Thanks to your way with words, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Vicious Cantrip
entries: You always have the {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrip prepared. If you already know the {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrip, you learn a new cantrip of your choice. A creature that fails its saving throw against your {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma saving throw that it makes before the end of your next turn, in addition to the spell's normal effects.

entries.name: Flyting Master
entries: You can use Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) in place of Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) checks to antagonize a creature into a fight, threaten a creature to avoid a confrontation, rile or soothe the attitude of a mob, or any other situation where your skill in weaving a story or applying a cutting insult would sway an opinion.

subclassFeature.name: Martial Training
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor and Shields. In addition, you can use a Simple or Martial weapon as a Spellcasting Focus to cast spells from the Bard spell list.

In addition, your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of one Simple or Martial weapon of your choice. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can practice weapon drills and change your weapon choice.

subclassFeature.name: Bragi's Rune of Speech
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you may expend a use of Bardic Inspiration to cause one of the following effects:

entries.name: Scorn
entries: Choose one creature within 30 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its attack rolls against you for 1 minute.

entries.name: Eloquence
entries: You may roll your Bardic Inspiration die and add the result to the first Charisma check or saving throw you make in the next hour.

entries.name: Vitality
entries: You may roll your Bardic Inspiration die. You and up to three allies within 30 feet gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the result of the roll.
You may have only one of these effects active at a time. If you use another, it replaces the one that is currently active.

subclassFeature.name: Battle Sagas
entries: You have learned to channel the power from the Eddas, epic poems of heroes, monsters, and gods ingrained into the hearts and minds of the Northlanders. You can spend 1 minute reciting selected passages from the Eddas. When you do so, each creature your choice (other than you) within 60 feet, that can hear you, gains several benefits for 1 hour.

items: It has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions.
Its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point Maximum} increases by {@dice 2d10}, and it gains the same number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
Once per turn, when the creature makes an attack roll or saving throw, it can add {@dice 1d4} to the roll or save.

entries: During the same one-hour period, you gain the following benefit.

When an ally you can see who is under the effect of your Battle Sagas fails a saving throw, attack roll, or ability check, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration. The ally can roll your Bardic Inspiration die and add it to their failed result, possibly making it a success.
Once you use your Battle Sagas feature, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Nornbound
entries: {@i Weaves the Threads of Fate}

The Nornbound Cleric pays homage to the Norns and in return is granted the ability to see and manipulate the threads of mortals' fates. This power, seen as tampering to some, can help or hinder the outcome of actions taken by the Cleric's targets. While Nornbound offer prayers to the other gods, the Norns are the guiding light to whom they have pledged their service.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Spells
entries: Your connection to the threads of Fate allows you to always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Nornbound Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

subclassFeature.name: Tailor the Skein
entries: You can see the threads of the celestial skein and manipulate them in service to your faith. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll a d6 twice and record the numbers rolled. These numbers are known as Skeins. As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, after learning the result of an attack, damage roll, saving throw, or ability check made by a creature you can see within 60 feet, you may add or subtract one of your Skeins from the result. This can cause the roll to succeed or fail when it otherwise wouldn't have. If you add or subtract a Skein from a damage roll, it could cause a creature to live or die when it otherwise wouldn't have.
Your die increases at higher level. At 7th level it, becomes a {@dice d8}; at 11th level, it becomes a {@dice d10}; and at 15th level it becomes a {@dice d12}.
Each Skein can be used only once. When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you regain all Skeins.

subclassFeature.name: Plucking at Threads
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you present your holy symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to alter the weaves of Fate around you. Allies within 30 feet of you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Intertwined Fate
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you expend a spell slot, twisting and altering the life threads of two creatures you can see within 30 feet of you, choosing one to be the primary and the other the secondary. The primary target must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 1d8} Force damage per spell slot level on a failure or half as much on a success. The creature may choose to fail this saving throw. The secondary target then receives {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage the first target took, either regaining lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, if injured, or gaining {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} if uninjured.

subclassFeature.name: Skein Weaver
entries: When you use your Plucking at Threads feature, enemies within 30 feet of you must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. An enemy that fails the save has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and saving throws for 1 minute. It can make a saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end this effect. An enemy that succeeds on its saving throw has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to this feature for 24 hours.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Fenris
entries: {@i Savage Devotee of the Great Wolf}

The bitter Northlands hold many dark groups and secrets. One of the most dangerous is the Circle of Fenris, a circle of Druids who venerate the Great Wolf. Inspired by the strength and tenacity of Fenris, these Druids feel a kinship to the wolf through their ties to the natural world. Despite their unsavory reputation in the North, not all Circle of Fenris Druids are savage killers or nihilists seeking to end the world. Some merely resent so-called progress, while others throw off the trappings of civilization to embrace the single-mindedness of the predator. Regardless, Circle of Fenris Druids are known for their untamed nature and unbridled enthusiasm for the hunt.

subclassFeature.name: Mantle of The Wolf
entries: You can manifest a tiny portion of Fenris's power within you. As an action, you can expend a single use of your Wild Shape to cause an ephemeral wolf's head, blazing with primal power, to appear above your own for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), manifest it again, or have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

While this mantle surrounds your body, you are filled with fierce primordial rage. You gain a bonus to your Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks and Strength saving throws equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1). Additionally, you can replace one of your melee attacks with a special bite attack using the spectral head. This bite uses your Wisdom modifier instead of Strength for the attack rolls, and it deals {@damage 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier Force damage on a successful hit.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Fenris Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of Fenris Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Circle of Fenris Spells
rows: {@spell Beast Sense|XPHB}, {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Ensnaring Strike|XPHB}, {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Improved Mantle
entries: While your Mantle of the Wolf surrounds your body, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Break the Chain
entries: Bite attacks you make with spectral wolf head deal double damage to objects and structures, ignoring the damage threshold of these targets.

entries.name: Dark Sight
entries: You have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} out to 60 feet. If you already have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB}, its range increases by 30 feet.

entries.name: Wolf's Sprint
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet.

subclassFeature.name: Defend the Pack
entries: Whenever a creature attacks an ally within 30 feet of you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and spend a use of your Wild Shape to conjure a giant phantom wolf to maul that creature. There is no attack roll required, and the creature is not entitled to a saving throw. The target takes {@damage 4d8} Force damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
At 14th level, the damage increases to {@damage 6d8} Force damage.

subclassFeature.name: Children of the Great Wolf
entries: Once per day, when you use your action to take on your Mantle of the Wolf, you can also summon a {@creature Fenrikyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} ({@book see Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|9}). You can telepathically order it to follow your commands (no action required). The {@creature Fenrikyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} is loyal to you and your allies. It lasts for as long as your Mantle of the Wolf lasts, until you dismiss it (no action required), it's destroyed, you travel to another plane, you're killed, you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, or it's more than 120 feet from you.

subclassFeature.name: Viking
entries: {@i Dangerous Raider of the Sea}

Vikings are battle-hardened warriors and sailors who ply the seas of the Northlands for glory and plunder. As followers of the Reaver's Way, they have their own sense of honor, yet they can be merciless in times of raiding and war. Vikings are known for their prowess with the spear and axe, and for their belief that they can earn a special place in the halls of the dead through their deeds of valor in battle.

subclassFeature.name: Seaborne
entries: You are used to being aboard rocking ships and other vehicles. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all Strength and Dexterity saving throws and checks to avoid being pushed, having the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, or otherwise being moved against your will.
In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to pilot or otherwise control a waterborne vehicle, such as a canoe or longboat.

subclassFeature.name: Viking Weapon Mastery
entries: If you have {@variantrule Weapon Mastery Properties|XPHB|Weapon Mastery} with a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}, {@item Longsword|XPHB}, or {@item Spear|XPHB}, once on each of your turns, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to a damage roll with that weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Savage Charge
entries: As an {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make a single melee attack. If this attack hits, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. With the movement from this {@action Dash|XPHB} action, you can pass through the space of the target and do not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

subclassFeature.name: Call of the Northlands
entries: You are used to facing the harsh conditions and vicious monsters of the Northlands. At the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you may choose one of these benefits. The one you choose replaces your choice from the previous day.

entries.name: Dragonslayer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls you make against Dragons, such as red dragons and wyverns.

entries.name: Hardy Swimmer
entries: You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Inured to Cold
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

entries.name: Trollslayer
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls you make against Giants, such as frost giants and trolls.

subclassFeature.name: Marauder's Reprisal
entries: When you become {@status Bloodied|XPHB} or if a creature scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make an attack against an enemy within your reach, if there is one. If the attack hits, you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, and you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half your level.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all uses once you've finished a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Unstoppable Assault
entries: As an action, you spin your weapon in a furious arc, decimating all creatures before you. You can attack a number of times equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} in addition to your normal attacks. If any of these attacks hit, they are {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB|Critical Hits}, and a creature struck by the attack must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier) or be pushed 10 feet away from you.
Once you have used this feature, you cannot use it again until after you've finished a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Valhalla
entries: {@i Demonstrate Bravery and Honor the Dead}

Paladins who take the Oath of Valhalla ensure they preserve the spirits of those who have died honorably in battle, even their foes. Of course, these Paladins also strive to prove themselves deserving of entry into Valhalla through their own deeds and words. The thunderous revelry of the heroic dead echoing from the gods' mead hall in Asgard fills these paladins, imbuing them with the might of deceased champions.

These Paladins look askance at those who restore heroes to life, but they assume such heroes have agreed to return from Valhalla to continue to fight as mortals. However, they offer no quarter to blasphemers who animate corpses into a mockery of life.

entries.name: Tenets of Valhalla
entries: These Paladins share the following tenets.

items: Protect the worthy dead.
Inspire courage in battle.
Bring justice to those who make a mockery of the dead.

subclassFeature.name: Encouraging Smite
entries: Immediately after you cast Divine Smite, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity and select creatures of your choice within 30 feet of yourself. Until the start of your next turn, these creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their attack rolls and saving throws against the target of your Divine Smite, and their attacks against the target deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Thunder damage.

subclassFeature.name: Guardian of the Dead
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to better protect the dead under your watch. For 1 hour, whenever you are within 10 feet of a creature reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your attack rolls and on saving throws against spells and effects that inflict the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition. After you gain your Aura of Courage class feature, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition when using this feature.

During this 1-hour period, when a creature you can see casts a spell to create Undead, or restore a creature to life, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and attack the creature that cast the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Valhalla Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of Valhalla Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of Valhalla Spells
rows: {@spell Beacon of Hope|XPHB}, {@spell Glyph of Warding|XPHB} (Thunder)
{@spell Aura of Purity|XPHB}, {@spell Guardian of Faith|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Thunderous Aura
entries: You and your allies have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Thunder damage while in your Aura of Protection.
Also, when you cast {@spell Find Steed|XPHB}, you can choose your Faithful Steed's attacks to deal Thunder damage instead of its typical damage.

subclassFeature.name: Valorous Soul
entries: When you reduce a foe to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a melee attack, you can choose any number of allies within 60 feet of you. For 1 minute, these allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their attack rolls and saving throws.

Should you die, your body is treated as if {@spell Gentle Repose|XPHB} had been cast on it, and if you choose, you can refuse to return to life when you are the target of {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB} and similar spells.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit of the Valkyrie
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you receive the blessings granted to Valkyries by Wotan. For 10 minutes or until you choose to end this effect (no action required), you gain the following benefits.

items.name: Flight
entries: You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} of 60 feet.

items.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

items.name: Restful Dead
entries: A creature within your Aura of Protection that attempts to create or summon Undead must make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attempt to create or summon Undead fails.

items.name: Thunderstruck
entries: When you cast a spell with "Smite" in its name, such as Divine Smite or {@spell Shining Smite|XPHB}, you can expend any level of spell slot but cast it as though you used a 5th-level spell slot. Additionally, when an enemy starts its turn in your Aura of Protection, it takes Thunder damage equal to your Charisma modifier plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and it must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Caller
entries: {@i Empowered by Ancestral Spirits}
You were born with a strong, otherworldly connection to the spirits of your ancestors and to the honored dead. You can call on these spirits to aid you and your allies, and to hinder your enemies.

Symbols are important in the cultures of the Northlands, and the spirits are no exception. Rather than manifesting as the people they were in life, the spirits take on a symbolic appearance, usually as ghostly animals that speak as their formal selves. In the Northlands, these animals reflect those found in that region, though it's possible that other animals might be represented as well. You can choose the animal form that your spirits take or roll on the Spirit Animal Form table.

Many spirit callers believe that when they wield magic, they are directly assisted by their ancestral spirits. The {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB} spell may be the spirit of a dead blacksmith crafting spiritual armor for you, while the {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB} spell may be fired by the spirit of your clan's greatest archer.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Caller Spells
entries: When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Spirit Caller Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Spirit Caller Spells
rows: {@spell Bane|XPHB}, {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Heroism|XPHB}, {@spell Protection from Evil and Good|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Occult Expertise
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Arcana|XPHB} and {@skill Religion|XPHB} skills if you don't already have it. When making checks with these skills, you can use your Charisma modifier instead of your Intelligence modifier, if it is higher.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Guidance
entries: You can call on ancestral and cultural spirits to help guide you. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on a skill check.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Aura
entries: You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to call on spirits to surround you or an ally. This takes the form of a spirit aura that extends 10 feet from you or a willing ally of your choice in all directions and lasts for 1 minute, until you have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition, or until you use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to dismiss it. Choose one of the following options when you use this feature.

entries.name: Maddening Whispers
entries: The spirits whisper dark secrets into your enemies' minds, unsettling them. An enemy creature that enters the aura or starts its turn there must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ability checks and attack rolls until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Bolstering Whispers
entries: The spirits whisper encouragements and alerts to your allies. An allied creature who enters the aura or starts its turn there has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks and attack rolls until the end of its next turn.
You can use this twice, and you regain all uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can use this feature again if you spend 3 Sorcery Points.

subclassFeature.name: Spiritual Secrets
entries: The spirits know secrets, collected from their time in the realms of the dead. These secrets might include a creature's weaknesses, a person's dreams, or the properties of a magic item. You can call on the spirits to share their secrets with you.
When you make an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, and the roll fails, you can call on the spirits' knowledge and roll again. You must take the result of the second roll.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If you have no more uses, you can spend 3 Sorcery Points to gain one (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Spiritual Storm
entries: Your spirit aura now extends 15 feet instead of 10 feet. In addition, an enemy that enters your aura or starts there takes {@damage 2d8} Psychic damage, though no more than once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Trickster
entries: {@i Imbue Life with a Touch of Chaos}

From the halls of the fey to the antics of Loki, there are entities who embody the primal nature of chaos. Your pact draws upon one of these powers, perhaps a creature with an aspect of whimsy or a deity relishing in tricks and ploys. Your patron asks you to sow chaos and delight in mischief. If you squint, you can almost make sense of the method behind their seeming madness.

subclassFeature.name: Context Switch
entries: Your patron grants you the ability to play a harmful trick on others while saving yourself from harm. When a creature makes a melee attack against you, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and choose a creature within 5 feet of you. If the creature is unwilling, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure (or if it is willing), it magically swaps places with you and becomes the target of the attack. If the attack hits the target, the target takes the damage instead of you, and if the target was an enemy, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.
You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Trickster Spells
entries: The magic of your patron ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Warlock level specified in the Trickster Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Trickster Spells
rows: {@spell Detect Thoughts|XPHB}, {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB}, {@spell Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB}, {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB}, {@spell Silent Image|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Nimble Trickery
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB} if you don't already have it. When you make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check to swap an item with another item that has similar dimensions, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check.

When you reach 6th level, you can swap an object with an unattended object of similar dimensions up to 30 feet away by succeeding on a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check. When you reach 14th level, you can replace the target object with an illusion rather than exchanging it for a real object. The illusory duplicate lasts for 1 minute. Once you use this aspect of Nimble Trickery, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} or expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Distant Switch
entries: When you use your Context Switch class feature, you can choose a creature within 30 feet of you (rather than within 5 feet of you). If you do not choose to do this, you can instead choose for the creature you swap with to have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its save. If your target (regardless of its distance from you) fails its save, you can choose to have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn or until immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell (whichever comes first).

subclassFeature.name: Painful Unreality
entries: Your patron teaches you how to see beyond the veil of unreality. You automatically succeed on your Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check when you take the {@action Study|XPHB} action to determine if something is illusory.

In addition, when a creature interacts with an Illusion spell you cast and fails to determine that it is illusory, you can choose to force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature interacting with the Illusion spell takes {@damage 4d10} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

subclassFeature.name: Harbinger of Chaos
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you announce changes to the reality of your surroundings. Each enemy that can see and hear you must make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. An enemy that fails its save believes the changes you announced to be true. It has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all d20 checks until the end of its next turn, and you and your allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls and d20 checks you make against it.
You can use this effect once, and you regain it when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium. Bearfolk are typically large and muscular, reaching a height of over 7 feet and weighing anywhere between 250 and 350 pounds.

entries.name: Apex Predator
entries: When you make a Charisma check, you can add your Strength or Constitution modifier to it (choose which during character creation). You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Wild Heart
entries: You and allied creatures within 5 feet of you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition while you are conscious and do not have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Thick Coat
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of extreme cold.

entries.name: Bearfolk Lineage
entries: You are part of a lineage that grants you supernatural abilities. Choose a legacy from the Bearfolk Lineages table. You gain a different benefit depending on your choice: Andari or Garhamr.

rows.name: Nature's Gift
entries: You know one cantrip of your choice from the {@filter druid spell list|spells|level=0|class=druid}. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability score for it.

rows.name: Bear Hug
entries: When you hit a target with an attack roll and deal damage to it, you can make an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (about 4-8 feet tall) or Small (about 2-4 feet tall), chosen when you select this species.

entries.name: Animal Instinct
entries: You have proficiency in either the {@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill (your choice).

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: You have claws, horns, hooves, fangs, spines, or a similar adaptation that serves as a natural weapon. Work with your GM to determine what type of natural weapon you possess and decide whether it deals Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage. You can use your natural weapon to make {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes}. When you hit with it, the strike deals {@damage 1d6} + your Strength or Dexterity modifier damage (choose which during character creation) of your chosen type, instead of the damage normal for an unarmed strike.

entries.name: Natural Adaptation
entries: You inherit one of the following traits determined by what kind of animal characteristics you want your character to have.

entries.name: Avian
entries: Leathery, feathery, or gossamer wings sprout from your back or connect to your outstretched arms. You have a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. You can't fly while wearing Medium or Heavy armor.

entries.name: Agile
entries: Sharp claws, cloven hooves, robust limbs, reversed joints, or suction pads on your hands and feet allow you to scrabble up trees, rock faces, and uneven surfaces with ease. You have a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. In addition, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to avoid having the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Aquatic
entries: Oily fur, scales, fins, webbed hands and feet, or long, gangly limbs are common for your people. You have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. You can hold your breath for up to 20 minutes.

entries.name: Sturdy
entries: Powerful limbs, fat reserves, or a thick hide allow you to endure harm and accomplish feats of remarkable athleticism. When you aren't wearing armor, you have an AC of 13 + your Dexterity modifier. In addition, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can drag, lift, or push.

sizeEntry.name: Size:
entries: Medium (height varies)

entries.name: Catch and Throw
entries: If you are hit by a ranged weapon attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to add 3 to your AC. If that causes the attack to miss, you can catch the missile, provided the attack included a projectile or was a small thrown weapon (GM's discretion), and throw it back at the attacker, using your normal ranged weapon attack bonus and the weapon's normal damage.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws that you make to end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. You also count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity.

entries.name: Giantkin Ancestry
entries: Your ancestry grants you supernatural abilities. Choose an ancestry from the Giantkin Ancestry table. You gain a natural resistance to the effects of certain natural environments or a condition, and a trait indicated by your chosen ancestry.

If a benefit grants you the ability to cast a spell, you always have that spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.

If a benefit of your ancestry requires a saving throw, the DC is 8 + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier (choose at character creation) + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.caption: Giantkin Ancestry
rows: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG} and high altitude.

entries.name: Airstep
entries: You can cast {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} at will (self only)

entries.name: Windcall
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can cause the air within 30 feet of you to move in a direction of your choice. This can push one Medium or smaller creature up to 5 feet away from you, move an unattended object up to 10 feet, or create a harmless sensory effect using air, such as slamming a door.

rows: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of {@hazard Extreme Heat|XDMG}.

entries.name: Burning Blood
entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when you take Piercing or Slashing damage, a creature you choose within 5 feet of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 1d6} Fire damage. You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
This damage increases by {@damage 1d6} when you reach character levels 5, 11, and 17.

rows: You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of extreme cold and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves against the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Iceshaper
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB}, you can choose an area of ice, snow, or water within 30 feet of you that fits into a 1-foot cube. You can move it up to 5 feet (in a direction of your choice), cause it to form into simple shapes, or freeze/unfreeze it, provided there are no creatures in it. After 1 hour, or if you use this ability again, the material reverts to its previous state.

entries.name: Snowsight
entries: You can see through areas obscured by snowfall, sleet, and other wintry precipitation without penalty. You also have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to snow-blindness.

rows: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves against the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} and {@condition Stunned|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Bulky
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves vs. the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, and if you succeed on such a save, you can push the creature initiating the grapple 10 feet.

entries.name: Iron Stomach
entries: You can ingest nearly any organic matter, treating 2 pounds of matter as equal to a day's worth of rations.

rows: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves against the {@condition Prone|XPHB} and {@condition Petrified|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Stonepulse
entries: Your ability to feel tremors in the ground gives you {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls if you and all your foes are touching solid ground.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You also have {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} with a range of 60 feet.

rows: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saves against Lightning damage. You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of high altitude.

entries.name: Crackling Personality
entries: While in an area open to the sky, you can cast {@spell Levitate|XPHB} (self only) at will.

entries.name: Stormsight
entries: You can see through areas obscured by clouds, fog, rain, and storms without penalty. You also have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to snow-blindness.

entries.name: Predatory Prowess
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, {@skill Perception|XPHB}, or {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill (your choice).

entries.name: Scent
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks relating to detecting scents and tracking.

entries.name: Shift Aspect
entries: You can transform as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, gaining the primal power of your lycanthropic forebears. The transformation lasts for 1 minute or until you end it (no action required). Once you transform, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.
When you transform, you gain one of the following options (choose the option each time you transform).

items.name: Bestial Strength
entries: You gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength checks as well as any checks or saves to resist or end the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition.

items.name: Primal Savagery
entries: You channel the raw savagery of your bestial side. When you use this option, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on each of your turns while it is active, you can roar. Creatures other than your allies within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Charisma saving throw (DC 8 + your Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. A creature that succeeds on the save has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to your roar for 24 hours.

items.name: Swift Hunter
entries: Your body becomes primed for the hunt. Until the transformation ends, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is increased by 10 feet, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Arcane Lore
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Dwarven Resilience
entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws you make to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Magical Crafter
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any checks made to create magical items.

entries.name: Sense Magic
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can sense the presence of magic within 120 feet until the end of your next turn. You see a faint aura around any visible magic object or active spell, and you know its school of magic. You also detect the presence and location of otherworldly creatures, such as Aberrations, Celestials, Fey, Fiends, and Undead. This ability can be blocked by 1 foot of solid material, such as stone or metal. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trance
entries: You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. You can finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in 4 hours if you spend those hours in a trance-like meditation, during which you retain consciousness.

When you reach character level 5, you learn the {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB} spell.

raceFluff.name: Bearfolk
entries: Hailing from the cold forests and mountains of the Northlands, bearfolk are massive people of iron resolve and deep nobility, who resemble bears that walk upright rather than all fours. They put their trust in family and tribe to stand against the world and the challenges of their homeland. Many outsiders assume that they are some form of beastkin, but bearfolk claim the fey lord Mesikammen elevated them from their bear cousins.

In contrast with their brutish appearance, bearfolk are deeply spiritual and artistic. They lack a bear's sharp claws, and their hands are as dexterous as any human artisan. They are covered in fur that often has light frosting on the chest, shoulders, and upper back. The color of their fur sometimes gives clues as to a particular bearfolk's ancestry and what tribe they hail from. As they get older, the fur around their muzzle begins to silver, giving them a distinguished look.

Much as their natural cousins, the natural environment causes minor differences between bearfolk if they inhabit it for generations. Two of these lineages are described below. Bearfolk have similar lifespans to humans.

entries.name: Andari
entries: You are slighter of build than your cousins, with reddish or pale fur. Your people, who are also known as "purifiers," tend to have a strong affinity for nature. Andari often serve as spiritual anchors in their communities. They are a recent branch of the bearfolk species. The majority of Andari originate in the settled communities, such as Bjeornheim or in other settlements across the North.

entries.name: Garhamr
entries: You are thicker and hardier than your cousins. Your people, who are also known as grizzlehides, have fur ranging from black to golden. Tough and ferocious grizzlehides are the original bearfolk stock of the Northlands forests.

entries.name: Bearfolk Names
entries: Bearfolk are given cub names by their parents, similar to names found throughout the Northlands. When a bearfolk comes of age, they earn a new name, either bestowed upon them by an elder or one they choose themselves. This name befits a deed undertaken during their rite of passage into adulthood, describes some honorable or prominent trait of the bearfolk in question, or honors an ancestor.
{@b Cub Names:} Anga, Beorst, Burli, Cauldvyr, Cirdhan, Daegna, Dorngal, Durtta, Erlundt, Farla, Gurralt, Hrosvir, Ingyrd, Johanna, Lhod, Nodhr, Padhra, Sivaer, Tuli, Yrn.
{@b Deed Names:} Fireheart, Ironhide, Lightblade, Moondancer, Razorclaws, Shadowbane, Stonebones, Valgerdsdottir, Yellowfang, Yrnsson.

raceFluff.name: Beastkin
entries: Born between civilization and the wilds, beastkin are as varied as the animal kingdom itself. Sometimes called wildkin, beastkin universally share the bipedal form of humans, elves, or dwarves, but they have pronounced traits of a specific beast, such as hawk wings, a scorpion's tail, rabbit ears, owl eyes, a crab-like carapace, razor-sharp shark teeth, or bony ox horns. Some beastkin show only slight bestial features, while others resemble bipedal versions of their animal kin.

Some beastkin believe they are relatives of the intelligent beasts that hold court in the Fey Realms. Others claim they are descendants of lycanthropes or other magically transformed beings. Whatever the case, all beastkin share a tie to the natural world, and many choose to live alongside the animals they resemble.

Beastkin are often driven by curiosity to explore. Though such wanderlust may last for years, most beastkin return home in later life, where they often act as wardens of their home territory. While all beastkin contend with primal urges, most are quick to form unshakable bonds with those who show them compassion and loyalty.

raceFluff.name: Giantkin
entries: The skalds don't admit to knowing stories of the first giantkin, but few giantkin care about or dwell on their origin. Descended from giants and smaller species in equal measure, they know they must walk their own path in lands where some look upon their ancestry with disfavor. Actions alone will forge their legacy.

Giantkin primarily inhabit communities on the fringes of giant-held territories like The Bleak Expanse, Thursrike, and Jotunheim, or else in and around human or dwarf settlements such as Bjornrike or Jomsborg. True giants place giantkin at the bottom of their social structure, viewing them as only a slight step above the smaller species. Human and dwarven communities make use of giantkin's great strength and other advantages, but many distrust them and their obvious connection to giants. These conflicting attitudes ironically mean giantkin spread throughout the Northlands, even in frigid regions they would otherwise find distasteful, to find their place in the world.

Today, giantkin are a true species, producing children of their own who take on traits from either parent. Culturally, giantkin generally draw more from the society they are raised in than from their ancestry, forging relationships and identities among from the other species of the Northlands.

entries.name: Hill Giantkin
entries: Hill giantkin have the hulking and often unsophisticated hill giants in their ancestry. Often believed to have quick tempers and voracious appetites, hill giantkin are individually quite varied. At about 6 ½ feet tall, they are the smallest of the giantkin, a fact some are sensitive about. They tend to be a sturdy species, with tanned skin and brown or black hair.

entries.name: Stone Giantkin
entries: Descended from their ascetic giant forebears, stone giantkin tend toward thin, angular builds and skin that resembles rough, gray stone. Stone giantkin are often bald, either naturally or by choice, and rarely grow beards, but some have short, dark hair. They occasionally adorn their faces and scalps with intricate woad designs. Stone giantkin are generally reserved and slow to anger. They typically stand 6 ½ to 7 feet tall.

entries.name: Storm Giantkin
entries: Storm giantkin descend from the temperamental and reflective storm giants. They are the tallest of the giantkin, standing nearly 8 feet high, with skin tones ranging from the deepest blues to regal purples, stark white hair, and eyes of white or violet. Many storm giantkin struggle with their moods, with small sparks of the innate lightning of their ancestry emerging in moments of stress or high emotion.

raceFluff.name: Trollkin
entries: In ancient times, ogres, trolls, and fey would sometimes take humans as mates. The humanoid children of these unlikely unions are known as trollkin. Such folk are typically lanky and smaller in size than their larger ancestors, and they have inherited some of the otherworldly traits of their forebears. They have carved out numerous settlements in the cold North, and while they are sometimes found in communities of their own kind, they also live alongside other species in various Northland locations.

Trollkin tend to be tall, often between 6 and 7 feet in height, and their skin tone favors green, though this can range from a green-tinged gold to aquas and blues. Some trollkin are rangy, reflecting strong troll ancestry, thin and wiry with long arms and legs. Others are broad and muscular, more ogre-like, with thick skin and large jaws. Some trollkin have tusks or horns, or long, coarse hair all over their body. Others are mostly hairless and might even have spots or other patterns on their skin.

Trollkin customs and traditions vary widely between settlements and are usually passed down from their ancestors. Since trollkin tend to heal more quickly and fully than other species, preventing tattoos from being effective, some will brand or scar their bodies in careful patterns using acid or fire, which leaves long-lasting marks. Some trollkin are quite musical, generally favoring songs heavy with percussion and with sinuous, mournful melodies.

raceFluff.name: Werekin
entries: Werekin are the descendants of shapechangers, and they can assume the forms of both animals and humanoids. A werekin might have a bloodline bearing the blessing of an animal lord or possess a remnant of lycanthropy passed down through their blood. In the cold of the Northlands, perhaps due to the influence of Fenris, most werekin tend to be lupine, but a werekin's animal ancestry can derive from other existing lycanthrope lineages, such as bears, boars, rats, and even arctic foxes.

While human-appearing in most respects, a werekin's features have aspects reflecting their bestial ancestry. This can include sharp teeth, pointed ears, larger eyes, hair or bristles on their limbs or face, and so forth. Though a werekin's ancestors possessed the ability to fully change their form, a werekin can instead assume a bestial aspect, channeling the predatory nature of a beast without significantly altering their physical form. In many cases, this aspect shows itself by a change in posture and poise, though some werekin do show subtle signs of a physical change—a yellowing of the eyes, lengthening nails or canines, or sudden hair growth.

raceFluff.name: Baugsmidr Dwarf
entries: Dwarves are one of the most prolific humanoid species of the Northlands, perhaps second only to humans themselves. Dwarves in the Northlands take on many roles, from hard-working wheat farmers to outstanding metal and leather crafters. Environment and circumstance have subtly transformed dwarves over the centuries and grant them different traits.

entries.name: Baugsmidr Dwarf
entries: A lesser known dwarven lineage is the baudsmidr dwarf. These dwarves are sometimes called "ring dwarves" by outsiders for their knack with crafting magical rings. Long ago, Gullveig, an obscure deity of magic and gold, lived for a time among an isolated community of dwarves, teaching them the divine art of binding magical runes into precious metals. Though this brought the dwarves great renown and power, it also led to jealousy and greed from others. After a series of raids nearly decimating their community, the baudsmidr dwarves retreated deep within the ground, creating hidden enclaves and redoubts. Today, the descendants of these dwarves remain guarded. Culturally, they consider the location of their communities a closely guarded secret, shared with only those they trust implicitly. Their isolationism has made them leaner than other dwarves, with hair the color of gold or silver. Their eyes are usually large and pale. The gift from Gullveig remains strong in the baudsmidr and many become spellcasters. The ring dwarves who leave the community often travel to find and recover new magical lore or lost artifacts.

raceFluff.name: Fjord Dwarf
entries: Dwarves are one of the most prolific humanoid species of the Northlands, perhaps second only to humans themselves. Dwarves in the Northlands take on many roles, from hard-working wheat farmers to outstanding metal and leather crafters. Environment and circumstance have subtly transformed dwarves over the centuries and grant them different traits.

entries.name: Fjord Dwarf
entries: Fjord dwarves are a distinct lineage of dwarves who long ago abandoned the halls and mines traditionally inhabited by their species, instead choosing to sail the fjords and dwell in rough coastal settlements throughout the Northlands. Indeed, many fjord dwarves find the ancient halls of their forebears to be a bit claustrophobic. They much prefer open sea air and the deck planks of a ship beneath their feet. Fjord dwarves, like other Northlands dwarves, are often menacing raiders and fierce warriors, yet they can also be deeply honorable and generous to their friends and allies.

raceFluff.name: Elf
entries: Millennia ago, elves were created in the Vanir War between the gods. Most were driven out of their original Northlands territories by the dwarves, forced to move south and join their kin before the Great Retreat. The elven communities remaining in the Northlands are generally isolationist, choosing to inhabit the farthest reaches of the Bleak Expanse or to hide themselves away from view with powerful magic. Ages of seclusion have subtly influenced the native elven populations of the North, granting them certain kinds of magic.

entries.name: Alfar (Hidden Elves)
entries: The alfar are an extremely rare lineage of elves who chose to remain in the North when their kin fled to southern lands. Faced with little to no support, as well as pressure from the dwarven empire, they withdrew to the region's most remote forests. Often known as the hidden elves due to their use of camouflage and illusions to conceal their isolated communities from view, the alfar are suspicious of outsiders and possess customs that are far more insular than those of other elves.

entries.name: Ice Elves
entries: The other major lineage of elves in the Northlands roams the tundra and icy hills of the Bleak Expanse in small bands, hunting caribou and mammoths from the backs of reindeer and white-furred saber-toothed tigers. Ice elves are largely insular and fiercely self-sufficient. This has given them the reputation of being secretive, while the truth is more that they have little interest in the larger world. They expect no aid from outsiders, nor do they freely give it. Yet, the ice elves are sometimes willing to trade with humans, dwarves, and trollkin. Despite what ignorant outsiders believe, only a few ice elf communities worship Boreas and do his bidding, and most wish nothing to do with the malevolent deity.

feat.name: Blessing of Baldur
entries: You gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Protective Aegis
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you or an ally within 10 feet of you takes damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce that damage by an amount equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).

entries.name: Radiant Aura
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you emit a bright golden light in a 10-foot-radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for another 10 feet. You may extinguish this light with another {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sunlance
entries: You know the {@spell Sacred Flame|XPHB} cantrip. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

feat.name: Blessing of Boreas
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cold Aegis
entries: If you take Cold damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give yourself {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage until the end of your next turn. You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Winter Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Ray of Frost|XPHB} cantrip. Choose either the {@spell Armor of Agathys|XPHB} or {@spell Ice Knife|XPHB} spell. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Eir
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Vitality Points
entries: You have a number of Vitality Points equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and can spend the points on the benefits below. You regain your expended Vitality Points when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vitality Surge
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and spend 1 Vitality Point to recover {@dice 1d4} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. If you are dying, you can spend 1 Vitality Point to {@variantrule Stable|XPHB|stabilize} (no action required).

entries.name: Channel Vitality
entries: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and spend 1 Vitality Point to cause a creature you touch to regain {@dice 1d4} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

feat.name: Blessing of Freyr and Freyja
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Wild Knowledge
entries: You have proficiency in either the {@skill Animal Handling} or {@skill Nature} skill.

entries.name: Green Magic
entries: You learn the {@spell Druidcraft|XPHB} and {@spell Thorn Whip|XPHB} cantrips. Choose either the {@spell Entangle|XPHB} or {@spell Hail of Thorns|XPHB} spell. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Jormungandr
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Poison Resilience
entries: If you take Poison damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to give yourself {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage until the end of your next turn. You can use this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Serpent Kinship
entries: You always have the {@spell Animal Friendship|XPHB} and {@spell Speak with Animals|XPHB} spells prepared. You can cast each spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. When you cast these spells without a spell slot, you may only target snakes and serpents. You can also cast these spells using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Serpent's Tongue
entries: You know the {@language Draconic} language.

feat.name: Blessing of Loki
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Expert Liar
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Deception} skill. If you already have proficiency in it, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it instead.

entries.name: Trickster Magic
entries: You learn the {@spell Minor Illusion|XPHB} and {@spell Vicious Mockery|XPHB} cantrips. Choose either the {@spell Disguise Self|XPHB} or {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} spell. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Sif
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gift of Dexterity
entries: When you make a Dexterity check, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll. If you already add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to a Dexterity check, you may add it an additional time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sif's Prowess
entries: You know the {@spell True Strike|XPHB} cantrip. Choose either the {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB} or {@spell Longstrider|XPHB} spell. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Thor
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Gift of Strength
entries: When you make a Strength check, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll. If you already add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to a Strength check, you may add it an additional time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Storm Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Shocking Grasp|XPHB} or {@spell Thunderclap|XPHB} cantrip (choose when you select this feat). You also always have the {@spell Thunderous Smite|XPHB} spell prepared. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Volund
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Crafter's Knack
entries: You gain proficiency with an {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB|Artisan's Tool} of your choice. If you already have proficiency with that tool, you instead have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks with it.

entries.name: Forge Magic
entries: You learn the {@spell Elementalism|XPHB} and {@spell Mending|XPHB} cantrips. Choose either the {@spell Burning Hands|XPHB} or {@spell Shield|XPHB} spell. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Wotan
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Lore Bound
entries: You gain proficiency with one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}. If you already have proficiency with the chosen skill, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in it.

entries.name: Secret Wisdom
entries: You know the {@spell Guidance|XPHB} cantrip. Choose a level 1 spell from any school of magic. You always have that spell prepared. You can cast the spell without expending a spell slot. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't cast that spell in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast the spell using spell slots you have of the appropriate level. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Brewer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item brewer's supplies|XPHB}.

entries.name: Discount
entries: You get a 50% discount when purchasing food and beverages.

entries.name: Quick Brewing
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can brew an invigorating mead, provided you have {@item Brewer's Supplies|XPHB} available. A creature can use a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to drink the mead, granting it {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. The mead's potency lasts until you start a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Cold Plunge Training
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cold Water Training
entries: While in water, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG} and on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) checks to swim.

entries.name: Arctic Dive
entries: On a turn when you dive from land into water, your movement in the water is at your normal {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} rather than half {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

feat.name: Fisher
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Survivalist
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Survival} skill.

entries.name: Boat Familiarity
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule d20 Test|XPHB|d20 Tests} made to operate water vehicles.

entries.name: Fishing Prowess
entries: When you are exploring and have access to a body of water, you can spend 1 hour to fish and obtain enough food for up to 6 people for 1 day.

feat.name: Norn-Touched
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Fates' Favor
entries: Once per day, when you make a {@variantrule d20 Test|XPHB}, you can add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the result. You can see the result of the roll before you use this feature.

entries.name: Fates' Scorn
entries: Once per day, when another creature rolls a {@dice d20} for an attack roll or ability check, you can subtract your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} from the result. You can see the result of the roll before you use this feature.

feat.name: Northern Raider
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Born on the Water
entries: You gain proficiency in {@item navigator's tools|XPHB}.

entries.name: Blood in the Water
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks that you make the turn that you exit the water or exit a ship.

feat.name: Sea Wolf
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Tactical Boarder
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics}) and Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks made to board vehicles.

entries.name: Reaver's Ferocity
entries: When you score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against a creature with a melee attack, you can make another melee attack against the same creature or an adjacent creature as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

feat.name: Snowrunner
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Ice Walking
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws and ability checks to maintain your balance on slippery surfaces and on snow.

entries.name: Winter's Edge
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks in snowy or icy terrain.

feat.name: Well-Versed
entries: You know the sagas of your people and others and can use that knowledge to help you. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Lore Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency in one musical instrument and one of the following skills: {@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}.

entries.name: Useful Knowledge
entries: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}, {@skill History}, {@skill Nature}, or {@skill Religion}) check, you can give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the roll. You can do this a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Axe Fighter
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Axe Flurry
entries: Once on each of your turns, if you hit a creature with a {@item Handaxe|XPHB}, you can make an extra attack with a {@item Handaxe|XPHB} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

entries.name: Precise Topple
entries: When you hit a creature with a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the Constitution saving throw to avoid having the {@condition Prone} condition caused by the {@itemMastery Topple} property of the {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}.

entries.name: Unending Cleave
entries: The number of additional creatures you can attack using the {@itemMastery Cleave} property of a {@item Greataxe|XPHB} increases by a number equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} (rounded down).

feat.name: Axe Thrower
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Returning Throw
entries: When you make a ranged weapon attack with a {@item Handaxe|XPHB} and miss on your attack roll, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on the same turn to catch the weapon as it whirls back to you.

feat.name: Battle Cry
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Thunderous Cry
entries: You can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to release a frightening battle cry. Roll a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check. One creature of your choice that can hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to your Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check result or have the {@condition Frightened} condition for {@dice 1d4} rounds. The target can make a new saving throw at the end of each of its turns to end the effect. Once you've used this ability, you can't use it again until you've completed a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

At higher levels, you can target an additional number of creatures with this ability. At 9th level, you can target two creatures. At 15th level, you can target three creatures, and the range of this ability increases to 60 feet.

feat.name: Blessing of Angrboda and Bergelmir
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Thunderous Strike
entries: When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you can choose to deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Thunder damage. You can use your Thunderous Strike a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Prophetic Vision
entries: As a {@action Magic} action, you can choose one Divination spell with a casting time of 1 action (from any spell list) of a level you can cast that is no more than half your character level and cast it without expending a spell slot. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability stat. Once you use this feat to cast the spell, you can't use it again until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Blessing of Bragi
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Love of the Vanir
entries: You gain {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} with the {@skill Persuasion} skill if you don't already have it, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) checks.

feat.name: Blessing of Heimdall
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Awareness of the Guardian
entries: You have {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} in the Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) skill. If you already have {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in that skill. In addition, when you make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check, you can decide to give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. You can do this a number of times per day equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Herald's Horn
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@item Horn|XPHB}.

entries.name: Vigilance
entries: When you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, you can reroll the check but must use the new result. Once you use this feature, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

feat.name: Blessing of Hel
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Forestall the End
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}.

entries.name: Resurgence
entries: If you become {@variantrule Stable|XPHB} following a third successful {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}, or if you are stabilized by another creature, you immediately recover {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 1d6} plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: The Bell Tolls
entries: You know the {@spell Spare the Dying|XPHB} and {@spell Toll the Dead|XPHB} cantrips. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this feat's spells (choose when you select this feat).

feat.name: Blessing of Njord
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Call Sea Serpent
entries: You can cast {@spell Find Steed|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. You can cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to cast it in that way when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Njord's Protection
entries: You can breathe water as well as air, and automatically succeed on saves against {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG} while submerged in water. You also have a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

feat.name: Blessing of Skadi
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Hunter's Eye
entries: When you use the {@action Attack|XPHB} action to make a ranged weapon attack, you can choose to give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll. Once you use this feature you must finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

entries.name: Snowpace
entries: Your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet when you move on ice or snow, and you never treat those types of terrain as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

feat.name: Blessing of the Snow Queen
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Frozen Edge
entries: You know the {@spell Ice Knife|XPHB} Spell. You can cast it without using a spell slot a number of times per day equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also cast this spell using any spell slots you have. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell (choose when you select this feat).

entries.name: Shield of the North Wind
entries: If you fail a saving throw against a spell or effect that deals Cold damage, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this feature you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

feat.name: Blessing of Tyr
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Bravery
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws made to avoid or end the {@condition Frightened} condition.

entries.name: Justicar
entries: As a {@action Magic} action, you can touch a creature and compel it to tell the truth. The creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature can't speak a deliberate lie for 1 minute. You know whether a creature succeeds or fails on this save. An affected creature is aware of the spell and can avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive yet must be truthful.
You can use this feature at will, but when you use it on a creature, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it on that creature again.

feat.name: Blood of the Berserker
entries: You inherited a touch of the ferocity of a berserker ancestor. You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Berserker Fury
entries: When you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to enter a frenzied state. While in this fury, your melee weapon attacks deal extra damage equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you don't have the {@condition Unconscious} condition when you are reduced to 0 HP (though you still make {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saves} as normal).
