monsterFluff.name: Brunnmigi
entries: {@i Poison-Spitting Plague Fox}
{@color A large bear or foxlike beast with mottled, patchy fur, and a distended belly scuttles about. It is covered in boils and pustules.|006abe}

A brunnmigi is a monstrous creature that spreads disease and pollutes sources of fresh water. Brunnmigi delight in the suffering of others, typically by befouling wells and streams with their plague-bearing spittle. Settlements in the Northlands rely on painstakingly dug wells, and having their source of water rendered unusable often leads to the entire village scattering, lest they succumb to thirst.

monsterFluff.name: Fafnir
entries: {@i Dwarf Cursed into Dragon Form}

{@color This bat-winged monster has a sinuous body covered in scales the color of weathered iron. Its limbs are powerful, but warped, bending in impossible ways. The monster's head is like that of a dragon, but it has too many eyes, and whiplike tentacles circle its skull like a crest. Its maw is lined with rows of long fangs, and its underside is speckled with golden coins, jewelry, and gemstones embedded between its scales.|006abe}

Fafnir was once a dwarf, one of the four sons of the famed smith Hreidmarr. When their brother was mistakenly slain by Loki, the clever god gave their father a magical ring as wergild. This item, called Andvaranaut, was supposed to bring untold wealth, but the ring bore a horrible curse. Inflamed by greed, Fafnir killed his father to possess the ring and drove his brothers into exile. The curse and his own avarice warped and changed the dwarf until Fafnir transformed into a serpentine dragon with gold coins and gems embedded in his belly. It also destroyed Andvaranaut.

Fafnir makes his lairs in isolated caves often carved into the base of a hills or into the side of high cliffs. He changes lairs frequently, paranoid that his hoard will be stolen from him. The area within 1 mile of Fafnir's current lair is warped, causing creatures to become greedy and possessive of their belongings.

monsterFluff.name: Nidhogg-Blooded Drake
entries: {@i Twisted Burrowing Serpent}
{@color This wolf-sized dragon has spindly legs and a wide jaw filled with numerous rows of small, sharp teeth.|006abe}

Nidhogg-blooded drakes are blessed, or some suggest, corrupted, by the dread wyrm Nidhogg, who lies imprisoned beneath the World Tree, constantly gnawing on the roots. Nidhogg's foul influence spreads from Yggdrasil infrequently, but drakes attracted to his lair are imbued with his darkness before they venture into the wider world.

monsterFluff.name: Eikthyrnir
entries: {@i Thorny Stag Horror}

{@color The creature's pelt resembles that of a deer, but denser and shaggy, like that of a bear. Its antlers are disproportionately large and curved into long, wickedly sharp points above eyes that burn with uncanny fire. Thorny brambles have pushed through the beast's skin from within, wrapping around its body and antlers like climbing ivy.|006abe}

Eikthyrnir are enormous stag-like horrors formed when stags consume World Tree acorns that have been corrupted by evil energies. They stalk the branches of the World Trees, occasionally reaching mortal planes, where they spread horror and carnage.

monsterFluff.name: Fenrikyn
entries: {@i Howling Fangs and Chains}
{@color This massive, warped canine has frothing jaws and chains that wrap around its body, obeying its every whim.|006abe}

Fenrikyn are warped worgs and winter wolves, altered by the influence of Fenris, the Great Wolf. Fenrikyn roam the cold forests and the hills of the Northlands, devouring all that they encounter. Generally solitary, fenrikyn have been known to gather into small packs or to take over a pack of wolves or worgs. Though they despise most living things, they reserve their greatest enmity for good-aligned canines and followers of the god Tyr.

monsterFluff.name: Fleshcrawler
entries: {@i Crawling Flesh that Wears a Face}

{@color This creature resembles a humanoid-shaped collection of partially formed body parts, including muscles, bones, organs, ligaments, and facial features. Countless small pseudopods squirm from every part of its body, occasionally falling off and writhing as if still alive.|006abe}

Horrific nightmares that somehow escaped from the sealed land of Hyperborea, fleshcrawlers seek to reproduce and spread their infestation across the world while causing as much pain and destruction as possible.

Their attacks temporarily warp the physical form of the target, twisting flesh and bone painfully. These attacks also renders the victim potentially vulnerable to infestation by the flesh-like webs that they spawn.

Once a host is infected, the fleshcrawler controls that creature's actions like a puppeteer. Over the course of a few days, the host grows weaker as it is consumed from within, until nothing remains of the original form but its skin. This becomes a cocoon for a new fleshcrawler, which emerges in its fully grown form.

Fleshcrawlers are typically encountered alone or in small groups, though some keep a clutch of newly infected humanoids nearby. Thanks to its limited telepathy, the fleshcrawler can sense the presence of others of its kind and rarely competes for prey or new hosts.

monsterFluff.name: Fossegrim
entries: {@i Cavorting Fey Musicians}

{@color This small being is attired in a fur-lined vest and pointed cap. It has greenish skin, a long nose, and twinkling black eyes. It smiles mischievously and pulls a fiddle from behind its back.|006abe}

Mysterious water fey that are mystically linked to waterfalls and streams, fossegrim resemble gnome-sized creatures with vaguely troll-like features, including pale green skin and bulbous noses. Fossegrim can also disguise themselves as attractive humanoids of the species most prevalent in the region to lure humanoids into heedless revelry.

Every fossegrim owns a musical instrument, such as a fiddle, lyre, or shawm, which it can play to weave powerful, enchanted melodies. While a fossegrim's musical instrument doesn't display any magical properties in the hands of others, some fossegrim have been known to teach talented humans and elves some of their tricks in exchange for companionship or food.

monsterFluff.name: Garmr
entries: {@i Roaring Maw of the Underworld}

{@color This large, foul-looking hound possesses a coat of worm-eaten fur in shades of black and gray, an oversized mouth, and glowing eyes. It snarls menacingly, the ground trembling beneath it.|006abe}

The garmr is a horse-sized canine fiend with mangy black fur dripping with maggots, and a massive mouth filled with razor-sharp fangs that rot anything it bites. Garmrs are said to be born from a mythical hound that serves the goddess Hel, or somehow related to Fenris. They are vicious and cruel creatures that bully fiends and spirits and sometimes lead groups of devils and lesser undead into battle.

Garmrs can create earth tremors with their howls, and several garmrs working together can cause powerful shockwaves similar to those produced by an earthquake. Their howls are particularly effective in subterranean tunnels and passages, and can be used to block off entrances or bury intruders.
Despite their similarities to hell hounds, garmrs are distinct creatures. Meetings between the two types of creatures almost always end in battle unless a more powerful fiend controls both groups.

monsterFluff.name: Jotun
entries: {@i World-shaking Primordial Giants}
{@color Tall enough to look a titan in the eye and strong enough to wrestle a dragon, jotun are the lords of giantkind and the immortal enemies of the gods.|006abe}

The enormous halls of the jotun are carved in mountains and glaciers throughout the North. As foes of the Northern gods, jotun plot to regain their former status as lords of creation. Many know ancient secrets and snippets of antediluvian arcane lore, and the most powerful among them straddle the line between mortal and demigod.

Like many giants, jotun enjoy a challenge. Only the mightiest heroes can challenge a jotun's might in physical combat, and most resort to cunning or trickery to defeat a jotun. However, jotun are no fools and catch on to trickery quickly.

monsterFluff.name: Lightning Giant
entries: {@i Wayward Children of Storms}

{@color Standing more than twice as tall as a human, this gray-skinned giant has pure white eyes and hands that crackle with tendrils of electricity. A bolt of lightning coalesces in the giant's hands into a staff of glowing blue-white energy that it wields with fearsome intent.|006abe}

Lightning giants dwell in large, windy caves and storm-struck keeps in mountainous terrain, raising giant goats and keeping dire wolves as pets. They are muscular and humanlike in appearance, with hair constantly blown as if by a gale, and eyes and skin crackling with electricity.

Northlanders sometimes refer to these giants as the children of Thor, a fact the Thunder God is quick to refute. They believe that the first lightning giant resulted from a union between Thor and a particularly attractive hill giant maiden. These tales do not amuse lightning giants, and they take umbrage with anyone who spouts them. The shield-maidens of Sif hold particular hatred for these giants, viewing their mere existence as a slight upon their patron goddess.

While they don't share the same habitat as storm giants, lightning giants revere them for their greater prowess and size, and defer to them whenever they meet. Storm giants don't view lightning giants quite as favorably, viewing them as overly clingy.

monsterFluff.name: Thrudgelmir Giant
entries: {@i Multiheaded Giant of Malice}

{@color Six distinct heads rise from the massive shoulders of this giant, which towers above its surroundings. Blue, runic tattoos adorn its exposed flesh, and it holds a black iron maul in each hand. It smashes the mauls together, releasing sparks of elemental energy as it prepares to attack.|006abe}

Millennia ago, a clan of giants in the far north discovered something alien in their endless realm of ice and snow. The exact nature of this object is not known, though some speculate it was a Hyperborean relic or perhaps a device from beyond the mortal plane. Whatever its origin, the strange item warped their minds and bodies, causing them to sprout additional heads and increasing their malevolence sixfold.

Thrudgelmir are intelligent and remorseless hunters that require substantial amounts of food to sustain their grotesque frames. Seldom do thrudgelmir giants gather in numbers, but when they do, the folk of the Northlands fear what may come of it.

monsterFluff.name: Thursir Giant
entries: {@i Canny Gluttonous Crafters}
{@color The giant's hair and beard are plaited with rings and other bits of decorative stone and metal, and it carries a large, rune-inscribed hammer.|006abe}

Greedy and aggressively competitive, thursir are smaller than most types of giants. They dwell in vast caverns under frozen mountains, where they labor to forge chains, armor, and massive engines of war. Items forged by a thursir are of the highest quality, and other giants often seek thursir smiths to outfit their people in times of strife.
When not toiling at the forge, these giants entertain themselves with gluttonous feasts and boisterous wrestling competitions, or they raid human settlements for food and valuables.

monsterFluff.name: Tundra Gnoll
entries: {@i Hunters of the Frigid Wastes}

{@color A lean hyena-headed hunter with dirty white fur leaps up through the cover of the snow, its hand clasped around a twisted metal blade. The creature emits a low rumble from the back of its throat as it fixes glowing blue eyes on the nearest threat.|006abe}

Tundra gnolls dwell in the blizzard-ravaged deserts and plains of the Northlands. They are fierce hunters that prey on nearly all other denizens of the lands they inhabit. A tundra gnoll's fur is a light, ice-white color, allowing it to blend seamlessly into the snowy background, though older hunters sometimes have a blue tinge to their fur.

Tundra gnolls are more cunning and patient than their brethren in other lands and can spend hours waiting for potential prey to pass by. This is often necessary, considering the bleak and inhospitable terrain in which they live. They typically dwell in small tribes in tundra regions but can also be found in pine barrens and snow-covered hills.
Giants and hags sometimes employ tundra gnolls in their forces, though they can only be adequately managed through the use of force, intimidation, or substantial bribes of food and treasure.

monsterFluff.name: Grendelkyn
entries: {@i Lurking Shadow of Terror}
{@color Appearing out of the shadows, this creature is a hideous patchwork of fur and scales, with ungainly arms and an elongated mouth filled with wicked teeth.|006abe}

A Grendelkyn is a monstrous fey clad in writhing shadows, with overly long arms, bloody talons, and a misshapen head. They despise humanoids and regularly creep into longhouses and other locations under the cover of night to snatch up unwary prey, focusing their attacks on the most vulnerable members of the household.

Grendelkyn can breathe and operate normally underwater, and their lairs are often located in deep lakes or ponds on the edge of civilization. Despite their appearance, they are not related to trolls and are thought to be tied to an ancient story surrounding a festive mead hall and the hero who frequented it.

monsterFluff.name: Hafgufa
entries: {@i Lurking Ship Destroyers}
{@color A massive predatory fish the size of an island just finishes gobbling the last of a whale when it turns its eyes on your ship.|006abe}

The hafgufa is a titanic sea monster that preys on whales and ships. A hafgufa often lurks near the surface along trade routes, its mouth open so wide that its teeth jut above the waterline and appear as rocks that must be navigated between.

When attacking, the hafgufa typically uses its terrible breath to incapacitate prey before plucking them up with its tentacles to feed into its open mouth. Alternatively, it simply attacks the ship, ripping it to shreds and then grabbing sailors from the water.

The hafgufa's gullet often contains valuable or interesting objects. Since the creature lives for centuries, the item could have been lost for generations. Roll on or choose a result from the {@table Swallowed Treasure|NorthlandsWorldbook} table (or any item of your choice) to determine what a swallowed creature finds.

items.name: Hafgufa Spawn
entries: Every 20 to 30 years, a hafgufa spawns thousands of worm-sized wriggling offspring. These spawn feed on one another, growing rapidly as they consume their kin. The few remaining spawn separate to find their own hunting grounds, often a fjord or bay where they can prey on fish, or the people who fish those waters.

This predation can last for weeks or months, until the hafgufa spawn has sated its hunger and swims to a deep, dark place in the ocean to sleep and grow into its full size over the course of the next few years.

monsterFluff.name: Hamingja
entries: {@i Friendly Guiding Spirit}
{@color There is a stirring in the air, and then a creature materializes out of the emptiness. The being is small and vaguely foxlike, with luminous fur and eyes that radiate a warm kindness.|006abe}

Hamingjas are beneficial celestial spirits that attach themselves to worthy individuals of good heart or heroic destiny. They are naturally invisible and only show themselves when their hosts are in mortal danger. When a hamingja is visible, it typically appears as a domestic animal, such as a cat or dog, or more rarely an attractive humanoid. No matter its shape, the hamingja's form is outlined with a shimmering radiance. Its natural form is that of a canine or feline creature with radiant eyes and iridescent fur.

Hamingjas provide their hosts with a shot of luck when needed, transferring some of their spiritual essence to the host. A hamingja only leaves its host when the host is killed, the hamingja is destroyed, or the host becomes evil in alignment.
Rarely, a hamingja stays with the same family or clan for decades or even centuries, jumping from one family member or clan member to the next.

monsterFluff.name: Jorumungkyn
entries: {@i Horrid Serpent of the Depths}

{@color This titanic monster is a chimera of fish and serpent parts, all covered in greenish-white scales and black spines. Its body leaks a foul greenish-black oozes. It roars, a wheezing shriek, its luminous green eyes the size of shields.|006abe}

Considered the lesser offspring of the famed World Serpent, jorumungkyn are gigantic sea serpents displaying a mix of a deep-sea fish and dragon features. Their ghostly coils rise from the frigid chasms of the world's oceans to encircle ships and drag them down to a watery grave. Jorumungkyn are infamous for the lethality of the poison that bubbles from their mouths and pores. This poison acts like oil in water, forming a deadly layer on the surface of any ground or liquid it touches.

Jorumungkyn stalk the seas and attack anything that gets in their way. They are a blight upon the oceans and are hated by most intelligent underwater species. Occasionally, aboleths attempt to enslave jorumungkyn to do their bidding. While this typically results in the aboleth being killed or severely injured, sometimes the aberration wins out, and it gains a powerful servant in the process.

monsterFluff.name: Sea Lindwurm
entries: {@i Seal Snake of the Bitter Waves}

{@color At first, this creature resembles a normal, if gigantic seal with a disturbingly large mouth. But when it gets closer, you realize that the beast is anything but normal. Its skin is covered in fine scales, and short spiny ridges sprout from its back. It opens its mouth to reveal shark-like teeth.|006abe}

Unwary or ignorant hunters and sailors often mistake sea lindwurms for enormous seals. However, while their heads are vaguely seal-like, their bodies are more serpentine in appearance, with smooth, blackish-purple scales and large flippers that allow them to drag themselves up onto ice floes and beaches on the rare occasions when they leave the water's safety.

Sea lindwurms use their seal-like appearance to sneak up on unwary boats, but this is not their only means of capturing prey. Their bite carries a potent toxin that causes a spreading paralysis in their victims, and they can slap their flippers on the water's surface to stun enemies.
Sea lindwurms and common lindwurms sometimes meet out on the pack ice or in fjords. Typically, these meetings end in a furious struggle between the two monsters.

monsterFluff.name: Malrgotr
entries: {@i Iron Bristles, Golden Tusks}

{@color A boar the size of a small cart, this monster has a mane of golden bristles covering its head and upper body, and large tusks and teeth that also seem to be composed of golden metal. The creature strikes the ground with sharp hooves, raising clods of dirt, and growls threateningly.|006abe}

The malrgotr is a monstrous boar-like creature inhabiting dark, misty forests and peatlands. Its body is covered in long metallic bristles, and its tusks shine gold in what little sunlight filters through the clouds and mist. While the malrgotr is a living creature, much of its body is composed of inorganic metal, almost as if it were the work of a divine crafter like Volund.

The malrgotr is not an evil creature and behaves much like an ordinary boar in the wilds. However, it appears to be infuriated by engineered structures, such as walls or farmsteads. It attempts to destroy any such structure it encounters, even if doing so would put it in danger.
Some have postulated a connection between the malrgotr and the legendary gullinbursti, a massive boar with golden features created by the dwarves for the goddess Freyja.
A malrgotr's dead body can be harvested for gold and iron. Its corpse provides 50 pounds of iron and 20 pounds of gold.

monsterFluff.name: Great Ogre
entries: {@i Hulk of Chaos and Ruin}

{@color This giant wears a mishmash of furs and leather and carries a massive ship's anchor in its hands. Its arms and chest bulge with rippling muscles, and its face radiates a brutish malevolence.|006abe}

Ogres are one of the more prolific giant species of the Northlands. Large groups of ogres frequently rampage across the forests and hills, attacking communities of dwarves, humans, and trollkin. At the head of many of these groups stands an ogre that towers over the rest, an abomination of bulging muscle and fearsome tusks.

Angrboda and Bergelmir created the first great ogre after a contest ensued between the two deities to see who could improve upon the ordinary ogre, often viewed as the weakest of all the giants. In the end, neither god won, resulting in a failed behemoth of enormous size that still retained the common ogre's avarice, selfishness, and lust for destruction.

Great ogres take enormous pleasure in smashing beautiful things and reducing humanoids to gory paste. They often wield tree trunks and anchors as mauls, and the vilest among them wear mummified humanoid limbs as jewelry.

monsterFluff.name: Runewright
entries: {@i Greedy Undead Wizard}
{@color A skeletally thin, robed figure saunters toward you, writhing runes on its gray skin glowing with putrid light.|006abe}

A runewright is a rune using wizard whose obsession with gathering magical knowledge and power continues beyond its death. Runewrights seek magic of all kinds, hoping that amassing it will give them insight into the nature of the runes, and indeed the fundamental nature of magic itself. It is a hunger that will never be sated and only ends with the runewright's destruction.

A runewright bears some resemblance to the person it was in life, especially with regard to its clothing and adornments. However, beneath its clothes, its skin takes on a stony hue, with glowing, almost writhing runes carved into it. When the runewright uses the power of a particular rune, that rune glows with a putrid light. The only rune not inscribed on the skin of a runewright is Dagaz, which symbolizes laying the dead to rest.

monsterFluff.name: Selkie
entries: {@i Seal-Skin Shapechanger}

{@color A young man dances on the shore, graceful upon the sand. When he notices you, he stops and reaches for a nearby cloak. As it swirls around his shoulders, he disappears. In his place, a seal slips beneath the ocean waves.|006abe}

Selkies are fey creatures that transform into seals using magical sealskins. Their humanoid forms are beautiful, with webbed hands and feet. If deprived of its sealskin, a selkie can't change its shape and will do all it can to retrieve the skin. Selkies vary in temperament; some are kind, while others are malicious tricksters.

Selkies live on secluded islands but travel to coastlands in summer to trade with coastal enclaves, sometimes even wooing or marrying fisherfolk. Selkies rarely remain, for the sea and its freedom call to them each high tide.

Selkies believe that long ago, an archfey of seals gave them their magical sealskins. Stealing a selkie's sealskin is considered the gravest of crimes, and they will band together to retrieve a stolen sealskin, often with violent consequences. Some selkies have learned to disguise their skins as items of clothing, especially disheveled or mundane clothing, such as belts, hats, vests, or cloaks, to avoid attracting the attention of thieves. An individual selkie's skin works only for them, becoming nonmagical when it dies, and can't be used by anyone else, even other selkies.

Legends tell of selkie tribes that use the skins of other sea animals to change shape. Such selkies use the skins of sharks, giant sea horses, or even orcas, and can assume those forms instead of a seal form.

monsterFluff.name: Skein Witch
entries: {@i Fell Fateweaver}
{@color The shambling figure is draped in writhing, diamond thread. Its skin is translucent, and dozens of quivering hourglasses are suspended inside its body in place of organs.|006abe}

Skein witches are curators of destiny and enforcers of what must be. They voyage across the planes, weaving the strands of fate at the behest of their goddess creator. Although they carry out their charge without regard to petty mortal concerns, they can be persuaded to bend fate for powerful petitioners whose interests align with those of their goddess.

Despite their supernatural abilities, a skein witch's physical body is frail. Because of that, they tend to surround themselves with undead, constructs, or other brutish, soulless guardians cut free from the thread of fate.
Legends say that if a Deck of Many Things is brought close to a skein witch, the witch emits a psychic wail and disintegrates.

monsterFluff.name: Skeljaskra
entries: {@i Scaled Rolling Doom}
{@color A hippo-sized beast with blue-white, pangolin-like armor, spits burning poison at a nearby villager.|006abe}

The voracious skeljaskra is known for indiscriminately devouring creatures, vegetation, and structures over the course of several days of constant movement and destruction. A single skeljaskra can consume hundreds of pounds of food in a single day, whether that takes the form of an elk, a field of crops, or an entire small house. Once it has sated its legendary appetite, the skeljaskra finds a cave to slumber in for weeks while it digests its massive meal.

Fortunately, the skeljaskra is typically encountered alone. However, in ill-fated years, an entire pack can emerge from the wilderness, descending on a village and devouring everything in its path. Such an event sends all living creatures fleeing from the utter destruction and leaves almost nothing behind.
Although skeljaskra can consume virtually anything, they don't digest minerals. Their droppings often contain metal or stone remnants of past meals, from iron nails to coins to small gemstones.
Once every few generations, a skeljaskra hibernates in a place suffused by magic. Over many years, it grows into a threat to entire settlements. Such horrors are known as dread skeljaskra.

monsterFluff.name: Dread Skeljaskra
entries: Once every few generations, a skeljaskra hibernates in a place suffused by magic. Over many years, it grows into a threat to entire settlements. Such horrors are known as dread skeljaskra.

monsterFluff.name: Skogsra
entries: {@i Bloodthirsty Spirit of the Woods}
{@color A bewildered traveler wanders through the forest ahead of you, clearly lost.|006abe}

The skogsra is a malign forest creature that feeds on mortal blood. It often presents itself as a beautiful person of friendly temperament, seeking the help of a traveler or hunter. It entices its victims into the forest, where it tears them to shreds as it reveals its true form: a hollow, bark-skinned monster with long, twisted limbs tipped with venomous claws. The skogsra can extend fleshy vines out of its hollow form to grasp and tangle its prey. It uses these natural weapons to overcome and paralyze its target, pulling the helpless victim into its hollow body, where it can consume the poor soul later at its leisure.
When outnumbered or facing a potent enemy, the skogsra channels the power of the storm, calling forth mighty winds, hail, and lightning.

monsterFluff.name: Fjord Troll
entries: {@i Canny, Regenerating Fisherfolk}
{@color What looks like a troll with slimy skin and webbed fingers is pulling up a net full of fish onto a boat. It spots you and grins maliciously.|006abe}

Fjord trolls dwell on the coastlines of the Northern fjords and fish for sustenance in boats of their own making. They are at home in water and possess a fatty layer beneath their skin that helps protect them from the near-freezing temperatures. Webbing between their fingers and toes aid them in swimming. Despite their ease in the water, fjord trolls often fish from canoes constructed of wood and hide, which they row using their long arms and webbed hands instead of oars or paddles. Those same hands end in hooked and barbed claws that secrete a paralytic poison. This makes them effective at capturing fish and other creatures of the coast. They also have a special craw that they can fill with ice cold water and spit at their enemies.

monsterFluff.name: Gilitrutt Troll
entries: {@i Loyal, shapeshifting guardian troll}
{@color A small troll lopes along the forest floor, muttering to itself. When it spots you, it shifts into a massive hound and charges.|006abe}

Gilitrutt trolls are among the smallest of troll-kind but make up for their diminutive stature by being able to shapeshift into the form of a giant hound. They mostly dwell with other trolls, acting in supporting roles, such as companions, guards, and hunting partners. Gilitrutt trolls have been known to abduct people from other settlements, and they sometimes do so after toying with the individual, making some kind of bargain the abductee typically finds difficult to fulfill.

Gilitrutt trolls are fiercely loyal, and if their companions or settlements are under threat, they defend them savagely, even giving their own lives in that defense. In addition to speaking Giant, gilitrutt trolls can communicate with one another through a series of grunts, growls, clicks, and whistles.

monsterFluff.name: Glacial Troll
entries: {@i Grotesque Glacial Terror}

{@color A layer of jagged blue ice covers the back, arms, and claws of this pale green troll. Its eyes glow with demonic cerulean radiance, and black veins pulse underneath its translucent flesh.|006abe}

Trolls have adapted to almost every environment in the world, from sweltering jungles to magically tainted sewers, yet few environments are as harsh as the glaciers and tundra deserts of the Northlands, places most trolls fear to tread.

Dwelling among these glaciers is the glacial troll, a giant that feeds on the frozen bodies of unlucky creatures. What makes the glacial troll even more repulsive is that many of the creatures trapped in ice are still vaguely aware of their surroundings when the troll begins to feed.
Glacial trolls sometimes work as guards for frost giants, though the frost giants are careful to provide the trolls with sufficient food to keep them satisfied.

monsterFluff.name: Wind Troll
entries: {@i Capricious Storm-chasing Prankster}
{@color A small troll with blue-green skin stands at the prow of the enemy ship, its blue hair whipping about, despite the absence of wind.|006abe}

Wind trolls delight in storms of all kinds and will seek them out to perform intricate dances in their gales. The true nature of their connection to storms is unknown. Some believe that a wind troll absorbs a storm's power to sustain it, drawing energy and even life from such powerful occurrences. Others believe that wind trolls worship storm gods, such as Thor, or might have connections to them, and so communing with storms is a kind of religious experience for them. Whatever the reason, they are often found in the midst of storms—the larger and more chaotic, the better.

Legends have it that the first wind trolls were created by Thor and Loki, who wished to turn some giantkin against Boreas and his minions. Thor soon lost interest, so instead of teaching the wind trolls to excel in battle, Loki taught them to be tricksters and stoked their interest in interfering with others.

monsterFluff.name: Buried Lord Vaettir
entries: {@i Restless Wrathful Undead}
{@color An armored undead warrior rises from the casket, its eyes glowing with righteous indignation.|006abe}

Buried lord vaettir are undead jarls and chieftains who arise from ancient barrows. The power and presence they possessed in life remains with them after death, allowing them to command other vaettir, who instinctively recognize their authority. They are almost always accompanied by a retinue of other vaettir who served them, or others like them, while alive.
A buried lord's status can be seen in the quality of the armor and scraps of clothing that still cover it, and in its poise, which retains its lordly quality.
While all vaettir fiercely guard their burial sites, possessions, and honor, buried lord vaettir do so with a ferocity greater than their brethren.

monsterFluff.name: Drowned Raider Vaettir
entries: {@i Rotting Waterlogged Warrior}
{@color Brown liquid drips off the corpse of a waterlogged warrior and with it, the stench of decay and mold.|006abe}

Drowned raider vaettir are like others of their kind—restless undead warriors who defend their belongings and burial places. They are called drowned raiders, however, because their burial sites have been flooded or otherwise contaminated with sea water, which alters their forms over time. A drowned raider vaettir has rotten, corrupted flesh that is falling off its skeleton, and it drips liquid constantly. It can regurgitate a stream of rotten, flesh-stripping seawater from its mouth.

While vaettir often defend their burial sites and possessions with a persistent fury, drowned raider vaettir tend to be more chaotic and unpredictable due to the disruption of their lairs and their bodies.

Sometimes, the flooding of a burial site pulls the vaettir's belongings out of their resting place and deposits them in distant places, drawn by the sea's currents. The drowned raider is drawn to these far-flung objects and will hunt them down in an attempt to restore itself to rest.

monsterFluff.name: Vedaja
entries: {@i Small Murderous Homunculus}
{@color A curious wooden statue, about the size of a child, stands alone, facing a forlorn corner of the desolate room.|006abe}

Vedaja are little constructs, usually made of wood or horn, and animated by rune magic. The runes are carved into the vedaja's body along with some of its creator's blood. Vedaja were once used for a variety of purposes, but in recent years, they have mostly been animated with violence in mind. Vedaja hands are malleable and can strike in the form of a fist or narrow to a sharp, piercing point.

The appearance of each vedaja varies, though they are usually created in humanoid form. The magical energy that animates a vedaja burns inside of it and is visible through its hollow eye holes, burning with baleful light. If the vedaja doesn't move, it appears to be an inanimate wooden statuette.
Given its size, a vedaja stalks its prey from the shadows, using its inanimate appearance at times to hide in plain sight. At times, only the blood from its previous prey betrays its nature.

monsterFluff.name: Andahestur
entries: {@i Wingless flying steeds}
{@color A majestic silvery grey steed soars through the air without the aid of wings, its silver hooves and eyes glinting in the waning afternoon sun.|006abe}

Andahestur are the mounts granted by Odin to the Valkyries to convey them in battle. They appear as white or gray steeds with silver hooves and eyes. They cannot be purchased, but they are sometimes gifted to mortals by the gods for heroic deeds or stolen from the shield-maidens by those with truly blackened hearts.

monsterFluff.name: Moose
entries: {@i Crown-Antlered Beast}
{@color The majestic beast stands nearly 7 feet tall at the shoulder, its head crowned with wide, palmed antlers.|006abe}
The temperamental moose (also called Elg) is respected for its size and majesty by the people of the Northlands.

monsterFluff.name: Reindeer
entries: {@i Snow-Treading Wanderer}
{@color Most of the brown in this large deer's coast has shed, revealing white underneath. It appears ready for the winter as it bounds through the first flurries of the year.|006abe}

Wild reindeer can be found in vast herds in the coldest parts of the Northlands. They are acclimated to cold weather. Wild reindeer are skittish, but domesticated ones have been bred for centuries for their meat, to pull sleds, and for milk.

monsterFluff.name: Sea Serpent
entries: {@i Swift Wave Snakes}
{@color Blue-green on top with white underbellies, these enormous eel-like creatures have prominent bony ridges on their heads and wide mouths with only four sharp fangs.|006abe}

Sea serpents are most often identified while approaching by the row of sail-like fins protruding from their backs. Wild serpents are dangerous predators, but those raised from an egg imprint on their owner and make formidable mounts or guards for raiding ships.

monsterFluff.name: Sleipnirspringr
entries: {@i Eight-Legged Divine Horse}
{@color The eight-legged horse stomps its hooves in frustration, as if the entire world moves too slow for it.|006abe}

Descended from Wotan's horse Sleipnir, this breed of eight-legged horse tends toward dark pelts with elaborate and unusual markings. Larger, more intelligent, and far more willful than any breed of mortal horse, sleipnirspringr rarely allow themselves to be sold and are more likely to bond to kindred spirits that they encounter in the wilds, doing great deeds, or sowing chaos. They are exceedingly rare in the Northlands, and those who are honored with a sleipnirspringr's company are said to be heroes of great renown.

monsterFluff.name: Merchant
entries: Merchants focus on trading in goods produced by others. Some are simple shopkeepers, while others sail to distant ports to buy and sell their goods.

monsterFluff.name: Berserker Trollkin
entries: {@i Fierce Raiders and Reavers}
{@color A lanky berserker with greenish skin charges toward you, bloody spittle frothing from her mouth.|006abe}

In the North, the masses huddle in fear at night, dreading the horns and howls of reavers come to slaughter and pillage. Trollkin have a well-deserved reputation for their prowess on the battlefield and longship deck. Raiding is a staple industry among the settlements in the North, and the trollkin are in high demand by recruiting captains and warlords.

In a trollkin village, warriors who prove themselves to be especially violent undergo special rituals to imbue them with the primal power of the North. Trollkin Berserkers push to fight in the front lines, eager to bring their power to bear against their foes.

Trollkin raiders might crew pillaging longships, hunt alongside a troop of other reavers, or be found among mercenary companies. They are trained equally in ranged and melee combat, depending on their regenerative nature to keep them in the battleline.

monsterFluff.name: Apprentice Witch
entries: Witches seek knowledge, power, and connection in their communion with nature and the forces beyond mortal perception. They cultivate their bonds to eldritch forces, some becoming the guardians at the gate, attendants of deep knowledge, while others hold darker desires.

charoption.name: Bloodsworn
entries: {@i You have been wronged. Now your fate is painted with blood.}

Among the Northlanders, no oath is more serious than an oath of vengeance. But when justice cannot be achieved by any other means, a sworn promise to mete out revenge for wrongdoing is the only answer that remains. Those who make such oaths are called Bloodsworn, and their vengeance becomes a tale told by skalds for generations.

As a Bloodsworn, your ultimate goal is revenge upon the one (or ones) who wronged you. Unfortunately, the wrongdoer is beyond your reach, at least for now. This means your plan must be carried out over weeks, months, or even longer. During this time, you'll no doubt be distracted by other adventures, but your focus demands that you always return to your oath. Bloodsworn must have been wronged or harmed in some way before the gods will accept their blood oath. In most cases, your vengeance will be fatal to your target, but in some situations, other punishments may be more fitting, especially if the wrong you're avenging doesn't itself involve a death.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Bloodsworn Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.caption: Bloodsworn Goals
rows: I must kill the one who murdered the one I love.
I cannot rest until the usurper who killed my jarl is dead by my hands.
A crew of scheming charlatans ruined my family's business. I vow to punish them in ways the law cannot.
The power-mad jarl of our lands has destroyed my community. I have a cunning plan to ensure he is overthrown.
My trusted shieldmate betrayed me and left me to die. Now I shall return the favor.
I was shamed by the false words of another. I will deliver vengeance tenfold upon my accuser.

charoption.name: Cursemarked
entries: {@i You bear the brunt of a curse of ill luck, and it'll get worse before the end.}

Northlanders place great faith in the existence of luck. The gods can bestow good fortune upon the faithful, and honorable actions can directly lead to successful endeavors. Likewise, disreputable behavior can bring failure not only to you, but to future generations of your family.

You are one of the unfortunates, chosen by fate or the gods to suffer from ill luck wherever you go. Perhaps you earned this curse through dishonor, oathbreaking, or cowardice. You might bear misfortune as a virtual heirloom, passed down to you by a disreputable ancestor. Other cursemarked are victims of witch's curses or similar supernatural effects. Whatever the reason, you can't seem to catch a break.

Strangely, the presence of a Cursemarked can often bring good fortune to those nearby. As long as your friends are willing to put up with your occasional mishaps, the long-term benefit might well be worthwhile. Meanwhile, however, the cursemarked searches for some way to atone for their misdeeds, real or imagined, knowing such a road will be long and will certainly grow worse before the end. Yet when the hand of fortune is turned against you, what else can you do?

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Cursemarked Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.caption: Cursemarked Goals
rows: I will atone for my dishonor by returning a sacred relic to a distant tomb.
I can only lift this curse by clearing the name of an ancestor falsely accused of murder.
I must prove my courage to the gods by defeating a tribe of marauding giants.
I will invoke Freyr's blessing by forging peace between two warring clans.
To end this curse, I shall endure trials of my honor, my valor, and my selflessness
I must convince Wotan himself to intervene and convince the Norns to reshape my fate.

entries.name: Cursemarked Milestone Rules
entries: Cursemarked milestones work a bit differently than those of other character threads. The milestones described below trigger when you roll for specific mechanics (saving throws, ability checks or attack roll, depending on the) and get a result within the range of numbers indicated in the bracket for each milestone.
Milestones never overlap, so if you trigger a, you can't trigger another until the start of your next turn after the duration of the previous one expires.

charoption.name: Explorer
entries: {@i Glory lies just over the horizon. Time to find it.}

Explorers occupy an unusual place in Northlands society. Though revered for their courage, they rarely find a comfortable place in a community. Driven by wanderlust, curiosity, boredom, or a simple inability to relate to civilized folks, the Explorer spends most of their time in the wilderness. Some climb mountains, others set sail for lost lands, and still others delve through dark tunnels beneath the earth. For an Explorer, the greatest treasure awaits beyond the next hill.

Whether by choice or by fate, you follow the path less traveled. Perhaps you're a rugged seafarer or mountaineer seeking discoveries in the wild. Other Explorers are treasure hunters, royal mapmakers, or seekers of truth. You might be an exile, outlaw, or iconoclast, who simply can't get along with others. Or you might be driven by vision or prophecy to forsake hearth and home for the unknown.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Explorer Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.name: GM Note
entries: This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Rangers in the party. Consult with your Ranger players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

entries.caption: Explorer Goals
rows: I shall find a route through the Bloodfjord Mountains never before traveled by mortals.
To avert Ragnarok, I must carry a prophecy to a far-flung land.
My mother died searching for the headwaters of the Tearstain River. I shall complete her quest.
I seek a sapling of the World Tree, rumored to be growing on a tiny island in the Nieder Strait.
Once I decipher the ancient map I hold, I'll delve into the depths of Narvegr Maw.
The Frozen Palace of the last Hyperborean lies somewhere in the Bleak Expanse. I'll find it and return with his icy crown.

charoption.name: Fatebound
entries: {@i Your fate is written. Make it glorious.}

Many warriors loudly boast of their desire for a noble death or an honorable end in battle, to thus earn a seat in the great hall of Valhalla. These boasts are but hopeful wishes since most individuals never see the path of their future. You, however, are not most individuals. You have been blessed, or perhaps cursed, with the knowledge of your end, though this knowledge doesn't tell you if you succeed or fail in the circumstance surrounding your death. You might know you will die facing a dark warlord, but you don't know if you will defeat her. Despite this, the Norns have given you a rare opportunity. The knowledge you possess will help you ensure your death is worthy of the sagas.

Some of those who are Fatebound are marked from birth. Others learn of their fate from seers, shamans, or divine visions. Some heroes earn this thread after engaging in activities that move the gods or the Norns to reward them with such a potent end.

entries.name: Fatebound and Death
entries: Keep in mind that having this thread may mean you can't die before your fated time, but it doesn't mean you will reach that point whole and healthy. While your fate is inevitable, luck alone determines your condition when you meet that end. Do you lead a glorious charge across the battlefield? Or are you left guarding the baggage? Has every confrontation leading up to your end prepared you to defeat your ultimate foe? Or has a lifetime of avoidance left you ill-prepared?

If a Fatebound PC is killed before their time, and magical resurrection is not an option, a GM could instead choose for them to be injured in a significant way—such as the loss of a limb or eye. These injuries should not be able to be healed without high-level magic. Alternatively, perhaps they lose one of their powerful magical items instead of their lives, or they might suffer a level of Exhaustion until they reach their next milestone. The GM and player should agree on this complication.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Fatebound Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.name: GM Note
entries: The Fatebound is an unusual thread in that its final milestone specifically describes the manner in which a character might meet with a permanent death, likely as part of the final accomplishment of their goal, and then empowers the PCs' allies as a reward. Most importantly, this thread should be something the player consciously selects.

entries.caption: Fatebound Goals
rows: I will die only after finding and facing the mightiest dragon in the land.
I will be slain by Utgard-Loki while attempting to thwart his plan to slay the gods.
To defend my people from invasion, I pledge to pay any price, including my own life.
I shall search for and find a fabled lost treasure, but I will die in the process.
I will rise to become the North's greatest reaver, then perish battling the World Serpent.
I seek the truth behind the fall of Nordheim, though it will cost my life to learn it.

charoption.name: Herald
entries: {@i Your stories don't just recount events . . . they shape history.}

Storytellers are revered in the Northlands. Whether a skald sharing tales around a fire, a lore keeper gathering sagas to pass down the generations, or a grizzled reaver frightening young warriors by recalling harrowing battles, the tradition of collecting stories is respected across nearly all cultures in the region. As a Herald, you are a proud, if temporary, part of this tradition, driven by a need to spread stories during your travels to accomplish a specific end.

Perhaps your stories encourage downtrodden karls to rise up against their cruel jarl, warn a region about an approaching invasion, or convince warriors to join your cause. Part skald, part herald, part envoy, you will use your tales and stories to sway the minds of your audience and help shape the world.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Herald Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.name: GM Note
entries: This thread brings flavorful Northlands themes into a campaign and can be taken up by characters of any class. However, it can tread on the toes of any Bards in the party. Consult with your Bard players before allowing a character to take on this thread to make sure no feelings will be hurt.

entries.caption: Herald Goals
rows: The feared invasion from Jotunheim approaches, and the country must be warned.
By telling the sagas, I will gather support for the greatest raid the North has ever launched.
My tales flatter Thor and Wotan in the hope they will support our struggle against the forces of Chernobog and Angrboda.
I spread the word of the great crusade to eradicate the darkness beneath Tanserhall. Heed my call!
I seek a lost treasure of Hyperborea, and by spreading tales of similar treasures, I hope to find a path to a hidden vault.
To rouse the people against their evil king, I shall assemble an array of sorrowful tales of corruption that cannot be ignored.

charoption.name: Legend Hunter
entries: {@i Neither storm nor night nor bloody fang shall slow your relentless pursuit.}

Hunting is as old as the Northlands itself. From volcanic peaks to frigid fens and aurora-bathed glaciers, the tales of hunters are sung alongside those of heroes and gods. While some may hunt for survival or vengeance, you are different. You are a hunter to be feared, as you hunt for the thrill of the chase and the glory of victory.

As a Legend Hunter, you may have been chosen by the Norns, blessed by a god, or forged in trials of blood and grift. No matter how you come to it, your extraordinary search for greater and greater prey sets you apart from those who hunt merely for survival. You do not merely forge trails; you craft sagas. You do not merely slay beasts; you end legends to become a legend.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Legend Hunter Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.caption: Legend Hunter Goals
rows: I will prove my valor by tracking down and slaying a legendary monster that has been destroying villages.
I hunt for a mythical two-headed jotun somewhere in the Bleak Expanse.
Besting a great dragon in its lair shall be my ultimate victory.
I will go beneath the waves to bring low the mother of all krakens.
I will bring back the head of Fenris.
My legend will be assured when I go among the roots of Yggdrasil to slay Nidhogg.

charoption.name: Sworn Huskarl
entries: {@i You carry out the will of your king, no matter the risk.}

You have pledged your loyalty to an important personage, promising to guard them or travel across the Northlands in their service, risking danger as you seek to accomplish a great task. In the past, it was expected that a huskarl would swear to serve a lord for life or until they were dismissed. While jarls still take huskarls in that way, they also accept the service of huskarls on a temporary basis, to perform specific deeds or until certain threats are dealt with. These are the types of huskarls described in this thread.

The sworn huskarl enjoys a position of respect within their lord's retinue. More than a mere bodyguard, you are a trusted agent acting on your ruler's behalf. You carry some of their authority with you, but that also comes with the responsibility to act in ways they would approve. Sworn huskarls who bring shame to their jarl don't remain in service for long.

A jarl takes on a new huskarl with a simple ceremony in which the huskarl swears an oath in the longhouse before a gathering of other members of the felag. During the oath-swearing, the goals or timeframe for the service are mentioned (unless the jarl keeps your mission a secret). Traditionally, your reasons for serving are respect for the lord, payment, or power. However, in some cases your oath may hold a secret. Perhaps you made it under threat of violence or under false pretenses. Or maybe your lord doesn't deserve such loyalty. You might serve under protest or with your own goal that's unknown to your ruler.

entries.name: Goals
entries: Work with your GM to create a goal specific to your campaign or use one from the Sworn Huskarl Goals table. The specific nature of each milestone is dependent on the goal selected and should be agreed upon by both player and GM. Use the suggested milestone benefits described in this section or create new ones based on the rules for creating a thread.

entries.caption: Sworn Huskarl Goals
rows: I will find my king's long-lost child so that my kingdom will have a true heir.
My queen depends on me to find and slay the pretender who claims a blood right to her throne.
I must root out a hidden sect of the Cult of Ragnarok that grows within my jarl's land.
Giant raiding parties threaten the land. My jarl calls upon me to destroy them and make the land safe once more.
I can only earn my freedom by finding the stolen crown of my sadistic monarch.
I serve only until I can discover a way to overthrow this corrupt king, who took the throne through dark sorcery.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Bloodsworn
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Cunning
entries: You gain proficiency in your choice of one of the following skills: {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Insight|XPHB}, or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}.

entries.name: Tool of Vengeance
entries: You gain a {@filter Common magic item|items|rarity=common} of your choice

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Bloodsworn
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Enemy of My Enemy
entries: You've made an ally, a person who is also sworn to oppose your enemy. They have granted you an underground hideout from which to conduct your campaign of vengeance.

entries.name: Wrath
entries: You can cast {@spell Wrathful Smite|XPHB}, using your choice of INT, WIS, or CHA as your spellcasting ability score. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Bloodsworn
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Tenacity
entries: You can resist effects that would slow your oath from being carried out. If you begin your turn with the {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition, you may choose to end one of those conditions. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Bloodsworn
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Dire Oath
entries: When you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, name a specific creature you swore your oath against or who stands in the way of you completing your oath. For the next 24 hours, that creature is marked by your dire oath. While the dire oath lasts, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls made against that creature, and {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on skill checks made to locate or learn about that creature.
After you use this, you must wait 7 days before you can use it again.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Cursemarked
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Tides of Fate [1–3, Saving Throws]
entries: You {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet. When this occurs, the {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} of another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you increases by 10 feet. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Greater Sacrifice
entries: When your Tides of Fate is triggered, you can choose to reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} to 0 until the start of your next turn. If you do so, in addition to the normal benefit, the chosen creature does not provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} and ignores {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} until the end of your next turn. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Cursemarked
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Burden's Shield [1–5, Saving Throws, Ability Checks]
entries: Your AC is reduced by 2. When this occurs, the AC of another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you increases by 2. These effects last until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Greater Sacrifice
entries: When your Burden's Shield is triggered, you can choose to reduce your AC by 4 instead of 2. If you do so, the AC of the chosen creature increases by 4 (instead of 2), or you can choose for it to receive the benefit of the Tide of Fate's Greater Sacrifice. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Cursemarked
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Threads Entwined [1–7, Saving Throws, Ability Checks, Attack Rolls]
entries: You can't take {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions} or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the end of your next turn. When this occurs, another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you can immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Help|XPHB}, or {@action Hide|XPHB} action, or make a single weapon attack against a target in range.

entries.name: Greater Sacrifice
entries: When your Threads Entwined is triggered, you can instead choose to do nothing this turn besides move. If you've already taken your action this turn, you instead forgo your action on your next turn. If you do so, the chosen creature can take one additional action on its next turn, except the {@action Magic|XPHB} action, or it can receive the benefit of one of the previous milestone's Greater Sacrifices. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Cursemarked
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you lose all prior milestone benefits from this thread and gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Two-Edged Gift [1–9, Saving Throws, Ability Checks, Attack Rolls]
entries: Your weapon attacks and spells deal half their normal damage until the end of your next turn. During this time, the first time a creature of your choice within 30 feet of you deals damage with a weapon or spell, that creature deals maximum damage.

entries.name: Greater Sacrifice
entries: When your Two-Edged Gift is triggered, you can instead choose deal no damage with weapons and spells until the end of your next turn. If you do so, the next weapon or spell attack the chosen creature makes before the end of its next turn is automatically a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, or it can receive the benefit of one of the previous milestone's Greater Sacrifice. Once you use your Greater Sacrifice, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Explorer
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Celebrity Explorer
entries: You receive a 30% discount on lodging, supplies, and food from innkeepers, merchants, and proprietors, and it's common for them to offer you things for free.

entries.name: Explorer's Aptitude
entries: Your travels instill you with new knowledge. You gain proficiency in your choice of one of the following skills: {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill History|XPHB}, or {@skill Perception|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Explorer
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Traversal Expert
entries: You have a knack for finding easy paths through the environment. You may use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to move your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. During this movement, you ignore {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks to climb, jump, or swim. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Scout's Awareness
entries: You have a preternatural sense that allows you to avoid dangers in your surroundings. For 1 hour, you and each ally within 30 feet who can see you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to resist the effects of nonmagical traps and hazards. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Explorer
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Ennobled
entries: A monarch has recognized your achievements as an Explorer in their or other territories by granting you a noble title, which comes with a moderately sized estate. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks with anyone who would be impressed or intimidated by your title. You also can avoid punishment for minor infractions, though if you abuse this, your title might be revoked.

entries.name: Wayfarer's Steps
entries: You can never become lost by nonmagical means and can always retrace your steps. Additionally, as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action and command up to 4 willing creatures who can hear you to use their {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to immediately take a {@action Dash|XPHB} action. Neither you nor your allies trigger {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} while moving in this way. Once you use this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Explorer
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Far Traveler
entries: While traveling, you and your companions may travel at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Fast Pace} without any penalties. You always find good campsites and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 rolls} related to camping or foraging in the wilderness. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Animal Handling|XPHB} checks to calm wild animals.

entries.name: One With the Land
entries: You may study the land from a good vantage point (such as a high position or advantageous overlook) for 1 minute and ask a question concerning the natural world or locations within 5 miles. This functions like the {@spell Commune with Nature|XPHB} spell. Once you use this, you must wait 24 hours before using it again.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Fatebound
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain your choice of one the following benefits.

entries.name: Dream Gift
entries: A god, Norn, or other powerful being has given you a gift in a dream. When you awoke, you had a {@filter Common magic item|items|rarity=common} of the GM's choice that may aid you.

entries.name: Fate's Blessing
entries: Once per day, while you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to get {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on a saving throw.

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Fatebound
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Strength of Wyrd
entries: While you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, once per turn you may add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to a damage roll. You may use this damage bonus a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Enduring Wyrd
entries: When you take damage, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. You cannot use this again until you complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Fatebound
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Doom Delayed
entries: When you would be killed, you may instead declare yourself as {@variantrule Stable|XPHB} with 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Knight of Fate
entries: You have become a legend in a territory, and the monarch there has knighted you, granting you holdings that will revert back to the monarchy upon your death. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma-based checks with the people of this land and are frequently showered with minor gifts and favors there.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Fatebound
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Last Act of Fate
entries: At a moment you have predetermined to be the time when you are to die, when you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or killed outright, you may (no action required) instead set your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to 1. You lose any detrimental conditions, and any harmful effects on you are ended immediately. Until the end of your next turn, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls and ability checks, you have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all damage and conditions (and other effects at the GM's discretion), and you add your character level to all damage rolls.
At the end of your next turn, you die and can never be restored to life.

entries.name: Glorious End
entries: If you achieve your destiny in a way that earns you a seat in Valhalla (or some other appropriate afterlife), the allies who witness your death have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|d20 rolls} for 24 hours as they are inspired by your heroism.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Herald
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Storyteller's Knack
entries: You learn three languages of your choice.

entries.name: Performer's Reward
entries: If you have at least 3 days of downtime between adventures, you can earn GP equal to 10 times your character level by performing your stories in taverns, on the street, or for powerful patrons. Additional downtime events don't increase this reward.

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Herald
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Enthralling Speaker
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance|XPHB} skill. If you are already proficient, you instead gain {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB}. Additionally, while performing before an audience, you can cast either {@spell Charm Person|XPHB} or {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} as part of your performance without requiring somatic or material components. Use Charisma as your spellcasting ability score. After casting one of these spells using this, you can't use the again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Herald
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Persuasive Words
entries: If you make a Charisma check to change a creature's attitude or convince them of your cause, you may treat a roll of 9 or lower on the {@dice d20} as a 10. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Herald
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Heroic Saga
entries: Your tales grow so powerful that they can briefly tamper with luck. After you spend at least 10 minutes telling an inspiring story or legend, choose either one creature who can hear you, or up to three creatures. You can't select yourself as a target. Once you use this, you can't use it again until for 7 days.
Depending on the number of targets, creatures can receive one of the following.

entries.name: Luck Boon (Three Targets)
entries: Once before the next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, a target can expend their boon to gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on a saving throw, attack roll, or ability check.

entries.name: Wyrd Boon (One Target)
entries: Once before their next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, if the target does not succeed on a saving throw or attack roll, they can choose to succeed instead. An attack roll succeeding in this way results in the minimum needed to succeed (not a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}, for example).

entries.name: Song of Matrimony
entries: A member of the royal family in a particular land has fallen in love with you and your performances, and the feeling is mutual. You are engaged to marry into the royal family.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Legend Hunter
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Predator's Mark
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks made to track creatures, and on a failed check it only takes you half the time to reacquire the tracks (5 minutes in a confined area, or half an hour outdoors).

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Legend Hunter
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Unclouded Sight
entries: Your honed senses let you ignore obscurement caused by weather, such as rain, snow, or fog. This includes magical clouds and weather effects, such as {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} and {@spell Sleet Storm|XPHB}, but not {@spell Darkness|XPHB}.

entries.name: Reliable Senses
entries: After failing an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}), Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}), or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check, you can reroll the check and take the higher result. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Legend Hunter
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Finish the Fight
entries: When you cause a creature to become {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, your next attack that hits it becomes a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB}. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Legend Hunter
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Legend Breaker
entries: When you hit a creature that has Legendary Resistance or Legendary Actions, you can choose to forgo dealing damage to force that creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength or Wisdom modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failed save, the target becomes unable use its Legendary Resistance or its Legendary Actions. The target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: The Ultimate Favor
entries: You performed a service for a powerful healer, who was caught in an animal trap set by another hunter. In return, they have offered to cast a single spell of healing of 6th to 9th level on you or a creature of your choice, at a time of your choosing, even if this puts them at great risk. This should be a spell that heals, regenerates, resurrects, or that removes conditions or curses.

optionalfeature.name: Least Milestone: Sworn Huskarl
entries: When you achieve the first milestone of this thread, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Jarl's Authority
entries: The authority granted you by your loyal service can sway the opinions of others. Before rolling an {@skill Intimidation|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} check to influence someone who knows and respects (or fears) your ruler, you can choose to treat the d20 roll as if you'd rolled a natural 15. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Lesser Milestone: Sworn Huskarl
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain your choice of one of the following benefits.

entries.name: Extreme Loyalty
entries: Your dedication to your ruler protects you from the control of others. If you end your turn with the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition, you may choose to take Psychic damage equal to your character level, then end that condition. Once you use this, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Jarl's Gift
entries: To help you carry out their will, your ruler gives you your choice of one of the following {@filter Uncommon magic items|items|rarity=uncommon} (or another you and your GM agree upon): {@item Bracers of Archery|XDMG}, {@item Defender Honey|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@item Sentinel Shield|XDMG}, {@item +1 Wand of the War Mage|XDMG}, or {@item +1 Weapon|XDMG}.

optionalfeature.name: Greater Milestone: Sworn Huskarl
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Undying Loyalty
entries: The strength of your oath steels you when the tides of battle turn against you. When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you can use this to instead set your {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to be equal to your character level. This doesn't help you against an effect that would kill you instantly without dealing damage. Once you use this, you can't use it again for 7 days.

optionalfeature.name: Superior Milestone: Sworn Huskarl
entries: When you achieve this level of milestone, you gain the following benefit.

entries.name: Grand Reward
entries: The completion of this milestone earns you a powerful reward. Work with your GM to determine an appropriate {@filter Very Rare magic item|items|rarity=very rare}, such as one of the following: {@item +3 Weapon|XDMG}, {@item Dancing Sword|XDMG}, {@item Oathbow|XDMG}, {@item Staff of Thunder and Lightning|XDMG}, or {@item Horn of the Hrimthursar|NorthlandsWorldbook}.
