entries: You touch another willing creature and bind your fates together until the spell ends. For the duration, if the target is within 60 feet of you and makes an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, you may use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to allow the target to reroll and use the new result. The target can do the same to you. Each time you do this, your, and only your {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB} maximum is reduced by {@dice 1d4}, and the same is true of the target. If this reduces your {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB} maximum to 0, you die. This reduction is removed when the spell ends.

spell.name: Bragi's Theatrical Fall

time.condition: which you take when an attack would reduce you to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but not kill you outright

entries: With a gasp and loud proclamation, you seem to fall dead to the ground. Instead of being reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, you are reduced to a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. At the same time, you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition, and an illusion of your dead body appears, lying in the space where your body would have fallen.

If a creature takes the {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine your illusory body, the creature can determine it is an illusion with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC. If a creature discerns the illusion for what it is, the illusion becomes faint to the creature.

The {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition ends if you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, use the {@action Magic|XPHB} action to cast a spell that lets a creature regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or use any action to cause harm to a creature.

spell.name: Branch and Root of Yggdrasil

components.m: branch, leaf, or bark from a World Tree

entries: All trees are intrinsically linked to Yggdrasil. When you cast this spell and touch a tree, you and up to eight willing creatures in contact with that tree are transported to a random location on Yggdrasil. If you are touching a World Tree found on the mortal plane (such as those found in the Northlands) when you cast the spell, you can specify a target destination on Yggdrasil in general terms, and you appear in or near that destination, as determined by the GM.

Using this magic requires a sacrifice from the caster. After casting this spell, your {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB} maximum is reduced by an amount equal to a roll of one of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice} until you complete a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

spell.name: Call to Action

time.condition: which you take in response to another creature's turn starting

entries: The creature starting its turn may immediately use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to take the {@action Dash|XPHB}, {@action Disengage|XPHB}, {@action Dodge|XPHB}, or {@action Help|XPHB} action.

spell.name: Claws of the Bear
entries: You imbue yourself with the claws of a bear. You transform your arms into a pair of muscular, furred paws and make a melee spell attack against a target. On a hit, the target takes Slashing damage equal to {@damage 3d10} plus your spellcasting ability modifier and, if the target is no more than one size category larger than you, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. For the duration of the spell, you can make attacks with the claws.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a 5th- or 6th-level spell slot, the damage increases to {@damage 4d10}. When you cast it using a 7th- or 8th-level spell slot, the damage increases to {@damage 5d10}. When you cast it using a spell slot of 9th level, the damage increases to {@damage 6d8}.

spell.name: Coldheart
entries: You cause a supernatural chill to fall upon one Beast or Humanoid that you can see within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it receives 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

At the end of its next turn, the target must make another Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the creature receives 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level. Then the spell ends. {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} applied by this spell is not removed by the end of the spell.

spell.name: Compel Avarice
entries: This spell twists the target creature's perceptions, inflaming its greed. You choose an object you can see when you cast this spell. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to try to take that item for itself for the duration of the spell. It will try to steal the item if possible, and if it is unable to, it will fight the item's current holder. If the target is able to claim the object, it will flee from all other creatures to jealously guard it until the spell ends. Creatures that have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition automatically succeed on their saving throws against this spell.

spell.name: Disrupt the Wyrd

time.condition: which you take in response to a saving throw being rolled by a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself

entries: The creature rerolls the saving throw, either adding your spellcasting modifier to or subtracting it from the new roll. It must use the new result.

spell.name: Drummer's Cadence
entries: For the duration, you radiate an aura in a 60-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Whenever an allied ship in this area moves by oar, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 ft. The vessel must be sufficiently crewed for this spell to have any effect.

spell.name: Earthsail

components.m: a handful of mud and a handful of sea water

entries: You touch a sailing vessel with a crew of up to 10 throughout the spell's casting, imbuing it with the ability to treat earth as though it were sea. For the duration, the vessel treats soil, mud, and packed dirt as though it were water, pushing through it and leaving a rippling wake of re-solidified terrain. Snow, ice, plants (including trees), and small stones are temporarily swept aside in the ship's wake, but boulders and mountains must be sailed around.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell with a 7th-level spell slot, it can affect a vessel with a crew of up to 30, and it lasts for 24 hours. If you cast this spell with a 9th-level spell slot, it can affect a vessel with a crew of any size, and it lasts for 1 week.

spell.name: Encase in Ice
entries: A crashing wave of water fills a 20-foot square on ground that you can see within range. The water instantly freezes in place. Each creature in the area makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature's legs are trapped in the ice, and the creature has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the spell ends. A creature with the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition can use an action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC, ending the condition on itself on a success. Another creature can take the {@action Help|XPHB} action to attempt to free the trapped creature, making the same check.

Creatures that were not in the spell's area when you cast it treat the area as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. If a creature that is not {@condition Restrained|XPHB} by the ice enters the area or ends its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell with a 3rd-level spell slot, the ice entraps the target's arms as well as its legs. The target cannot take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action or cast spells with somatic components until the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition ends.

If you cast this spell using a 5th-level spell slot, the ice completely entombs creatures in the area when you cast the spell. Creatures that fail their initial save are {@condition Restrained|XPHB} and have {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} for the spell's duration. An affected creature can make a Strength save at the end of each of its turns to break out, but whether it succeeds or fails, it takes {@damage 2d6} Cold damage as its flesh, which was stuck to the ice, tears.

spell.name: Ensnared Threads
entries: {@deity The Norns|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} allow you to briefly force a connection between the threads of your fate and those of another creature. A creature you can see within range must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, you form a connection between yourself and the target.

Once per turn, until the spell ends, the first attack that hits you hits the target creature instead, if it can be targeted by the attack. If that creature cannot be the target of the attack, the attack hits you normally.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell with an 8th- or 9th- level spell slot, all attacks that hit you instead hit the target. Any of the attacks the creature cannot be the target of still hit you normally.

spell.name: Extinguish
entries: You extinguish all magical and nonmagical flames of your choice in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} originating from you. Creatures made partially or completely of fire take {@damage 1d12} Force damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot above 1st that you use to cast this spell, the cube increases by 10 feet and affected creatures take an additional {@dice 1d12} Force damage.

spell.name: Eyes of the Raven
entries: You call upon the power of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s all-knowing ravens, Huginn and Muninn. While the spell lasts, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence checks and Intelligence saves.
As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can gain {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet. This lasts until the start of your next turn. Then the spell ends.

spell.name: Fenris's Howl
entries: You channel the piercing, death-dirge howl of the {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} wolf at a point that you can see within range and gain strength from others' fear. Creatures that you choose within 60 feet of that point that can hear you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition (with you as the source) for the duration of the spell. While at least one creature affected by the spell remains {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is doubled, and you deal an extra {@damage 3d6} Necrotic damage to a {@condition Frightened|XPHB} enemy with each of your attacks.

spell.name: Fiery Siege
entries: You touch a siege weapon, imbuing it with pyroclastic power. For the duration, the siege weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d10} Fire damage when it hits. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can touch a different siege engine, transferring the effect to it.

spell.name: Fire Rune
entries: You touch a melee weapon and place a magical effect into it, creating a visible rune etched into the weapon. Attacks made by the invoked weapon deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Fire damage on a hit.

spell.name: Fist of the Frost Jarl

components.m: a drop of water melted from an icicle

entries: A fist of solid ice filling a 5-foot {@variantrule Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube} hurtles from you in a direction you choose in a 120-foot {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. Each creature in the {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d8} Cold damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage.

You may choose for one creature of Huge size or smaller that fails its save to have the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, which has an escape DC equal to your spell save DC. A creature that ends its turn {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by the fist takes {@damage 2d8} Cold damage. When a creature escapes the grapple, the fist shatters.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 4th. If cast using a spell slot of 7th level or higher, the spell ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistance} to Cold damage.

spell.name: Freezing Fog
entries: You create a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of bone-chilling fog centered on a point within range. The {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} and considered {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. The fog lingers in the air for the duration or until a strong wind (such as one created by {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB}) disperses it.

Each creature that starts its turn in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}, or moves into its area, must succeed on a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved until the end of its next turn.
When a creature moves into or within the area, it takes {@damage 2d4} Cold damage for every 5 feet it travels.
You have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to all of the effects of this spell.

spell.name: Freyja's Allure
entries: One creature of your choice that you can see within range makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and can't willingly move farther away from you for the duration.

At the end of each of its turns, the creature can make another Charisma saving throw. The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the save if it can see you and you are within 30 feet of it. On a successful save, the spell ends on it.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Freyja's Grace

time.condition: which you take after failing a saving throw.

entries: Reroll the saving throw as a Charisma save, regardless of the original save type.

spell.name: Ghostly Crew
entries: You summon intangible spirits to crew a touched vessel. For the duration of the spell, as long as you are within 30 feet of the vessel, it is considered to have a sufficient number of sailors to take a full complement of normal ship actions (including movement and using siege weapons). The spirits can't take other actions or engage in any other activities, such as fighting independently or repairing the vessel.

spell.name: Giantbane
entries: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against Large or larger creatures, and your attacks deal an extra {@damage 2d6} Force damage against such creatures.

spell.name: Giantdodge
entries: Increase your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by 20 feet. You gain a +2 Bonus to your AC against attacks made by Large or larger creatures, and you do not provoke {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} from them.

spell.name: Giant's Teeth
entries: Two half-circles of enormous teeth erupt from the ground and slam together to crush a creature of your choice within 90 feet.

The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition. The escape DC is equal to your spell save DC. At the beginning of each of its turns while it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition, the creature takes {@damage 2d10} Bludgeoning damage. If the target escapes, the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a 5th-level spell slot, the damage increases to {@damage 3d10}. When you cast it using a 7th-level spell slot, the damage increases to {@damage 5d8}. When you cast it using a spell slot of 9th level, the damage increases to {@damage 6d8}.

spell.name: Glimpse the Wyrd

time.condition: which you take when a creature succeeds or fails on a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}

entries: You add or subtract {@dice 1d6} from the {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}.

spell.name: Hearthfire
entries: You touch one Large or smaller object that isn't being worn or carried by someone else. Until the spell ends, the object sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet. Within the spell's area of {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}, you and each creature you choose have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the harmful effects of {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG}.

spell.name: Hungry Jaws of Fenris
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you channel the power of {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the Great Wolf, transforming your mouth into a gaping maw. This doesn't impede your movement or actions, but you can't speak or cast spells with verbal components for the duration.

While the spell is active, you can use your jaws to make a bite attack. On a hit, the target takes Piercing damage equal to {@damage 4d10} plus your spellcasting ability modifier, and it has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition (escape DC equals your spell save DC).

If you bite a target already {@condition Grappled|XPHB} by you, you can choose to swallow it, and the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} condition ends. A swallowed creature is shunted into a pocket dimension. While there, it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions, has {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover} against attacks and other effects outside the dimension, and takes {@damage 3d12} Force damage at the start of each of your turns. You can't swallow a creature if you have already swallowed a creature using this spell.

A swallowed creature can make a save at the end of each of its turns. On a success, you vomit the creature to the nearest unoccupied space of your choice. The same thing occurs if the spell's duration elapses.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage dealt by the bite attack increases by {@dice 1d12} for each spell slot level above 6th.

spell.name: Ice Shape
entries: You touch a section of ice no more than 5 feet in any dimension and form it into any shape you like. For example, you could shape the ice into a weapon, statue, or coffer, or you could make a small passage through the ice that is 5 feet thick. You could also shape ice to seal a narrow cavern opening shut. Any object you create is crude but functional, but finer mechanical detail isn't possible.

spell.name: Icewalker
entries: For the duration, you radiate an aura in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. While in the aura, you and creatures of your choice gain the following benefits:

items: Treat slippery ice as normal terrain
Treat your weight as one-tenth normal for the purpose of breaking through thin ice

spell.name: Inbar's Giant-Friend

time.condition: which you take when a Giant sees you

components.m: a hair or nail clipping from a goblinoid

entries: Your eyes flash with golden light. The Giant must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, its attitude toward you improves 1 step, such as from {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} to {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} or {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} to {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly}. A creature's attitude is dynamic, so how you behave toward the giant from this point on can further affect its attitude. A Giant with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to this spell. Once you have cast this spell on any given Giant, you cannot cast it again on that Giant.

spell.name: Infectious Skal
entries: You sing a boisterous drinking song that compels others to stop what they are doing and sing along. A creature that can hear you within the spell's range must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} condition until the spell ends. While the creature is {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, it is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} toward you, and it takes no actions other than to sing along with the song. For the duration of the song, you may use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to target a new creature that is within 30 feet of you or of another creature singing the song. You can affect a total number of creatures equal to your Spellcasting ability modifier at any one time, adding them progressively. A targeted creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition Charmed|XPHB} by you and begin singing along. If any of the singers other than you is attacked during the song, the song stops with a loud discordant note, and the spell ends for everyone affected.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell with a 3rd or higher-level spell slot, you can affect 2 creatures each time you take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to spread the song.

spell.name: Jotun Form

components.m: a shard of a giant animal's bone

entries: You shape-shift into a {@filter Giant|bestiary|type=giant|miscellaneous=} for the duration or until you take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to shape-shift into a different eligible form. The new form must be of a creature of the {@filter Giant|bestiary|type=giant|miscellaneous=} type that has a {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB} no higher than your level or {@variantrule Challenge Rating|XPHB}. You must have seen that sort of creature before.

When you cast the spell, you gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} of the first form into which you shape-shift. These {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} vanish if any remain when the spell ends.

Your game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the chosen form, but you retain your creature type; alignment; personality; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}; {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Dice}; proficiencies; and ability to communicate. If you have the Spellcasting feature, you retain it too.
Upon shapeshifting, you determine whether your equipment drops to the ground or changes in size and shape to fit the new form while you're in it.

spell.name: Loki's Escape

time.condition: which you take after taking damage

entries: You have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn. While the spell lasts, you may use your {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to move your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} without provoking {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}. The spell ends early immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell.

spell.name: Luckfingers
entries: You touch one Medium or smaller creature, suffusing it with confidence and skill. Until the spell ends, the creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all ability checks. If such a check results in failure, the creature can choose to end the spell and automatically succeed on the ability check.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 3rd. If a creature chooses to end the spell to automatically succeed on an ability check, the spell ends only for them.

spell.name: Melody of Sheltered Rest
entries: You sing or hum an upbeat melody. For the duration, an aura radiates from you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. A creature within the aura (including you) can extend the duration for another 2 hours, as long as it continues singing. This can repeat for as long as a creature within the aura continues singing. While in the aura, creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks and cannot be {@condition Surprised|XPHB}.

spell.name: Murmurs of Doom
entries: You begin a whispered dirge that is magically accompanied by the howling of spirits and other grim portents. For the duration, an aura radiates from you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. When you create the aura and at the start of each of your turns while it persists, you can choose one creature in it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes {@damage 3d8} Necrotic damage.

spell.name: Noble Sacrifice

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or fails its third {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}

entries: The creature is restored to 1 {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB}, and you lose half of your current {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

spell.name: Ode to Wrath
entries: You begin a poetic chant that is magically accompanied by a trio of pounding drums beating an angry rhythm. For the duration, an aura radiates from you in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. While in the aura, you and your allies each add your spellcasting ability modifier to damage rolls made with melee weapons.

spell.name: Pawn of the Wyrd

time.condition: which you take when another creature takes a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}

entries: You cast your fate to the winds and accept the guidance of {@deity The Norns|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook|the Norns}. The creature does not take that {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and cannot take a different {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. If the {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} would have expended a spell slot or other ability, nothing is expended. You lose your next {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

spell.name: Protection Rune
entries: You touch a creature, creating a visible rune etched into its skin. The creature has {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to a damage type of your choice.

spell.name: Reaver's Rune
entries: You touch a melee weapon and place a magical effect into it, creating a visible rune etched into the weapon. No more than once per turn, a creature wielding the weapon can make an attack roll with the weapon with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} when it would not otherwise have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. If the weapon leaves the creature's possession, the spell ends.

spell.name: Regenerative Hull
entries: You touch a vehicle. At the start of each of your turns, the vehicle regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your spellcasting modifier. A vehicle must have 1 HP or more to be affected.

spell.name: Reinforce Hull
entries: A vehicle you touch has its damage threshold increased by your spellcasting ability modifier for the duration. A vehicle with no damage threshold can't be targeted by this spell.

spell.name: Repair Hull
entries: A vehicle you touch regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to {@dice 4d12} plus your spellcasting ability modifier. The target vehicle must have 1 HP or more to be affected.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d12} for each spell level above 3rd.

spell.name: Sailor's Shanty
entries: You touch a vehicle. The crew of the vehicle has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|d20 Tests} to control or operate the vehicle.

spell.name: Shared Expertise
entries: For the duration, you radiate an aura in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}. Choose up to 2 skills that you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in. If you have no {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in a skill, this spell has no effect.

While in the area, allied creatures are treated as having {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} in the chosen skills. If an ally already has {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB} or {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in the skill, they gain no benefit.

spell.name: Shield-Maiden's Favor

time.condition: which you take when you or an ally takes damage

entries: A spiritual echo of a Valhallan shield-maiden appears and interposes herself between the triggering attack and its target, then the shieldmaiden vanishes. The triggering attack's damage is reduced by {@dice 1d10} plus your spellcasting modifier.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage reduction increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell level above 1st.

spell.name: Sif's Grace

components.m: two silver beads of equal weight

entries: You grant a measure of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s speed and sure-footedness to a creature within reach. Until the spell ends, the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} doubles, and creatures that make {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks} against the target have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their attack rolls. If the target moves on its turn, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) checks.
If the target is subject to an effect that requires it to make a Dexterity save, it can choose to automatically succeed. That ends this spell for it.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Skaldic Scolding

time.condition: which you take in response to taking damage from a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself

entries: The creature that damaged you is bombarded with a barrage of scathing insults and must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature takes {@damage 4d10} Psychic damage and has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn. If the creature fails the save by 5 or more, it has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition instead. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell level above 4th.

spell.name: Song of the Shield Wall
entries: You begin a chant that is magically accompanied by the clanging sound of hammers against iron. Glowing, spectral, circular shields appear before a number of creatures equal to your spellcasting ability modifier who are within 30 feet of you. Each creature gains a +2 bonus to their AC.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: If you cast this spell with a 6th level spell slot, the bonus to AC increased to +3, and if you use an 8th level spell slot, it increases to +4.

spell.name: Speechmaster's Rune
entries: You place a magical effect into the stone used as the spell's material component, creating a visible rune etched into the stone. Any creature holding the stone has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks.

spell.name: Storm Maiden's Edge
entries: You touch a weapon and imbue it with the power of the storm. Until the spell ends, the chosen weapon deals an extra {@damage 2d8} Lightning damage on a hit.

A creature hit by the weapon must make a Strength saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the target is pushed back 10 feet. If the target fails the Strength save by 5 or more, it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The amount of extra Lightning damage dealt by the weapon increases by {@dice 1d8} for every two spell slot levels above 3rd.

spell.name: Summon Leviathan Avatar
entries: You call forth the spirit of the mythical leviathan. It manifests in an unoccupied space that you can see within range and uses the {@creature Leviathan Avatar|NorthlandsWorldbook|Leviathan Spirit} stat block. The space you choose must be filled with enough water to contain the size of the leviathan, otherwise the spell ends immediately. The creature disappears when it drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or when the spell ends.

The leviathan is an ally to you and your allies. In combat, the creature shares your {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your verbal commands (no action required by you). If you don't issue any, it takes the {@action Dodge|XPHB} action and uses its movement to avoid danger.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: Use the spell slot's level for the spell's level in the stat block.

spell.name: Sun Rune
entries: You place a magical effect into the stone used as the spell's material component, creating a visible rune etched into the stone. You can only have one Sun Rune spell active at a time.

Once while the spell lasts, any creature holding the stone may use an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} to invoke the rune's power and throw it at a target up to 60 feet away. It stops early if it impacts against a solid surface. When the stone lands or impacts, the rune triggers.

When the rune triggers, the blazing heat of the sun flashes in a 30-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on the stone. Each creature in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} Fire damage and {@damage 4d6} Radiant damage, or half as much on a successful one.

Flammable objects in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} that aren't being worn or carried start burning. Ice or snow within the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} vaporizes into a fog that fills the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}, making it {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} for 1 minute or until a strong wind (such as one created by the {@spell Gust of Wind|XPHB} spell) disperses it.
After activating the rune's power, the creature cannot activate another Sun Rune again until after a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

spell.name: Talons of the Eagle
entries: You imbue yourself with the power of the eagle. While the spell lasts, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saves.

As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can briefly transform your hands into a set of talons, then move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make a melee talon attack. On a hit, the target takes Slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d8} plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for every two spell slot levels above 1st.

spell.name: Thought Rune
entries: You place a magical effect into the stone used as the spell's material component, creating a visible rune etched into the stone. A creature holding the stone has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Intelligence and Wisdom checks and on Intelligence and Wisdom saving throws.

spell.name: Trickster's Bluff

components.m: the petrified tongue of a serpent

entries: You are graced with a measure of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s silver tongue. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) checks. If you fail such a check, you can choose to deal {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage to the creature you failed to deceive, and that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the beginning of your next turn.

spell.name: Trollblood Infusion
entries: A creature you touch is magically infused with the regenerative properties of troll blood. For the duration of the spell, the target regains 5 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} at the start of each of its turns, if it has at least 1 {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB}, and automatically succeeds on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}. If the creature takes Acid or Fire damage, this effect does not function at the start of its next turn.

spell.name: Truth's Blade

components.m: A silver pin, which is not consumed

entries: You punish one who would speak falsely to you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. If it fails, for the duration, it takes {@damage 4d8} Psychic damage whenever it lies.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The amount of Psychic damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Valhalla's Cohort
entries: You conjure warrior spirits from Valhalla, the hall of the honored dead. The spirits appear as a Huge cohort of spectral, intangible warriors in an unoccupied space you can see within range. The spirits brandish spears, axes, and blades, striking at anyone nearby. The cohort lasts for the duration, and you choose the spirits' appearance (such as their species and any insignias worn).
You can also move the cohort 30 feet as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your subsequent turns.

If the cohort ends its move within 5 feet of a creature, or if a creature moves within 5 feet of the cohort, you can make a melee spell attack against that creature. On a hit, the target takes Force damage equal to {@damage 2d10} plus your spellcasting ability modifier. A creature can be attacked in this way only once per turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 4th.

spell.name: Valkyrie's Guidance
entries: You consult the Valkyries and ask them to guide your hand to glory in Valhalla. Choose a creature you can see. For the duration of the spell, you gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on melee attack rolls against that creature and Intelligence checks to recall lore about it. The spell ends immediately if you don't attack the creature on your turn.

spell.name: Valkyrie's Vision
entries: You see how near to death other creatures are. Until the spell ends, you know the current {@variantrule Hit Point|XPHB} total of each creature you can see within 30 feet of you, and you can see how many levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} it has.
As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on your turn, you can cause a creature within 30 feet of you that is dying to become {@variantrule Stable|XPHB}. Doing so ends the spell immediately.

spell.name: Wall of Snow
entries: You create a wall of packed snow on a solid surface within range. You can make the wall up to 50 feet long, 15 feet high and 1 foot thick. Or you can make a 10-foot-radius, hemispherical dome. You can shape the wall in any way you choose so long as it makes one continuous path along the ground. The wall lasts for the duration.
If the wall cuts through a creature's space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall (you choose which side).

The wall is an object that can be damaged and thus breached. It has AC 10 and 10 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} per 10-foot section, and it has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold, Poison, and Psychic damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Fire and Radiant damage. Reducing a 10-foot section of wall to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} destroys it.
Creatures within an undamaged dome have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the effects of {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG} while the spell lasts.

If you cast this spell in an area of snowy terrain, it blends seamlessly with the existing snow. If a creature takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the wall, the creature can differentiate the wall from the surrounding terrain with a successful Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC.

spell.name: Weave Detonation
entries: An invisible, soundless burst of fate erupts at a point you choose. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on that point makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests} for 1 minute.
A creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the spell on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot level above 3rd, you can exclude up to five creatures within the radius from the spell's effects.

spell.name: Whiteout
entries: You must be outdoors to cast this spell, and it ends early if you go indoors.

When you cast this spell, you create a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} of heavy fog and flurrying snow centered on you. The {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} is {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} and the terrain within it is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Any creature that begins its turn in the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} or enters the {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} on its turn must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or receive 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level. Creatures that have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage automatically succeed on this save.
When you cast the spell, you may designate a number of creatures equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. These creatures do not receive levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} from the spell.
When the spell ends, all snow created by it disappears instantly and the {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels end.

spell.name: Wotan's Retribution

time.condition: which you take when a creature scores a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} against you

entries: You teleport directly behind the creature that triggered this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and make a melee attack against it with a weapon you are wielding. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on your attack roll. On a hit, the creature takes the damage from your attack as well as an amount of damage equal to the damage it dealt to you when it triggered this {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

spell.name: Wyrd Sight
entries: You manipulate the threads of luck and fate to work in your favor. No more than once per turn, you can roll {@dice 1d12} and add or subtract it from a d20 roll made by a creature you can see.

action.name: All Stop
entries: The crew attempts a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check to strike the sails and drop the anchor, bringing the ship's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} to 0 feet after it completes its movement this round. If the check fails, the ship continues moving for another round before the anchor catches. This check can't be attempted in deep water.

action.name: Come About
entries: The crew attempts a severe change of direction with a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check. If successful, the ship turns 90° instead of the normal 45°. If the check fails, the ship doesn't turn at all. This check has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} if the ship is crossing against the direction of the wind unless the ship is being rowed.

action.name: Disable Station
entries: The crew fires to disable stations on the enemy vessel. This attack has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. If the attack hits, instead of dealing damage to the hull, one station is damaged according to the {@table Disable Station|NorthlandsWorldbook} table. Roll a {@dice 1d6} to determine how many crew members in that area are {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} and dying.

action.name: Escape a Grapple
entries: A member of the crew leads a number of crew members in cutting lines that tie their vessel to another. A successful {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check cuts the lines.

action.name: Evasive Maneuver
entries: The crew makes a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check contested by the enemy crew. On a success, attackers have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ranged attacks to hit the ship.

action.name: Force Position
entries: The crew makes a contested Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check opposed by the enemy crew to force the enemy into a disadvantageous position. On a success, the enemy ship has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check to determine {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} next round. On a failure, the enemy gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} to its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} check next round.

action.name: Full Speed Ahead
entries: The crew uses its action to adjust the sails and gain a burst of speed. The ship can {@action Dash} this turn. If the ship is powered by oars, it must succeed on a {@dc 12} Constitution save or the crew gains one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

action.name: Grapple
entries: A member of the crew leads a number of crew in throwing grappling hooks onto an enemy vessel within 5 feet and tying the ships together. While tied together, neither ship can move, and the crews can't use the {@action Come About|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@action Evasive Maneuver|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@action Force Position|NorthlandsWorldbook}, Full {@action Speed Ahead|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@action Hold Her Steady|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@action Ram|NorthlandsWorldbook}, or {@action Sheer|NorthlandsWorldbook} shipboard actions. This action requires a successful {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check.

action.name: Hold Her Steady
entries: The crew holds the ship steady, giving the crew members operating ship-mounted weapons {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} to hit one enemy ship. All enemy ships have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} to hit the ship holding steady.

action.name: Motivate
entries: {@b PCs Only.}

As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}, the PC shouts encouragement to the crew during a shipboard action. On a successful {@dc 13} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, all crew rolls related to the triggering Shipboard Action have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

action.name: Operate Ship Weapon
entries: As an action, the crew loads and aims a ship-mounted weapon. It still requires a separate action to fire the weapon.

action.name: Patch
entries: A member of the crew leads a damage repair team to put in a temporary patch on the hull or repair a damaged station. The crew has a +4 bonus to this check. This action can only be used once per hole or damaged station (see the {@table Disable Station|NorthlandsWorldbook} table). The DC to restore {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to the ships is 10 + 2 per hole the ship has suffered, and {@dc 15} to repair a station. A successful check restores {@dice 2d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} to the ship or restores a station to working order.

action.name: Ram
entries: If the ship is moving, the crew can attempt to ram another vessel within a number of feet equal to half the ship's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} by making a successful Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check against the other ship's AC and moving that number of feet. If successful, both ships take {@damage 2d10} damage for every size category of the ramming ship. If the ship is equipped with a ram, it takes only half damage. Both ships become hopelessly {@condition grappled|XPHB} and can't be separated without several minutes of work. If the attempt misses, the ships graze each other and both take one-quarter damage. You can't take the Ram shipboard action against the direction of the wind unless the ship is being rowed.

action.name: Sheer
entries: Only effective against ships with oars, the crew brings their vessel within 5 feet of the enemy vessel, sheering off all the oars on one side of the enemy vessel. This reduces its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} to 0 feet for 3 rounds until new oars can be deployed. To succeed, the crew member at the helm must make a successful Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check with a DC equal to the other ship's AC.

hazard.name: Extreme Cold
entries: When the temperature is 0 degrees Fahrenheit or lower, a creature exposed to the extreme cold must succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level and may suffer from {@hazard Hypothermia and Frostbite|NorthlandsWorldbook|Hypothermia}. Creatures that have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage automatically succeed on the save.

hazard.name: Foraging for Food
entries: In the summer/spring, creatures need to spend {@dice 1d4} hours and succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check to find food. The amount of food and water gained is a number of pounds equal to the creature's Wisdom modifier. In the fall/winter, the DC increases to 18 in most areas, and {@dc 20} in the mountains, tundra, and glaciers. These DCs are suggested averages to ease gameplay. Creatures in a cold environment use up more energy than normal and consume more food and water. As a general rule, creatures must consume twice as much as normal in winter months in the Northlands. If they venture into arctic conditions (such as high mountains or glaciers), they must consume three times as much.

hazard.name: Frigid Water
entries: A creature can be immersed in frigid water for a number of minutes equal to its Constitution score before suffering any ill effects. Each additional minute spent in frigid water requires the creature to succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level. Creatures with {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage automatically succeed on the save, as do creatures that are naturally adapted to living in ice-cold water.

hazard.name: Heavy Precipitation
entries: Everything within an area of heavy rain or heavy snowfall is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}, and creatures in the area have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks. Heavy rain also extinguishes open flames.

hazard.name: High Altitude (10,000 ft–25,000 ft)
entries: Traveling at altitudes of 10,000 feet to 25,000 feet above sea level is taxing for most creatures because of the reduced amount of oxygen in the air. Each hour such a creature spends traveling at high altitude counts as 2 hours for the purpose of determining how long that creature can travel. Creatures can acclimate to a high altitude by spending 30 days or more at this elevation. Creatures can't become acclimated to elevations above 20,000 feet unless they are native to such environments.

hazard.name: High Altitude (25,000 ft+)
entries: Many of Jotunheim's peaks reach so far into the sky that there's simply not enough air to sustain normal life. Northlanders call these places daudavangr, the "Death-Fields." Above 25,000 ft., any creature not naturally acclimated to the environment or that doesn't have {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage must succeed on a Constitution saving throw each hour ({@dc 15} +1 per previous check) or take {@damage 2d6} Cold damage and gain one level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

Creatures with levels of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} in a daudavangr suffer blinding headaches, disorientation, and confusion. They have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|d20 rolls} based on Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.

entries.name: Magic in the Death Fields
entries: Fire burns very poorly in a daudavangr. Spells and effects that deal Fire damage only deal half as much as normal.

hazard.name: Hypothermia and Frostbite
entries: Creatures that have a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} from the cold must make a Constitution saving throw (DC is 8 plus the level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}) every hour they are exposed to cold conditions. With each failed saving throw, the creature gains one of the following levels of hypothermia. Finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in a warm place removes one level of hypothermia. The conditions listed below are in addition to the normal {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} penalties.

items.name: Frostnip
items.entry: Skin aches; numb yellow and white patches form. {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength and Dexterity checks.

items.name: Shiverstruck
items.entry: Creature trembles uncontrollably. Spellcasters casting spells with verbal or somatic components must succeed on Constitution saving throws (DC 10 + the spell's level) to cast spells. On a failure, the spell isn't cast, and the slot and action are wasted. Tasks involving Strength and Dexterity take twice as long.

items.name: Frostbite
items.entry: Skin is numb and develops black blisters. Creatures take {@damage 1d10} Cold damage each hour they aren't in a warm location and must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity check to accomplish physical tasks, like drawing a weapon, loading a bow, retrieving items, picking locks, or disarming traps.

items.name: Ice-Addled
items.entry: Creatures are confused and their speech is slurred. Creatures take {@damage 2d10} Cold damage each hour they aren't in a warm location, they have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB|d20 rolls}, their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is halved, they can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}, and they can't cast spells.

items.name: Kissed by the Ice Maiden
items.entry: A creature with severe hypothermia believes it is overheating the moment it suffers this level of hypothermia. It must succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw or begin to remove its warm clothing. It refuses to wear warm clothing or enter warm locations.

hazard.name: Slippery Ice
entries: Slippery ice is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. A creature that moves onto slippery ice for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must succeed on a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

hazard.name: Snow Blindness
entries: Snow blindness is a burn on the cornea of the eye by light reflected off snow and ice. The condition typically occurs at high altitudes on white, reflective snow fields. After 1 hour of exposure to a bright, snowy area, a creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (DC is 8 + number of hours spent in the area). On a failure, the creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls and ability checks that rely on sight for 24 hours. If the save fails by 5 for more, the creature has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for the same duration instead. Creatures with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Cold damage or who are naturally adapted to arctic environments automatically succeed on the saving throw.

hazard.name: Strong Wind
entries: Strong wind imposes {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on ranged attack rolls with weapons. It also extinguishes open flames and disperses fog. A flying creature in a strong wind must land at the end of its turn or fall. A strong wind in a snowy area can create a localized snowstorm that imposes {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks.

hazard.name: Thin Ice
entries: Thin ice has a weight tolerance of {@dice 3d10 * 10|3d10 × 10} pounds per 10-foot-square area. Whenever the total weight on an area of thin ice exceeds its tolerance, the ice in that area breaks. All creatures on broken ice fall through. Below the ice might be frigid water (see {@hazard Frigid Water|NorthlandsWorldbook}).

hazard.name: Travel Pace in the North
entries: Travel in the Northlands is made more difficult by snow, ice, and mountainous terrain. While traveling in snow or arctic conditions, creatures can only maintain a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Fast Pace} if they have appropriate equipment (such as {@item Snowshoes|NorthlandsWorldbook} or {@item Skis|NorthlandsWorldbook}).

variantrule.name: Character Threads
entries: Normally, backgrounds reflect a character's training before they became adventurers and provide various bonuses, such as skills, proficiencies, and equipment. For many characters, a background remains an element of their past. It occasionally impacts a campaign, but it mostly serves an important function as roleplaying fodder and thematic color. For example, a character might sometimes use their nobility as an adventurer, but this background doesn't change or grow.
On the other hand, what if an element similar to a background could continue to develop and even change over the course of a character's adventuring career?

Character threads are positions, occupations, and situations a character might pursue while they continue to go on quests or battle foes. Though threads are similar to backgrounds, they are less about what your character did before becoming an adventurer and more about what your character does in the "background" while they are adventuring.

Perhaps the PC is appointed as an ambassador to a neighboring country or elevated to the position of minister in a royal court. Or perhaps a character with a noble background learns their family has been cheated out of their fortune and is now impoverished.

Threads are aspects added to characters at any time during their career that have a specific short or long-term goal. They reward characters with news and abilities as they advance along milestones toward that goal. Once that endpoint of a thread is achieved, new threads can be applied as they occur during the course of the campaign. You can add threads to your character by choosing one of the ones presented below, or you can use the options presented in this section to create your own tiered threads.

entries.name: Elements of a Character Thread
entries: All character threads establish a specific goal as well as thematic milestones that the character must reach in order to achieve that goal, and each new milestone unlocks a new benefit or. When the specific goal is ultimately accomplished, the character can change their thread to a new one {@b (see Adding or Abandoning New Threads)}. A character can have only one thread at a time.

The use of Threads in your campaign can lead to a balancing issue between characters taking on threads and those who do not. The easiest way to handle this is to just acknowledge that threads may make some characters slightly more powerful than others. GMs uncomfortable with this can also hand out some magic items or other rewards to non-thread using characters.

When adopting a thread, a certain amount of personalization is required to fit the milestones to the goal at hand and to the overall direction of the campaign. Players should work with their GMs to adjust the goal and milestones for their thread as described below.

entries.name: Goal
entries: All threads begin with a goal determined by the player. The goal helps to guide the creation of the thread's milestones and should thematically fit with the character and with the nature of the campaign.

More importantly, the goal should be a specific, achievable objective, something the character hopes to accomplish in the future. The more specific this goal, the better, for this will ease the creation of its milestones. For example, a character picking up the Bloodsworn thread might choose a goal of defeating the giants who destroyed their village.

entries.name: Milestones
entries: With the goal in hand, the milestones must be decided. These are events of personal achievement or significance. They act as obstacles or thresholds on the path to reaching the thread's goal. A thread isn't restricted in its number of milestones, but four is recommended. On achieving each milestone, a benefit is unlocked, depending on its ranking—least, lesser, greater, or superior (see {@b Milestone Benefits}).

While the goal or motivation of a thread is specific, milestones usually are not. This allows the GM some flexibility in applying them to individual campaigns. Each thread description includes a few example milestones, but there are no strict rules about what a milestone might be or when it can occur.

Milestones can even change as the path toward the character's goal shifts. The player and GM might even retroactively determine that an unexpected event counts as a milestone to that thread's goal. Ideally, the player should work this out with the GM, agreeing on applicable milestones and determining how (and when) they are achieved.

entries.name: Spacing Milestones
entries: When creating or adding a thread to a character, decide with the GM how long (in theory) it should take to reach the goal. This might depend on the scope or length of the campaign and on the nature of the thread. An Impoverished Noble thread, for example, might be quite short, ending when a certain wealth threshold is reached. Conversely, the Illegitimate Scion thread might only end when the character is adopted into a new family, an event which could take 20 levels.
Once the length of the thread is determined, add in the milestones, spacing them out evenly in terms of levels.

entries.name: Milestone Benefits
entries: The four ranks of milestones—least, lesser, greater, superior—have recommended level ranges that serve as guides for determining the types of benefits a character receives. These correspond to the level range the character is expected to be within when they reach that milestone. Threads can have multiple milestones of the same rank. Sample benefits are listed in the Milestone Recommended Levels table.
Characters should generally earn only one benefit for each milestone unlocked, but GMs can always choose to reward additional benefits.

entries.name: A Sample Thread Progression
entries: Halbera Gap-Tooth, a bearfolk Viking Fighter, begins her career with the Northlands Reaver background and the Bloodsworn thread. Halbera's player chooses "I must defeat the storm giant who slew my jarl" as a goal.

Working with the GM, the player determines that this thread should only go to 10th level, or thereabouts, because after that the campaign might shift away from the area where the storm giant operates. They create four milestones that can lead Halbera to that final confrontation with her foe, plus benefits for each of those milestones.

items: Uncover the identity of the storm giant. (Least: Cunning)
Learn the location of the storm giant's hidden lair. (Least: a seeking charm usable once per day.)
Defeat one of the storm giant's minions who has important information. (Lesser: Wrath.)
Defeat the storm giant. (Lesser: Gain the lair as a new base of operations.)

entries: This progression assumes a 10-level arc, but threads can be as long or as short as the GM wishes. Shorter-range goals merely require fewer milestones.

entries.name: Adding or Abandoning New Threads
entries: Threads give characters another way to show how they change and grow over the course of a campaign. When a thread is completed, or even abandoned, a character can adopt a new thread to reflect the altering events of the story. Having proven themselves to their estranged parent, for example, a character with the Illegitimate Scion thread now looks to rebuild the family fortune. The Illegitimate Scion thread might shift then to that of the Impoverished Noble thread. The player and GM should agree when circumstances are correct for a new thread, but the GM has the final say.

When adding new threads, the character retains all milestone benefits of previous threads. When abandoning a thread (that is, relinquishing it before achieving its stated goal), the character loses all of the thread's milestone benefits already gained. Thoses were temporary benefits that didn't become permanent because the character's focus changed, leaving the source of thoses unresolved.

entries.name: Thread Descriptions
entries: This section describes seven sample threads from which to choose. Though these threads presume a long arc of milestones, reaching from 1st level all the way to 20th level, they can be adjusted for shorter arcs by reducing the number of milestones or by reducing their spacing.
If a more personalized approach is preferred, simply use the structure of the provided threads as inspiration for creating new threads.

variantrule.name: Reputation
entries: An individual's reputation is of paramount importance to the people of the North. As canny {@deity Wotan|Norse|source} said, "Cattle die, kin die, even the self dies, but glory never dies for the one able to achieve it." To be a hero in the Northlands, and thus earn a place in the afterlife, is to perform deeds with an eye toward how they shape your reputation. Yet, renown isn't static—it ebbs and flows. A hero might gain great honor for killing a mighty dragon, but if they act dishonorably, their reputation will tarnish and rot away.

Reputation is an optional rule that tracks your character's prestige and provides a way to leverage that renown to perform cinematic and epic actions by temporarily assuming narrative control of the game.

entries.name: Character Reputation Score
entries: Your character's reputation is measured by a score much like an ability score modifier. A novice warrior might have +1 reputation, while the greatest champion of the realm might have +10 or higher. Unlike ability scores, this modifier begins at 0 and is not adjusted due to skills or characters levels. Reputation increases when you perform gain renown for deeds and noteworthy acts of daring, and it decreases if you are caught committing dishonorable acts. Multiple characters can gain reputation by performing the same deed together. The {@table Reputation Thresholds|NorthlandsWorldbook} table shows the levels and benefits of reputation.

Note, this system specifically governs what people know about you. If no one witnesses you committing a dishonorable act, your reputation in the mortal world won't suffer. Similarly, if you slay a great wyrm, but no one believes you, your reputation won't improve. Gods, {@deity Norns|Norse|source}, and other divine beings might be aware of what you did, and it might affect your chances of going to Valhalla, but unless other people witness or learn of what you did, your reputation modifier will not change.

entries.name: Deeds and Dishonorable Acts
entries: Deeds are acts of heroism accomplished by the PC or party, like saving a village from raiders, slaying a dragon, or finding a fabled lost treasure. Acts need not be victorious combat to count as deeds. A merchant who brings back a longship laden with goods can gain renown, as can an artist who creates a masterpiece. As your character accomplishes deeds, they gain more reputation, advancing through various thresholds or stages, but they can lose reputation by getting caught acting dishonorably. You should keep track of the number of deeds you have accomplished, as they determine your reputation threshold.

entries.name: Rule of Five
entries: If you accomplish five deeds, and others learn of them, you advance to the next threshold level.

It is important to note that a deed isn't every amazing thing an adventurer does. Deeds need to be notable, worthy of saga and song. As a general guideline, a deed is something a PC or party does that dramatically alters the storyline of the game. So fighting monsters is not necessarily a deed since almost everyone in the Northlands does that frequently, but driving away the legendary ice worm might be. If you accomplish the same deed twice, the second usually doesn't count as a deed. The GM and the player should decide together what accomplishments count as a deed.

entries.name: Dishonorable Acts
entries: The antithesis of deeds are dishonorable acts. Violence isn't necessarily dishonorable nor is killing. In the North, major dishonorable acts include murdering an innocent, breaking an oath, breaking the rules of hospitality, violating the peace of the althing, and cowardice in the face of danger. The GM should determine if your actions are dishonorable acts and if enough people have found out about them to damage your reputation.

entries.name: Rule of Three
entries: If you commit three dishonorable acts that others learn about, you lose all accumulated deeds and are reduced by one threshold level.

entries.name: Thresholds
entries: Thresholds are best described as "reputation levels" measuring your character's renown. Each stage has prerequisites based on character level and provides small regional bonuses.

At each stage, you must accomplish five deeds to advance to the next threshold, however, you can't move to the next threshold until you reach the character level minimum of that threshold. For example, a level 3 character with 5 deeds can't gain more reputation or move from the Obscure to the Known reputation threshold until they reach level 5. Each time you advance to a new threshold, your deeds counter resets to 0.

Your threshold level also determines what type of reputation challenge you can attempt and a few minor benefits. You must be in an area where your reputation is known (as determined by the GM) to benefit from the regional bonuses.

entries.name: Reputation Challenges
entries: Once per character level, you can leverage your fame and renown to attempt a Reputation Challenge. If you succeed, you take narrative control of the game for a limited time, essentially becoming the GM to resolve the dramatic moment. If you fail, you lose reputation as the word of your failure spreads. This places a tremendous amount of power in your hands, and as such, the GM can always step in if things get out of hand.

entries.name: Making a Challenge
entries: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} at any time, you can announce you are making a Reputation Challenge. With GM agreement, you can even do so if you have already used a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} this turn.

When you make a Reputation Challenge, you must explain to the GM what your PC plans to do. Be descriptive and dramatic as this moment should be a heroic! The GM might suggest alterations but generally should work with you to agree on what happens to your character, the other PCs, and the world of the game. This is called the "narrative."

items.name: Challenge Types
items.entry: As part of the narrative, you must also decide what challenge type you are attempting: Low, Medium, High, or Epic. You must meet the reputation threshold prerequisite to attempt any challenge. The GM might rule your proposed narrative sounds like a higher type than you qualify for, so you might have to scale things back.

items.name: Low Challenge ({@dc 10})
entries: This represents a heroic action or dramatic moment that influences the immediate situation or a small group of people. It might turn the tide of a small battle, impress a local lord, or rally a frightened village.

items.name: Medium Challenge ({@dc 12})
entries: This represents a major feat that affects an entire town, settlement, or faction's immediate course of action. It can reshape relationships, affect regional politics, or change the direction of a local conflict.

items.name: High Challenge ({@dc 14})
entries: This reshapes the destiny of an entire region, kingdom, or major power. It brings about permanent shifts in the world's politics, military balances, or magical forces.

items.name: Epic Challenge ({@dc 16})
entries: This represents mythic-level events that echo across nations, planes, and generations. These deeds are worthy of legend and saga and may change the course of the world.

entries.name: Challenge Roll
entries: After you and the GM agree on the narrative and challenge type, you must roll a {@dice d20} plus your reputation bonus to determine the outcome.

entries.name: Success
entries: If you succeed, your proposed narrative happens as you described it.

entries.name: Failure
entries: If you fail the challenge roll, you lose all of your accumulated deeds and are reduced by one reputation threshold.

entries.name: Challenge Guidelines
entries: Taking control of the game is intended to give you a narrative way for your characters to overcome obstacles and be the dynamic heroes you've imagined them to be. It is NOT a method to one-shot a bad guy or to suddenly gain personal wealth. While this feature gives you control of the narrative for a moment, don't forget that your character's story is also part of the world and part of the rest of the party's story. Be polite, be respectful, include others, and have fun!
Here are some general guidelines for your narratives:

items: Your narrative can happen during combat or outside it.

The amount of time your narrative takes is enough to complete the description of the challenge you discussed with the GM. As indeterminate as it sounds, the time of this can vary. Low challenges might only be a couple of rounds, while an Epic challenge might take an hour, a day, or even more.
What you describe should be within the bounds of logic, even if it's rather unlikely.
In general, you don't need to roll for narrative actions, though the GM may add new obstacles into your narrative that require a roll.
Your narrative takes the same amount of time as your normal turn, or longer if the GM allows.

Your narrative can include multiple actions, but unless the GM allows it, you can't cast more than one spell or make more than your normal number of attacks, unless you could otherwise cast more than one in a turn or make more than your normal number of attacks in a turn, such as through a Fighter's Action Surge feature.

If you attack a foe with weapons or spells, you can choose to roll normally, or with your GM's approval, you can automatically hit and kill a number of foes equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} if each creature's CR is equal to or less than half your character's level.
You can add or change elements of the world to fit your narrative, if the changes are logical and approved by the GM.
Don't interfere with other players' agency for their characters, and/or be sure to consult with other players if their characters have a role to play in your narrative.

variantrule.name: Holmganga (Dueling)
entries: Questioning someone's honor, accusing them of a crime or of cowardice, or falsely claiming credit for heroic deeds is asking for a fight. Sometimes it happens by accident—especially at drunken feasts—and Northlanders laugh off such offenses with a flyting contest or over rounds of mead once a sincere apology is given. But at other times, only bloodshed can heal wounded pride.

If the offender fails to publicly apologize for the offense within three days, a duel called a holmganga ("going to the island") results. Such duels typically occur on an island, at a crossroads, in a sacred glade, or on a cloth staked to the ground. Each warrior can take personal arms, armor, and three Holmganga shields to the dueling ground.

entries.name: Matching Equipment
entries: It is considered honorable to match your opponent in terms of arms and armor. So a PC with powerful magical gear facing a warrior with nonmagical equipment is expected to use similarly nonmagical arms and armor. This isn't a "rule" so much as expected custom, and it's possible those present are unaware one opponent has an unfair advantage. A combatant who doesn't do so might gain a dishonorable act (see Reputation above), as determined by the GM.

entries.name: Holmganga Shields
entries: The shields used for Holmganga are not the same as normal battle shields. They are thinner and break when their wielder is struck with an attack dealing 15 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or more. A critical hit always breaks a holmganga shield. Breaking a shield or throwing it down ends a "round" of fighting, allowing a brief respite (no more than a minute) to catch one's breath. The fight ends only when one combatant flees or cannot continue.

entries.name: The Duel
entries: It is traditional for a Holmganga duel to end when one opponent is knocked unconscious. In mechanical game terms, it means you reduce your foe to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} with a melee attack, but you choose to instead reduce them to 1 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point} and give them the Unconscious condition. However, deaths have been known to occur during duels over serious matters, such as deciding a jarldom or the ending of a long feud. Killing an opponent in the holmganga isn't dishonorable unless the reason for the duel is viewed as minor.

Honorable folk of all professions are expected to duel when necessary. If a duel is grossly mismatched, a champion can fight in one's place, or the defender can appeal to the local althing and petition to have the duel declared unfair. Failure to show up earns a reputation as a nithingr (coward) and outlaw for a year or two.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Victory at the Holmganga Simple upholds your side of the triggering argument or dispute. It can count as a deed, as determined by your GM.

variantrule.name: Flyting Rules
entries: Feasts in the Northlands tend to be rowdy affairs with much boasting, drinking, and carousing. At times, a jarl may wish to size up a visitor and test their cunning, or a quarrel may need to be defused before it becomes a duel or a murder that triggers a generational feud. This is where flyting comes in.

Flyting is a duel of insults where two participants take turns insulting one another, in more and more creative ways, until anger or embarrassment reduces one side to speechlessness. The contest can be used for entertainment, to resolve simple quarrels, or to defuse a situation. A flyting typically begins when one person challenges another publicly in a manner not egregious enough to trigger a duel—perhaps a verbal insult or a social misstep.

Facts aren't relevant in a flyting. The "truth" of the insults thrown around in a flyting is of lesser importance than the speaker's rhyming skill and humor. The winner of the contest is the one who best sways the audience with their creative insults.

entries.name: Rhythm and Rhyme
entries: The challenger gives an insult and the challenged replies with their own. Importantly, the answering insult needs to copy the rhythm of the challenger's insult, and the last word of both insults must rhyme. For example, if {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} is taunted with "Foul deceiver, you are a snake with an uncouth manner!" He might reply with "Pale braggart, you wield your wit like a drooping hammer."

entries.name: How Many Rounds?
entries: This depends on the participants, but often it is 3-5 exchanges total. The GM should determine how many rounds the contest is to last before it begins.

entries.name: Flyting Steps
entries: When a flyting is called, use the following steps.

items.name: Appoint a Judge
entries: The two participants agree on a judge chosen from among the people in attendance. This individual is usually not personally connected to either participant or at least is someone who can remain neutral. The judge gauges the reaction of the audience to determine which participant has swayed the greater number of attendees. At the game table, the judge is usually the other players and the GM.

items.name: Participants Face Off
entries: They usually stand atop a long table in the longhouse or some area where they can be seen and heard by the audience.

items.name: Challenger Goes First
entries: This is typical, but if not, the two participants can roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} to see who begins.

items.name: Round 1: Opening Insults
entries: Often the first round of insults is part boast, part stating the grievance against the opponent, and part insult.

items.name: Rounds Continue
entries: The rounds continue until the predetermined number is reached, one of the participants stumbles (can't respond cleverly, repeats themselves, or fails to rhyme), or when the audience declares a winner as determined by the judge.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: Often the honor of the participants is at stake or the resolution of some squabble. It is considered very dishonorable to dispute the result of a flyting or to seek revenge because of one. At a feast, rewards of mead is common. Victory at flyting can count as a deed, as determined by your GM.

entries.name: Easing Flyting Gameplay
