items.entry: Fish, honey, timber, ale, mead, venison, berries, cider

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Bjornrike know the following information:

items: The Kingdom of the Bear sits at the edge of known lands. Stout walls surround the scattered communities, and travelers set close guard against the coming night. Dark beasts and fell dangers lurk just beyond the firelight. It is not uncommon for the unwary to be taken by trolls, fey, or more mysterious beings.

The inhabitants of Bjornrike work hard and spend their leisure time hunting, drinking, and brawling. Most communities consist of a dozen immediate familial units, and the intermingling of families creates deep relationships often lasting generations. While not overly welcoming, bearfolk tolerate newcomers and show them respect and courtesy until the moment they no longer deserve either.

Hives of ferocious bees guard the kingdom, and each settlement of Bjornrike is likely to have at least one hive. These unique defenders swarm out to attack anyone who threatens during the day. Bjornrike citizens are largely immune to their stinging rampages, since they eat so much local honey that they smell of it and are accepted by the hives.

The land is rich in timber, its rivers thick with steelbelly trout and spined pike and its fields in summer buzz with the drone of grand honeybees. Bearfolk breeders train fine horses, and orchards of cherry trees produce sweet fruit, most of which is turned into Bjeornheim's famous sweet cherry wine and cherry liqueur. Trade in these bountiful natural resources forms the base of the kingdom's exports.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Most of Bjornrike's population is concentrated in the capital, Gloaming Crag, and the trading port of Bjeornheim, but there are also scattered smaller settlements and communities beyond the major cities.

items.name: Alfrgan Gap
entries: This secluded, circular valley lies near the eastern border of Bjornrike, at the foothills of the Hrygangur Peaks. Covered with a dense forest of oak and brambles, the gap hides ancient ruins left when the elven courts withdrew from the world. Brave, or perhaps foolish, treasure hunters occasionally delve into the Gap searching for riches, but few return. Those who do speak of attacks from the flora and fauna of the regions, all acting at the behest of spectral elven knights, who continue to guard secrets.

items.name: Bjeornheim
entries: The second largest city, and easily the most cosmopolitan portion of the realm, Bjeornheim has a well-earned a reputation as a safe and profitable trading destination. The high walls of the city offer protection from the dangers of the North, and the guardian bees that protect all of the country began here. The hives of Bjeornheim remain the largest in Bjornrike. Traders from across the North, the lands to the south, and even the far east regularly make port here to barter for rich honey, fish, and lumber, or to worship in the golden-hued Temple of Hive and Flower, dedicated to {@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. The brewers of Bjeornheim produce the finest mead and ale in the north.

items.name: Dalrstadr
entries: A fortified community in the center of the wide valley between the two rivers of the bear kingdom, Dalrstadr is ruled not by a bearfolk but by an old and canny werekin druid named Jarl Vantir Wolfhide. The farmers of Dalrstadr produce much of the crops that feed the kingdom. In recent weeks, the town has been plagued by a family of bulettes. Scouts managed to track the beasts to a series of tunnels and halls running beneath the town, which don't appear to be of dwarven origin yet are unquestionably ancient.

items.name: Gloaming Crag
entries: The capital of the Honeyed Kingdom is the Gloaming Crag, a formidable fortress resting on a massive outcropping of granite. Beyond the imposing defenses, the crag is a comfortable lair of expansive dining chambers, festive mead halls, and tapestry-lined, saffron-hued corridors. Here, the King and Queen of the Bearfolk rule over a court of bear jarls and a cadre of witches and oracles. The interior of the crag is a warren of caves and passageways built from ancient dwarven tunnels discovered during the construction of the fortress above. Guardians, traps, and magical protections ward the cells of the prison, the vaults of the treasury, and other secrets. Recently, the Crag has been a buzz of activity as Mesikammen and his jarls train their best warriors, ratatosk spies scurry through the halls delivering the latest missives, and smiths work tirelessly to produce arms and armor.

items.name: Hrygangur Peaks
entries: Reaching heights of up to 7,000 feet, the Hrygangur Peaks form the eastern border of the kingdom and are home to pockets of bearfolk, werekin, and stubborn fey. Ancient dwarven fortifications line the peaks and ridges of these mountains. These were either laid to ruin during the Mountain War or long since abandoned to monsters, bandits, or hostile underground dwellers.

items.name: Icewood
entries: Known as "Issvaedis," this large forest of pine and oak is perpetually covered with snow and ice, no matter the time of year. A deep stone well at the heart of the wood emits a constant stream of freezing fog, called the Whispered of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, which drifts between the trees. The forest is occupied by garmr, frostveils and thuellai. Galdby, a small community of bearfolk and werekin, persists at the edges of the trees; its residents venture within the Icewood to harvest pelts, enchanted ice, and other treasures.

items.name: Moonrise Lodge
entries: Located in northern Bjornrike, this fortified lodge shelters former werewolves who have been cured of their lycanthropy. The site is regularly attacked by lupine raiders from Vargrike.

items.name: Skass Moors
entries: North of Bjeornheim, the forests give way to a region of barren hills and wind-swept stones. Few choose to settle in this wasteland, but the open country provides easy access for raiders from nearby Vargrike. Covens of hags gather in old hilltop ruins at auspicious times of the year to conduct disturbing rituals and glean words of prophecy from the spirits, or so they claim.

entries.name: Rulers: The Bear King and Queen
entries: King Mesikammen and Queen Yohana Honeyhair are a striking but decidedly odd couple. He is a fey lord, an immortal being who often appears as a bearfolk with brown and silver hair, but sometimes takes the form of a massive, bearded human in worn hunting leathers. Both forms typically wear a crown of holly leaves. The fey lord is brash, short tempered, and self-indulgent. Conversely, Queen Yohana is a voice of dignity and serenity weaving comfortably with her husband's roars. A mature and beautiful bearfolk druid with golden fur, she favors simple robes of fine material and wears a silver circlet decorated with carved gemstone bees.

Though Old Honey Paws founded Bjornrike, the kingship is decided by yearly challenges, theoretically open to anyone. The bearfolk who compete treat the challenge as a way to prove their might and worth to their king, rather than a serious attempt to seize power. Mesikammen does not hold back during these bouts, and he has defeated all comers since the founding.

Talk of omens, Fimbulwinter, or Ragnarok are largely ignored by Mesikammen, who is preoccupied with the more pressing issues afflicting his family. In times past, he and his retinue would spend most of their days hunting in the hills, brawling, and reveling, while the queen divided her time between Beeulf Hall in Bjeornheim and the capital. Today, tensions over the plight of the bees and the young prince's illness cast a pall over the usually festive court. The queen remains in Bjeornheim with the prince, in the hope her agents will return with a cure, and the king prepares for war.

entries.name: Roleplaying King Mesikammen
entries: Old Honey Paws presents a gruff and coarse demeanor, but beneath his rough façade, he hides a warm and caring spirit. He is fiercely protective of his family and his people, which occasionally leads him to act without due consideration.

entries.name: Personality Trait
entries: "There's a time for feasting, but also a time for battle."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "It is my duty to protect these lands and these people."

items.name: Bond
entries: "My mate and cub hold my heart."

items.name: Wants
entries: "To destroy the ones responsible for harming my cub!"

entries.name: Roleplaying Queen Yohana
entries: The queen is dignified and wise when dealing with others, and she is a shrewd negotiator. Though she was slow to accept her husband, she loves his great heart and the fact that he dotes on their child. A druid of the Bear Maiden, the queen always gives thoughtful deliberation to every decision.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "It is a balance between duty and family."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "As my bees guard us, I shall safeguard these lands."

items.name: Bond
entries: "I am one with the land and the people."

items.name: Wants
entries: "To find a cure for my child's illness!"

entries.name: NPCs, Plots, and Conflicts
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Bee-Blight and Heir's Illness
entries: Most of the kingdom's current efforts focus on the twin issues of the bees and the prince, both seemingly stricken by the same ailment. The queen sends envoys to lands in the North and elsewhere to beg for aid while also hiring adventurers to pursue every rumor of magical cures or alchemical sovereign specifics. For his part, the king views the situation as an attack on Bjornrike and possibly a herald of war. He actively trains his bearfolk for war and, following the advice of his counselor Brother Fjal, has begun sending raids into neighboring Vargrike.

entries.name: Notable NPCs
entries: The following NPCs can often be encountered in the Gloaming Crag, Bjeornheim, or elsewhere in the land:

items.name: {@i Brother Fjal},
entries: a werekin (bear) cleric and self-proclaimed "prophet," who purports to follow {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. He is one of the king's advisors but is actually a member of the Cult of Ragnarok. He plays upon the Bear King's fury and paranoia over the prince's illness and whispers words of betrayal regarding neighboring Vargrike, hoping to spark an open conflict between the nations.

entries.name: {@i Karfinn Half-Troll},
entries: a massive bearfolk with scar-marked brown fur, is one of the greatest warriors of Bjornrike. She spends most of the year fighting monsters near Alfrgan's Gap. Her surname comes from her size and her willingness to eat almost anything. Karfinn wields a halberd in war, and she hates the fey, her king notwithstanding, for reasons she refuses to discuss.

items.name: {@i Ulla Argensdottir},
entries: is an older human wizard who adventured with Mesikammen in her youth. A wizened woman with steely grey hair and piercing blue eyes, she is the Bear King's oldest surviving friend and his advisor on all things arcane. She suspects Fjal's treachery but has yet to find proof.

entries.name: Oni's Resurgence
entries: Across the mountains to the east, an old threat returns. Five years ago, a band of errant adventurers inadvertently released the lich oni Dakhad Atlan from his 500-year prison. The undead warlord currently works to rebuild his power base and army, subjugating one tribe after another. Yet his eyes turn toward Bjornrike and revenge against the Bear King. Scouting raids of ogres and trolls now cross over the Hrygangur Peaks to massacre communities of bearfolk.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The following hooks can be used for stories set in Bjornrike:

items: A dwarven band of adventurers called {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Warrior has vanished in the mountains northeast of the Gloaming Crag while hunting a powerful frost giant known as Coldmaw. The only sign of the missing adventurers is a strange glowing rune hurriedly carved into a stone near some ancient fortifications. Can the PCs brave the cyclopean ruins and save {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Warriors from Coldmaw?

The high priest of {@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} hires the PCs to recover a stolen relic called Twin's Delight, a drop of divine wine crystalized into amber. The trail of the item leads deep into the Icewood, where a coven of hags plans a dark ritual. Can the heroes recover the relic before it is corrupted?

Karfnn Half-Troll directs the PCs to join her in Alfrgan's Gap, but when they arrive, the heroes walk into a trap. Can the PCs rescue Karfnn and foil the new alliance between agents of Dakhad Atlan and the spectral elves of Alfrgan's Gap?

entries.name: Skaldholm, Island of Bards
entries: The small realm of Skaldholm occupies a unique niche in the Northlands. The inhabitants are known for their relatively peaceful ways, though other Northlanders might use terms such as "spear-shy" or cowardly. Its hot springs are famous for their restorative properties, and the island boasts numerous skaldic schools, each run by a famed bard who insists their style is greater than any other. To many, Skaldholm's abundant geothermic comforts, lack of natural hazards, and relatively peaceful populace, make it a sanctuary, yet conflicts both new and ancient simmer beneath the surface.

What the scholars here don't know isn't worth knowing—or so say the scholars. This is a well-earned reputation as the skalds, bards, and sages of the island have painstakingly collected the written and oral histories of the North and elsewhere to compile one of the best known "histories" of the world. The graduates of the academies and schools can commonly be found in the courts of jarls, kings, and even distant emperors. It is a matter of pride to have a Skaldholm-trained skald visit your village or perform before your longhouse fire. These bards typically carry messages, news, and rumors along with their songs and sagas. More than anywhere in the Northlands, Skaldholm demonstrates the power of the spoken or sung word. Many adventurers discover that the difference between a legacy heralding them as a hero or a villain comes down to the skald singing of their exploits.

Skaldholm sits to the south of Trollheim at the end of a volcanic island chain left over from the formation of the Swive. The island is 1,800 square miles of lush, temperate rainforests separated by rocky ridges radiating out from the dormant volcano called Bragafjall Mountain. Numerous geysers and hot springs dot the landscape, filling the air with a slight mineral tang, rather than the sulfurous odor one might expect. Visitors from across the North journey to bathe in the steaming waters to make use of their curative properties. Several communities of druids carefully cultivate the waters to ensure the springs remain clear and their magic strong. Ash, elm, spruce and rowan trees make up the woodlands along with tonrosp ("music aspen"). A durable yet flexible hardwood found only on the island, tonrosp possesses fantastic resonance, a warm golden color, and a fine, straight grain. The finest musical instruments, as well as wands and staves, are carved from tonrosp. Birds and small mammals are the majority of fauna found on Skaldholm, leaving the region largely safe from the usual threats commonly found in the North.

Long ago, magma flowed from the caldera of Bragafjall Mountain, and fire giants held court in obsidian halls built around these rivers of lava. The mountain was the last of a chain of volcanoes extending south from the Reaching Mountains, following (some say) mystical ley lines. The first dwarven empire drove the fire giants away from their ancient halls and soon discovered the healing properties of the springs bubbling up from the mountainous terrain. Though the hold of Ishamagard was founded on a nearby peak, no settlement was built upon the Bragafjall, as groundfire still burned deep within the mountain. Nevertheless, a community of dwarven druids thrived on the slopes, tending the healing pools and their sacred groves. Where the rest of the Northlands turned to war and reaving, the druids promoted a sanctuary of balance and peace. Then came the Swive. When the plains below flooded with the sea god's wrath, and Ishamagard fell into the waves, the druids invoked a great working to raise the mountain, lifting it above the surging waters. Most of the druids perished in the attempt, but when the sea settled, a new island remained. {@deity Bragi|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the son of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, looked upon this new land with favor, guiding his followers there to settle. They called their settlement Skaldholm for it was there that their god commanded them to study the art of song, story, saga, and history. In time, the settlement grew into a city populated by bards, sages, and, of course, skalds.

Society on the island centers on the city of Skaldholm. Most of the inhabitants work in, with, or provide services for the various skaldic schools. The various bardic schools produce the finest musicians in the North, but conflicts between the academies often spill beyond ribald songs. It is not uncommon for feuds between students to result in injuries, damage, and even death. The Master of Thyles condemns this publicly, but they secretly encourage these rivalries, believing it only strengthens his skalds. The leaders of the academies, in turn, owe fealty to the Master of Thyles, who leads the entire island nation. The title is an ancient one, said to be bestowed upon the first leader of the island by {@deity Bragi|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} himself. Each subsequent ruler has abandoned their birthname in favor of this epithet. Skaldholm's kingship is decided by a contest of singing, taletelling, and flyting (a contest-exchange of insults) every nine years. The Master of Thyles sits at the heart of a network skalds, who all report to them, and little escapes their notice. Few Northlanders dare to vex this ruler openly, since the skalds can destroy reputations with a few choice words or songs in feast halls across the North.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: Golden lyre

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Eirik Ellefsen, The Master of Thyles} (human {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook})

items.name: Important Personages:
items.entry: {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas}, Herald of Skaldholm (dwarf {@creature Priest|XMM}); The Academy Masters; Nalgar the Sailor Skald (human {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}); Stonespeaker Randulfr Shield-Wolf (human {@creature Mage|XMM}); Klemens Birchstine ({@creature Worg|XMM} wolf reaver); Brynja Firegrin (fire giantkin {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook}); Frothi Issulfsson, Senior Wyrm-Slayer (human {@creature Northern Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook})

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 8,425 (3,900 humans, 2,950 dwarves, 650 elfmarked, 450 werekin, 300 gnomes, 100 trollkin, 75 giantkin)

items.name: Capital:
items.entry: Skaldholm, population 5,000 (2,600 humans, 1,200 dwarves, 300 elfmarked, 200 werekin, 100 gnomes, 50 trollkin, 25 giantkin)

items.name: Towns:
items.entry: Draugrholt, The Retreat, Volsungar

items.name: Great Gods:
items.entry: {@deity Bragi|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Baldur|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}(Lada), {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} (Kvasir), {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} (Horus)

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Fish, mussels, tonrosp wood, musical instruments, ships, paper, music and lore books, silver amulets

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Skaldholm know the following:

items: The streets and lanes of Skaldholm are awash with music, singing, and storytelling. It is rare to find actual silence here as even the birds of the island provide a constant soundtrack. If the inhabitants can't hear, even distantly, some sort of song or tale, they will break into song themselves. It is not uncommon to see an entire village square happily singing as they go about their daily tasks.

The fishing fleet brings in the bounty of the Swive, and the farming villages grow a variety of crops in the rich volcanic soil. The hot springs of the island allow the inhabitants to cultivate rare medicinal herbs, cloudberries, and even ice peppers.
The Master of Thyles has a semi-secret group of agents called the Shadowsingers. Known but never discussed, these operatives handle espionage, blackmail, and the occasional assassination.

Those who wish the favor or assistance of the Master of Thyles can compete in the Four Magnificent Challenges of Skald Thalwyn Rotjun. This contest changes yearly but pays honor to the famed skald. Making the challenges perilous deters flippant requests for the favor of the Master of Thyles, ensuring that only matters of great import are determined in this way.

entries.name: Skaldholm, City of Bards
entries: The small city of Skaldholm rests in the gentle curve of a natural harbor. The buildings are constructed from smooth, pale stone native to the island, giving the streets a light and airy atmosphere. The structures are low and wide, built to endure the frigid storms rising from the Swive.

entries.name: Bathhouses
entries: The city is renowned for its hot springs. Bathhouses scattered across Skaldholm offer a variety of services from healing and restoration to relaxation and community. The baths are a popular gathering place where bards, scholars, and common folk come to exchange stories, songs and gossip.

entries.name: Feast Halls
entries: The feast halls are a central part of Skaldholm's culture. Part tavern, part inn, and part performance venue, the feast halls tend toward spacious interiors with long wooden tables, massive hearths, and high ceilings. One of the most infamous of these is Hemmelig's Feast Hall located near the harbor. Run by Klemens Birchstine, it is a popular gathering place for visiting reavers, and it is one of the halls most often visited by the current Master of Thyles.

entries.name: Skaldic Schools
entries: There are numerous schools within Skaldholm dedicated to the study of the arts and scholarship. Each believes, of course, that its skalds are the most talented, and recording the resulting feuds between them would fill tome after tome. Among the most well-known skaldic schools are the following:

items.name: {@i Hrafnaskald's Academy}
entries: This school specializes in mixing songs with runes and magical utterances.

items.name: {@i Ljodrun's Hall}
entries: The largest, oldest, and most traditional academy, Ljodrun's skalds are renowned for their focus on the great sagas.

items.name: {@i Rjodr's Grove}
entries: This school combines natural sounds and music, often attracting many beastkin and werekin students.

items.name: {@i Tromma's Pit}
entries: The newest academy. Tromma's Pit features rage-fueled drumming from berserker bards.

entries.name: The Hall of Sagas
entries: This extensive collection of written and oral histories and sagas is one of the few multi-story stone buildings in Skaldholm. The interior is a labyrinth of shelves, manuscripts, and scrolls curated by Stonespeaker Randulfr Shield-Wolf. The irascible human wizard seldom leaves the archives, but few are as knowledgeable about Northlands lore.

entries.name: Thyles Hall
entries: The jarl's home at the center of the city is a strange mix of Northern and Southern styles. It features three tall stone towers attached to a more traditional longhouse. The central hall is designed to ensure every word spoken from the raised stage can be heard, and the walls are carved with intricate images of legendary skalds, heroes and gods.

entries.name: Wyrmhaunt Hall
entries: A faction guild hall of the Wyrm Slayers, this longhouse consists of a large feasting hall, where every kill is rowdily celebrated. The hall is decorated with dozens of stuffed monster heads and other trophies, including the bones of the white dragon, Izrilthandis, whose skull sometimes speaks. Outside is a training ground for experienced Wyrm Slayers to pass on their dragon-slaying skills to newer members.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: While the city of Skaldholm houses most of the island's population, there are small, scattered villages on the northern side of the island. The terrain of the southern side is considered too rocky for permanent settlements.

entries.name: Draugrholt
entries: A small farming village southwest of Skaldholm surrounded by numerous burial mounds. At certain times of the year, the inhabitants claim the vaettir within the mounds speak to them of ancient riddles and lost treasures.

entries.name: Echoing Vault
entries: Fifteen miles to the southwest of the city, a massive adamantine door set into the side of a sheer rock outcropping marks the location of the Echoing Vault. Guarded by a cadre of Shadowsingers, the vault is a repository for dangerous eldritch songs and musical artifacts deemed too hazardous to use. Whispers suggest that the maze-like halls of the Echoing Vault contain eldritch recordings of words of power not uttered since the Vanir War.

entries.name: Gigslag Caldera
entries: At the top of Bragafjall Mountain, Gigslag is a depression awash with poisonous vapors leeching up from the volcano. Once nine mighty fire giant halls ringed the caldera, but eight have fallen into the basin below. The last surviving hall is Eldir's Tree, a towering structure consisting of three multi-spired towers, each with three smaller caps. Few explorers have survived the poisonous fumes from the caldera long enough to uncover the tower's secrets.

entries.name: Hljomr's Tower
entries: The "Singing Spire" stands tall on the most northward spar of the island. Enchanted harp strings span the openings of arches set into the top of the 150-foot, octagonal tower. When the wind blows, as it often does in the Swive, the strings play hauntingly beautiful melodies. There is no obvious entrance to the tower, and the brave few who have attempted to climb it have reported no visible means of ingress, despite the arches seen from the ground.

entries.name: Lyric's Garden
entries: In the middle of the farmlands ringing the city is a raised mound topped with a forest of carved stones called menhirs. Each stone records the epic poems written by the legendary skalds buried within the mound.

entries.name: The Retreat
entries: The Retreat is a village-sized lodge nestled along the coast with beautiful views and clusters of relaxing hot springs. It is the perfect place to rub elbows with the elite, debate with famed orators, and listen for rumors. The Retreat features suites of rooms for rent at exorbitant prices, along with delicious meals to be enjoyed in their spacious dining hall or while lounging in the healing waters of the springs.

entries.name: Tonewood Forest
entries: A woodland of rare and valuable tonrosp trees, the Tonewood is inhabited by the last of Skaldholm's druidic circles. Lately, the forest has been plagued by a flood of undead that the druids seem unable to stem.

entries.name: Volsungar
entries: A fortified and isolated village nestled at the southeastern foothills of Bragafjall, Volsungar hosts a community of bardic smiths who combine skaldic magic with metalwork.

entries.name: Ruler: Master of Thyles
entries: Eirik Ellefsen, the current Master of Thyles, is a thick-browed human man in his late sixties whose worn features, weathered by age, still captivate, with deep-set piercing green eyes and long, silver hair tied back in a braid. He dresses in a combination of practical Northlands clothing. His one affectation is an outer robe of wool-lined silk embroidered with subtle patterns of musical notes and ancient runes. A gift from the child of a southern emperor, he wears the robe as a reminder of his time in the desert courts where the dry sands whispered against ancient stones.

Before winning his position, the Master of Thyles was a noted harpist; his fingers could dance over delicate strings to transport his audience into the heart of his tales. Though now crooked with age, his hands still remember a bit of their skill. In quiet moments, he will turn to his harp, bringing tears to the eyes of his audience with soft melodies and half-remembered tunes. He ascended to his role seven and a half years ago. During his tenure, the Master has demonstrated that his passion for the skaldic arts remains fierce despite his age, and he has built a reputation not just for his deft political machinations but also for his understanding of the power of stories, songs, and words.

As Master of Thyles, Ellefsen has deftly led his people, serving as a bulwark against the werewolves of Vargrike and lending support against the vampiric incursions in Wolfheim. Continuing the policy of his predecessors, the current Master has engaged in a cold war with agents of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the North Wind. Due to his many connections within Northlands courts and cults, the Master was among the first to hear the rumblings that Ragnarok was nigh. While investigating the matter, he stumbled upon the truth: the rumors were false portents! Ragnarok was not coming. The ever-devious {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} stole this knowledge from the Master as payment for a past bargain, and now he only knows that there is something he has forgotten. This lost knowledge has become known as the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing.

All the skalds of Skaldholm puzzle over the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing to no avail. The Master routinely sends his best explorer, Nalgar, to seek wisdom over the sea, and his finest eldritch-spinner, Randulfr, to seek the lost memory in the Shadow Realm and beyond. The Master has sent Sylvoll, his herald and longtime confidant, to entreat the gods for aid.

entries.name: Roleplaying The Master of Thyles
entries: The Master is cunning and shrewd, often engaging in plans within ploys within schemes. He sees no moral issues with manipulating others for the advancement of his causes. Yet his ethical flexibility is tempered by a fierce sense of honor and purpose. He knows his real power lies in the careful application of the information gathered by his skalds.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "Before we act, we must learn all we can."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "In these dangerous times, song and story will hold us together."

items.name: Bond
entries: "Knowledge is the shield I use to defend my people."

items.name: Wants
entries: "I must discover what {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} has taken from me."

entries.name: NPCs, Plots, and Conflicts
entries: Many individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in Skaldholm.

entries.name: Academy Masters
entries: The following NPCs are the leaders of the most renowned skaldic schools in the city:

items.name: {@i Arne Hrafnaskald}
entries: is a competitive and sarcastic ravenfolk bard who has mastered a vocal method of using mystic runes.

items.name: {@i Cyra Rjodr}
entries: is a somewhat shy and reserved wren beastkin druid. She promotes blending nature and music.

items.name: {@i Einar Tromma}
entries: is a hot-tempered trollkin berserker who only recently took up the bardic arts after finding a pair of leather drums during a successful raid.

items.name: {@i Rurik Ljodrun}
entries: is an overbearing dwarven skald who never smiles. He is deeply committed to tradition and comportment, at the expense of innovation and style. He is the current Master of Ceremonies for the Magnificent Challenges (see the {@adventure Trials of the Lost Skald|NorthlandsSagas|5} adventure in {@adventure Northlands Sagas|NorthlandsSagas}).

entries.name: Darkening Song
entries: A rash of strange afflictions has broken out among the musicians of Skaldholm. For each of the past six months, a bard has been found nearly lifeless. They have no memory of what befell them and retain nothing resembling musical skill or training. Oddly, in the weeks before they were found, friends of the victims report the afflicted were particularly inspired, performing well beyond their usual levels. So far, no cause or culprit has been found. In truth, a particularly intelligent ostinato is preying on the skalds of Skaldholm. It has learned to hide itself within the body of its eventual victim, enhancing the musician's skills before feasting on their talent.

entries.name: Fira Wolfsdottir
entries: After making her reputation as an adventurer, blending both lute and blade, Fira returned to Skaldholm to perfect her art. Though the shadowsingers have no official leader, Fira (now in her early forties) is honored and respected by many, often mentoring younger members and offering wisdom to those who seek her out.

entries.name: Jorunn Iron-Head
entries: Until recently, Jorunn was a skald who sailed with a band of reavers called Halfdr's Crows. After a disastrous raid, Jorunn retired to Skaldholm with a sizable dent in his skill and, apparently, the gift of prophecy. He operates out of the back of a tavern called the Singing Salmon, where he tries to mute his blinding headaches with ale. With enough coin or a worthy cause, he will perform in the tavern. The lyrics of his songs change to give hints of the future to those listening.

entries.name: The Master's Trio
entries: The following NPCs are old friends and advisors of the Master of Thyles.

items.name: {@i Nalgar the Sailor Skald}
entries: is a proud and daring human reaver and captain of the longship Seahowl.

items.name: {@i Randulfr Shield-Wolf}
entries: is an irritable human wizard who'd rather be left alone with his studies than converse with others.

items.name: {@i Sylvoll the Herald}
entries: is the Master's closest friend. She has managed his court since his ascension to the post. It is a well-known secret that the two hold deep romantic feelings toward each other.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The following hooks can be used for stories set in Skaldholm:

items: Viggo Golden-Voice, the famed skald, has vanished from his estate outside of Skaldholm after taking delivery of a mysterious relic. Hired by his apprentice, the adventurers must find him before his rivals and creditors descend to ruin his legacy.

The key to the PCs' ongoing quest may lie in the lyrics of a forgotten song last performed before the Reaving. The only possible source for the song lies within the Echoing Vault, and a would-be thief named Jurd Half-a-Hand just happens to know a hidden entrance.

Ground tremors shake Skaldholm, leading the Master of Thyles to hire the PCs to venture into an entrance at the bottom of Gigslag Caldera, where they follow the journal of an ancient explorer on a mission to the volcanic heart of the island.

entries.name: Trollheim, Kingdom of Two Trees
entries: South of the clash between the great northern glaciers and the Reaching Mountains are the fertile forests and fields of Trollheim, where vibrant flora and fauna are sheltered from the worst excesses of cold and wind. It is the largest of the reaver nations, a place where cunning hunters, fearless explorers, and fearsome raiders embrace the culture of the North, regardless of lineage. The power of Trollheim could counter the icy reach of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, his encroaching glaciers, and the giants of the North, if its squabbling jarls could be persuaded to put aside their personal ambitions. Instead, internal conflicts, species tensions, and generational feuds threaten to erupt into new waves of war.

Trollheim stretches from Huldramose to the East all the way to the edge of Vargrike in the West. The main settled area of the nation covers about 77,000 square miles of deep forests and valleys south of the mountains. To the southwest lies the Trollheim "frontier," a 25-mile-wide swath of land running down the eastern side of the Huldramose peninsula to the edge of the Swive. Few settlements exist in this coastline of rocky cliffs, crumbling ruins, and treacherous caverns. Trolls, goblin clans, and kobold warrens have overrun several small communities, but these setbacks only spur the determination of the people of Trollheim to settle the frontier.

In this region of natural bounty, divine omens, and ancient legends, Trollheim stands as a realm of both promise and strife. Most inhabitants of Trollheim live in independent farmsteads and villages that come together in regional althings when danger threatens but otherwise have little patience for talk of kings and kingdoms.

In the past, catastrophes shaped the region now known as Trollheim. Dwarven legions during the Vanir Wars drove the fire giant thanes from their obsidian fortresses and built Ishamagard, most northerly of the dwarven empire's provinces, on the volcanic remains. The Reaving decimated the Ice-Hammered Halls, forcing the surviving dwarves to contend with elves, trolls, giants, and the humans who were just beginning to migrate into the area. Much of dwarven culture was adopted (or forced upon) humans and the other lineages of the region, but the mixing of these peoples taught the dwarves restrained diplomacy, cooperation, and peaceful trade. Then, the glaciers of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, God of the North Wind, breached the Wall and threw down the Vanguard Kingdoms. Close behind, the creation of the Swive flooded the wide, verdant plains cradled between Trollheim and Bjornrike. These calamities forged the people of Trollheim into a hearty folk who farm, brawl, raid each other, toast the gods, and consider themselves the best of all peoples.

For the past seven years, the western population of Trollheim has been almost leaderless after Jarl Asvaldr of the Havardr clan led a combined fleet of his longships (see {@i Midgard Tales}) and those of many other clans on a great raid to the south only to vanish without a trace somewhere in the Nieder Strait. The chaos left behind in the wake of so many vanished jarls and warriors has ended many feuds and created room for more trollkin and even scattered frost goblin (fraugashar) tribes. Many turned to aged King Uffi Toothless to take charge or surrender to Signy Fridrad a younger, stronger ruler. Uffi, finally facing a serious threat to his reign, elevated several young jarls, including a trollkin. This shocking and controversial decision granted legitimacy to the rising population of trollkin, but it alienated hardline dwarves and humans, who saw the newcomers as nothing but monsters. Fanning the flames of discontent, one year ago, Jarl Asvaldr returned without his great fleet, telling a harrowing tale of imprisonment by seafolk.

Trollheim teeters on the brink. Some rally behind Jarl Asvaldr, who pushes for a return to "traditional" customs, while others flock to King Uffi and Veska Flamehair, the first trollkin jarl. Cults and ancient powers look at the turmoil as an opportunity, and with Trollheim divided, not enough turn their gazes northward, where the eternal glaciers continue to grind into populated lands.

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Trollheim know the following:

items: Active trade between human settlements in the lowlands and the dwarven communities in the mountains provide ready access to wood, metal goods, and agricultural products. This fuels shipbuilding and the forging of arms and armor for reaving expeditions each year.

All year round, various settlements host gaming festivals called "leikmots" where the people gather to play various games and sports with prizes and status as rewards. Two of the most popular are knattleikr, a full-contact game involving wooden bats and a leather ball, and a wrestling contest called grima. While deaths are rare, they do occur.

The landscape is dotted with ancient ruins from the old dwarven empire and more recent civilizations. The Vanguard Kingdoms left numerous fortifications, redoubts and crumbling keeps. Belowground, miles of tunnels built to provide respite from the great glaciers remain as frozen labyrinths haunted by ice demons, elementals, and vaettir.

Trollheim's frontier regions contain the largest collection of unexplored dwarven ruins in the Northlands. Many of these sites are inhabited by trolls, goblins, and monsters. Others host bandit reavers who target local caravans and shipping.

Ice mephits, hill giants, and elementals wander down from the glaciers, crossing through gaps in the wall to plague western Trollheim. Marauding werewolves raid eastern communities, and aquatic threats, such as selkies and sea elves, cause trouble for coastal settlements.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Human settlements can be found in sheltered fjords, while dwarves claim the more mountainous regions, and trollkin struggle to find a place in both areas. Fey, goblins, trolls, and various creatures nest in the forest's depths.

entries.name: Amberhall
entries: A large coastal village with a lively trading post, Amberhall is named for the irregular nodules of amber found in the soil of the nearby hills. Its ships and sailors are known for their skills and wily evasiveness. They have sailed even to far distant southern cities, though lately they focus their efforts more locally.

entries.name: Dead Skalds Tor
entries: A bare rock pinnacle in the eastern hills, the tor hosts the ghosts of three dwarven skalds who perished here long ago. The spirits charm mortals to sit and listen to their songs until they succumb to hunger or cold.

entries.name: Great Moss Hall
entries: A moss-covered boulder along a fjord hides the entrance to a revered trollkin feast hall. Here, trollkin shamans of {@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} host feasts, rituals, and religious rites. On rare nights, shamanistic workings allow spirits to interact with the living. Runes of great power enforce peace and goodwill on those in the hall.

entries.name: Gorsewood Lodge
entries: On the shores of Lake Dreken in the Trollheim frontier, senior Dancing Bear Guides meet twice a year in this fortified lodge.

entries.name: Isby
entries: Nestled at the mouth of a fjord on the eastern border, the fortress settlement of Isby straddles the River Tyskr. Werekin hunters and dwarven lumber guilds have made this a popular trading destination for furs and timber. Unfortunately, it also experiences frequent raids from nearby Vargrike.

entries.name: Jarrgard
entries: Atop a low hill on the shore of Black Lake, the squat, snow-covered Jarrgard is an isolated dwarven fort protecting a lucrative silver mine. Visitors are discouraged as the jarl keeps his holding apart from the rest of the country. He even sent word to Uffi Toothless to stay out of Jarrgard's affairs, a threat the king scoffed at yet hasn't challenged.

entries.name: Noatun, City of the Sea Wall
entries: The largest city in Trollheim, Noatun was founded by the god {@deity Njord|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} after he protected the city from the Swive. Rare for a human settlement, Noatun is built more of stone than wood thanks to the skill of local dwarf clans. High, thick walls guard against landward attack, while trading docks and famous shipyards are surrounded by the enchanted sea wall, which magically calms both wave and weather. The city features the Grand Temple of the Shield-maidens, the North's largest temple to {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Noatun is rich and cosmopolitan, welcoming traders and visitors from far afield: longships laden with plunder and thirsty raiders, centaur caravans, and occasional flying islands of cloud giants or magicians of distant lands. Even trolls with gold to spend are welcome (but watched closely).

King Uffi rules from Tannlaus Hall in the center of Noatun. Built from dwarven masonry and human-hewn timbers, the hall is decorated with banners and shields taken in raids and trophies from battles against giants and beasts. These are the king's unsubtle reminder to his jarls of the threats beyond their own squabbles. Nine rival lords, each commanding and maintaining a tower on the seawall, form the core of the royal court.

entries.name: Reaching Mountains
entries: This massive range of snow-capped granite peaks looms over Trollheim like an army of weathered stone jotun. High among their peaks is the Jormulglatz Glacier. Skalds say the greatest heroes may commune with the Valkyries here.

entries.name: Skali
entries: Seat of the Ranulfr Clan, this walled settlement is a popular launching point for expeditions into the frontier. The jarl maintains a lucrative bargain with the nearby ravenfolk at {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Tree, trading protection for prophetic blessings.

entries.name: Stone Meadow
entries: This rocky meadow is marked by dolmens and guarded by a vættir known as She Who Sleeps Lightly—in life, a troll shaman of great power.

entries.name: Threksetr
entries: The regions newest jarldom, Threksetr rises from a rugged hillside, its new-cut wooden halls and stone walls unweathered by wind or time. Here, Jarl Veska Flamehair rules with a relentless determination, offering not only trollkin but also clanless members of other lineages a chance to carve a new path if they swear fealty. Once outcast, they now regain their honor, standing firm against raiders, beasts, and the encroaching greed of others.

entries.name: Varnerhall
entries: Seat of Jarl Vngvarr Ironsides, Varnerhall is a remote but prosperous village perched on a cliff at the end of a heavily forested valley. Clever use of the terrain and shrewd placement of defensive fortifications make Varnerhall surprisingly secure, considering the wild country that surrounds it. The jarl maintains good relations with the nomadic people who pass through the region, trading for furs, ivory, and reliable cold weather equipment and clothing.

entries.name: Viezla
entries: This fortified fishing village has long been home to hearty reavers under the rulership of the Havardr Clan. The hardships suffered by the settlement from the absence of its jarl now begin to heal with his miraculous return.

entries.name: Wotan's Tree
entries: A World Tree stands in Trollheim near the mouth of the Tearstain River. It is one of the safest World Trees, since its ravenfolk guardians make sure that only those ready to fly beyond the mortal world enter its weaving branches. Legends claim that {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} learned the runes here, and the ravenfolk maintain a shrine in his honor, though few humans visit this sacred grove.

entries.name: Ruler: King Toothless
entries: Uffi Toothless, King of Trollheim, is nearly 80 years old, with wrinkled, pale skin; tufts of white hair on his bad, liver-spotted scalp; and a noticeable hunch to his back. He favors fur-lined robes nearly year-round and forgoes his engraved iron crown for a warm woolen cap. Once a powerful warrior, Uffi is now physically frail, suffering constant aches from old wounds and weather-swollen joints. Yet his green eyes remain sharp, as does the mind behind them.

Uffi may be old, but his cunning has only increased with age. He looks to forge alliances among his often divided and independent people, knowing the future of Trollheim can't be secured with brute force. Long experience, natural guile, and (some whisper) a blessing from {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} keep Uffi one step ahead of his power-hungry jarls.

By elevating the trollkin Veska Flamehair, he gambled on a vision for his nation's future. The trollkin, long despised and shunned, could be a great force both militarily and socially, if they can be folded into Trollheim society. His progressive stance pits him against hardline traditionalists, like Jarl Asvaldr, who support a claim that an obscure Ragnarok prophecy begins with a trollkin jarl. Though he publicly welcomed Asvaldr back, Uffi doesn't trust the jarl's "miraculous return" and has sent agents far and wide to investigate what actually happened to Asvaldr. Outside of internal conflicts, the threats of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and Jotunheim remain ever present. The glaciers slowly creeping down into western Trollheim show no sign of halting, and raids from giants increase every season.

Above all, Uffi knows time is his greatest foe. While he is confident a more united nation can be forged, he fears Trollheim will tear itself apart when he passes. He has begun secret negotiations with eldritch sects and southern powers, which may save Trollheim—or doom it.

entries.name: Roleplaying King Toothless
entries: Uffi presents himself as a kindly old grandsire, or as a ruthless politician of the highest order, whichever gives him the best advantage. He has a wicked sense of humor, trending toward the bawdy and crude, and he uses it to hide his frustration over his increasing infirmities. Driving all his schemes and plots, Uffi cares deeply for his land and people, and fears for their future.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "I may be old, but I've more wits in my pinky than half these young fools have in their skulls."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "I will see Trollheim unified and strong no matter the cost."

items.name: Bond
entries: "I recall those who stood by my side and those who spat at my feet."

items.name: Wants
entries: "The fire in me dims with each passing year. If only I could rekindle it."

entries.name: NPCs, Plots, and Conflicts
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Abolethian Influence
entries: Compounding the threats facing Trollheim, Asvaldr Returned-Again prompts hate and opposition to King Uffi among the traditionalist jarls. However, his celebrated "return" was more of a "release," for Asvaldr is an unwitting agent of a group of {@creature Aboleth|XMM|Aboleths} recently established in submerged dwarven ruins beneath the Swive. Controlled mentally, the jarl believes he is acting of his own volition and sees himself as the destined ruler of Trollheim. The true goals of the aboleths are as alien and mysterious as the creatures themselves.

entries.name: Aldric Frostbourne
entries: An obsessive and eccentric elven scholar from the southern lands, Aldric claims to be searching Trollheim for ancient sites of his people from before their Great Retreat. In truth, he is the blood thrall of the vampire thane Osvald Thalrik (see {@area Vargrike|078|x}). Aldric's true mission is to locate pieces of the Dominion Orb.

entries.name: Issvardr Tower
entries: Near Viezla, an ancient tower protrudes from an encroaching glacier. The marble tower lists southward, partway up the side of the ice and nearly horizontal at a 15-degree angle. The tower is home to numerous frozen vaettir and ruled by an Ice Maiden of Morrinn, the daughter of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Trapped within the tower during the fall of the Vanguard Kingdoms, she sends her elementals and vaettir to bring living individuals to warm her cold heart.

entries.name: Juri Jensson
entries: Juri Jensson is an acknowledged shipbuilding genius. His discovery of square-rigged sails 200 years ago helped establish the sea dominance of the Northern reavers. Disgusted with the "progress" in Trollheim, he has been divulging information about merchant ships to the pirate reaver Draga Stormcaller. As the number of waylaid ships mounts, Juri fears his bargain with the elemental controlling pirate will be his downfall.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The following hooks can be used for stories set in Trollheim:

items: The PCs are hired to escort a group of treasure hunters called the Seekers to an ice fortress high in the Reaching Mountains. The Seekers believe a popular series of skaldic poems—the Tales of Halva Wayseeker—are real and point to a hidden Hyperborean artifact.

In the eastern Trollheim settlement of Isby, Grima Twin-Blades needs a discreet band to infiltrate the jarl's longhouse in Varnerhall and rescue a prisoner named Eldri Blue Eye. Grima neglects to mention that Eldri is her lover, is accused of murder, and is secretly a werewolf.

Veska Flamehair needs a champion to represent her new jarldom at the annual leikmot of Noatun. Victory in the games brings fame and rubs dirt in the faces of the more traditional jarls. Perhaps that is why Veska's old champions were recently assassinated.

entries.name: Vargrike, Kingdom of the Wolf
entries: Where the shadows of the Reaching Mountains lie upon boreal groves and rolling taiga, there lies Vargrike, Kingdom of the Wolf. In this grim domain, the lupine reigns supreme. Its hills echo with howls uttered in praise of {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the Great Wolf, and its shrouded forests bear witness to bloody rites and macabre ceremonies. Though outsiders may view it as nothing more than an accursed wilderness plagued by werewolves, worgs, winter wolves, and werekin, the truth of Vargrike is as elusive as the arctic aurora.

Bordered by the Reaching Mountains, Vargrike sprawls across 65,000 square miles of untamed land with few inhabited settlements and little in the way of farming or agriculture. To the east, the Tyskr River creates a border with Trollheim, while the Ulfsorr River and mountains mark the edge of Bjornrike. Despite its foreboding reputation, the land is rich in game, such as elk, reindeer, moose, and deer. Saber-toothed tigers compete for hunting grounds, polar bears prowl the high peaks, and rocs or giant eagles snatch up the unwary. Young giants, trolls, and ogres descend from the peaks to test themselves against pack warriors. Hidden in this foreboding land are untapped natural resources. The forests boast towering oak and spruce, the hills have iron and copper, and the looming mountains hide pockets of gold, labradorite, and gemstones. But woe betide trespassers for the only law here is the law of tooth and fang.

Lupine packs, containing both four-legged and two-legged folk, range across the taiga, hills, and forests, squabbling for territory and prey. Other sentient lineages are tolerated if they are strong and rendered down to food if they are not. Benevolent lupines may treat the unfurred as pets, but most view them as little more than cattle. A wolf jarl, called an uljar (roughly translated as "alpha"), rules each of the five major Vargrike packs. Uljars control vast swaths of land and guard weaker lupine folk in their territory from monstrous threats, as well as the raids and hunts of other packs. The lycanthropic origin (natural-born or cursed) tolerated in each pack can vary, but packs overall tend to either have all natural-born or all cursed werewolves. The origin of the werewolves in a pack often colors their opinions on the morality of spreading the curse of lycanthropy and other issues. Only one pack, the Quickclaws, accepts members of both lycanthropic origins, much to the consternation of the other uljar. In addition to lycanthropes, pack members include werekin, winter wolves, worgs, regular wolves, and non-lupine humanoids, such as humans (who are minor but still-legitimate members of the pack).

Vargrike holds only a few scattered communities, mostly settled by werekin. The rest of the land remains largely unworked since only the sedentary, such as old werewolves, werekin, and "cattle" (non-lupine folk) need fields to farm. Only one city, albeit a ruined one, exists within the borders of the Wolf Kingdom. Amid the moss-encrusted stones of an ancient elven city, Wargaz the Cruel, queen and varulfur (or "alpha of alphas") of the lupine packs, rules from the remains of a palatial citadel called the Moon Palace.

Few creatures escape fear altogether, and the same is true of the lupine folk. Hidden among twisted trees or secluded dales, are ancient elven ruins abandoned during the Great Retreat, and even primordial redoubts from the Vanir War. Increasingly, these ruins have seen a large influx of enigmatic and perilous fey, who have taken to capturing and "curing" two-legged lupine folk, whether they consent or not. Cursed-born return cured, but few live through the following days as old rivals take advantage of their weakened state. Even those who profess to love the cured often slay them out of pity or disgust. Captured natural-born lycanthropes and werekin never return. So far, the fey have remained elusive, but the furious Varulfur Wargaz has decided it is time to purge her territory of these fey interlopers.

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Vargrike know the following:

items: Vargrike settlements are organized around extended family units, similar to those of wild wolves, with the entire community working together to ensure their mutual survival and gleefully destroying nearby packs that show signs of weakness.

Leadership in Vargrike is less a matter of physical prowess, as outsiders assume, and more one of strength of personality, savage determination, and the support of the pack. Failure or hardship leads to leadership changes far more often than personal challenges.

Travelers in Vargrike tend to stay close to the coast, hoping to flag a passing merchant vessel or even a reaver's longboat. Despite the dangers, intrepid souls do occasionally venture into its mountains and forests to marvel at the raw, primal beauty or hunt among its many ancient ruins.
Vargrike raiding parties often cross their borders to pillage communities in Trollheim or Bjornrike, returning with plunder, foodstuffs, and livestock.
Each season, a few mammoths cross the Reaching Mountains, typically followed by hill giants or trolls, an annual migration celebrated by organized hunts of both prey by the lupine packs.

{@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} the Great Wolf is imprisoned in a hidden den somewhere in the northeast of the Kingdom of the Wolf. The average Vargriker avoids discussing the location let alone searching for it.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Vargrike's population is spread out across the territories of the five major packs, inhabiting towns and tiny villages. Some lupines prefer to remain nomadic.

entries.name: Blodtindr Pass
entries: Giants and trolls, as well as ogre raiding parties from the east, often attempt to enter Vargrike through this rocky pass cut through the Reaching Mountains by the Ulfsorr River. Flocks of harpies nest in caves on the flanking peaks, and guard duty on the western end of the pass is a common posting for young lupine warriors.

entries.name: Court of Masks
entries: This crumbling ruin of alabaster arches, marble towers, and moss-shrouded domes was once the court of the fey lord Reynard, but it was abandoned after the Vanir War. Today, Reynard's trusted agent, Count Rauthun, leads a mixed company of fey and returned elves from the ruins, on a quest to eradicate the curse of the wolf. Fey raiding parties abduct lupine folk from nearby communities, curing and releasing the cursed lycanthropes among them. Those who cannot be "cured" are put to death.

entries.name: Den of Fenris
entries: Past the mouth of a fanged cave hidden in the far northeast of Vargrike is a labyrinth of trapped tunnels guarded by divine servitors of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Shackled by the enchanted gold links of the chain known as Gleipnir, {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} the Great Wolf sleeps in a colossal cavern at the heart of this maze.

entries.name: Drakla
entries: This small mountain-side town operates several key mines of iron, silver, and mithril, one of the few sources of metal in Vargrike. Most of the miners are dwarves or werekin who do not fear the effects of silver. Though under the protection of the Wildsong pack, the town is frequently raided by the nearby Storm Howlers.

entries.name: Grim's Hollow
entries: The vast stump of a severed World Tree stands alone on the tundra. Traditionally, young worgs and winter wolves crawl into one of the holes in the tangle of roots as a rite of passage, following the warren of crawlspaces until they reach a cavern deep below. There, the spirits of their ancestors snarl words of prophecy into their pricked ears.

entries.name: Korpn
entries: A riverside village inhabited by werekin and trollkin, Korpn is unique among the settlements of Vargrike in that it owes no fealty to any pack. Instead, it is ruled by Mother Hyndla, a grumpy and enigmatic red hag. She protects the town in exchange for monthly donations of the blood she needs to survive. It is rumored that Mother Hyndla and Varulfur Wargaz were once lovers.

entries.name: Moon Palace
entries: Once a palatial elven citadel during the Vanir War, the Moon Palace is mostly a ruin, yet it remains the largest city in Vargrike. The seat of Varulfur Wargaz the Cruel, the capital boasts a sizable population spread out in dens and houses built into the ruins. Wargaz's throne room is adorned with the hides of her former rivals.

entries.name: Pallid Tower
entries: One of three fey ruins, this thin, helical tower reaches for the sky from atop a peak at the edge of the Reaching Mountains. The tower is only accessible by climbing or flying, and there is no obvious entrance to the pale stone structure. The fey inhabiting the tower all fly and use their speed to raid nearby lupine settlements.

entries.name: Rokvi
entries: This small, fortified village was built where the River Ulfsorr opens into the Klosfjord. Rokvi's battle commander, Tvor Helskarn (nightgarm) uses the village's location to lead regular raids into neighboring Bjornrike.

entries.name: Runewell
entries: This fey ruin rests at the end of a secluded valley and is composed of a stepwell featuring nine levels connected by steps leading down to a deep reservoir of cerulean water. Doorways on each level lead into a network of connected rooms and passages. Despite its location in the mountainous hills, the water at the bottom of the well never freezes. Many of the fey inhabiting this ruin have an affinity to water.

entries.name: Tursa
entries: This walled fishing village on the coast of Vargrike is technically a neutral port for trading ships sailing the Swive. It offers skilled shipwrights, fresh water, and provisions. However, the inhabitants of Tursa have made a profitable deal with several sea reavers, exchanging information on rich traders in exchange for a portion of the plunder.

entries.name: Yfirgefin, the Forsaken Forest
entries: This dense, primeval wood of oak and ash spreads across the southern half of Vargrike, following a curve of the Reaching Mountains. Two cursed packs (Bloodtide and Verdant Fang) inhabit the woods, hunting each other or raiding across the border into Bjornrike. Both packs fear the fey ruin at the heart of the wood and consider it to be a cursed place.

entries.name: Ruler: The Queen of Fang and Fury
entries: Wargaz the Cruel, Varulfur of Vargrike, is an ancient werewolf with gray-white fur scarred from countless challenges. She prefers to appear in her hybrid form, wearing a blood-stained coat of plate fashioned from mithril and chitinous remorhaz hide. When she takes the form of a human, she appears as a wrinkled but still tall and proud woman with long grey hair. She wears a thin, unadorned silver circlet as the only sign of her rulership, despite the pain it causes her. The puckered scarring left by the silver stands as a testament to her fortitude and might.

As a leader, Wargaz is canny, treacherous, and often violent. She manages the rowdy and dangerous politics between packs by setting them against each other or upon Vargrike's neighbors. The Varulfur maintains a hidden supply of silver weapons gathered from over-confident werewolf hunters. Each day, she doses herself with small amounts of the metal, trying to build up some resistance to its usual effects on lycanthropes.

New rumblings among the Uljars suggest the pack lords are beginning to view the growing threat of the fey and their lycanthropic "cure" as signs that Wargaz grows too old or fearful. Yet the common people still hold Wargaz with near mythical reverence or, at the very least, great fear. Her exact age is unknown, and she's outlived a thousand mates and rivals. Some whisper that she is a semi-divine daughter of {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, a fact supported by her personal guard of monstrous wolves called moon hounds. Easily two times the size of worgs, some say these loyal creatures are signs of {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s favor. True or not, Wargaz does little to debunk such rumors, parlaying "signs of her divinity" into political leverage. She knows well how quickly and easily the balance of power can shift, so she moves with stealth and attacks with fury lest anything breaks her hold on Vargrike.

entries.name: Roleplaying the Queen of Fang and Fury
entries: Wargaz comes across as harsh and vicious with barely restrained bloodlust when first encountered. Those who survive the meeting quickly realize that behind her brutal countenance is a shrewd and intelligent mind always calculating how to accomplish her goals. She revels in the lifestyle of the lycanthrope, fiercely defending Vargrike's existence from those determined to destroy the home of the werewolves.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "I have defeated a thousand rivals; I shall defeat a thousand more."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "The only law is strength and survival."

items.name: Bond
entries: "I keep my foes close and silver weapons closer."

items.name: Wants
entries: "The fey think themselves clever, but I have outwitted gods. Let the hunt begin."

entries.name: NPCs, Plots, and Conflicts
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Fox's Revenge
entries: Ysengrim, uncle of the fey lord Reynard and his greatest rival, is gone. Reynard believes his uncle sacrificed himself to create the first lycanthropes but views this as a "cheater's way out," robbing him of revenge. In truth, Ysengrim willingly gave his life to grant his followers the power to become animals, unaware of Reynard's resentment. Now, Reynard encourages his followers to work under the command of Count Rauthun to "cure" his uncle's "children" as a way of settling the score. In secret, he suspects his uncle's essence lingers in their blood and fears Ysengrim might be reborn through the right lineage. He won't let that happen.

entries.name: Frozen Oracle
entries: Four months ago, a delirious werekin explorer stumbled into Korpn claiming to have found a prophetic pillar of ice high in the Reaching Mountains. He soon perished but not before providing a sketch of where he believed the pillar to be located. Many now travel through the Blodtindr Pass and into the peaks searching for the "frozen oracle." Most return empty-handed or not at all.

entries.name: Lycanthropic Cure
entries: Word has spread beyond Vargrike's borders of the "cure" offered by the fey. An increasing number of newly made lycanthropes flood into the kingdom, as do individuals eager to seize the secret of the cure for themselves.

entries.name: Osvald Thalrik
entries: Once a dwarven wizard of Ishamagard, Osvald used forbidden arcana to transform himself into a vampire to survive the Reaving in a half-dead state. Freed last year by an elven explorer named Aldric Frostbourne, Osvald turned the elf into a blood thrall and now seeks to reunite the pieces of the Dominion Orb and undo the Reaving. He lurks in an ancient dwarven tower hidden high in the mountains above Blodtindr Pass.

entries.name: Packs of Vargrike
entries: The major packs of the nation (and their Uljar) include the following:

items.name: Bloodtide
entries: Vicious cursed lycanthropes led by Kaedryn Odd-Eye ({@creature Werewolf|XMM})

items.name: Moonwarden
entries: Protective natural werewolves led by Wargaz the Cruel ({@creature Werewolf|XMM})

items.name: Quickclaw
entries: A mixed pack of cursed and natural lycanthropes led by Grima Half-Tooth ({@creature Werewolf|XMM})

items.name: Storm Howlers
entries: Blood-thirsty cursed werewolves led by Folkmar the Howler ({@creature Werewolf|XMM})

items.name: Verdant Fang
entries: Shadowy natural werewolves led by Var Ironpelt ({@creature Werewolf|XMM})

items.name: Wildsong
entries: Communal natural werewolves led by Hjrulf Hag-Mate ({@creature Werewolf|XMM})

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The following hooks can be used for stories set in Vargrike:

items: Wargaz the Cruel offers a princely treasure to secretly free young werewolves from the Court of Masks—without revealing the PCs work for the Varulfur.
Thyra Ashgrip of the Mile-Steppers hires the PCs to sail a cargo-laden longship to Tursa in the hope of luring reavers into an attack to expose the village's ties to them.

Mother Hyndla suspects her lover, Hjrulf of the Wildsong pack, has been taken prisoner by the Bloodtide pack on orders from the Cult of Ragnarok. She needs a brave band to agree to be given the curse of lycanthropy, find Hjrulf, and investigate the connection to the cult.

entries.name: Wolfheim, the Reaver's Hold
entries: Wolfheim is an isolated kingdom clinging to an uncompromising locale in the wild country between Jotunheim and the sea, west of Trollheim and Huldramose. Prideful, bold, and highly traditionalist, the people here hold to the old reaving ways more fiercely than any other nation. Where others might consider settling in this rocky and inhospitable land a suicidal mistake, the inhabitants of Wolfheim think of it as a worthy challenge.

Wolfheim is a mountainous peninsula of high peaks, craggy valleys, and steep hillsides stretching clawlike into the Nieder Strait. The inhabitants of this cold, windswept kingdom divide the realm into three distinct geographical regions: the Spine, the Claw, and the Roof. The Spine is the central area of Wolfheim, where the high ridges of the Rygg Mountains run down the length of the land. The communities of Wolfheim cling stubbornly to the coastline of the Spine, where conditions allow for scattered farms and forests. To the south is the Claw, a savage badland of storm scoured, bare stone; twisting shale; and tough flora, said to be haunted by the spirits of the dead lost in the Reaving. North is the Roof, a series of heavily forested mountain valleys dotted by ancient ruins and failed settlements of more recent years. The Roof is populated by trolls, hill giants, and hidden communities of tribal elves. Though a source of valuable timber, harvesting the wood requires significant investment in armed guards and labor.

Ages ago, dwarven vampire lords secretly gained control of the hold called Glymshall, casting the beautiful holding and its fertile valley into a nightmare of blood and death. Then came the Reaving. The lands were sundered, the sea rushed in, and the vampire lords withdrew deep underground. Where other dwarven settlements were abandoned for the new secure holds of Tanserhall and elsewhere, the survivors of Glymshall stubbornly refused to leave. The dwarves might have starved for their obstinacy if not for an unlikely alliance. According to the skalds, old King Ragnr sacrificed himself to the twin gods {@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, begging them to aid his people. The next night, packs of winter wolves and worgs brought newly slain reindeer to the dwarves. Though old foes, the dwarves and the wolves made a sacred alliance, standing together so both might survive and thrive. Together, they named their new land Wolfheim. Despite the alliance, the fear and hatred of the undead has never left the cultural make-up of Wolfheim.

Since its founding, Wolfheim has had a reputation as the spiritual home for traditionalist reavers. Yet, the reavers take in other lineages as long as those folk accept their ways. This makes Wolfheim a beacon for young dwarves, humans, trollkin, and others who want to embrace the fearsome reaver culture. The jarldoms of Wolfheim raid and feud constantly, but nearby trolls and giants feel most of their wrath. Since the settlements lack the farms that surround most Northlands communities, they tend vast reindeer herds and raid other kingdoms. They even venture south across the Nieder Strait to claim treasure, grain, and hops as plunder or in trade.

The recent secession of the Wolfmark jarldom, which lies across the Nieder Strait from Wolfheim, is a cause of both relief and fury in the Wolfheim. The new region was carved away from the southerners to cultivate desperately needed farmland. The busy trade ships affiliated with the new jarldom soon returned with a scourge vampirism, necromancy, and undead. Tensions between Wolfmark and Wolfheim grew worse until Wolfmark declared itself independent and crowned its ruler, King Skuti the First. Some in Wolfheim reason they are better off without the upstart young nation, while others seethe over the insult and prepare longships to raid their former kin. The common folk huddle around their longhouse firepits, setting guards in the long, cold nights to protect themselves from vampires or worse.

Despite their local trouble, the chaos in the surrounding regions offers opportunities to the reavers of Wolfheim, and some now consider leading their karls to reoccupy and cultivate the lands south of the ruins of Nordheim, though steering clear of the ruins. If successful, the new farm and grazing grounds would return the trade lost with the secession of the Wolfmark holdings. A small settlement has been established in anticipation of the endeavor finding approval.

Wolfheim's push to the north has not gone unnoticed. The giants and trolls of Jotunheim have no wish to return to the days when the dwarven holds challenged their might, and even now they send their young warriors to test themselves against the reavers of Wolfheim.

items.entry: Anvil of {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} over a wolf's head

items.entry: 25,024 (17,650 dwarves, 2,124 humans, 4,300 trollkin, 750 werekin, 200 giantkin, various packs of trolls, winter wolves and {@creature Worg|XMM|worgs})

items.name: Capital:
items.entry: Wolfheim, population 5,500 (4,000 dwarves, 700 trollkin, 500 human, 150 werekin, 50 giantkin)

items.entry: Eyrsvik, Hjortvik, Havnir, Ljoshorn, Rafrborg

items.name: Great Gods:
items.entry: {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} (patron), {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Hodr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} (Charun), the Hunter

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Gems, gold, reindeer, iron

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Wolfheim know the following information:

items: Arable land is limited in Wolfheim. The people grow hearty crops, such as oats and root vegetables, on hillside plots, and various types of fungus in underground caverns. Fishing vessels venture into the waters of the Nieder Strait for fish and whales. The primary staple of the local diet, both meat and milk, comes from herds of reindeer carefully tended by each community.

Wolves play an important part in life in the realm, from guarding the herds to patrolling wild places alongside dwarven and human scouts. Harming a wolf, worg, or winter wolf is a serious crime in Wolfheim, one punishable by death. Each year, when the first snows fall, the ancient pact with the wolves is renewed in a ceremony called Vetrnaetr.

A rash of vampirism and necromancy plagues communities throughout the realm. Outside the walls of the towns, the mountainous terrain plays host to trolls, ogres, and other fearsome monsters. Scouts are constantly on guard against raids from other Wolfheim communities as well as attacks by giants from nearby Jotunheim.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Most of Wolfheim's population is concentrated in the capital and the four major jarldoms, but there are also scattered, smaller, fortified settlements and communities.

entries.name: Alvavann Forest
entries: A dense forest of oak, ash, elm and rowan, the Alvavann hides many mysteries beneath its towering branches. Great bears, elk, and a scattering of megafauna inhabit the area, as do wolves, worgs, and other creatures. The Refused, a clan of "ghost" elves, dwells in hidden tree communities, guarding ancient ruins and fighting the giants and trolls that occasionally travel down from Jotunheim.

entries.name: Eldfjall Island
entries: A small volcanic island off the southern coast of Wolfheim, Eldfjall is surrounded by jagged shoals and ever-changing tidal swells. The island's rocky landscape, broken by stream geysers, magma pools, and thermal pits, slopes upward to Eldfjall itself, a mighty volcano sending plumes of dark smoke high into the air. Eldfjall is a playground for flame-loving monsters such as mephits, fire drakes, and firebirds. The ancient red dragon, Visandred, makes his lair within the caldera of the volcano, sleeping for decades at a time on his hoard of treasures.

entries.name: Eyrsvik
entries: The seat of Jarl Kjar Valdsson, Eyrsvik is a sizable town for the Northlands. Notable for its deepwater harbor nestled in a curve of the Rygg Mountains, the town boasts some of the best farmland in Wolfheim.

entries.name: Havnir
entries: This jarldom is ruled by the traditionalist Jarl Orvar the Bald and is renowned for its sheltered bay and skilled shipbuilders. The nearby Twistwood provides ample timber, but attacks on logging parties by {@creature Malrgotr|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@area Chapter 8|541|Malrgotr}) have increased in the recent past, and reports now indicate {@creature eikthyrnir|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@area Chapter 8|531|x}) are growing closer to the town.

entries.name: Hjortvik
entries: A small village along the banks of the Feilan river, Hjortvik is an important waypoint for overland trade from Huldramose and Bjornrike. The village's buildings are arrayed around the three-story Aegir's Horn, an inn dedicated to the god of ale, and surrounded by a stout wooden palisade.

entries.name: Grattenn Fens
entries: The "Gray Teeth" cover a sizable area of northeast Wolfheim. Misshapen granite runestones jut randomly from the mires, bogs, and swamps, at times changing positions when no eyes are upon them. Gloomy and shrouded with mists, the fen is home to several covens of hags and their monstrous allies. The covens conduct dark rituals to bring the runestones into advantageous alignment. The hags prey upon travelers skirting the edge of the fens, or bog iron hunting prospectors.

entries.name: Ljoshorn
entries: The seat of Jarl Brok Stouthand, this fortified town sits at the entrance to an extensive network of dwarven mining tunnels dating back to before the Reaving. Precious metals, and even mithral, provide the bulk of the town's exports. Adventurers are always in high demand to battle dark things in the depths.

entries.name: Rafrborg
entries: The seat of the progressive Jarl Sigtove Amberbraid, this bustling town is the most accepting of new ideas and other lineages. Many of the best shield-maidens of the kingdom come from Rafrborg. The town has a busy trade with nearby Huldramose, and an embassy of trollkin from that nation was recently given land within the town's palisade.

entries.name: Reaver's Cave
entries: Once the launching point for Wolfheim's reavers, this large sea cave is now a pirate port tolerated by the local jarls to whom the pirates give a portion of their take as tribute. Lady Astrid Seafang runs the port, managing the fine line between profit and provoking the reaver towns.
