Many explorers use Reaver's Cave as a base to venture into the nearby mound rumored to be the final resting place of the notorious reaver Skjorr Skullsplitter.

entries.name: Skali's Peak
entries: The highest mountain in the Rygg, Skali's Peak is named for the famed hero of ancient tales. During clear nights, the burning light seen upon the peak is said to mark the entrance where Skali battled an elder demon of fire and woe.

entries.name: Twistwood
entries: A wide swath of tangled forest perpetually covered in dense fog, the Twistwood is aptly named. Many explorers who enter its borders quickly become lost. Those who survive speak of plagues of ghosts and phantasms, hungry trees, and ancient barrows occupied by vengeful vaettir. Lumber expeditions from nearby communities are sizable and well-armed.

entries.name: Wolfheim
entries: The largest community in the kingdom, Wolfheim is a bustling town clinging to the steep hill rising from the port. The seat of King Thulsamir Wolfbrother, the city is designed for wolves as much as it is for two-legged citizens. The king's longhouse is called Wolfheim Hall, or more commonly the Fortress of Fangs, and it is famous for its wild winter revels, when enormous barrels of ale are drained in a single night, with fire magic presented by the forge-priests and rune magic by the one-eyed priests of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. The Company of Mile-Steppers also has its headquarters here.

entries.name: Ruler: The Wolf King
entries: King Thulsamir Wolfbrother is a cheerful dwarf with a ruddy complexion, an impish grin, and fiery red hair greying at the temples. Though past his third century, his blue eyes are still sharp and bright. He commonly wears stout woolen garb, richly decorated with threads of precious metals, a cloak of elk fur, and a crown hewn from the anchor of his first longship. The winter wolf, Longtooth, the king's friend of many years and the alpha of the local wolf packs, is typically by his side.

Thulsamir was the first of his line to come to power after the Reaving. As a young ranger, he helped seal the ancient alliance with the worgs and wolves, earning the name "Wolfbrother." He ascended the throne in his 121st year, after his father perished during a kraken attack on the city. Where his father and uncle before him clung to the legacies of the past, Thulsamir looks toward the future. Embracing the raiding lifestyle fully, he helped forge the reaver culture still followed today across the Northlands.

King Thulsamir's greatest ambition is to make his kingdom less dependent on raiding for grain and foodstuffs. He believes the lack of arable land constantly holds back the true might of Wolfheim. After his dream of conquests across the Nieder Strait ended with the independence of Wolfmark, a revolution he still seethes over, he turned his sights northward toward reclaiming the land around the ruins of Nordheim. However, his current plans have been dashed by the death of Blovurr, his nephew and heir. Now, the king struggles against simultaneous threats from the plague of vampires and necromancers, the encroachment of giants from Jotunheim, and the endless conflicts between his jarls.

entries.name: Roleplaying King Thulsamir Wolfbrother
entries: The king tries to present himself as stern and gruff, but he can't help showing his rakish humor. He delights in tales of valor and heroism. As cunning as his wolf companion, Thulsamir has guided Wolfheim through crisis after crisis. He hides a deep, abiding fear of the undead, so the current rash of vampirism brings out the worst in the aging jarl.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "In times of trial, we must meet conflicts head-on."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "I will not allow challenges to my rule to linger."

items.name: Bond
entries: "I honor my friendship with the wolves more than some of my political alliances."

items.name: Wants
entries: "Our future relies on securing new farmlands, by any means necessary."

entries.name: NPCs, Plots, and Conflicts
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

items.name: Hidden Vampire Lord
entries: King Thulsamir's oldest friend, Fraenir the Glutton, has been secretly replaced by Valdric Hohendrak, a vampire warlock displaced from across the Nieder Strait by the founding of Wolfmark. While directing lesser vampires in seemingly random attacks across the realm, Valdric uses his guise of Fraenir to slowly and patiently insert his own thralls into the king's household.

items.name: Wolfheim Jarls
entries: The following NPCs can often be encountered in the capital, their jarldoms, or elsewhere in the land:

items.name: {@i Jarl Brok Stouthand of Ljoshorn},
entries: is a measured and somewhat doddering ruler. Approaching his fourth century, he has little patience for political squabbles and prefers his passion for antiquities. He still leads mining expeditions into the tunnels beneath his jarldom, searching for ancient relics of fallen Glymshall.

items.name: {@i Jarl Orvar the Bald of Havnir},
entries: is a belligerent traditionalist, and his love of reaver culture runs deep. When not leading his reavers, he spends as much time as possible in the slips building new longships.

items.name: {@i Jarl Kjar Valdsson of Eyrsvik},
entries: is a sly and ambitious ruler who holds no genuine appreciation for the reaver ways of Wolfheim. He formulates many plots and schemes to advance his own wealth and power.

items.name: {@i Jarl Sigtove Amberbraid of Rafrborg},
entries: is a passionate and progressive ruler and a former shield-maiden. She pushes boundaries and eagerly embraces new ways and practices to make her reavers more effective.

entries.name: Skadi's Sisters
entries: An offshoot of the famed mercenary group {@deity Skadi|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Sons, this company of female warriors specializes in alpine warfare. Led by Mist (human {@creature Scout|XMM}), they have accepted a commission from King Thulsamir to patrol the northern regions of Wolfheim and guard against giant incursions from Jotunheim.

entries.name: Volund's Forge
entries: Recently, Eitri the Smith reopened a dwarven magma forge long thought to be merely a myth. Located in a secret location in the Rygg Mountains, the temple-forge bears the mark of {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and, if the stories are to be believed, was created by the smith god, {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, himself. Though Eitri has relit the forge and is ready to begin smithing, an incursion of corrupted undead from the adamantine mines below threatens to extinguish the forge for good.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The following hooks can be used for stories set in Wolfheim:

items: A daring reaver named Brynjar Grimfire offers adventurers a place in his felag and on his longship. He is planning a daring raid on Wolfmark with the goal of confronting and slaying King Skuti the First.

The ice maidens of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} have begun a ritual at a perpetual frozen spire south of Nordheim. It is designed to blanket Wolfheim beneath an endless freezing fog. Allied with some of the reaver vampires, the ice maiden's plans would allow the undead to hunt the living with impunity.
Local children are being kidnapped by a trollkin witch in the Grattenn Fens, who claims, spuriously, to be protecting the young people from the vampires infecting their town.

Word has reached Wolfheim of a treasure ship traversing the Nieder Strait loaded down with riches plundered from an ancient dungeon. Time is short to gather a felag and longship to seize the treasure!

entries.name: Giant Jarldoms
entries: In the giant jarldoms of Jotunheim, you can taste magic in the air and feel its tingle in your bones. It's a land of towering mountains, treacherous glaciers, scalding geysers, and magical hot springs, where the Northern Lights can be clearly seen from every summit. Giants rule this land, and even gods walk cautiously. The giants have claimed Jotunheim, which they call the Bones of Aurgelmir after their slain progenitor, since the beginning of the world. All varieties of giants dwell in Jotunheim and live much as their human neighbors do—crafting, hunting, farming, raiding down to the dwarven and human settlements, and bending their knees only to whoever can make them.
This section details the regional settlements of the giant clans as well as other important locations.

entries.name: Agnalan, Giantkin Headlands
entries: South of the towering mountains of Sengajordensblod, two peninsulas reach out into the Nieder Strait on either side of the Munnrfjord. These coastal lands are not a true kingdom. Instead, the Agnalan Headlands is a region sparsely settled by widely scattered giantkin villages. The name the giants give this region is translated literally as "Land of the Bait," and it is appropriate. Reavers from elsewhere in the Northlands regularly descend on Agnalan villages only to be met by young true giants lying in wait. This dubious guardianship is intermittent, however, and more often than not, the giantkin must see to their own protection.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: None

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: Individual village jarls (listed in {@area entries below|0ba|x})

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 4,700 (2,700 giantkin, 1200 trollkin, 500 humans, 300 werekin)

items.name: Major Villages:
items.entry: Eikinstad, Nyrdalr, Orstagr, Svartnaer, Vetrbyr, Vaettrey

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Fish, whale oil and meat, scrimshaw, agricultural products

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Agnalan know the following:

items: Agnalan is too far from the chill of the more northerly glacial heights for most giants, yet too close to Jotunheim for human or dwarven settlers.
Clinging to what arable patches exist, giantkin villages struggle to survive in this inhospitable rocky terrain inhabited by trolls, ogres, and other monstrous threats.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Most of the inhabitants of Agnalan reside in six coastal villages, but other smaller settlements exist.

entries.name: Eikinstad
entries: Possessing perhaps the most fertile land in Agnalan, Eikinstad grows hardy root vegetables and keeps shaggy cattle. Jarl Thyra Anjadottir is renowned for her skills as a druid and a farmer. Rumors say something is tunneling beneath the village, the crops grow strangely sweet, and the night holds whispers.

entries.name: Nyrdalr
entries: Once a struggling farming village, Nyrdalr now bristles with masts and sharpened axes. Jarl Asgaut Thornheel, a brutal, dwarf-hating giantkin, transformed the village into a haven for Northlands pirates. He even leads raids in his own longboat. Loot flows freely, but the raids place a large target on the village.

entries.name: Orstagr
entries: Veiled in near-perpetual fog, this fishing village is a cold and quiet harbor town. Jarl Ismar Cut-Tongue, a grizzled former reaver, struggles to safeguard his people as the bodies of villagers and livestock have been found drained of blood and scarred with sigils.

entries.name: Svartnaer
entries: Perched on sea cliffs blackened by volcanic rock, Svartnaer is known for its metalwork. The dwarven Jarl, Vorni Tiny-Giant, runs both the bellows and the village through her mix of charm and grit. A recent cave-in has uncovered ancient ruins, but they have yet to be explored.

entries.name: Vaettrey
entries: Built on a rocky spit above whale-rich waters, this island village thrives on fishing and whale-rendering. Jarl Hrolf Greasebeard, a former harpooner himself, keeps the peace with brutal efficiency. While always dangerous, whaling risks have increased with the appearance of ghostly dwarven revenants rising from the depths of the Nieder Strait.

entries.name: Vetrbyr
entries: Built from jorumungkyn bones and broken ships, Vetrbyr clings to a wave-battered coastline. The inhabitants harvest ambergris from the sea and herd goats in the hills. Acknowledged as a sea-witch, Jarl Kelta Three-Tooth boasts beguiling hexes that have kept the village safe, but age has diminished her powers.

entries.name: Ymir's Pyre
entries: On a lonely island, a cyclopean pillar of obsidian and gneiss rises more than 100 feet into the air. Atop this primordial spire, an enchanted fire has burned since history began. Northland sailors use the pyre as a guide beacon but are careful to give the island a wide berth because no one who has landed there has ever returned.

entries.name: Bjarmia, Flying Island of the Cloud Giants
entries: The proud cloud giants of the Northlands reside in high mountain holds or floating cloud steadings sheltering tight-knit families, but the greatest number dwell in Bjarmia, the flying island of the cloud giants. Resembling a mote of land encircled by a white cloud, the island is a rough, 3-mile-diameter oval. It is covered in longhouses and great halls of white marble with soaring golden rooftops. Each hall is separated by gently meandering cobblestone paths bordered by cold weather gardens. Ever-flowing enchanted streams feed terraced farm plots and animal pens before falling from the edge of the island.

Eldritch power pervades Bjarmia, illuminating magical orbs with flickering golden fire and imbuing the crystal pylons that maintain the subarctic climate regardless of the year or altitude. Bjarmians claim that the goddess Gulveig taught them the art of cloud weaving, as well as how to empower their floating steadings, though she has not been worshiped in ages.

Most of the time, Bjarmia is above the clouds, drifting to and from Jotunheim. Occasionally, the island touches down upon the waves near coastal ports to trade. The giants deal in luxuries, rare magic, and valuable objects, but they're sharp-eyed traders, and their "deals" have unexpected consequences.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: A golden tower on a gray cloud

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas|Queen Azala Stormsinger}

items.name: Important Personages:
items.entry: Dunvak ({@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}); Sverre Stone-Brand ({@creature Cloud Giant|XMM}); {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas} (Storm Giantkin)

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 1,790 (600 cloud giants, 520 giantkin, 470 human thralls, 150 thursir, 45 {@creature Wind Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Wind Trolls}, 5 {@creature Liosalfar|ToB1-2023})

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Ice wine, jewelry, magical items, lore and music

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Bjarmia know the following:

items: Bjarmia moves slowly but constantly. It regularly stops to trade at major settlements in Jotunheim, and annually near Stannasgard and Skaldholm.
Cloud giants still construct small floating palaces, but the secret to building whole islands was lost long ago.
Bjarmians enjoy luxury goods, such as fine cloth and wine. They trade for these, if possible, or take them in raids.
Outsiders are viewed with suspicion but not outright hostility.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Aetherarium. This tall observatory is for planar observations. Its magical viewing crystals can display locations across the Northlands.

entries.name: Circle of Gold
entries: Cloud giants come to this marble-paved market yard to trade for goods or peruse the latest haul of the hunters and merchants. Many magic items, crafted by local artists or taken by traders, can be found in the stalls and stands.

entries.name: Hanging Groves
entries: These terraced farms are on the cardinal points of the island and are fed by enchanted streams. The giants grow barley, rye, and root vegetables. Rows of mountain apples and pear trees are overladen with fruit, and pens hold various flying creatures, such as wyverns, giant eagles, and hippogriffs.

entries.name: High Halls
entries: Unlike the longhouses elsewhere on the island, this colossal palace of marble and gilded glass harkens back to an older time, when the giants ruled creation. The court of Queen Azala meets in her crystal-domed throne room to settle disputes and greet dignitaries. At the heart of the High Halls is an eldritch machine providing power to the entire island.

entries.name: Silver Hearth
entries: The largest mead hall on the island is a spot where cloud giants and visitors often gather among leviathan-rib pillars for feasting, music, and game playing.

entries.name: Twin Altars
entries: Near the High Halls, daily offerings decorate {@deity Bergelmir|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s obsidian altar and {@deity Angrboda|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s shrine of World Tree ash and natural stone. Deep below, the great bloodstone temple vaults hold the greatest riches given to the deities.

entries.name: Ruler: The Sky Queen
entries: Queen Azala Stormsinger is a strong-featured cloud giant with blue-white skin and golden hair braided into a single plait. She wears white robes with a wide belt set with golden disks from which hang a ceremonial scepter of state. A diadem of silver and diamonds rests on her brow. Azala came to the throne at a young age, but her determination has won over most of her detractors. She is very concerned about the Cult of Ragnarok's influence on the other giant clans and is unwilling to march in step to orders from the warlords in Jotunheim.

entries.name: Roleplaying Azala Stormsinger
entries: As with most cloud giants, the queen believes herself to be superior to everyone and isn't afraid to show it. Azala presents as strong and unyielding, but she truly cares for her people and worries over their place in the world.

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Disruptive Maintenance
entries: Dunvak, king of the thursir, operates the eldritch artifact below the High Halls and has been blamed for a recent swath of power interruptions, but he believes spire walkers in the lightning tunnels beneath the device are responsible.

entries.name: Lagertha Giantblooded
entries: This storm giantkin recently arrived on the island, leading a delegation from the Order of the Thunderer. In truth, she is a spy for the Cult of Ragnarok seeking to determine how loyal the cloud giants are to the cause. So far, Queen Azala has succeeded in keeping them in the dark, but the situation can't endure forever. For more about Lagertha, see the {@adventure Descent of Cloud Castle|NorthlandsSagas|6} adventure in {@adventure Northlands Sagas|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: Skyholm Light
entries: At the edge of the island is a crumbling lighthouse whose function no one remembers. Recently, a strange light has flashed directly upward from the ruin every new moon.

entries.name: Sverre Stone-Brand
entries: A powerful cloud giant warlord, Sverre actively courts Azala's hand, but it is no secret that he harbors ambitions to rule Bjarmia himself. He is elitist and snobbish, meeting any slight to the glory and honor of his people with violence.

entries.name: The White Wyrm
entries: Dread Isandradr, a cunning white dragon, threatens to make Bjarmia her new home by murdering all the inhabitants unless she is given sufficient treasure to change her mind. If the queen can't pay the wergild, someone must track Isandradr to her lair and deal with the dragon.

entries.name: Blodejord, Fire Giant Halls
entries: The spine of Jotunheim is the Blodejord—"Crib of Earth's Blood" in the Jotun tongue. This wild land is marked by a range of active volcanoes rising around the charred and desolate remains of once-fertile valleys. The smoking peaks belch fire and burning stones into the air, and the ash, drawn from the primordial heart of the world, carries dire enchantments that turn those who die covered by it into twisted undead.

Clans of fire giants inhabit this foreboding landscape, toiling in their mountain fortresses to hone their skills at battle and metalworking. Fire giants are generally short-tempered and warlike, but they are also passionate and creative. Perhaps due to this, their society is more regimented than other Jotunheim cultures. While some choice is expected, most fire giants are strongly encouraged to pursue callings suited to their individual abilities. Fire giant smiths consider themselves to be the greatest crafters in the world, a boast long disputed by the dwarves. Relations between fire giants and dwarves fluctuate. Sometimes, they bond over their love of the craft, and other times, they feud over the same issue.

The majority of the population inhabits obsidian fortresses built on and within volcanoes along the Blodejord. Each of the Blodejord's volcanic fortresses is commanded by a "svidari," a title translated literally as one-who-burns. All current svidari were chosen by King Isen Brekssen and owe allegiance to Drottenbrand, the seat of the fire giant ruler.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: A crimson erupting volcano and a black sword

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: The Flamelord, King Isen Brekssen the Proud ({@creature Fire Giant|XMM})

items.name: Important Personages:
items.entry: Svidari Droka Ragiirsson of Jattebrand (fire giant); Molgru the Hollow ({@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}); Vrali Embercall (fire giant); Sertha Broken Helm (fire giant)

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 5,300 (3,700 fire giants, 1000 thursir, 600 giantkin)

items.name: Capital:
items.entry: Drottenbrand, population 1,200 (800 fire giants, 200 thursir, 200 giantkin)

items.name: Major Fortresses:
items.entry: Jattebrand

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Refined metals, gems, rare minerals, thralls, fire magic

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Blodejord know the following:

items: The warlike fire giants are often the first to heed the calls to war, and they train constantly to be ready for battle.
Raw ore from across Jotunheim is processed in lava-powered smelters into refined ingots of iron, steel, mithral, and adamantine.
The fire giants enjoy embermead, a spiced drink infused with flecks of gold to give it a fiery glitter.
The fire giants largely ignore the land outside of their volcanoes, leaving the region to fell monsters such as lindwyrms, ashwalkers, and elementals.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: The majority of the population lives in Drottenbrand and Jattebrand, with the rest spread among the other fortresses.

entries.name: Drottenbrand, Seat of the Flamelord
entries: This formidable obsidian fortress is among the oldest structures in the Northlands, dating back to the First Age. Encircling the caldera of the volcano that shares its name like a crown, Drottenbrand is sacred to the fire giants as the seat of their king but also for its Golden Sky Hall. Within this hall of perfectly carved cyclopean stones, fire giant king, Isen Brekssen, issues decrees and appoints his jarls and underlings to gather and strengthen the giant kingdom.

At the heart of the hall is the First Flame, a hearth fire said to have been kept burning from the days when the blood and bones of Aurgelmir first made the world. This fire grants a powerful tempering to those who bathe in it, sometimes reinforcing the body, sometimes healing, and other times transforming non-giants into fire giants.

entries.name: Galgvidr Forest
entries: Southeast of Drottenbrand is a large forest of towering oaks, twisted elms, and gnarled pines. This dark wood bears many names—Galdvidr, Idavoll, Jarnvidr, or the Ironwood—and it has long been the personal refuge of the giant goddess Angriboda. The children of the "mother of monsters" roam the woods, fiercely guarding their sire's domain.

entries.name: Jattebrand
entries: Located toward the center of the Blodejord range, Jattebrand is a fortress built almost entirely within a volcano. Near its heavily guarded core is a rift gate connecting to the plane of fire. The giants of Jattebrand believe it is their sacred task to guard this end of the gate, a task Svidari Droka Ragiirsson takes seriously. His father, Ragiir Blisterbrand, commands Helspyre, the fortress on the other side of the gate.

entries.name: Ruler: The Flamelord
entries: King Isen Brekssen, Flamelord of Blodejord, is a powerfully built fire giant with the red-black skin and the flaming hair typical of his people. He wears a suit of intricate armor made from adamantine and red dragon scales. Young for his rank, he rose to power by defeating the former king in personal combat.

entries.name: Roleplaying the Flamelord
entries: Called "the Proud," Isen believes it is his sacred task to bring his people to greatness. He struggles to temper his pride and inexperience with wisdom.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "The other giant kings conspire against me. They will fail."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "All flames yearn upward, and so must we."

items.name: Bond
entries: "The first flame whispers the secrets of Aurgelmir if we but listen closely."

items.name: Wants
entries: "To forge a mighty legacy and win the hand of Iselra Hvitrosa, the frost giant."

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Burning Love
entries: Despite all of his plans and ambition, King Isen the Proud is haunted by his unrequited love for Iselra Hvitrosa, the frost giant daughter of Jarl Vaknir of Kaldrgard. She has lingered in his mind ever since she defeated him during a sparring bout when they were young.

entries.name: Cursed Blade
entries: At the request of jotun patrons, fire giant necromancers have nearly completed crafting crib-ash and undead bodies into a perfect copy of Surtr's blade, the great weapon of Ragnarok. However, giantkin agents of the Glorious Order (see {@area Chapter 3|0f5|x}) seek to sabotage the work, hoping to trick the giants into creating a jotun-slaying blade.

entries.name: Molgru the Hollow
entries: A self-proclaimed prophet, the thursir Molgru wanders the valleys of Blodejord, coating his skin with crib-ash. He claims to hear Aurgelmir's whispers in the necromantic coating and says his "visions" tell of future events.

entries.name: The New Fortress
entries: Vrali Embercall and her family of followers hope to establish a new fire giant community in an unsettled volcano. However, none of the scouts sent into the lava tunnels have returned. Vrali ignored the old tales whispering the site is home to a legendary salamander and its apprentices, but now she begs for aid.

entries.name: War Calls
entries: Isen's champion and ardent Blood Reckoning follower, Sertha Broken-Helm, urges the king to launch scorched-earth raids into Wolfheim and burn out the followers of the accursed gods.

entries.name: Kaldrgard, Frost Giant Jarldoms
entries: Where the great glaciers of the Bleak Expanse collide with the mountains of Jotunheim lie the scattered frost giant jarldoms of Kaldrgard. This frigid, barren realm of ice and snow centers on the Fjorhrim Glacier and the mountains surrounding it. Few permanent settlements exist in Kaldrgard, most notably a trio of towering, primordial ice castles glittering upon high mountain slopes, their crystalline towers shining as a symbol of their might.

Frost giants believe Aurgelmir bestowed the coldest reaches of the North upon their forebears, deeming them to be the strongest among the giants and thus the only ones worthy of dwelling in such an inhospitable climate. This pride runs through their culture to this day, and displays of strength determine a frost giant's social standing. Yet while individually competitive and even brutal as a group, they are fiercely protective of their families and clans.

Recently, a schism has divided Kaldrgard. A growing number of young frost giants have turned aside from their traditional veneration of {@deity Bergelmir|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Angrboda|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, seduced by the banner of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} in the Bleak Expanse or the militaristic plans of the Blood Reckoning. The older jarls seem helpless to curb the exodus of the younger generation, torn between concern for the future of the clans and their deeply held individualist tendencies.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: Blue stone wall in front of a white glacier

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: Queen Atla Gunnlodottir of Hrimthursalr ({@creature Frost Giant|XMM})

items.name: Jarls:
items.entry: Grim Holgi of Kyrsasalr (frost giant); Vaknir Rimepaw of Drifasalr (frost giant)

items.name: Important Personages:
items.entry: Iselra Hvitrosa (frost giant); Forn Gjaldrsson ({@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}); Laska Mistharp (frost giant)

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 7,800 (5,500 frost giants, 1,250 giantkin, 750 {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls}, 300 thursir

items.name: Capital:
items.entry: Hrimthursalr, population 1,450 (900 frost giants, 450 giantkin, 100 thursir)

items.name: Towns:
items.entry: Drifasalr, Kyrsasalr

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Mammoth tusks and fur, iced steel, frost magics, rare arctic herbs

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Kaldrgard know the following:

items: The giants hunt herds of mammoths, reindeer, and caribou that wander the mountainous valleys at the edge of the glaciers.
Tribes of yeti, saber-toothed tigers, and other arctic threats offer decent challenges to train young warriors.
Frost giants cultivate exotic cold-weather herbs, lichens, and medicinal brews.
Kaldrgard is the main source for iced steel, a rare metal deeply prized by other giant realms and beyond.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Most frost giants dwell in nomadic families, but a sizable portion of the population dwells in three ice castles.

entries.name: Drifasalr
entries: Centuries of wind and snowfall have shaped the domed towers and sloped walls of Snowdrift Hall. Within, labyrinthine corridors thrum with laughter and the ring of arms. Jarl Vaknir Rimepaw trains with his warriors daily, while his daughter Iselra duels three at once, her laughter bright as splintering ice.

entries.name: Fara's Stone
entries: This 20-foot-tall, blue-green spire of native stone sits on the far eastern edge of Kaldrgard. Nomadic humans and elves in the region have anointed a flat altar shelf at its base with reindeer fat, carved antlers, and other offerings to bring them luck in hunting. The centuries of veneration have awakened an elemental locus, which guards the area and protects those who honor it.

entries.name: Frozen Bastion
entries: In a hidden location somewhere on the great glacier is a repository of wealth and devastating weaponry commissioned by {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. A squadron of eighteen fanatical frost giants guards the vault, and a nearby white dragon has been bribed to provide additional protection. Spectral undead wander the frozen halls within. As yet, the rest of Kaldrgard is unaware of the vault's existence.

entries.name: Hnitbjorg
entries: The ruins of a once mighty giant fortress crumble upon the side of a grey mountain. Once home to the jotun Suttungr and his daughter Gunnlod, Hnitbjorg was built to protect the mythical Mead of Poetry, but it was stolen by {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} long ago. It is said whoever drinks the mead could recite any information and answer any question.

entries.name: Hrimthursalr
entries: Crowned in frozen mist, Hrimthursalr gleams like a blade of sky-forged ice, its walls jagged and translucent. Icicle-laced bridges span its many towers, and frost-slick ramparts overlook the endless glacier below. Within, Queen Atla Gunnlodottir broods on her throne of carved dragon horn, as whispers of division swirl like a blizzard.

entries.name: Krysasalr
entries: This castle rises atop a cliffside like a shard of shattered starlight, its walls and towers hewn from blue-white crystal that catches every shimmer of sun or moon. The jarl ruling this stunning structure, Grim Holgi, ignores the splendor to focus on omens and fell prophecies.

entries.name: Ruler: Frost Queen
entries: Queen Alta Gunnlodottir presents as an imposing figure. She possesses smooth blue skin and hair the color of shining snow, bound in thick braids set with carved bone decorations. The queen wears a mantle of white mammoth fur and a crown of jagged ice-white crystals. Alta won her throne by defeating her predecessor in personal combat.

entries.name: Roleplaying the Frost Queen
entries: The daughter of the last giant to drink from the Mead of Poetry, Alta is uncommonly eloquent and fiercely wise. Yet she sees the fading of traditions and worries the realm is slipping out of her grasp.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "I wield metaphor as others wield axes."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "Old songs teach us not how to die but how to live."

items.name: Bond
entries: "I will not see my people divided by old fools or reckless youths."

items.name: Wants
entries: "I must keep Kaldrgard whole despite the blows seeking to shatter it."

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: False Skald
entries: The wandering bard, Laska Mistharp presents as a bright-eyed, poetic young woman with tales of snow spirits and ancestral glories. Her visits to the castles and communities of Kaldrgard are widely anticipated by music lovers and children. Her performances are laced with subliminal invocations to {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, each stanza quietly sowing seeds of doubt, as well as reverence to the North Wind.

entries.name: Forn Gjaldrsson
entries: A thursir elder smith and expert at refining elemental ice into iced steel, Forn operates an enchanted cold forge in Hrimthursalr.

entries.name: Hearts of Ice
entries: A growing number of young frost giants have begun wearing shards of a strange pale crystal said to "protect" them. The crystals are imbued with {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s will and anchors for his expanding influence.

entries.name: Iselra Hvitrosa
entries: The daughter of Jarl Vaknir, Iselra is a frost giant warrior who seeks to forge a legacy based on her prowess rather than her great beauty. She is unaware that King Isen the Proud of Blodejord has loved her since they were young.

entries.name: Tombs of Frost
entries: Scattered across the Fjorhrim Glacier are frozen stone doors opening into enormous barrows carved into the ice. Here, frost giant jarls and renowned warriors lie buried with their grave treasures. These tombs are targeted by {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@area Chapter 8|53b|x}) looters who dig tunnels too small for the giants to pursue them.

entries.name: Sengajordensblod, Land of the Jotun
entries: At the heart of Jotunheim, the fallen blood of the First Giant is said to have fed mountains until they nearly pierced the sky. Among these peaks lie the halls of the jotun, the near-immortal children of Aurgelmir. Some remember the Gods War and their father's murder, a crime that still defines their culture. Many know ancient secrets and snippets of antediluvian arcane lore, and the most powerful among them straddle the line between mortal and demigod.

The vast jotun halls are carved into mountains and glaciers across Sengajordensblod. From their icy thrones, the jotun lords exert nominal control over all of Jotunheim, though in practice the kingdoms of the lesser giants are self-governing. They see themselves as the true heirs of creation, and most bear eternal hatred for the gods. Only {@deity Bergelmir|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Angrboda|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} earn their reverence. The jotun mourn the decline of giantkind, blaming the Aesir's rise for their people's dwindling size and strength. Some seek restoration; others hoard power. Though long divided, hatred smolders beneath the surface, ready to forge Sengajordensblod into a force that could make the gods tremble.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: Skull of Aurgelmir

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: Individual jotun lords

items.name: Important Personages:
items.entry: Utgardlok (jotun {@creature Archmage|XMM}); Berfinn Thjazason ({@creature Storm Giant|XMM}); Karn Rune-Sworn ({@creature Stone Giant|XMM}); Kolrjot Icehowl of the Bloodhail ({@creature Jotun|NorthlandsWorldbook})

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 35,100 (13,800 jotun, 7,500 {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}, 3,000 storm giants, 2,000 giantkin, 1,400 {@creature Troll|XMM|Trolls}, 1,200 {@creature Stone Giant|XMM|Stone Giants}, 750 trollkin, 600 {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Lightning Giants}, 400 {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants}, 250 {@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thrudgelmir Giants}, 200 {@creature Fire Giant|XMM|Fire Giants}, 4,000 thralls)

items.name: Capital:
items.entry: Sengajordensblod, population 12,975 (5,300 jotun, 2,500 thursir, 1,150 storm giants, 1,000 giantkin, 500 trolls, 375 frost giants, 300 stone giants, 250 trollkin, 200 fire giants, 1,400 thralls)

items.name: Towns:
items.entry: Gastropnir, Gifrvagga, Griotunagardar, Thrymheim, Ut-Gard

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Gems, gold, exotic giant beasts, primordial relics and magic, thralls

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Sengajordensblod know the following:

items: The jotun lords rule from primordial fortresses located on high peaks or in ancient redoubts dug into the sides of mountains.

All forms of giants can be found in Sengajordensblod. As the most powerful, jotun are respected and feared, but even the physically weaker thursir are valued for their crafting skills. Stone giants, however, hold a low social status, due to some age-old crime few will discuss.

When the omens indicate, the jotun lords call the greatest giants to gather for the Blodting, a council held in the Temple of the Skull at the center of Sengajordensblod. Decisions made there can shape the fate of the Northlands for generations.
Titanic beasts are herded by the giants, including huge muskox, elk, axebeaks, and mastodons. Cave bears, dire wolves, and saber-toothed tigers regularly prey on the herds and travelers alike.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Most of the giant population dwells in ancient cities, towns, or fortresses, but other scattered settlements can also be found here.

entries.name: Gastropnir
entries: A large town built around a trap-filled hollow mountain, Gastropnir is where the imprisoned jotun goddess Mengloth resides. Pilgrims seek the aid of the corrupted deity for healing or resurrection, but those who enter her dungeon prison may receive a boon or face punishment for disturbing her, based on her whims.

entries.name: Gatusalr
entries: A ruined hall atop a wind-blasted peak, Gatusalr was once home to Vetrgautr, a jotun lord and druid runemaster, who raised enchanted giant goats. Desiring the goats, {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} destroyed the hall and slew Vetrgautr and most of the herd, before departing with a pair for himself. The remote site remains largely untouched.

entries.name: Gifrvagga
entries: An ancient, basalt-towered stronghold on a winding river, Gifrvagga is ruled by Jarl Jorva, a jotun priest of {@deity Angrboda|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Built for intimidation, it's poised within easy striking distance of Wolfheim and the villages of the Agnalan Headlands. By its looming threat, it proclaims itself to be a place where giantkin kneel and lesser creatures remember their place before the true lords of the North.

entries.name: Griotunagardar
entries: The southernmost settlement in Sengajordensblod, this fortified town of stone giants is ruled by Grithyrnir Ironboot, a jotun overseer. The stone giants are only too aware they are always watched and judged by the other giants for the ancient crime that exiled most of their ancestors. Many of the young warriors crave freedom, but rebellion is swiftly crushed by the jotun lords.

entries.name: Sengajordensblod
entries: Capital of the jotun realm, Sengajordensblod sprawls across mountain peaks and glacier-carved plateaus, its titanic halls and rune-scored towers linked by massive stone bridges. The Temple of the Skull at the center of the city holds the court of the jotun lords and is where the Blodting meets. The city seethes with primordial power and ancient hatreds. The ruler of the city is King Bolthorn, the oldest surviving jotun and grandfather of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Bolthorn is alternately respected and feared across the Northlands, and if anyone can be said to rule Jotunheim, it is him.

entries.name: Stjarnarad
entries: In the southern peaks of Sengajordensblod is a sacred amphitheater arrayed around the Heartstone, a cracked red crystal that pulses rhythmically with an inner light. The jotun believe the stone marks where the First Giant's heart fell after the Aesir used his body to form the world. Jotun seers gather here for ecstatic rites, seeking communion with Aurgelmir's spirit through ritual and trance.

entries.name: Table of Nerthus
entries: A blood-stained granite shelf, the Table of Nerthus is revered by ogres as the birthplace of the first of their kind. Ogre and troll shamans perform sacrifices on the slab, marking themselves in blood. Unbeknownst to them, each offering weakens the prison of She Who Waits in Hollows, a void-born entity sealed beneath the table.

entries.name: Thrymheim
entries: The mountain castle of the storm giants is perpetually shrouded in lightning-etched storm clouds and driving winds. Tall metal rods extend from every tower, drawing lightning down to orbs decorating nearly every chamber of the castle. Passing storm giants touch these crackling spheres, allowing the trapped lighting to play across their hands. Jarl Berfinn Thjazason (storm giant), ruler of Thrymheim, dreams of avenging his famous father's death at the hands of {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Ut-gard
entries: In eastern Sengajordensblod stands Ut-gard, the enigmatic stronghold of the archmage Utgardlok. Protected by layers of impenetrable illusions and enchantments, it's said not even the gods themselves can find the entrance unless the Lord of Ut-gard wills it. Utgardlok is famed for humiliating the Aesir in a series of confrontations, much to the delight of his people. Despite his cunning, the archmage truly believes the lies spread by the Cult of Ragnarok. He has allowed the cult to establish a presence in his domain, but the ways of Utgardlok are never obvious, and he could be using the cult for his own purposes.

entries.name: Ruler: The Jotun King
entries: King Bolthorn the Eternal is a towering figure of impossible age, his golden hair turned gray and skin weathered like jagged stone. His beard hangs to his waist, and his eyes glow with the weight of ages. He wears no crown, only a mantle of relics taken from kin slain by the Aesir. As {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s grandfather, he is tied to the gods but bears them no love. To the young, he is a relic; to the old, he is a reminder that the war is not over.

entries.name: Roleplaying the Jotun King
entries: Impossibly old, Bolthorn remembers the shaping of the world and the murder of the First Giant. He has forgotten more magic than the greatest wizards ever knew. Though he rarely speaks, Bolthorn's words carry great weight among the giants. However, the person he wishes to influence most is his estranged son, Skymir.

items.name: Personality Trait
entries: "I forget names but never faces or deeds."

items.name: Ideal
entries: "I was once devoted to the revival of our supremacy, but now I doubt the wisdom of revenge."

items.name: Bond
entries: "With each passing year, I fear more for the future of my people."

items.name: Wants
entries: "I must change my son Skymir's path. Destroy the gods, yes. End the world, no."

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Blodting
entries: Following the omens read by his seers, Bolthorn issues the call for the greatest giants to gather in Sengajordensblod to discuss if Jotunheim should embrace the cause of the Blood Reckoning and at last launch their campaign of revenge against {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and the gods.

entries.name: Karn Rune-Sworn
entries: A stone giant skald, Karn has searched for the truth behind his people's ancient crime for decades. Recently, he has uncovered clues pointing to a hidden repository of lore at the heart of a trapped labyrinth deep beneath Griotunagardar. But the tunnels are too small for a giant to navigate.

entries.name: Mimir's Heir
entries: One of Yggdrasil's three mighty roots stretches into a hidden cavern deep within Sengajordensblod, fed by a pinpoint planar rift into the Well of Mimir. For untold ages, Mimir's Head was hidden here until it was relocated to Runaskr. Now, Mimir's daughter, Tove Mimirsdottir, dwells in this cavern, plotting with void dragons to recover her father.

entries.name: Thraka Blood-Hook
entries: An ogre shaman corrupted in her dreams by the entity beneath the Table of Nethus, Thraka believes She Who Waits in Hollows to be a nascent ogre deity. She gathers a cult of followers to abduct and capture more sentient creatures to feed the birth of her goddess.

entries.name: Thursrike
entries: Stretching along the Western coast of the Northlands, and bordered on three sides by glaciers, Thursrike is a land of hill giants, ogres, trolls, and others on the fringe of giant society. This frontier region wears the scars of the past like badges of honor. Some of the oldest structures in the Northlands can be found here. Several primordial fortress settlements have stood in all their glory as far back as the oldest legends, when their walls withstood the great battles that were waged between the jotun and the gods. Strange Hyperborean ruins dot the tundra, beckoning the brave or foolish to intrude on their ageless rest. A wasteland of fractured hills, where the laws of nature are superseded by twisting madness, dominates the middle of the region. The ever-encroaching glaciers reveal ancient ruins and antediluvian monsters as they grind across the land. Amid the remnants of ages past, Thursrike strives to carve its place, defying looming threats that imperil its future.

Thursrike sprawls across almost 475,000 square miles, most of which is unsettled wilderness. The mountainous southern region, Haamu Hills, presses up against Jotunheim, before descending into the dense Blaleir Forest. The rest of the landscape is made up of low, arctic grasslands and tundra dotted by fens and bogs. Much of the population can be found in or around four titanic fortress-settlements—Drekholl, Jarnskul, Kjothall, and Kupparsheim. The land surrounding each of these redoubts supports vast herds of livestock, from sheep and shaggy northern cattle to mammoths and aurochs. The rest of the terrain is wild and treacherous, populated by remorhazes, white dragons, thuellai, liosalfar, and warlike bands of yeti.

The jarls of Thursrike represent a cross-section of giants, and this confluence of cultures makes Thursrike more tolerant of other peoples than the rest of Jotunheim. Even non-giants can forge a future here, as long as they are strong enough to hold their own. This reputation sometimes attracts outlaws and exiles, who flee into Thursrike to avoid the consequences of their actions. Most, however, discover this land is indeed accepting, but it is never kind.

items.name: Symbol:
items.entry: A shield with a red bend sinister

items.name: Ruler:
items.entry: King Guthmundur Raggnarson ({@creature Jotun|NorthlandsWorldbook})

items.name: Jarls:
items.entry: Listed individually in the Pasture Fortress section below

items.name: Important Personages:
items.entry: Laughing Kettil ({@creature Jotun|NorthlandsWorldbook}); Glytta Weggesdottir, priest of {@deity Jormungandr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} ({@creature Stone Giant|XMM}); Kaprasius Quickstep (trollkin); Vekona Darkbrow (trollkin); Haakon Drakechoker ({@creature Frost Giant|XMM}); Ulf Lacknose ({@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook})

items.name: Population:
items.entry: 46,450 (13,000 ogres, 9,000 trollkin, 4,000 humans and dwarves (Haamu Hills area), 4,000 {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}, 3,500 {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants}, 3,000 giantkin, 1,200 {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls}, 1,050 werekin, 500 {@creature Stone Giant|XMM|Stone Giants}, 500 beastkin, 300 {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants}, 200 {@creature Bugbear||Bugbears}, 200 {@creature Goblin||Goblins}, 6,000 thralls)

items.name: Capital:
items.entry: Kupparsheim, population 4,180 (1,000 ogres, 950 trollkin, 850 giantkin, 250 thursir, 200 hill giants, 100 tundra gnolls, 50 werekin, 25 beastkin, 25 stone giants, 1000 thralls)

items.name: Towns:
items.entry: Brimholt, Crokeheim, Drekoll, Gralheimr, Jarnskul, Kjothall, Nidvik, Uroby, Tuskgard

items.name: Great Gods:
items.entry: {@deity Angrboda|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Bergelmir|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Jormungandr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}

items.name: Trade Goods:
items.entry: Wool, sheep, cattle, leather, mammoth tusks, herd animals, archaeological relics

entries.name: Noteworthy Features
entries: Those familiar with Thursrike know the following:

items: The four fortress-settlements contain massive grazing territories, and meat from the herds feeds the giant kingdoms of Jotunheim. These pastures are patrolled by mounted giantkin wielding dragonbone warhorns to warn of approaching threats.

Most communities consist of hill giants, ogres, and trolls, plus a scattering of other peoples. Guesting traditions are fiercely kept, but visitors are required to drink the strong local mead as a sign of thanks to the host.

The famed jotun, Kettil Buckbridge, sprawls across a ravine on the murky River Mjorkan. Locally constructed ramps and scaffolding across his belly act as a bridge, though travelers must earn passage by telling him a joke. If they aren't amusing, they risk being swatted like flies.
Some of the ruins dotting the tundra are Hyperborean, and they pulse faintly with indecipherable runes. Explorers speak of stairwells that descend too far and doors that open into stars.

entries.name: Settlements and Sites
entries: Most of Thursrike's population is concentrated in the major fortress-settlements, but there are smaller communities beyond these fortified areas.

entries.name: Alvatrad
entries: A dark and twisted World Tree, Alvatrad was long ago shaped by the Vanir into a temple to forgotten gods. It no longer leads to Yggdrasil, and those who climb its gnarled trunk often find themselves in strange planes. The hollow roots contain passages and winding stairs, which are said to open onto the shore of a vast subterranean sea.

entries.name: Birgkrona
entries: This primordial jotun fortress was constructed during the wars with the gods. Currently, a large contingent of the Blood Reckoning sect of the Cult of Ragnarok makes its home here among giant allies.

entries.name: Blaleir Forest
entries: This dense woodland is bisected by the River Niflnott and is known for its peculiar blue clay soil. {@creature Brunnmigi|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@area Chapter 8|52e|x}) and {@creature Malrgotr|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@area Chapter 8|541|Malrgotr}) dwell in the forest, and a number of {@creature Fleshcrawler|NorthlandsWorldbook|Fleshcrawlers} (see {@area Chapter 8|533|x}) hunt in the Eastern Reaches, near small craters filled with glowing crystals.

entries.name: Brimholt
entries: This small whaling village of giantkin appears unfriendly to outsiders, but in truth, the villagers are merely fiercely protective of the selkie clans living in the waters outside the harbor. The two communities have a close partnership, and members of the two communities even marry on occasion.

entries.name: Crokeheim
entries: This crude ice fortress is the seat of King Haakon Drakechoker, a frost giant exiled from Kaldrgard for unsavory tendencies. Haakon's frost giants hold a fearsome reputation for feasting on the remains of those they defeat in combat, and they travel far to strike communities along the Trollbane Coast and Havsfjord. Recent reports suggest the giants have taken to abducting villagers instead of immediately consuming them.

entries.name: Drowned Tower of Xulgrun
entries: This multi-level Hyperborean tower rises from the middle of a glacial river. It appears to be formed from solidified water. Its murky walls ripple occasionally like a liquid, but they feel like stone to the touch. An entrance lurks beneath the river's surface, allowing access to the interior chambers, which all appear to be filled with water.

entries.name: Gralheimr
entries: Squatting among looted burial mounds, this village of bugbears and goblins worships a one-eyed skull idol that whispers instructions for the construction of a strange eldritch device. The current leader, a warlord named Skrath Mar-Pelt, conducts raids far and wide for the components needed to complete the item. He believes the device will bring glory to his people.

entries.name: Isherjar Halls
entries: The edge of the glacier reveals an army of dwarves in a colossal stone great hall, frozen within the ice. The style of their gear and decorations mark them from a time before the Reaving. Those who listen closely can hear the dwarves' hearts beating impossibly slowly.

entries.name: Kittelberg
entries: A stone temple rests at the edge of the caldera of this smoking volcano, hanging over the slowly bubbling magma. Many sacrifices are made to {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Hel|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} here, and the area is tended by the clerics, Kaprasius Quickstep and Vekona Darkbrow, a trollkin couple.

entries.name: Narvegr Maw
entries: A vast sinkhole, 500 feet in diameter, plunges miles-deep, its walls riddled with caverns and spanned by natural bridges. Strange subterranean creatures emerge periodically to destroy nearby sources of magical corruption, then vanish back into the depths.

entries.name: Nidvik
entries: This small, ramshackle village on the edge of the Blaleir is a known refuge for outlaws and pirates. It pays tribute to the fey of the forest for protection.

entries.name: Pasture Fortresses
entries: Each of the fortified settlements and their jarls are listed here.

items.name: {@i Drekholl}
entries: Ruled by Jarl Ingemar Varblut ({@creature Hill Giant|XMM}), this coastal fortress also boasts a well-equipped fishing fleet.

items.name: {@i Jarnskul}
entries: Ruled by Jarl Enevold Hraundrykkir ({@creature Ogre|XMM}), this crumbling keep resembles a broken skull.

items.name: {@i Kjothall}
entries: Ruled by Jarl Ulli Wotanson ({@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}), this ordered and organized fortress has the largest herds and specializes in tending mammoths.

items.name: {@i Kupparshiem}
entries: The seat of King Guthmundur Raggnarson, the two levels of this stone-walled fortress rest above a much larger subterranean labyrinth, whose walls are covered in strange, indecipherable murals.

entries.name: Tuskgard
entries: This riverside fortress houses a warlike population of trollkin and goblins dedicated to {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Led by Ulf Lacknose ({@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook}), Tuskgard boasts several skilled shipwrights. From here, reavers sail south to raid, bringing plunder and thralls from coastal settlements and southern shores. Captives begin a punishing journey inland to be bartered as thralls, food, or sacrifices to giants.

entries.name: Twisted Ulnoth
entries: Spiraling like a frozen helix, this Hyperborean ruin perches atop a jagged stone outcrop rising from the glacier's heart. Inside, black stone galleries curl inward, etched with runes that change as they are read. Strange winds coil through the halls, echoing like chants. Those who enter rarely reach the center, and fewer still return.

entries.name: Uroby
entries: This village of {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls} (see {@area Chapter 8|53b|x}) clings to a glacier-fed river near the edge of Lengjorn's corruption. Though they avoid the wasteland, the gnolls' dreams are haunted by dark whispers. Void-touched aberrations approach their territory, and Ygruhild, the gnoll matriarch, fears the glacier no longer holds back the cursed land.

entries.name: Volmyrr
entries: The largest boggy marsh in Thursrike, the Volmyrr has a bloody reputation as the home of a coven of hags who demand tribute of flesh from nearby communities (including Drekholl and Kupparsheim). That the jarls unquestionably pay this wergild indicates the coven's infamy is well earned.

entries.name: Vornthuul's Spire
entries: The top of a crimson monolith rises out of the glacier, its sides marked with strange Hyperborean glyphs and symbols worn from time and weather. Investigations suggest that a much larger structure lies beneath the ice.

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the kingdom.

entries.name: Guthmundur Raggnarson
entries: The jotun King of Thursrike rules in name only. In truth, his authority stops at the four pasture fortresses, but he dreams of bringing the entire region under his direct control. To that end, he trains an elite force of hill giants to be the core of his new army.

entries.name: Koltha Cindereye
entries: A fire-scarred werekin, Koltha's eyes burn with orange light. She claims she was blessed by "great powers" while exploring Vornthuul's Spire. Her charismatic words attract growing numbers of followers among the thralls of Thursrike.

entries.name: Lost Herd
entries: A large missing herd of auroch from Drekholl has been found, stripped of flesh and muscle, on a straight line toward the Field of Lengjorn.

entries.name: Rakhred's Spear
entries: The ghost of the dwarven adventurer who once conquered Kupparsheim (and was later slain by Guthmundur Raggnarson) now belligerently haunts the fortress, demanding the return of her ancestral spear so she can go to Valhalla.

entries.name: Other Settlements in the Northlands
entries: The following list details other nations, cities, and settlements found in the Northlands. More information about these areas can be found in the Midgard Worldbook.

entries.name: Bleak Expanse, Realm of Boreas
entries: Beyond Jotunheim lies the Bleak Expanse, a boundless tundra of ice so deep some believe no ground lies beneath. Here reigns {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the cruel, capricious, and eternal God of the North Wind, who seeks to drown the world in endless winter. His living glaciers advance like armies, driven by divine hatred, while rebels and exiles—human, giant, and beast alike—struggle to survive his storm. {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} counts giants, dragons, and fell beasts among his worshippers, as well as mortal zealots who venerate the North Wind with fanatical devotion. Few other mortals survive here: the nomadic human Skraelings roam the ice fields, and hidden enclaves of other species hunt the frozen rifts, always wary of the ancient evils sleeping beneath the glacial ice. Geskleithron, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s capital, gleams like carved ice beneath his mountain fortress of Black Tower, where frozen souls are traded for divine favors. At the southern end of the Expanse lies the Boiling Tower of Auvindri Against-the-Wind, a fire giant archmage waging lonely war against {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and his encroaching ice.

items.name: Hrafnheim, Kingdom of Leaf and Quill
entries: Perched on a new World Tree is Runaskr, the City of Thought, and capital of the North's newest settlement. Long ago, Hrafnheim was formed by a pact between {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Ratatoskr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} to secretly preserve the knowledge spouted by the prophesy-speaking severed head of the jotun Mimir. This invaluable resource is coveted by a clutch of void dragons, so within the last year, the two deities grew the new World Tree and transported the Runaskr from its previous location in Yggdrasil to the Northlands. Today, the City of Thought is home to ravenfolk Speakers and ratatosk Seekers who gather and study lore from across the planes. The unique arboreal community's vine-draped bridges and glowing branchways bustle with scholars and couriers trading knowledge for secrets. Its leaders—Speaker Lord Hruthen Inkbeak and High Seeker Yllka Punchleaf—struggle to preserve unity as prophecy, ambition, and awakening forces threaten to unravel Hrafnheim's fragile harmony. Aside from Runaskr, Hrafnheim controls two small port villages, Akby to the north and Draumvik to the south.

items.name: Huldramose, Land of Marsh and Tree
entries: This sizable nation is situated in the cold marshlands and is ruled by two elfmarked monarchs, Thorgerd and Dark Irpa. An unconventional land, Huldramose is named for the "huldra," trollkin warriors considered to be among the first Valkyries. Trollkin make up a large portion of the population. For years, the two monarchs have hidden a World Tree sapling, nurturing and protecting it. The swift growth of the tree makes it likely the general populace will soon learn of its existence. Recently, Dark Irpa found a number of void creatures descending out of the immature World Tree and quickly slew them. The incident has put the rulers at odds. Thorgerd wants to protect the tree and heal it as it is obviously ill. Dark Irpa is convinced the tree is not a World Tree sapling at all and is instead a root leading to {@deity Nidhogg|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s domain.

items.name: Jomsborg, Isle of Berserkers
entries: This island is home to the Jomsvikings, a force of berserker mercenaries renowned for their brutality and ferocity. Though they are despised across the Reaver Coast, the berserkers abide by a strict code of honor and conduct. During the winter months, or between contracts, they train constantly in an austere and punishing regimen designed to harden their bodies and perfect their fighting rages. Until recently, the Jomsvikings accepted only humans into their ranks, but the victory of the trollkin Solveig Rockhurler over Beoric Thorson radically changed matters on the island. As Hersir (or "battle lord"), Rockhurler opened the Isle of Berserkers to other giantkin and non-humans. This move proved too much for some; Thorson gathered a faction of those angry with the loss of their traditional ways and split away from the Jomsvikings to settle the town of Harmarstad on the far side of Jomsborg. With skirmishes between the opposing berserker camps growing more frequent, the entire island may soon erupt into war.

items.name: Tanserhall, the Forge Hold
entries: The most sacred dwarven city, Tanserhall alone remained intact after the Reaving. At its heart is the Cradle Cave, where {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} forged the first dwarves, gifting them metal, jewels, and courage. The city is a vast underground fortress, fiercely guarded and closed to outsiders. Uninvited guests face a deadly labyrinth that few survive. Heeding {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s advice after the Reaving, the very pious population honors {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} in strict balance, enacting elaborate sets of rituals to ensure both patron gods are placated equally. On the surface, the dwarves farm terraces using hired karls of other species, preferring them in the fields rather than allowing them underground to work the mines. Two years ago, the monstrous spawn of {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} rose up from the depths of the Cradle Cave, and for a time, the brave Tanserhall warriors held them back. Now, they battle ink-black hulks in the lower streets of Tanserhall itself. The dwarves know the war turns against them, and so the call for "Vigferth," or crusade, has gone out, summoning dwarves from across the Northlands to aid their beleaguered cousins.

items.name: Stannasgard, Sea Hold
entries: The most open of the dwarven reaver kingdoms, Stannasgard is a key trading enclave and gateway to the Nieder Strait. Its wealth comes from rich iron and adamantine mines, fueling a renowned craft tradition, especially in shields and armor. Home to great temples of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, its vast priesthood funds the crafting of divine relics, and pilgrims travel from afar to {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Shrine of a Thousand Anvils atop a craggy peak. Though rarely at war, Stannasgard's warriors seldom fail when they march. Two years ago, the city was attacked by the red dragon Visandred, which burned its docks and shipbuilding slips and decimated its trading fleet. Jarl Beragorn Shipkeeper (dwarf) sent his army to bring down the beast, but they never returned. This loss plus the decimated trade strain Stannasgard's coffers, and foreign foes eye the weakened city with avarice. Yet Stannasgard's forges burn on, fueled by determination. Over the last year, many giantkin and trollkin settlers have established new settlements along the coast, creating both tension and hope for the beleaguered country.

items.name: Thrumagard, Thunder Mountain Hold
entries: North of Stannasgard lies Thrumagard, the newest of the dwarven reaver holds. Abandoned after the fall of the old dwarven kingdom, the site was retaken 150 years ago by Alaric the Mithral-Dwarf (dwarf wolf reaver) and his Band of the Thunder Hammer. Settling there after their victory, Jarl Alaric reopened the mithral mines and welcomed non-dwarfs, including humans, halflings, and ravenfolk. Since that time, the hold has prospered, delving deep and building the Shire of Golden Hammers to {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Though more conservative holds such as Tanserhall disapprove of its inclusive stance, none dare challenge its strength. The Order of the Thunderer, a militant dwarven order, defends Thrumagard against Jotunheim's forces. Two years ago, they stood against the Cult of Ragnarok, rooting out spies and attacking safehouses. The cult retaliated by assassinating key figures, including the archmage Delric. More recently, Thrumagard dispatched much of the Order to defend Stannasgard after a dragon wiped out its army. With its focus shifted, giants and other monsters now flourish in the nearby hills and mountains.

entries.name: Adventure Locations
entries: All these places are believed to be legends, and some are said to be no more than a skald's imaginings. None are readily found on a map, but surely some are true and could be found by a bold explorer.

entries.name: Ansaroth
entries: North of Reykurbrand Volcano lies the ruins of Ansaroth. Ancient beyond memory, no written record of Ansaroth's original purpose exists. The majority of the original site rests underground, with newer and cruder structures on the surface. {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} long ago sent a force of {@creature Troll|XMM|Trolls}, {@creature Bugbear||Bugbears}, trollkin, and {@creature Fraughashar|ToB1-2023} to Ansaroth for purposes known only to the North Wind. Today, their descendants, known collectively as Ansarothr, inhabit the ruin, continuing their predecessors' work, forcing captives to explore the subterranean labyrinth and violently driving off any outsiders who approach. Though hearty warriors, the inhabitants consider the ruins below ground cursed and haunted. Only the worst winter weather, or most serious punishments, drive those above to seek dubious shelter in the dark of Ansaroth.

entries.name: History
entries: While nothing is known of ancient Ansaroth, the current settlement was established about 100 years ago when thuellai escorted the first minions of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} to the ruin. No reason for their presence was given then, and few dare to question the ineffable schemes of the North Wind. Though the ruins below bear the marks of dwarven stonework, these signs are only found in the passages near the surface. The deeper chambers are decorated with unsettling iconography and alien glyphs.

entries.name: Locations in Ansaroth
entries: Ansaroth is divided into three different sections: Above, the Darkness Beyond Torchlight, and the Descent.

entries.name: Above
entries: On the surface, trollkin and {@creature Fraughashar|ToB1-2023} dwell in sturdy buildings constructed from axe-hewn logs and stone carved from the Haamu Hills. The two groups of inhabitants mostly keep to themselves, divided along ancestral and social divides. Feuds and squabbles over resources are common. Trollkin warbands live in longhouses in groups of thirty, each led by a pair of mated warriors or a troll warlord. Fraughashar live in log cabins, where their beds are stacked like cordwood. Groups of ten to fifteen form familial units that are protected by as many bugbears as they can entice into their home—or at least for as long as they can stand the stench of wet bugbear.

At the center of Ansaroth is a stone floor and six feet of a short defensive wall, all that remains of the original structures on the surface. Next to these vestiges are many holes and openings leading to the subterranean labyrinth. Nearest to the surface ruins is a crevasse called the Darkening Step, the largest of the passages below and the only one to feature circular stairs of dwarven craftmanship. All openings are heavily guarded.

Over the stone floor of the original ruin is Rimespike Vault, a thatched roof supported by four massive pillars of bundled mammoth bones. Here, the Ansarothr mete out punishment to those who transgress the laws of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and the community. Minor infractions are answered with flogging, while more serious offenders are escorted by a dozen of their kin belowground, handed a modest weapon, and ordered not to return until five nights have passed or be slain on sight. Thus far, none have returned.

Ansarothr raiders venture far to take captives from settlements or to trade with some of the giantkin villages of Jotunheim. Those taken by the raiding parties languish in heavily guarded stockades, suffering from malnutrition and abuse. Yet they are the fortunate ones. The unlucky are forced belowground to explore the rooms, halls, and chambers of the Darkness Beyond Torchlight. While rare, some captive explorers have returned to report seeing fell monsters, traps, and disturbing wonders. Any relief they might experience at seeing the sunlight again is short-lived, as they are routinely forced below.

entries.name: Darkness Beyond Torchlight
entries: The openings in the Above lead down to winding subterranean halls and rooms whose purposes have long been lost to time. From the fragmented reports of the forced explorers, the upper levels of the Darkness Beyond Torchlight are wider than the layers beneath. Aberrations and other horrors are commonplace. Disarmed or triggered traps appear to reset magically or by unknown beings. Every manner of frightening sight or sound has been reported at one time or another, but groups of warriors as large as a dozen have gone missing.

entries.name: The Descent
entries: Dwarven captive, Arnka Shuthamar, the most successful (and longest lived) of the forced explorers, believes as one descends through the chambers, galleries, and passages, the rooms begin to taper toward a single, spiraling stairway. She reached this location on her last delve and reported that the stairs are cut into the inside of an enormous shaft she called "the Descent." The walls of the shaft are carved into titanic statues of humanoids with strange, alien faces. The steps descend for several hundred feet before breaking off, but the shaft continues to descend, at least as far as a dropped torch can illuminate. The Ansarothr keep Arnka separated from the rest of the prisoners, believing she isn't telling them the whole truth. In fact, she is not, but she will die before she reveals what she saw in the depths of the Descent.

entries.name: NPCs, Plots, and Conflicts
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in Ansaroth.

entries.name: Kissan Virnstyr
entries: A fraughashar {@creature Priest|XMM} of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, Kissan keeps control over Ansaroth's bugbears through a combination of fey guile and frost bolts. In recent days, the Ansarothr hunters have struggled to hunt the fresh meat necessary to sate bugbear appetites.

entries.name: Blarban Eye-Eater
entries: The king of the trolls and trollkin has a problem. For the past dozen fortnights, at least one troll has woken covered with blood from a wound healed by their regeneration. None have memories of being attacked or even being woken by the assault. Fear and anger increase with every attack, causing many to question Blarban's leadership. In truth, a cunning redcap named Raudmir has been using {@item Spell Scroll (Level 1)|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} of {@spell Sleep|XPHB} on the trolls to keep them docile while he dips his cap in their blood.

entries.name: Songs of Gold and Betrayal
entries: Spjuka (trollkin {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook}) wanders from Stannasgard to Jotunheim to Wolfheim, telling tales in the mead halls and longhouses of the wonders and riches waiting to be plucked from Ansaroth. She entices the greedy and the foolish with honeyed words, eventually giving them a worn map to the site. The skald receives remuneration twice: first, from the adventurers in exchange for the map, and second, from the unseen agents of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} once the adventurers are captured by the Ansarothr.

entries.name: Grokeheim, Snow Queen's Palace
entries: Delicate spires erupt into the sky, piercing the horizon like frosty spears. Carved entirely from ice, Grokeheim is the realm of Her Crystalline Majesty, the Snow Queen Morrinn, Daughter of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} the North Wind. Created by powerful enchantments, this great castle of ice and rime magically relocates to different areas of the Bleak Expanse every morning when the dawn brushes its towers. The distances crossed by Grokeheim are vast, and its destinations are chosen at the whim of the Snow Queen. The allure of shimmering Grokeheim (and its beautiful ruler) often lures foolish and lost travelers to its gates, and they are soon met by the Snow Queen's servants. Those lucky enough to survive the initial encounter soon learn that the Mistress of Grokeheim is much like her realm—beautiful, cold, and unforgivingly deadly.

Grokeheim is hard to find unless its ruler wishes it, and the castle is never encountered in the same place twice. The palace appears each morning on a new glacier or frost-covered tundra on the Bleak Expanse. Whispered stories suggest the Snow Queen can command Grokeheim to appear anywhere in the Northlands, but she simply hasn't chosen to do so yet. The population of the castle consists mainly of fey ice maidens, {@creature Fraughashar|ToB1-2023}, {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres}, {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants}, {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}, and trollkin. Outside the keep, Grokeheim is coated in deep snow that slows all but the Morrinn's ice maidens. Inside, the floors and walls are crafted from blue ice that traps and reflects sunlight at odd hours. This gives the impression that the castle is dimly lit at all hours, even during the night. Grokeheim is inhospitably cold, except in the brief, rare moments when a visitor causes the Snow Queen to laugh.

The palace is a towering ice castle consisting of delicate towers, great halls, vaulted hallways, bedchambers, barracks, and libraries. The air within is frigid, and most of the structures, furniture, and decorations are formed from blue-white ice. Morrinn often changes the physical layout of Grokeheim to suit her whims, yet a few areas remain constant.

items.name: Throne Room
items.entry: The seat of the Snow Queen's power, this domed, circular chamber houses Morrinn's crystal throne on its alabaster dais. Fey functionaries mix with foreign courtiers and visiting emissaries. The court of the Snow Queen often hosts guests, such as {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and other beings of power.

items.name: Arboretum
items.entry: Nothing green grows in the unforgiving wastes of the Bleak Expanse—except in Grokeheim itself. At no small expense, the Ice Queen commissioned five panes of glass from the lands to the south, which form the walls and roof of a greenhouse. Inside, a leshy grows winter squash, snow peas, and iceberg lettuce.

items.name: Library of Broken Bindings
items.entry: When not hosting guests or entertaining herself with her many diversions, Morrinn can be found in her library. Here, on shelves of eternal ice, are tomes of lore from across the North and beyond—ancient secrets of sunken kingdoms, eldritch rituals wrested from behind the towering walls of Hyperborea, and primordial spells whispered by {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} to his only daughter.

items.name: Dungeon
items.entry: Deep beneath Grokeheim, the Snow Queen houses her prisoners. To provide a modicum of warmth, three {@creature Fraughashar|ToB1-2023} wardens stoke a small forge at all hours. The resulting heat occasionally thaws out monsters trapped in Boreal ice. While the ill-equipped prisoners typically bear the brunt of rampaging monsters, the monsters sometimes reach the Snow Queen's court.

entries: Despite its frigid ruler and foreboding terrain, adventurers occasionally seek out Grokeheim. Typically, they seek to ransom a prisoner kept in the dungeon below Grokeheim. Those who come are often surprised, as the Snow Queen seeks remuneration through service and not coin. Other times, they seek magic items recovered from the vast wastes or knowledge that may only be discovered in the Library of Broken Bindings.

entries.name: History
entries: Few who roam the Bleak Expanse recall a time when Grokeheim was not in the periphery of their fears. Many say that in this land where {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} rules supreme, the North Wind gifted Grokeheim to his only daughter out of sheer benevolence. Other suggest that {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} grew envious when he learned a god in the lands to the south gifted an entire duchy to his daughter. However, the bold suggest that Grokeheim demonstrates the limitations on the North Wind's power, as {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s gift never seems to pass beyond the borders of the glaciers.

In truth, the palace is both a gift and a threat. In birthing the castle from the air in his lungs, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} placed a portion of his power and awareness into the walls of Grokeheim. {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} is only too aware of the Snow Queen's power and has no desire to be overthrown by his daughter.
