By gifting Grokeheim to Morrinn, the God of the North Wind allows her to act in his name but also keeps track of her activities. The Snow Queen is aware of her father's paranoia and continues to develop secret rituals to sever her bonds to {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} without sacrificing any of her mighty powers.

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in Grokeheim.

items.name: Bride for the North Wind
items.entry: {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} seeks to woo and win the hand of a worthy wife. As bold as only a god can be, the North Wind alternately courts two potential brides, Atla Gunnlodottir, the Queen of the Frost Giants, and Nicnevin, the Fey Queen of Witches. The Snow Queen, Morrinn, disapproves of her father's dalliances and subtly works to sour {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s ardor for his potential brides, often utilizing mortals to steal her father's treasure, rustle his winter wolves, or uncork sweet spring air in his tower. While perhaps risky to tempt the wrath of a god, the Snow Queen's rewards are well worth the risk—except when they aren't.

items.name: Handmaidens
items.entry: The Snow Queen's newest ladies in waiting—Rella, a dwarven tinker; Lumibelle, a human sailor; and Sinikka, a trollkin vintner—are strange additions to court. Grokeheim's lack of mechanical gears, ships, and grapes make the mysterious appearance of the three mortals particularly odd. It's rumored that these may be ice maidens in training, future ambassadors to the Northlands, or even possibly suitable brides for her father. While Morrinn has not seen fit to shed light on their presence, what is clear is these women have both the favor and attention of the Snow Queen.

items.name: Mysterious Offerings
items.entry: The morning after every full moon for the last six months, butchered game has been left in plain view of Grokeheim's south tower. Despite the Snow Queen's demands, the ice maidens have been unsuccessful at solving the mystery of who is leaving the game. Some at court view the offerings as a mocking challenge to the Snow Queen's power in the area, while others suggest it is a move to curry favor by supplementing the diet of the Snow Queen's lesser subjects. In truth, the game is left by a crafty ice elf ranger named Czarlis, who has been pursuing Grokeheim across the Bleak Expanse. He is smitten by Sinikka, who for years made her home in Huldramose, and she sneaks gifts to the ranger using small arctic creatures.

entries.name: Islands of the North
entries: Numerous small isles dot the fjords and rugged coastlines of the Northlands. While many are uninhabited and perhaps unremarkable, others hold dangers and mysteries alike. A few of these are described below.

entries.name: Black Tooth Tower
entries: Perhaps the most mysterious of the islands is the sunken peak that supports the darkened ruin known as Black Tooth Tower. Strange lights glimmer beneath the crashing waves that flood in and out of the gaps in its ancient stones. These witch lights illuminate still-surviving glass windows, perhaps from submerged chambers shored up against the sea. When the moon is a sickle in the sky, odd shadows move across these windows, and strange chanting echoes up from the depths. Those who brave the dangerous landing and pick their way through the tumbled-down stone might find a path below to riches or horrors, perhaps maybe even a route into the Drownstone Road.

entries.name: The Drownstone Road
entries: Though the halls and citadels of the ancient dwarven empire may have sunk beneath the waves, they're far from empty. Over the centuries since the Reaving, exploring dwarves have returned with stories of half-submerged passages and damp chambers that survived the deluge, home to degenerate survivors and things better left unnamed that came up from the seabed to occupy flooded mines.

This network of dripping tunnels far beneath the surface is called the Drownstone Road. It runs the entire width of the Strait. Few brave the journey to the road, however, for the many leagues of darkness, the oppressive weight of water above, and the piping and howling of lurking aberrations is enough to break even the stoutest of dwarves.

entries.name: Isle of Loki
entries: This massive island rests off the western coast of the Northlands in an area called the Lung of the Sea, named for the billowing clouds of frost fog that enshroud the region. Few have dared to explore the island. Sailors who have seen it say it is enshrouded with glacial ice that rises a hundred feet above the few places where a ship might land. Dwarven reavers, giants, and humans have avoided this ice-swathed expanse for centuries, ever since oracles proclaimed it the earthly seat of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and his private hunting estate.

entries.name: History
entries: {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} first ventured onto this island shortly after the Vanir War, after a particularly contentious argument with {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} over something neither god remembers. The wild loneliness of the place appealed to {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, so he paid thursir and frost giant artisans to build a great hall on the island's eastern side, and he struck a bargain with {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} to protect his new holding. The God of the North Wind summoned mile-high glaciers to line the coastline of the island, forming a wall of magical ice to prevent visitors from reaching the interior. According to seers who have dreamed of the island, the land beyond the ice is lush and warm and full of fantastic flora and fauna.

About 50 years ago, however, {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} turned on his then-allies, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, when he discovered that their plans to promote a false Ragnarok weren't false at all. As punishment for his betrayal, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} caused the glacial walls to spread inward across the whole island, burying {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s private garden beneath a five-mile-deep blanket of blue-white ice.

entries.name: The Loom of Fables
entries: Though thursir and daring adventurers sometimes seek to plunder the Isle of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, it seems to be truly uninhabited, except by enigmatic skein witches, the servants who do their bidding, and the descendants of the creatures who once dwelled in the jungles and forests of the island. All are known as servants of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and hostile to visitors.

In the heart of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Hall, enshrouded by ice, is a powerful magical treasure known as the Loom of Fables, an artifact that interfaces with the skeins of fate woven by the {@deity Norns|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. The Loom does not change reality or fate, but rather, it copies the Norn's warp and weft, threading divination magic through its heddles (the pins that guide the threads and create the pattern), which are placed where the weaver wishes to deviate from fate. The Loom then creates a powerful illusion, interfering with divination magic and obfuscating the truth. The {@deity Norns|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} dislike the contraption, but since it does not actually interfere with their work (only the perception of it), they can or will do little about it. Some scholars and sages speculate that the Loom could be used to view particular strands of fate to learn about a specific individual or even to pluck specific information from the weave, but none has yet determined how this might be accomplished.

entries.name: Isle of Swords
entries: Just over a mile in diameter, this forested isle is sacred to {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. According to legend, The Isle of Swords is the location of the first holmganga, a form of duel practiced by Northerners when a dispute is so serious that it must be settled in blood. Not all holmganga occur on the Isle of Swords, but the resolution of a duel on the island is never questioned. The Valkyries, or perhaps {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} himself, are known to magically whisk those in conflict to the island so they might settle matters before {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s judgement.

Once two combatants step onto the isle, they are greeted by the Valkyries, {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s shield-maidens, who ensure that those who set foot on the shingle beaches can fight without interference. The One-eyed God himself is said to bestow his curse on any faint heart that attempts to leave the isle before their matter is settled in blood.

Small groves of pine dot the island, while numerous barrow mounds mark the final resting place of countless combatants. Many of the moldering corpses therein date from ancient times, though some are more recent, for many disputes find their end here. The Valkyries also bring dangerous beasts to the island, releasing them into the pines and oaks so they might compete with each other to bring the beasts down.

The Order of the Thunderer has been searching for a complete version of a ritual said to summon a person to the island. They seek the spell as a way to force confrontations early, before they have the opportunity to fester and draw others into bloody feuds, or so they say. Their primary motivation, however, is to draw members of the Cult of Ragnarok to the island one by one. Whether such magic truly exists remains a mystery. Some among the order suspect that the recent surfacing of rumors concerning the ritual might actually be part of a trap laid by the cult.

entries.name: Nordheim, Lost Reaver Hold
entries: The subterranean ruins of Nordheim lurk in a wide valley between five kingdoms: Wolfheim to the south, Huldramose to the southwest, Trollheim to the east, Jotunheim to the west, and the Bleak Expanse to the north. One of the three Vanguard Kingdoms, the other two being Aurvang and Issedon, Nordheim stood as a bastion against the encroaching glaciers of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} for centuries. It was a fortress-city, featuring towering walls of rune-carved stone built in the foothills of the nearby mountains. The streets were wide to accommodate a phalanx of marching soldiers. Reinforced towers guarded the gates, and the skies above were patrolled by trained giant eagles. The structures on the surface, while cunningly fashioned to withstand siege and weather, were merely the visible part of Nordheim. Miles of tunnels, galleries, workshops, temples, and homes stretched out beneath the city, hewed from the bedrock by generations of dwarven miners and artisans.

Today, however, the surface ruins of this fortress-city are mostly buried. A few crumbling tower peaks reach into the light, amidst broken and scorched blocks of the city's collapsed walls. A deep pit on the southern side of the site contains a desecrated temple to {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. From here, shuffling lines of undead work slowly but tirelessly to excavate more of the city.

The countryside around Nordheim is forested hills, rocky crags, and ice-capped mountains. A wide radius of nearly silent countryside around the ruins is devoid of birds and animals, and migrating herds go out of their way to avoid crossing into the area. Instead, the ruins and the nearby forest abound with a creeping horde of restless dwarven corpses. The range of the undead coincides with the underground borders of Nordheim. Ominously, according to reports from the priests of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, this is also a boundary Valkyries are forbidden to cross.

entries.name: Lost Cities of Aurvang and Issedon
entries: The other two Vanguard Kingdoms remain a mystery. As they fell, the last of the Hyperborean magics sealed many of their greatest sites behind runes and sigils that remain potent today.

Aurvang, on the shores of the Tearstain River, was a dwarfhold of deep ring magic and a site of pilgrimage, for the {@i Eye of Wotan} and the {@i Graven Shield} of the dwarf maiden Grajvar were both kept there. Aurvang's last king, Regni Othinson, came up short while bargaining with a red dragon to protect the city from {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. The wyrm lingers in the ruins of the city, while various fiery wyrmlings and linnorms hunt reindeer, elk, and humans in the river valley. No settlement there has thrived since dwarven days, but the halls of treasure are still rumored to stand intact somewhere behind a stone door.

Issedon's ruins lie to the southwest of Aurvang, frozen within a blue-white glacier a half-mile thick. The ice never melts yet stops at the city walls. Seen through the blue ice, broken crenellations of once-mighty towers stretch toward the surface. A few provide a means of ingress to adventurers armed with ice-breaching spells or who are foolhardy enough to brave remorhaz tunnels. Remarkably, some of Issedon's residents survived its demise. Entombed and reduced to depravity, their descendants still scrabble through Issedon's chill tunnels, scavenging in an instinctual search for treasure. Every Issedon lair is filled with worthless detritus and salvaged artifacts, which they constantly steal from each other. Only the promise of fresh meat distracts them from the lure of Issedon's ancient relics.

entries.name: History
entries: The greatest of the dwarven holds after the Reaving, Nordheim was also the first to fall, and the grief of this loss was compounded because the dwarves did not know how it came to pass. "Never from siege," the dwarves say with fierce certainty. In truth, only a few inhabitants escaped Nordheim's end to tell the tale, and those who fled were on the outskirts of the city, too far away to understand the truth. What is known is this: A millennium ago, during a terrible winter in which the overland routes to Nordheim were blocked, something crept up from the depths of the earth to extinguish its hearths and forge fires, destroying the dwarven city from within. Dwarves variously blame frost giants and their jotun lords, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and his freezing winds; fey conspiracies and elven ghosts; and even demons from the far side of the endless void of Ginnungagap. Whatever the truth, Nordheim was beaten first, and far worse, than any other fallen hall.

Most scholars place the blame for Nordheim's fall on {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Having been stopped by the combined might of the Vanguard Kingdoms, the North Wind conspired with {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} to break the dwarven hold, knowing the fall of one of the three kingdoms would doom the rest. How this was accomplished is known only to the gods. Of the many potential causes bandied about, none have captured the popular imagination quite like that proposed by a group of dwarven scholars in Skaldholm. They believe that the Nordheim reavers took their holy fervor for bloodshed a bit too far, sacrificing of sentient creatures, which angered the thunder god, {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Though the skalds' work was quickly discredited and suppressed, one of their number ventured within Nordheim to find out more, only to disappear.

Nordheim fell from within, and the inhabitants perished. Though reinforcements from the other two Vanguard Kingdoms were sent to free the city, none returned. For nearly 50 years, larger and larger forces failed to liberate Nordheim. Then the wall was breached by the glaciers, and the Vanguard Kingdoms had other issues to contend with. It is important to note that when the armies of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} broke through the Wall to raze Aurvang and Issedeon, a force twice as large was dispatched to Nordheim, where it worked for two years to bury the city beneath earth and stone. Interestingly, only a quarter of the giants, elementals, ice maidens, and other warriors sent to perform this task survived the experience.

A year ago, a disciple of {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} named Kenas Sipkiln took control of many undead in Nordheim during his quest to seek out the perfect cult sanctuary for the Night Cauldron (see the adventure {@i Empire of the Ghouls}). He used the undead to delve into the ruins to reach the Temple of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. As he explored the exposed underground halls of Nordheim, Kenas discovered the fate of its people. They died, true, but none crossed over to Valhalla. Indeed, not a single soul left this plane for any heaven, the Eleven Hells, or anywhere in between. Called the Murmuring Dead, every dwarf of Nordheim is trapped within the withered shell of its mortal body, caught between the flickering memories of their life and the abyss of death.

Ultimately, the Kenas's plans to conduct a ritual to create an unholy marriage between Dark Gods was ruined by the interference of a group of adventurers, who defeated the cultist and recovered the fabled {@i Holy Robes of Sister Adelind} before departing for foreign shores. Left behind, Kenas's undead continue to follow his last orders to excavate the city, inadvertently releasing increasing numbers of Murmuring Dead into the region.

entries.name: The Murmuring Dead
entries: The population of Nordheim today consists almost entirely of the undead. Most are murmuring dead, undead creatures who possess inconsistent, dim recollections of their mortal lives. Unpredictable in the extreme, these creatures infest the woods and hills of their old home, as well as the tunnels below. They constantly whisper and babble, reciting who they were as if trying to force themselves to recall glories unremembered. At times, they can understand and even be reasoned with, but these moments of lucidity are few and far between. The continuing power of whatever killed the dwarves lingers in the murmuring dead. It is a dark curse that drives the dwarven corpses to prey upon the minds and souls of those who dare traverse the area. Thousands of corpses walk the land between the river and the borders of Nordheim.

entries.name: Nordheim Locations
entries: A few of Nordheim's most notable locations are described below.

items.name: Chernobog's Teeth
items.entry: During his time in Nordheim, Kenas Sipkiln and his minions erected a number of rune-etched standing stones in the ground, ringing the Midnight Temple. These stones form a web of power running both around and through the ground, surrounding and suffusing the building with magic. While these stones stand, {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s fell blessing fills the building, and celestials can't enter the temple. Since Kenas's death, more standing stones have appeared in the area, crudely crafted by some of the murmuring dead. With each new stone, {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s darkness expands.

items.name: Court of the Lost Bifrost
items.entry: At Nordheim's height, the fine obsidian gallery of this wide council chamber held the nobles of the city, who advised the High King while he sat upon the Skurdr Throne. The center of the oval court was the Bifrost, the rainbow bridge connecting the mortal world to Asgard, the realm of the gods. Shortly before the fall of the city, the Bifrost was somehow stolen by elven archmages and spirited away to southern lands. Later, the gods took back the bridge and now it falls where they will it. The mark of the lost Bifrost lingers in the Court, thinning the barriers between the mortal world and the planes. Travelers can cross to far-flung realms more easily here.

items.name: Midnight Temple
items.entry: This Shield Temple of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} was desecrated during the fall of Nordheim and then re-consecrated as a shrine to {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} by Kenas Sipkiln. The spire that once bore the arrows of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} now sports an ebony bear's paw, its long, black claws polished and gleaming. Even after Kenas's death, the sorrow, shame, and despair associated with this place called to the chosen of the Lord of the Night like a beacon. Currently, the Midnight Temple is the largest intact exposed structure in Nordheim. A rubezahl demon has taken up residence in the temple while collecting strange rune-carved tokens from the ruins beneath the city.

items.name: Tholos of Nordheim
items.entry: The greatest temple in Nordheim remains buried deep beneath the city. A towering structure, hewn from gold-veined marble, the temple's dark interior is dimly lit by a flickering arcane portal resting between the massive altars to {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. The gateway once acted as a magical passage between the temple and the Court of the Bifrost, the seat of the High King of Nordheim. Nearly a millennia of neglect has rendered the portal somewhat unpredictable. On the days corresponding to important dwarven holidays, it still connects to the Court; the rest of the time it transports those who enter it to random locations within Nordheim or out into the planes. Imposing iron golems, as well as vaettir clerics and mages, stand as eternal guardians of the temple and the gateway.

items.name: Vault of the High King
items.entry: At the heart of Nordheim lies an adamantine vault cunningly protected by concentric, interlocking trap-filled corridors that revolve around each other in opposite directions according to some system now lost with the ancient dwarves. Even the great darkness that destroyed Nordheim has yet to worm its way past the warding runes and shielding glyphs. Though many of the treasures once stored in the vault were removed during the fall and subsequently lost when the last king and his family perished, the greatest wonders still languish within. If fragmentary letters dating back to the Vanguard Kingdoms can be believed, the vault still holds the legendary Axe of Forseti and a crown set with a piece of the Dominion Orb.

items.name: Void Rift
items.entry: In the deepest cavern beneath Nordheim, thirteen liches stand motionless around a crackling tear hanging in the air. The story goes that the mages, who were the last of the mighty Hyperborean wizards who established the Vanguard Kingdoms, arrived too late to save Nordheim from its fall, but they sacrificed their own lives, and chance at the afterlife, to attempt to contain the darkness. Though they continue to mitigate the worst of the evil, dark shadows flow out between the liches, corrupting the ruins and the murmuring dead above.

entries: For the wizards, there is no salvation, and most of their intellect has long since been lost, leaving only their unbreakable focus on their task. Their transformation to lichdom was rushed, and their undead bodies slowly decay from the energies they hold at bay. If they could feel fear, despair or anything at all, they might weep for the world when the last of them falls.

entries.name: Reykurbrand, the Hall of Surtr
entries: Reykurbrand is the holdfast of Surtr and Sinmara. The word Reykyrbrand is used as the name of this titanic, solitary volcano, as well as for the jotun-sized fortress ringing its caldera. A small army of fire giants occupies the keep, constantly on guard against the gods, some of whom foolishly believe that slaying Surtr will save them from their inevitable fate.

The towers of Surtr's hall spear into the sky, and its obsidian ramparts are lit by the magma below, yet this cyclopean keep is eternally shrouded with volcanic smoke. The open outer wall of Reykyrbrand's throne room overlooks the churning magma of the caldera that hides a portal to dread Muspelheim, the plane of fire. Twin thrones are the only decor in this great hall, save for a pair of obsidian crowns hanging above a chest of solid diorite. When Ragnarok comes, Surtr and Sinmara will don their crowns, Surtr will draw his burning blade, {@i Jordbani the "World Slayer,"} from the chest, and together they shall set the world ablaze.

Until then, however, Reykurbrand is a place of grim patience, rather than comfort or joy. Whole tomes could be written about the wonders to be found in this primordial fortress or its surrounding lands. Here are a few notable ones.

items.name: Hall of Memories
items.entry: This strange spherical chamber uses eldritch mechanisms not seen since the fall of the First World. Hewn from a massive natural crystal, the chamber thrums with the barely heard murmur of thousands of voices. Sitting in the throne-like chair in the center of the room causes the memories of the sitting creature to be recorded into the crystalline structure of the chamber. Only Surtr and his fire giant seers know the secret of safely capturing memories (or listening to recorded ones). Attempting to use the Hall of Memories without this knowledge would destroy a creature.

items.name: Reykur Gate
items.entry: Arcane energy fills this twisting archway of black rock submerged beneath the lava of Reykurbrand. None save fire giants have entered it in a millennium, but legend holds that it leads into the mustering halls of the greatest palace in Muspelheim. When Surtr or Sinmara wishes something brought back to Reykurbrand, they call a hunting-pack of titanic hellhounds through the portal and set it upon their quarry.

items.name: Slag Galleries
items.entry: The Slag Galleries are a series of ancient lava tubes running through and beneath Reykurbrand. Over the millennia, they have been converted into a massive, secretive museum. An uncountable amount of wealth in art, treasure, magic items, and artifacts is displayed in the Galleries, each piece neatly labelled in niches cut into the rock walls. The Slag Galleries are guarded by burning beasts from Muspelheim, who hunt any who enter without Sinmara's permission.

entries.name: History
entries: Surtr and Sinmara claimed Reykurbrand in the aftermath of the first war with the gods. For decades, it was a nerve center from which jotun plotted against their divine foes. Impossible weapons, forbidden arcane rituals, and terrible creatures were all birthed in the magma. But as decades turned to centuries, Surtr and Sinmara moved on. Their burning need to avenge Aurgelmir, to take their rightful place, or destroy the gods, faded. Eventually, they split with the other jotun and giants. Those who remained on the path of revenge departed to settle Sengajordensblod. Surtr and Sinmara accepted any who would spurn the vengeance of the giants and forge something new. Reykurbrand became an isolated refuge for their fire giant descendants, for other giants who had given up on their grudges, and for other curiosities and outcasts who caught their eye.

entries.name: King and Queen of Reykurbrand
entries: Surtr and Sinmara are a married pair of ancient jotun, the grandchildren of Aurgelmir, who were among the scant few to survive the destruction of the First World. Surtr is destined to play a pivotal role in Ragnarok, to stride forth with his blazing blade at the head of a host of giants and bring ruin to the world. However, where most jotun are consumed with their fury over the death of Aurgelmir and can't look beyond thoughts of vengeance against the gods, Surtr and Sinmara have moved on. They acknowledge that Ragnarok is inevitable, that eventually Surtr will find reason to draw his great blade and set the world ablaze. However, they also appreciate the world as it exists now and see it as something worth remembering, memorializing, and enjoying, even if they disagree on how to do so.

Surtr wants Reykurbrand to be a testament to life in the world to be shared with those who survive Ragnarok. He wanders the lands, seeing and experiencing as much as possible, though his world-ending sword, {@i Jordbani}, remains behind under Sinmara's care. As he travels, he occasionally captures interesting individuals, storing them in a massive {@item Portable Hole|XDMG} that keeps them alive. Upon returning home, he records experiences in his Hall of Memories, and the captives are given to fire giant scholars, who record their life stories for eventual inclusion in the hall. Surtr has no strong feelings about the captives once their tales are told. Some are released, while others are dispatched quietly by the fire giants so as not to bother their king.

Sinmara seeks to turn Reykurbrand into a memorial of the greatest treasures of the doomed world—a testament to creation as destruction looms. She procures treasures and art pieces from across the world to be stored in the grand Slag Galleries. That the previous owners are often less than thrilled at this, or that the means of acquisition are often fire giant reavers, is not something that concerns her. Much like her husband, Sinmara hopes the items she collects will withstand Ragnarok and be found by the survivors.

One of the Queen's most prized acquisitions is the mighty sword known as {@i Laevateinn}, the {@i "Sure-Strike Wand."} Crafted ages ago by {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the sword is said to be the only weapon capable of slaying the eagle that nests at the top of Yggdrasil. {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} wore {@i Laevateinn} when he snuck into Reykyrbrand to steal Surtr's sword, only to be outwitted by the ever-watchful Sinmara. {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} was forced to flee in raven-form, leaving his weapon behind. Now it hangs in the Slag Galleries, though the queen has never told her husband how she acquired it. For his part, {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} seems to acknowledge Sinmara's right to the sword for defeating him.

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the Reykurbrand.

items.name: Egil's Mail
items.entry: An ancient set of magical armor from the first dwarven empire has rested in the Slag Galleries for a millennium. The mail was crafted for the greatest dragonslayer of the age. Now a group claiming to be Egil's descendants wants the armor back and is sponsoring a team of thieves to retrieve it.

items.name: Vistag Shah
items.entry: A captive of Surtr's most recent wanderings, Vistag is a kobold merchant from far to the south. A skilled liar and storyteller, he has spun a web of false tales for almost a year while fire giant scribes hang mesmerized on every word. Vistag knows that when his story ends, so too will his life, so he struggles to keep his convoluted tales engaging and interesting, but he is running out of ideas.

items.name: Whispered Plots
items.entry: Agents of the Cult of Ragnarok have disrupted the normal routines of life in Reykurbrand. The rumors of the end of the world rise to a dull roar of panic, conspiracy, and insistence. As more of Reykurbrand's inhabitants come to believe Ragnarok is imminent, the cult uses the chaos to recruit fire giants with the goal of gaining access to the Hall of Memory or the Slag Galleries.

entries.name: The Shards of Aurgelmir
entries: When the gods killed Aurgelmir, they destroyed the First World he had created. It was shattered, plucked from the World Tree, and a new world carved from Aurgelmir's corpse hung in its place. But that process, that grand creation, that unimaginable destruction, was not seamless. Across the world, there exist testaments to this divine carnage.

Some are tiny. Trivial. A rock around which water cannot freeze, no matter how cold it gets. A shard of glass, razor-sharp yet unable to cut flesh. A cave that visits nightmares of an empty and ever-changing Other upon any who sleep within.

Others are larger. Entire plateaus where the sky is a bleeding red, the ground a metallic grey. Where humanoids never became the dominant lifeform, and spiders, squid, or stranger things make up civilization. Where you can feel the horrors that lie beyond the World Tree straining at your dreams, begging to be let in.

These are the Shards of Aurgelmir. Each is a piece of Aurgelmir or his First World that preceded the current mortal realm. They are fundamentally alien places, where the rules of reality, the very basics of magic and life itself, work differently. On the borders of these shards, the barriers between the planes and the mortal world run thin, if they exist at all, and the things that live there remember impossible yesterdays and fell tomorrows that few mortals could bear to witness.

Mortals can't live in these shards for long, and even visiting is beyond reckless. But such hostile impossibility is marred with incredible power, and the Shards of Aurgelmir possess wonders and magical properties that constantly tempt mortals into their reach.

entries.name: Known Shards
entries: The following are the most famous Shards of Aurgelmir known to the Northlands, whether in truth or in rumor.

entries.name: Fields of Lengjorn
entries: Surrounded by glaciers, the Fields of Lengjorn present as another world. While upon this 85-mile-wide stretch of wasteland, the sky appears purple-red, the clouds have a greenish yellow hue, and the sun seems larger and far more orange than normal. Even the air feels heavier, somehow, and tinged with odd accents. Lengjorn is a cancerous remnant of the First World, long ago destroyed by the gods, plagued by unstable magics, random portals, and vile aberrations from the void.

Few travel into the Fields due to their unrelenting hostility. Travelers might find themselves shunted miles out of their way with a single step, or their tent turned to metal as they rest, entombing them within. Navigating across the featureless expanse is a nightmare, lodestones point to unexpected directions, and celestial navigation becomes worthless when unknown stars hang in the sky. The truly unfortunate run into odd aberrations or other strange beings, many of whom dismember travelers as grisly trophies unless offered a trade that suits their macabre whims.

entries.name: Sarslod, The Mountain-Veins
entries: North of Trollheim, in the Reaching Mountains, lies Sarslod, where blood-red, necrotic capillaries stretch across glacial mountainsides and a great valley-floor slowly beats with the long-faded pulse of a dead god. The air here is thick, flight impossible, and awareness all-encompassing. All creatures within a few dozen feet of each other share their senses, an experience that is profoundly disorienting.

The crimson veins burrow down into the ground, forming passages and tunnels into the rock. There, within the vein-etched network of subterranean capillaries, lies a treasure to entice doomed treasure hunters: divine ichor. A drop can heal wounds, regenerate limbs, unlock hidden power, and fuel impossible magics. But finding the smallest drop of ichor entails days of venturing through Sarslod. Worse, alien parasites call the region home, and each explorer is a welcome infusion of fresh food in a barren landscape.

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the Shards.

items.name: Blood Delve
items.entry: A king's ransom has been put on a single drop of ichor from the Mountain-veins. The arduous journey into the Reaching Mountains and terrible beasts of the vein network are only the beginning of the party's troubles, however. A dozen-strong group of treasure hunters has decided that venturing into the Veins is far less profitable than waiting at the exit and murdering any who make it out.

items.name: Dreaming Cure
items.entry: A debilitating curse eludes all attempts at removing it. Only one solution exists: journey two days into the Fields of Lengjorn, undergo a ritual to undo the curse, and find your way back out. A troupe of Folk of Leng intercepts the characters once they enter, offering guidance on their journey in exchange for a year's worth of their dreams and a single service, to be rendered to their unnameable patron in the future.

items.name: The Green Shard
items.entry: A missing Skald from Skaldholm claimed to have a map to Lost Hyperborea. His family believed that he journeyed to it before his disappearance and is looking for anyone willing to follow him north and bring him home alive. Retracing his route brings the PCs to an undiscovered shard far north of Thursrike. In a glacial valley, life runs rampant, spawning a living jungle in the heart of the arctic snows. The skald still lives, but the Living Shard has changed him beyond recognition and will warp his mind if he is not rescued soon.

entries.name: Shoals of the Selkies
entries: South of Huldramose and Hrafnheim, razor shoals surround what were once grand mountaintops. They slice the bottoms out from ships and dash their crews against unforgiving rocks. Countless dead litter the shallows around these sunken peaks, killed by the waves, and yet more brave the passage to spirit away wealth. They seek the wisdom of the ancient {@i Skandersteinn} (see {@area The Skandersteinn|0dc|x} section), treasures from before the Reaving hidden within its caves, and selkie-thralls to bolster their crews.

These are the Shoals of the Selkies, once one of the most peaceful realms in the Northlands. Life here is quiet and rural, even by Northlander standards. There are no true cities, or even towns, and most live in tiny fishing villages and mountainside homesteads, fishing, herding, or farming to get by. The famed selkies dwell among the scattered population, hiding their true numbers from inquisitive outsiders. Anyone in the shoals could be a selkie. They make their families among the mortal populace and reveal themselves rarely. Selkie or not, a connection to the sea runs strong through all shoalfolk. Shoal-born navigators are famed throughout the North, and it is said they can sail a fishing boat through a raging squall and never go off course.

Sailing, fishing, and swimming are the acceptable outlets for adventure. Fishing captains in the shoals are often skilled navigators who fish alongside seals, providing a share of the catch in exchange for schools of fish herded into their nets. Others guide travelers through the dangerous shoals around their home in exchange for luxuries and loot from raids, or dive into the shoals to retrieve treasure from lost wrecks.

The selkies themselves are the shoals' hidden guardians. They live among the populace, to the point that most families in the Shoals claim at least some selkie blood, revealing themselves only to ward off threats. They lead herds of seals to attack raiding vessels, cracking open their hulls, drowning their crews, and distributing their cargo ashore. The selkies reveal themselves once a year for a great althing, where selkies and other seafolk of the Nieder Strait gather around the {@i Skandersteinn} to discuss the year's happenings.

entries.name: History
entries: The Shoals were settled shortly after the flooding of the Reaving. Selkies whose island homes had been swallowed by the torrent resettled atop the highest peaks, diving beneath the waves to drag lost treasures to their new homes. Among the first treasures retrieved from the deeps were the {@i Skandersteinn}, which the selkies dragged to the highest peaks of their islands.

Mortals came later. Fishing boats washed ashore full of lost traders, the beloved of selkies and other sea-people who would abandon everything they knew rather than their loved ones. In time, the mortals outnumbered the selkies, and the selkies disappeared into their number. Over the last half-decade, raiders from Trollheim and Stannasgard have attacked the Selkie Isles. The first sought the wisdom of the {@i Skandersteinn} and, when denied access, brought enormous raiding parties with them to take what they willed. Most died, but the treasures and glory won by the survivors inspired wave upon wave of copycats.

Some of these invaders sought treasures retrieved from the depths; others came for captives, sailors, skilled navigators, and even mythical selkies to bolster their ship crews. The raids overwhelmed the selkie defenders for a time, ravaging the local people. Gradually, the inhabitants of the isles learned to flee from their villages at the first sight of reavers. Enraged at the treatment of their kin, the selkies of the isles have become vengeful, indiscriminately ravaging passing ships and luring them into the rocks.

entries.name: The Skandersteinn
entries: At the very peak of each of the Selkie Isles rests a stone obelisk, twice the height of a man and covered in ancient runes. Each stone hums constantly, a low drone that sharpens into an unending chant if one concentrates on it. These are the {@i Skandersteinn}, artifacts crafted by Vaknir Grathegn, the High King of the fallen dwarven empire, to codify his glory forevermore. Drawn by the artifact's power, selkies recovered the obelisks from Grathegn's sunken palace and hauled them to the top of the peaks.

The powers of the {@i Skandersteinn} are rumored across the Northlands. Some claim they reveal the single greatest glory one will ever achieve. Others insist they know all the secrets of the Northland's past and will reveal them to worthy applicants. Some revere them as holy objects, capable of imbuing the faithful with power. Those few who have been allowed access to the obelisks provide wild, contradictory stories: their pasts drawn to the fore, their worst fears scoured from their bodies, the exact moment of their deaths revealed to them, or the secrets of their enemies reverberating through their minds.

The {@i Skandersteinn} are centers of religious and political life in the Shoals. Local althings are held around them, Holmganga must be performed within sight of a {@i Skandersteinn} to be legal, and major religious rites invoke their magic or expose petitioners to a carefully measured taste of their power. The selkies protect them more fiercely than they do anything else on the isles, even allowing reavers to attack their families or steal their sealskins if it lets them fend off an attack on the sacred stones.

entries.name: NPCs, Conflicts, and Hooks
entries: Many individuals, factions, cunning plots, and dangerous conflicts abound in the Shoals.

items.name: Bjorg Thrice-Burnt
items.entry: This strong-bodied human mage has webbed fingers and burn scars all across her lower chest and legs. Bjorg is a skilled diver and an expert in water-breathing magics, and she plays into the (incorrect) rumors that she is secretly a selkie. She is also one of the few Shoal natives still willing to trust outsiders. She fears Silla's (see {@book Silla Grey-Coat|NorthlandsWorldbook|2|Silla Grey-Coat}) attacks on shipping will trigger a violent reprisal from the Northlands kingdoms. While the selkies can always flee into the sea, Bjorg and her fellow surface dwellers aren't so fortunate. Bjorg now believes help from outsiders is her best shot at stopping the reaver attacks she dreads are soon to come.

items.name: Lore Seekers
items.entry: After exhausting seers and library across the North, the PCs now believe the Skandersteinn are their best option to find the knowledge they need. However, gaining access to the obelisks means either braving the wrath of the selkies or finding some way to earn their approval.

items.name: Perilous Voyage
items.entry: A trading convoy is headed through the shoals and is hiring protection. However, Silla (see Silla Grey-Coat) has planned a massive raid to dash the convoy against the rocks and use their ruined hulks as a bulwark against future reavers.

items.name: Silla Grey-Coat
items.entry: The eldest selkie within the shoals, Silla claims she was there when the Swive flooded and helped to pull the first Skandersteinn from the depths. Those were happier times, before the raids and deaths. Today, she remembers every offense dealt to her kin, and it has made her bitter. Under her orders, the selkies launch indiscriminate, vengeful attacks against passing ships. Her mortal guise is a wizened seer charged with tending the Skandersteinn, a role she uses to encourage further violence against foreigners and, increasingly, locals who disagree with her approach.

items.name: Watery Graves
items.entry: Eirikr Thraelbrand, a Wolfheim trader and occasional reaver, has lost two brothers sailing past the Shoals. He wants someone to return to the isles and retrieve their armor and bodies from the deep so that they might be buried.

entries.name: Vaettir Mounds
entries: Vaettir mounds are traditional burial mounds scattered across the Northlands. Meant to honor the fallen, these sites contain the most valuable treasures the dead owned in life so they might be prepared when Ragnarok comes. The smallest mounds are mere rises in the ground where poor warriors are buried with their weapons, armor, and favored possessions. The grandest are great hills, within which dozens of corpses may rest alongside hoards of treasure. The most renowned heroes or leaders may even be entombed with the longships they crewed in life.

The vaettir mounds are meant to entomb their occupants and keep them undisturbed. Often, there is a shrine alcove in the side of the mound where families of the entombed can leave offerings and prayers for guidance, help, and protection. The mounds are intended to be memorials; however, on rare occasions, those laid to rest do not sleep peacefully. Some are disturbed by grave robbers, or restless spirits return to their graves to complete unfinished responsibilities.

The risen vaettir who return to protect their communities from reavers and monsters, train new warriors, or offer the wisdom of generations past are a boon to their descendants. However, the fallen who return because their rest was disturbed by robbers or fell monsters unleash all their undead rage and fury upon entire regions.

entries.name: Why They Rise
entries: Many vaettir were warriors whose deaths did not earn them passage into Valhalla. These worthy souls are returned to their mounds as a second chance at a more glorious end. Some immediately set out to find such an end, while others establish a watch over the communities they loved in life, sure that battle will find them where they stand.

Others rise through a confluence of wealth, cowardice, and unpleasantness. In life, they had the resources and comfort to never risk a warrior's death, yet the ego to demand the honor and respect they had never bothered to earn. Afforded an unearned warrior's funeral, their mounds piled high with treasures and the bodies of more worthy souls, a soul may find that even {@deity Hel|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} holds them in contempt. Such a spirit is expelled back to its body until it receives a death more appropriate to its burial. However, the dead's personality ensures that most such vaettir are more concerned with re-amassing the wealth and prestige they had in life than earning a more worthy death.

The sokknair or "the sunken dead" are vaettir who were entombed beneath what is now the Nieder Strait and the Swive. When the two cataclysms flooded the Northlands, untold thousands of Vaettir mounds were submerged beneath the waves. Hills and mountains fell, battering corpses and scattering their treasure across the lightless depths. This mass, accidental sacrilege awakened many vaettir, who have been trapped beneath the waves for untold years. The sunken dead occasionally pull themselves onto anchored ships or into fishing nets. Those that retain their own minds wish for fitting second deaths and reburials on dry land. Those that do not are a threat to whatever poor souls they encounter.

Rarest are the so-called witch-vaettir. These are skilled spellcasters who plan their own return well in advance. They layer their future burial-places with powerful magic, carve runes into their own living bones, and even arrange the circumstances of their own death. Sometimes, they conduct rituals to become runewights or liches. These vaettir often assemble entourages of other vaettir, bending them to their will before revealing their return.

entries.name: Recent History
entries: Lately, more and more vaettir have begun to wake. This has become a serious issue in poorer settlements, which find themselves under assault from vengeful undead, their meagre wealth drained by would-be protectors, or their peace shattered by feuding vaettir, who each demand the locals' loyalty.

The Cult of Ragnarok holds that this is a sign of Ragnarok's coming. They claim Ragnarok's return is so obvious, so imminent, that the dead themselves rise to meet it. However, the cult has found most vaettir uninterested in aiding their machinations, with even the foulest of witch-vaettir viewing the Cult as an embarrassing rival rather than a potential ally.
The bearfolk skalds of Bjornrike find the trend more concerning. They believe there is an intelligence behind the trend and suspect that the feared and ancient vaettir, Ottar Harjaz, is responsible.

entries.name: Famous Vaettir
entries: Though many vaettir never leave their mounds and their names are known only to nearby locals, others have earned wider reputations. A few of these are described below.

items.name: Bloody Revna
items.entry: A vaettir located north of the Haamu Hills, Revna formerly protected her fishing village from reavers. However, her mind has deteriorated over the centuries, leading to days or weeks when she lapses into a semi-conscious state. During one of these lapses, raiders attacked her village, slaying the inhabitants and burning everything to the ground. When her mind is her own, Revna is driven by rage, grief, and guilt to attack settlements from Nidvik to Tuskgard, blaming everyone for her people's death.

items.name: Liv Iron-Eyes
items.entry: One of the sunken dead, Liv pulled herself ashore near Eikinstad nearly 25 years ago. Despite the metal orbs set into her skull in place of her eyes, she came to the aid of local giantkin settlement. The grateful jarl has hosted her ever since. Currently, Liv dwells in a ruined tower, where she oversees the giantkin who have pledged to retrieve and rebury the bodies and belongings of the warriors who died with her. Unfortunately, their sunken graves have been claimed by a nest of coral drakes. Worse, several of her fellow vaettir, warriors who died with her, have lost their minds in the long isolation and will attack any living being they detect.

items.name: Ottar Harjaz
items.entry: Crueler than any giant, the would-be dwarven king Ottar Harjaz once attempted to unite the Northlands in a tide of blood and cruelty. He seized large portions of Trollheim and Huldramose before turning to Bjornrike, where the Bear King slew him in battle. His realm fractured, but Ottar Harjaz had foreseen his doom and arranged for his crow-eaten body to rise again. He has spent centuries hiding, binding other vaettir to his will and scheming for the day he will unite the scattered dwarves of the North beneath his rotting, icy grip.

items.name: Skarde the Reaver
items.entry: Once a famed pirate and raider, Skarde perished from an illness while returning from a failed expedition. Such was the loyalty of his crew that he was buried with his longship along the Wolfheim coast, but he didn't stay buried for long. Now a vaettir, all Skarde wants is to die in a worthy duel. However, his immense strength and skill at arms have seen all challengers to him felled. He has taken to hiring passing skalds with treasure from his mound to spread the word of his need in the hope that this will eventually produce a proper foe.

data.name: Chapter 3: Factions of the North
entries: Factions are groups of NPCs unified by a shared set of goals and values that play a meaningful role in your Northlands campaign. Some are formal organizations, such as guilds, unions, mercenary bands, or ruling councils, while others are more informal groups, such as cults. The factions described in this chapter have interests spanning multiple regions of the North, as opposed to more local factions, which are listed in individual kingdoms in {@book Chapter 2|NorthlandsWorldbook|2}.

entries.name: Using Factions
entries: Active factions in a campaign communicate to players that things are happening even when the PCs aren't around. Factions often operate behind the scenes, working toward goals that the PCs hear about in passing rumors or skald songs. Ultimately, the PCs can interact with one or more factions that might potentially become allies or recurring enemies.

items.name: Factions as Allies
items.entry: Putting PCs in touch with an allied faction early in the game provides them with resources, information, and quests (especially before the main plot of a campaign kicks off in earnest). If a friendly faction has a base of operations, the PCs have a potential safe place for rest and downtime activities between adventures. Introducing an allied faction later in the game can help the party acquire powerful magic items, lend heavy hitters for special occasions, or provide other resources to defeat the larger-than-life villains that dominate high-level gameplay.

items.name: Factions as Villains
items.entry: Factions can also become successful villains. Their values and goals are often less tangled and complicated than those of individuals, so players can more easily identify why they need to deal with them. Even better, a villainous faction likely has members of varying power levels, which allows them to scale with the PCs over the course of a campaign. Low-level adventures might be defined by taking down foot soldiers, and as PCs gain more levels, they can progressively take down local bosses and then mid-level leadership, working their way up to powerful faction leaders.

entries: Villainous factions are also likely to have more and greater access to resources than individual villains might, and this allows you to tell stories on a grander scale. After all, an entire faction likely has political ties, troops, bases, and other avenues to create a host of challenges for heroes to overcome.

entries.name: Joining Factions
entries: Consider providing opportunities for PCs to join a faction that interests them. Make any requirements for membership clear, along with what the benefits and risks might be. This will encourage players to interact with the faction. The price of membership might be a small quest, a donation of funds or items, or similar elements. Some factions might feature ongoing costs, such as dues in GP or a tithe of treasure. GMs shouldn't make membership in a faction feel burdensome or punishing to the players. If it makes sense for your Northlands campaign, you might even consider allowing PCs to be part of one or more factions from the beginning. This is a great topic to bring up in the first game or session zero.

entries.name: Status and Factions
entries: The status system allows you to track a PC's (or where applicable, an entire party's) relationship with important factions (or groups of NPCs) within a Northlands campaign. If their status with a particular faction is positive, the PC gains access to new quests, favors, and influence with that group. If their status is negative, the PC might instead find themselves inconvenienced, stonewalled, or even attacked by the offended faction.

All factions have certain values that define them, what they find important, and how they go about reaching their goals. When a PC (or party) takes actions that support or hinder a faction's values and goals, their status is likely to increase or decrease with that faction. Assume that a PC (or party) starts with a status of 0 with any given faction, then increase or decrease that number based on their ongoing relationship with the faction.

Note that the factions system in this chapter is only intended to track an individual PC's or party's relationship with a faction. In many cases, this will have no effect on the PC's or party's wider reputation in the world. In some cases, however, a PC may have sufficiently impressed or infuriated a faction that the faction talks them up or badmouths them, potentially causing a change in their wider reputation. See {@area Chapter 7|4dd|x} for more details on the reputation system.

entries.name: Blood Reckoning

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Asgard must fall!"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Destruction—kill priests of the Northern gods and destroy their temples. Vengeance—slay the gods and their allies. War—wage war on the human and dwarf kingdoms.

entries: While nearly all giants harbor ill will toward {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and the other gods for slaying the first giant Aurgelmir back in the mists of time, their enmity is usually confined to raiding the occasional human or dwarf community, reducing their temples to rubble, and slaying their priests. Although the Blood Reckoning, also known as the Blodgjold, enthusiastically takes part in such activities, this giant vengeance cult is much more ambitious, seeking to bring down the gods as revenge for killing their progenitor.

The leaders of the Blood Reckoning are {@creature Jotun Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Jotun Giants} (see {@area Chapter 8|537|x}), the mightiest of giantkind and immortal foes of the gods. From their base in Jotunheim, they plot potential paths to vengeance against {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and the other Aesir, including hastening the arrival of Ragnarok. Once Asgard lies in ruins and the gods are all slain, the jotun will regain their rightful status, and giants will rule over the whole of creation.

entries.name: Blood Reckoning in Your Campaign
entries: The Blood Reckoning attracts giants of all types to its ranks, as well ogres, ettins, and trolls. The membership also includes giantkin and trollkin. These humanoid cultists are perfect for infiltrating and spying on human or dwarf communities, and for keeping a close eye on the hated Glorious Order of Giant Killers, one of the cult's biggest enemies.

Although based in Jotunheim, the cult's message of vengeance against the gods has spread beyond its borders, and Blood Reckoning cells can be found throughout the Northlands, wherever there are giants, including in Thursrike and the Bleak Expanse.

Since {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and the other gods are fated to die when Ragnarok arrives, the Blood Reckoning sees bringing about the end times as the most likely means of achieving vengeance, and it has allied with the Cult of Ragnarok following an introduction from Utgard-{@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. While not a member of the Blood Reckoning, the mighty jotun ruler is an ally of the Doomforgers' Creed cultists and has become convinced of the inevitability of Ragnarok. If the Blood Reckoning can bring down the gods and restore jotun power and status after the end times, Utgard-{@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} is glad to act as a broker.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is invited to meet the leaders of the Blood Reckoning at Blood Eagle Hall and is asked to undertake a deadly attack on a temple or raid on a village.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is invited to a great feast held in a giant's hall where they can take part in one or more physical challenges.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: A Blood Reckoning cultist is willing to meet the PC. After sounding the PC out on their attitude to the gods, the cultist will outline the faction's beliefs.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The cult regards the PC as tiny and insignificant and pays them no mind.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: A Blood Reckoning cultist becomes suspicious of the PC's motives and sends a giantkin or trollkin spy to keep tabs on their activities.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: The Blood Reckoning tell any giants living nearby that the PC is a dangerous giant killer. Encounters with giants are tense, and violence is likely.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Blood Reckoning sees the PC as a troublesome threat and sends a giant warband to pulverize them.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: The Blood Reckoning has a faction hall or cult temple in each of Jotunheim's towns, as well as bases in the wilds of the Thursrike and the Bleak Expanse. Two important cult sites are described below.

entries.name: Blood Eagle Hall
entries: The Blood Reckoning's headquarters are at Blood Eagle Hall, an enormous stronghold carved into the mountainside north of Griotunagardar in Jotunheim. The treacherous path leading to the hall is lined with the mutilated, rotting corpses of human and dwarf priests who have been ritually murdered by the giants. Inside lies the great feast hall of the jotun jarl {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and his wife Geirhild, where the Blood Reckoning's leadership meets every few months to decide its next move.

Huge wooden tables made from the trunks of mighty redwoods run the length of the chamber. Twin thrones of granite stand at the head of the hall, covered in runes and carved with depictions of a great battle between gods and giants, which the giants, of course, are winning. Many powerful artifacts and weapons are said to be kept in the vaults beneath the hall, ready for when the giants march on Asgard, guarded by a menacing son of {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Nine Warriors Shrine
entries: The Blood Reckoning has established an outdoor shrine to Aurgelmir inside a huge stone circle between Kupparsheim and Birgkrona, in the desolate, frozen wastes of Thursrike.

Each of the nine standing stones in the circle is around twenty feet high and is marked with worn, ancient runes. These stones are the sleeping forms of primordial giants, children of Aurgelmir who were imprisoned by the gods after they slew their father and built the world from his body. Other such stones can be found elsewhere in the world, but these are the only known "sleeping giants" in the Northlands.

The Blood Reckoning cult meets here on each new moon to sacrifice captured priests of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} on the blood-stained stone altar in the center of the circle, hoping to awaken the sleeping giants. Since the circle is built on the titanic ley line known as {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Bridge, the cultists believe that the ley line's magic is keeping the giants imprisoned. If enough blood is spilled, they might be able to divert the ley line away from the circle and free the primordials.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Blood Reckoning are described below.

items.name: Krusgr Ironcap
items.entry: The {@creature Fire Giant|XMM} warlord, Krusgr Ironcap, is one of Skymir Godkiller's most trusted lieutenants and a fanatical follower of the Blood Reckoning's doctrine. Krusgr wears a large helmet and heavy iron armor covered in dents over his lava-red skin, and he wields a huge, flaming greatsword. Quick to anger, Krusgr can be tricked into making mistakes by clever individuals who manipulate him into losing his temper.

items.name: Malfngur
items.entry: Malfngur is Skymir Godkiller's devoted {@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thrudgelmir} bodyguard and is never far from his lord's side. Each of Malfngur's six heads possesses a pair of glowing red eyes, and he wields an adamantine axe named Shatterburn said to be able to cut through any substance. Malfngur is a giant of few words, only speaking if asked a direct question, and then giving a terse response from his central head, the only one that ever utters a word.

items.name: Skymir Godkiller
items.entry: Standing over twenty feet tall and with an impressive build, the fearsome jotun, {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}, is the leader of the Blood Reckoning. Skymir has blond hair, a thick blond beard, and bright blue eyes. His left hand is missing three fingers, lost while tearing the jaws of a white dragon apart with his bare hands. In battle, he wields a huge greataxe of gleaming blue steel and takes joy in slaughtering his foes with its icy blade.

entries: After Skymir founded the Blood Reckoning together with his cold-hearted wife Geirhild, they took the name "Godkiller" and set out to make the gods pay for what they had done. Skymir is determined to achieve the vengeance he yearns for, and to that end has allied with {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} of the Cult of Ragnarok. Cunning and two-faced, Skymir does not make a trustworthy ally, however. His arrogant pride is his weakness, and Skymir finds it very hard to refuse a challenge or a wager.

entries.caption: Blood Reckoning Members
footnotes: {@sup *} Humanoid faction members are typically giantkin or trollkin.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The cult has spilled nearly enough blood at the Nine Warriors Shrine to free the sleeping giants. The PCs must rescue four priests of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} before they are sacrificed in order to stop the primordials from awakening.

The PCs learn from a ravenfolk seer that a spear held in the vaults beneath Blood Eagle Hall is part of a plan of the Blood Reckoning to slay {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} himself. If the PCs can steal the spear and throw it into the Swive, {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s fate can be avoided.

A hilltop temple to {@deity Baldur|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} has been targeted by Blood Reckoning cultists, and the PCs must get the priests and their priceless collection of poetry to safety before it is burned to the ground.

entries.name: Cult of Ragnarok

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Heed the signs! Ragnarok grows near!"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Deception—spread false prophecies and stage omens. Destruction—bring about Ragnarok, the end of the world. War—commit acts of violence, and sow discord between kingdoms and rulers.

entries: The Cult of Ragnarok was originally an invention of the trickster god {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and his allies, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Working together, the three dark gods fostered the birth of a cult that would spread false prophecies and fabricate omens to convince Northlanders that Ragnarok was imminent. The malevolent humans, dwarves, giants and others drawn to the cult shared an interest in bringing about the end of the world or exploiting the chaos of a false Ragnarok. {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s motives were—as always—obscure, but it seems plausible that he intended to merely cause mischief rather than bring about the end of existence sooner than fated.

Whatever the Trickster planned, the Cult of Ragnarok's power and influence has expanded rapidly as its members formed a widespread network of sects and cells across the Northlands, forging alliances with the apocalyptic Night Cauldron of {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the giants of the Blood Reckoning, and other evil organizations.

As the Cult of Ragnarok's reach grew, its leaders switched focus from merely spreading false rumors of prophecies fulfilled and signs witnessed. Now they are performing dark rituals and other activities that would precipitate its arrival. These tactics include corrupting World Trees, manipulating the weather, and stirring up trouble between kingdoms. As the bad omens multiply, surely it cannot be long before the Fimbulwinter arrives?

entries.name: Cult of Ragnarok in Your Campaign
entries: Unlike most factions, the Cult of Ragnarok is not a single, unified entity. Instead, there are dozens of sects and cult cells scattered across the Northlands, each with its own leaders, members, rites, and creed. What brings them together are their shared goals and values. The individual sects may not agree on what robes to wear, which bloody sacrifices to make, or which villages to burn, but they all strive to bring about the end of the world.

Three major sects are behind the Cult of Ragnarok's most dangerous plots—the Doomforgers' Creed, the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, and the Coiled Ring. Although these groups see themselves as independent, they do cooperate from time to time. If the three were ever to truly coordinate their activities, the end of days would be almost guaranteed.

items.name: The Doomforgers' Creed
items.entry: This is the largest and most notorious Ragnarok cult. Based high in the snow-covered peaks of Jotunheim, the members are responsible for manufacturing many of the signs and omens that foreshadow the arrival of the end times. Through a combination of vast amounts of treasure and a series of flattering lies, the Doomforgers have convinced Utgard-{@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, a mighty Jotun ruler, to grant them refuge in his kingdom. With the help of Utgard-{@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s fire giant magesmiths, the cult is forging Surtalogi, the great weapon of Ragnarok.

items.name: The Apostles of Inexorable Ruin
items.entry: This is the second most influential sect. Led by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} the apostles are based in the ancient fortress of Birgkrona in Thursrike. Allied with the giants of the Blood Reckoning, the Apostles are working actively to bring about Ragnarok (see {@adventure Northlands Sagas|NorthlandsSagas}).

items.name: The Coiled Ring
items.entry: This sect takes its name from the Great Serpent that encircles the world. Its members engage in ritualized murder, arson, and necromancy, believing that acts of violence against innocents and the righteous all serve to bring forth the Fimbulwinter.

items.name: Minor Sects
items.entry: Smaller sects exist, such as the Children of the Blood Moon, a cult of werewolves that conducts howling ceremonies and mass sacrifices to {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} in Vargrike, and the Nightbringers, a sect of {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} worshippers that recently split off from Night Cauldron following a debacle in Huldramose. They believe they can summon the Fimbulwinter by snuffing out the sun.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is invited to meet cult leaders and asked to play an active role in in an upcoming violent mission. Refusal to take part results in a -3 penalty to status.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is invited to attend a cult ritual and witness a bloody sacrifice to the dark gods in exchange for performing a task for the sect.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: A cult member spends time talking to the PC about signs and omens pointing to the arrival of Ragnarok, and may attempt to recruit them into the sect.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC can listen to cult "seers" making public proclamations about the end times.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: The cult becomes suspicious of the PC and assigns someone to spy on their activities.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: The cult spreads lies about the PC in an attempt to have them ostracized or beaten up by the locals.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: Cult members attack the PC on sight. It routinely sends assassins to kill the character.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: Longhouses, underground temples, and blood-spattered standing stones serve as meeting places for Cult of Ragnarok sects throughout the Northlands. The headquarters of the three major sects are described below.

items.name: Birgkrona
items.entry: Located in the far northwest of Thursrike, the ancient cyclopean fortress of Birgkrona serves as the headquarters of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin. Garrisoned by giants, ogres, and trollkin, as well as human cultists under the command of {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} this circular, stone-walled fortress is surrounded by a palisade made from huge tree trunks and warded by powerful magical defenses, enchanted centuries ago by stone giant sorcerers. A sinister temple to the dark gods of Ragnarok lies beneath the fortress, its floor paved with the skulls of the cult's sacrificial victims.

items.name: Borgarbani, "Bane Castle
items.entry: " Concealed from prying eyes by illusory magic and warded against scrying and other divination magic, Borgarbani is the hidden headquarters of the Doomforgers' Creed and many would say, the Cult of Ragnarok itself. The sturdy, ringed fortress is situated high in the Blodejord Mountains, at the edge of Jotunheim's capital, Sengajordensblod, and is well-defended by human and dwarf cultists and their giant and troll allies. The Doomforgers dug deep beneath the castle until they reached the volcanic fissures they needed to power their magical forges. Here in the blistering heat, under the watchful eye of the fire giantkin archmage Torsten Vigfusson, skilled smiths are mixing the enchanted ashes of cremated undead with molten star metal to forge the mighty magical blades to be wielded at Ragnarok.

items.name: Forstol Cirkel
items.entry: Deep in the forests north of Stannasgard stands Forstol Cirkel, a circle of rune-carved megaliths that serves as the main sanctuary of the Coiled Ring. Here, prospective members are initiated into the cult after they have performed the required act of violence in a ceremony that involves being bitten on the neck by a giant poisonous snake, the earthly representation of the Great Serpent. Those that survive are considered worthy enough to join. The runes carved on the stones ward against intruders; anyone who enters the circle who isn't a cult member must succeed on a {@dc 17} Charisma saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and flee.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: The three leaders of the major sects are described below.

items.name: Diar Mats Sandquist
items.entry: A high-ranking cleric of {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, Mats Sandquist (human {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook}) assumed unofficial leadership over the Coiled Ring after he murdered its founder, Jorgen Coppenkoller. Now his dead friend haunts him, urging him to ever-grander acts of destruction. Mats has thrice found himself on the executioner's block, and each time, he survived the experience while killing dozens of those who came to witness his death.

items.name: Thyrin the Black
items.entry: An imposing figure with a nest of thick, black hair and an exceedingly bushy beard, dressed in black chainmail and a black fur cloak, {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} is the human leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin. The left side of his face is badly scarred from burns inflicted by a remorhaz he tried to ride in an ill-judged attempt to prove his bravery to his elder brothers.

entries: Thyrin is a fanatical disciple of the dark gods and the cunning mastermind behind an ambitious and terrifying plan to bring about Ragnarok. His greatest ally is Skymir Godkiller, the jotun leader of the Blood Reckoning, and his trusted lieutenants include {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}, Hrolf Slit-throat, and {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas} (see {@adventure Northlands Sagas|NorthlandsSagas} for more on these NPCs).

items.name: Torsten Vigfusson
items.entry: The leader of the Doomforgers' Creed and the de facto head of the entire Cult of Ragnarok is Torsten Vigfusson (frost giantkin {@creature Archmage|XMM}). This thin, stooped figure has pale blue skin, piercing ice-blue eyes, and is nearly bald, only a few strands of lank, white hair remaining on his head. He dresses in gray robes and leans heavily on a staff of black iron topped with a likeness of {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries: Torsten was initiated into the newly created Cult of Ragnarok by {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} himself, and since then, he has devoted his long life to spreading word of the apocalypse, using illusion magic and trickery to convince others that the end of the world is imminent. From time to time, Torsten invites the leaders of the other major sects to a meeting at Castle Cataclysm where they discuss joint initiatives to hasten Ragnarok's arrival.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The cult's lies and machinations have stirred up a nasty three-way feud between local families, and much blood has been spilled. The jarl suspects outside involvement and calls upon the PCs to investigate before violence erupts.

Leaves are dying and withering on the branches of the living temple of Alvatrad in Thursrike. The Doomforgers' Creed and its allies in the Coiled Ring have found a way inside Alvatrad's hollow roots and have poisoned the subterranean sea under the temple.
The Nightbringers are raiding villages and dragging off the inhabitants to be sacrificed in their bloody rituals. They believe that if enough victims are slain, they can dim the light of the sun.

entries.name: Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Blood, Guts, and Glory!"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Boldness—test your mettle and fighting prowess against fearsome creatures. Glory—slay a dragon or other huge beast. Protection—keep the Northlands safe from rampaging monsters.

entries: The Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers is an association of thrill-seeking monster hunters and adventurers who undertake dangerous quests to remote parts of the Northlands to slay the biggest beasts they can. Dragons are regarded as the ultimate prize by the Wyrm Slayers, but members of the faction will happily hunt other large monsters, such as lindwurms, nightgarms, remorhazes, and saber-toothed tigers.

Many Wyrm Slayers claim that fighting and killing these monstrous creatures will earn them a seat in Valhalla and is perfect training for fighting by {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s side when Ragnarok arrives. In the meantime, they argue, they are helping to keep the Northlands safe by getting rid of these dangerous beasts. Jarls and other local rulers often seek the help of a Wyrm Slayer if monsters are marauding in their lands. Cynical folk suggest the Wyrm Slayers hunt monsters for the bragging rights or the sheer fun of it. Both things are probably true.

The Fellowship has longhouses, known as Fellows' Halls, in several cities and major towns in the Northlands, including Skaldholm, Stannasgard, and Wolfheim. Each local branch is led by a triad of hunters but acts largely independently.

Once a year, at least one leader from each branch gathers in one of the Fellows' Halls to discuss matters affecting the entire membership. In the most recent meeting, they voted to expel disgraced warrior Solveg Runeflare from the Fellowship for using poison to slay the white dragon Verglastronth and then lying about it.

entries.name: Wyrm Slayers in the Campaign

items.name: Most Common Classes
items.entry: Barbarian, Fighter, Ranger, Wizard

entries: The Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers attracts rangers and other martial adventurers in numbers, but it also draws wizards along with clerics of {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, who enjoy using powerful magic to rain down destruction on their foes.

To join the faction, a character must demonstrate their prowess in fighting fearsome monsters by slaying a Large or bigger creature with a CR above their level and bringing its head or another suitable trophy to their local Fellows' Hall. There, the character must recount the story of their battle against the monster at a rowdy gathering of the local membership. If the audience cheers and bangs their tankards on the table loudly enough, the character is accepted into the Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers with payment of the 20 GP annual membership fee.

The Wyrm Slayers rely on the Skaldic Brotherhood to spread tales of their valor far and wide, and some members have even been known to have a skald accompany them on their expeditions to chronicle their exploits firsthand.
