Wyrm Slayers sometimes hire Dancing Bear Guides to escort them to a dragon's lair or use the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers for overland or sea transportation. They dislike the Glorious Order of Giant Killers, disapproving of the faction's cult-like tendencies and rigid hierarchy, and they abhor the Cult of Ragnarok for wanting to hasten the end of the world. The Wyrm Slayers know they need to kill a lot more dragons before they are ready to fight in {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s armies!

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is invited to join the annual gathering of leaders and meet senior members of the Fellowship. If something bad happens to the Ps while on a dragon slaying expedition, the faction sends a rescue party.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is granted access to the Fellowship's extensive collection of monster lore and may be given permission to borrow a magic item from the faction's armory. They can purchase {@item Potion of Resistance|XDMG|Potions of Resistance} and other consumable magic items from the faction's allies at standard prices.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: The PC can purchase weapons and adventuring gear from local shops at a discount by mentioning the Wyrm Slayers.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC is free to visit their local Fellows' Hall and view its trophy collection.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: Attempts by the PC to join the Wyrm Slayers are snubbed.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: The PC is banned from the Fellows' Hall. Local shops selling weapons and adventuring gear charge them 20% higher prices than standard.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Fellowship offers a splendid trophy to the first group of adventurers to hunt down the PC and kill them.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: These are the important places where Wyrm Slayers congregate in the Northlands.

items.name: Fellows' Halls
items.entry: The Wyrm Slayers maintain Fellows' Halls across the Northlands. These longhouses consist of a large feasting hall decorated with dozens of stuffed monster heads and other trophies, where every kill is rowdily celebrated. Outside is a training ground for experienced Wyrm Slayers to pass on their dragon-slaying skills to newer members. Each hall is named after the biggest monster in its trophy collection, meaning halls may change names when an impressive new kill is recorded. A sample hall is described below.

items.name: Wyrmhaunt Hall
items.entry: Located in Skaldholm, the skeleton of Izrilthandis, a powerful white dragon, hangs from the lofty ceiling of this huge longhouse. The dragon was slain decades ago by a pair of legendary dwarven brothers who now spend their days feasting and fighting in Valhalla, but a vestige of Izrilthandis's spirit remains inside her bones, and every so often her voice booms forth from her skull. The last occasion was a month ago when the dragon's spirit laughed and announced that Thorkel Half-Bear had died by the claws of an ancient red dragon.

entries: Wyrmhaunt Hall is renowned for its raucous atmosphere and its many contests, including drinking, axe-throwing, and arm-wrestling. Most popular are the weekly boasting competitions, with local skalds attending as guests.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Wyrm Slayers are described below.

items.name: Anana Tuuluuwaq
items.entry: A skilled hunter based at Serpentsbane Hall in Trollheim, the stealthy Anana Tuuluuwaq (gnoll havoc runner) prefers to hunt alone. The white-furred gnoll spends a lot of her time in the mountains bordering Jotunheim, supposedly hunting trolls and ogres but actually spying on the Cult of Ragnarok, who seem to be allying with certain giants. Anana believes that the Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers needs to act against the cult soon and is ready to argue this point at the next gathering of leaders.

items.name: Brynhild Fireshaper
items.entry: Standing over 7 feet tall with reddish-brown skin and bright orange hair often woven into long plaits, Brunhild Fireshaper (fire giantkin {@creature Mage|XMM}) has always loved blowing things up or setting them on fire. As soon as she began studying the arcane arts, she knew she wanted to focus on pyromancy. Thrown out on the streets by her mentor after accidentally burning down his tower, Brynhild put her magic to good use, slaying the nightgarm that had been attacking her hometown. Shortly afterward, she joined the Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers, where she is free to unleash her destructive magic on marauding monsters. Brynhild is currently looking for adventurers to accompany her on a remorhaz hunt, aware that much of her magic will be ineffective.

items.name: Frothi Issulfsson
items.entry: A senior member of the Skaldholm court, hoary hunter Frothi Issulfsson (human {@creature Northern Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook} [see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|8|NPCs}]) hung up his greataxe a year ago, and now he devotes himself to training the next generation of Wyrm Slayers. Despite giving up dragon slaying, Frothi still loves taking part in the boasting contests, where he regularly gets away with outrageous tales of derring-do that stretch the truth to its limits. What Frothi doesn't realize is that the mate of the last dragon he slew is out for revenge and is close to tracking him down.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The local jarl asks the Fellowship to slay a marauding sea dragon that is attacking ships sailing into the harbor. The Wyrm Slayers are mounting a hunting expedition and put out a call for brave warriors and doughty sailors to join them.

The ghost of the famous Wyrm Slayer Eldgrim Stormhammer is haunting the Fellows' Hall. Eldgrim perished in an icy remorhaz lair, and his spirit cannot go to Valhalla until his bones and sword are recovered and he is given a proper funeral.

A pack of lindwurms is hunting fisherfolk in the frozen seas off the coast of Amberhall. The jarl, Gunhilda the Lefthanded, appeals to the Wyrm Slayers to track down the lindwurms' lair and kill the serpentine dragons.

A dragon-slaying axe forged long ago is rumored to lie somewhere in the abandoned dwarfhold of Aurvang, and the Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers would pay a fortune for its recovery. Unfortunately, retrieving the weapon involves facing the young flame dragons that inhabit the surrounding valley.

entries.name: Glorious Order of Giant Killers

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Guardians of the North"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Cunning—prove the worthiness of the Giant Killers. Domination—unify the Northlands under one banner. Glory—wage war on the giants and destroy the Blood Reckoning.

entries: The Glorious Order of Giant Killers is ostensibly a military organization dedicated to keeping the Northlands safe from depredations of the giants of Jotunheim and Thursrike. The order maintains chapterhouses in several cities and towns from which it responds to giant attacks and launches raids into giant-controlled territory. Many of these chapterhouses are sponsored by local jarls or kings, who see the order as both a valuable deterrent to neighboring giants and a useful way to keep its rowdier warriors busy.

The Giant Killers are organized into a more rigid hierarchy than many Northlanders are used to. Each chapter is led by a "hersir" (commander) who reports into the faction's charismatic leader, Jarl Folkvar Jotunslayer, who is based in the Glorious Order's ring castle at Jokulsborg. Folkvar is the subject of cult-like adoration by many of the Glorious Order's members for his near-legendary giant-killing exploits, and there are portraits of the "Glorious Leader" hanging on the walls of every chapter house.

In reality, the Glorious Order's giant-slaying creed is a front for Folkvar Jotunslayer's true goal—to unify the disparate Northlands kingdoms under one banner, with himself as High King. This aim is known only to Folkvar and his inner circle. As the Glorious Order builds up power and influence through its heroic defense of the Northlands against its enemies, the faction uses all manner of dirty tricks, including inciting giant attacks, blackmail, and murder to advance its hidden agenda.

entries.name: Giant Killers in Your Campaign

items.name: Most Common Classes
items.entry: Cleric, Fighter, Rogue

entries: Although the Giant Killers are a villainous faction, this fact is not known to any but the cult's highest-ranking members. PCs may be interesting in joining the organization because of its name and its publicly stated aim to protect the Northlands from giant attacks. The faction is always on the lookout for suitable new recruits.

Prospective members must visit their local chapterhouse, where they will be asked to describe their previous fighting experience, including any battles against giants, ogres, or trolls. The hersir decides whether a potential recruit has what it takes to join (possibly requiring a successful Charisma check), then the recruit must swear an oath of allegiance to the faction's founder, Jarl Folkvar Jotunslayer.

Once accepted as a Giant Killer, members are expected to provide their own weapons and armor and to always keep them in tip-top condition. Pay is 1 GP per day while training or on active duty, with room and board at the chapterhouse provided to those who need it. New members train in the chapterhouse, learning how to fight giants and other larger monsters, before being sent on initial missions against giant opposition. Other tasks may involve reconnaissance, delivering messages, or caravan guard duty.

Each evening, tales are told of the deeds of the Glorious Leader with an almost religious reverence, which may seem odd to the PCs. There are also meetings they are not privy to and areas of the chapterhouse that are off limits, things which are sure to arouse suspicions that all is not as it seems. PCs who get caught poking around are likely to be thrown out of the faction, while those who keep their heads down may gain enough status to be told the organization's true purpose.

The most hated foe of the Giant Killers is the Blood Reckoning cult, and the two groups come into frequent, bloody conflict. The faction also skirmishes regularly with the Cult of Ragnarok. While the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers is willing to work with the Glorious Order, the leaders of most other heroic factions are (rightly) somewhat suspicious of Jarl Folkvar's motives.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is invited to Jokulsborg to meet Jarl Folkvar and briefed on a covert mission that advances the organization's true agenda. If they successfully carry out three such missions, the true purpose of the Giant Killers is revealed to them. If they question or fail to carry out the mission, they lose status, earning the faction's enmity.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is offered the opportunity to join the Giant Killers on a mission against the Blood Reckoning or Cult of Ragnarok. They can purchase weapons and armor from local shops at a discount by showing the symbol of the Giant Killers.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: The Giant Killers attempt to recruit the PC into the order.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC is free to visit the local chapterhouse and tour the training facilities.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: The PC is refused entry to the chapterhouse. Giant Killer recruiters give them the cold shoulder.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: A group of Giant Killer warriors pick a fight with the PC in the local tavern.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Giant Killers send assassins to eliminate the PC.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: Giant Killer chapterhouses can be found across the Northlands, with greater numbers in the kingdoms bordering Jotunheim. Here are two of the order's important strongholds.

items.name: Jokulsborg
items.entry: The headquarters of the Giant Killers is the ring fortress of Jokulsborg, located on the river northeast of Thrumagard, about 100 miles from Reykurbrand. The stone walls of this mighty circular fortress are tall and thick enough to keep out giants, and they bristle with siege weapons. A large eyrie sits atop the central keep, home to a convocation of snow-white giant eagles, which are used by the faction as mounts for scouts and messengers. The great foundry beneath the castle is used to forge weapons for the Glorious Order, which are enchanted with giant-slaying magic by the dwarven ringmages who serve Jarl Folkvar.

items.name: White Wolf Chapterhouse
items.entry: Located in the town of Wolfheim, this longhouse serves as the local base of the Giant Killers in the reaving stronghold. The entrance is shaped like a wolf's jaws and is enchanted with a {@spell Magic Mouth|XPHB} spell that roars when someone who isn't a member of the Giant Killers touches the doors.

entries: The hersir is a one-eyed priest of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} named Aevar Splintershard (dwarf {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook}), who gave up reaving to fight the Jotuns instead. Aevar gained the ear of Thulsamir Wolfbrother, ruler of Wolfheim, after the Giant Killers dealt with a group of giants and {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} cultists who were slaughtering farmers in the northern part of the kingdom. He is urging Thulsamir to allow the Glorious Order to march north and lay claim to the lands of the fallen reaver kingdoms.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Giant Killers are described below.

items.name: Jarl Folkvar Jotunslayer
items.entry: The founder and "Glorious Leader" of the Giant Killers is Folkvar Jotunslayer (dwarf {@creature Northern Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook}), commander of Jokulsborg, a handsome and charismatic dwarf with an elegantly braided beard, deep blue eyes, and a winning smile.

entries: Folkvar has long believed that the Northlands could become a force to be reckoned with if only their squabbling kings and jarls would work together. An accomplished and cunning military commander, Folkvar successfully defended his lands against several giant raids before he took matters into his own hands and marched into Jotunheim. Invited into the castle of the jotun warlord Gorm Foehammer to parley, Folkvar tricked his host into drinking drugged ale and slew the drowsy giant, thereby putting an end to the attacks once and for all.

More battles against the giants followed, and tales of Folkvar's deeds spread, bringing new recruits to the banner of the Giant Killers. The charismatic Folkvar has won support for his organization from jarls and kings from Stannasgard to Tanserhall, allowing the Glorious Order to expand into other kingdoms. The showy victories of the Giant Killers against the giants have grown Folkvar's personality cult, and some folk are already talking about him as a future king—a message his agents are doing their best to spread.

items.name: Krista Giantbane
items.entry: Sometimes the Glorious Order needs to employ cloak and dagger tactics to get what it wants. Kristag Giantbane (winterfolk halfling {@creature Assassin|XMM}) is a devious spy and cold-hearted killer devoted to his Glorious Leader's ideals and prepared to do anything to put his lord on the High King's throne. Standing just 3 feet tall, with jet black, spiky hair, Kristag wears black leather armor studded with throwing knives and rides a white-furred dire wolf named Volkova. He is responsible for the untimely deaths or political downfall of at least three jarls who failed to align themselves with the Giant Killers. If the PCs upset the order, they may end up with Kristag on their tails.

items.name: Osk Silverpaws
items.entry: When the Giant Killers need to win over a local noble or jarl, and Folkvar Jotunslayer is unable to attend personally, the jarl sends his lieutenant and chief diplomat Osk Silverpaws (bearfolk {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook} [see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|8|NPCs}]). The exuberant Osk always creates a big impression, swooping down on Snowwing, her giant eagle, when she arrives in town. The bearfolk is a talented storyteller, weaving tales of the Giant Killers standing up to jotun aggression with aplomb and putting forward a convincing case for financial or military support. She rarely leaves without new recruits.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: Rumors of dishonorable and corrupt acts by King Uffi Toothless are being spread on the streets of Noatun and at court by agents of the Giant Killers. Signy Fridrad, the king's adviser, asks for the PCs' help in identifying the source of these vile lies and putting a stop to them.

Something has riled the normally peaceful stone giants living in the southern Haamu Hills, and they are marching south toward the farmholds of Thunder Mountain. The Giant Killers send their new recruits, the PCs, to deal with the incursion, not revealing that it was the Glorious Order that provoked the attack in the first place.

Pairs of well-turned-out dwarf and human warriors in shining armor are going around the taverns and longhouses of Skaldholm recruiting new Giant Killers. Sylvoll, the Master of Thyles's herald, thinks there is something weird about the recruiters and hires the PCs to determine their motives.

entries.name: Lodge of the Dancing Bear

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Cherish the wondrous beauty of the Frozen Lands."

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Exploration—discover and enjoy the wonders of the natural world. Nature—protect wild places from harm. Teaching—share the beauty of the wilderness with others.

entries: The Lodge of the Dancing Bear is a loose, widespread organization of guides and explorers, with members across the entire region from the Bjornrike in the east to as far as Thursrike and the Isle of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} to the west. Members of the Lodge, known as Dancing Bear Guides, are a rough and tumble lot, most at home in the wilds of the Northlands. They make regular forays into civilization for the express purpose of exposing city-dwellers to the freedom and beauty of the wilderness. Guides believe that closed-off streets strewn with garbage and filth mask the truth the wider world has to offer, and it's their duty to show town dwellers what they're missing out on. Offering their services as wilderness guides, or working as trappers, teamsters, and smugglers, the guides take any job that involves dragging civilized folk through the brambles to expand their horizons.

entries.name: Dancing Bears in Your Campaign

items.name: Most Common Classes:
items.entry: Barbarian, Druid, Ranger

entries: The Lodge of the Dancing Bear appeals to adventurers with an affinity for nature—those who prefer to sleep outside under the stars, rather than in a flea-ridden bed in a cheap inn. The faction also draws those who love to explore the wilderness and discover new places they can mark on their weather-stained maps.

Prospective members of the Lodge must pass an initiation test presided over by an experienced Dancing Bear Guide and designed to assess the candidate's survival skills and knowledge of nature. Each test is unique, but all involve spending several nights alone in the wilderness, often in inclement weather or in areas inhabited by dangerous wild beasts.

Members of the Lodge are on good terms with the Skaldic Brotherhood and act as guides for the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers, though some worry that too many well-traveled trade routes will lead to large settlements being built and so refuse to have anything to do with them. Dancing Bear Guides will sometimes escort members of the Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers through the wilds, but only when they are convinced that their quarry poses a threat to other wildlife. The Glorious Order of Giant Killers is viewed with even more suspicion. Lodge members are hostile to the Cult of Ragnarok for wanting to bring about the end of the world and will not knowingly work with other villainous factions.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: PC is invited to Gorsewood Lodge to meet the Counselors. They are welcome to stay in lodges across the Northlands and can freely use the services of Dancing Bear guides.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is invited to stay at a lodge. Dancing Bear guides offer to escort them to a Northlands destination of their choice at a discounted rate.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: The PC is offered the services of a Dancing Bear guide at a discounted rate in exchange for helping the faction pursue its goals. A faction member offers an initiation test to a PC interested in joining the faction.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC is free to hire the services of a Dancing Bear guide at standard rates.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: Dancing Bear guides charge the PC 50% more for their services and may refuse to escort the PC if the destination is considered dangerous.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: Dancing Bear guides refuse to conduct any business with the PC.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The PC is attacked by Dancing Bear members when they leave the safety of the town and travel through the wilderness.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: The Dancing Bears have dozens of lodges, big and small, scattered across the Northlands. Two examples are described below.

items.name: Gorsewood Lodge
items.entry: No single individual leads the Lodge of the Dancing Bear. Instead, a group of senior members, known as counselors, meets twice a year on New Year's Dawn and at the summer solstice, at Gorsewood Lodge on the shores of Lake Dreken in the Trollheim frontier. After debating long into the night, they agree on the faction's direction for the coming months, then they disseminate their decisions to the guides, a process that can take several weeks.

entries: A herd of giant elk lives in the woods around the four-story, wood and stone lodge, led by an awakened bull named Silvertine.

items.name: Moonrise Lodge
items.entry: Hidden deep in the pine forests on Bjornrike's northern border, this two-story wooden lodge serves as a haven for former werewolves fleeing Vargrike after they've been cured of lycanthropy by the fey. They are welcomed here by Asa Brokefang (trollkin {@creature Wandering Druid|NorthlandsWorldbook}). She might invite worthy individuals to join the Dancing Bear Guides. Adventurers who wish to brave the ruins of Moon Palace or track down the infamous Den of Fenris are well advised to come to Moonrise Lodge for a guide.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Dancing Bear Lodge are described below.

items.name: Gyda Nightpaws
items.entry: While some Dancing Bear guides focus on inspiring others by sharing their love of the wilderness, Gyda Nightpaws (bearfolk {@creature Berserker|XMM}) has devoted herself to proactively defending it from those who would burn it all down. Her current target is the Coiled Ring, a Ragnarok cult that has been wreaking havoc from Stannasgard to Skaldholm. Gyda has been waging a private war on the cult, and her muscular, brown-furred body is covered in scars, souvenirs from the exploding bodies of cultists she has slain single-handedly. Sensing she is getting in over her head, Gyda is keen to recruit like-minded souls to her cause.

entries.name: Knud Among-the-Pines
entries: An experienced wilderness guide and counselor, Knud Among-the-Pines (trollkin {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook}) operates from Stannasgard to the Haamu Hills and Thursrike. The tattooed trollkin has a well-deserved reputation for cunning and a talent for saving adventuring expeditions from dangerous situations, recently extricating one group from the clutches of a flurry of yetis beneath the buried fortress of Kupparsheim. Knud keeps a close eye on the giants of Jotunheim and grows concerned that some have allied with the Cult of Ragnarok.

items.name: Tove Ulfdottir
items.entry: Longest serving and eldest of the counselors, the grey-haired, almost toothless, Tove Ulfdottir (human {@creature Wandering Druid|NorthlandsWorldbook}) has retired from guiding explorers, and now lives the life of a hermit in the windswept tundra of the Bleak Expanse, with only Snowfoot, a polar bear, for company. Tove loves the frozen beauty of the landscape and the isolation, only speaking to others on monthly visits to isolated settlements for supplies or when she attends the twice-yearly counselor meetings where her wisdom is highly valued. Otherwise, she wanders the wilderness, from time-to-time rescuing travelers from remorhazes and lindwurms and guiding them to safety.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: A lodge comes under threat from bloodthirsty giants, and the desperate guides turn to the PCs for help fending off their attackers.
The PCs obtain a treasure map showing a buried dwarven ruin in the fallen kingdom of Issedon, but they need a guide to steer them safely past the deadly living glaciers.

The Cult of Ragnarok has defiled a beautiful forest grove, butchering the wildlife and using it as a site for its foul rituals. The Lodge of the Dancing Bear appeals to the PCs for aid in putting a stop to the cult's murderous activities.
The Dancing Bear Lodge is guiding an expedition into the Lands of the Falling Wall in search of legendary realm of Hyperborea and offer the PCs jobs as guards.

entries.name: Shield-Maidens of Sif

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Resolute against the darkness"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Honor—strike down evil and fight with honor. Learning—achieve excellence with the bow or in other fighting skills. Protection—defend the innocent from harm.

entries: Renowned throughout the Northlands, the Shield-Maidens of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, also known as the sifjar, are a mostly female faction of clerics, paladins, and warriors devoted to {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} the Sword Maiden, Mistress of the Valkyries and Patron of Warriors and Archers.

The Shield-Maidens battle bravely against the forces of evil and darkness wherever they might be found, hoping to die a valorous death and be carried off to Valhalla by the Valkyries. There, they will spend eternity drinking, feasting, and fighting until the day of Ragnarok when they shall line up alongside their beloved goddess in Asgard's armies.

The Valkyries appear regularly at the three Holy Musters of Remembrance, Fortitude, and Repentance, held in Spring, Autumn, and Winter at {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s new Grand Temple in Noatun in Trollheim, so many Shield-maidens make a pilgrimage there to offer sacrifices to the goddess and receive the Valkyries' blessing. Other strongholds of the Shield-Maidens include Huldramose, where {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} is the patron goddess; Stannasgard; Thunder Mountain; and a small number of southern cities across the Nieder Straits.

entries.name: Shield-Maidens of Sif in Your Campaign

items.name: Most Common Classes
items.entry: Cleric, Fighter, Paladin, Ranger

entries: Several different orders belong to the Shield-Maidens of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and each is linked to a different temple or stronghold in the Northlands. Renowned orders include the Huldra (trollkin shield-maidens of Huldramose), the Spear Maidens of Hope (devoted followers of Sister Adelind), the Order of the Broken Rune, the Sisters of Selection, and the Shield-Bearers. A group of dwarven shield-maidens is known as the Shield-Maidens of Grajava (a mask of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}) and is allied with {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Order of the Thunderer.

Warriors of all genders and lineages are eligible to join the Shield-Maidens of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, though women dominate the ranks. Prospective members must demonstrate their fighting skills and swear an oath to uphold the values of the shield-maidens. Once they have joined, ongoing weapons training is a major part of belonging to the faction. The bow is {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s favored weapon, so all shield-maidens are taught archery and receive instruction on how to fight with axes, spears, and, of course, shields. To ensure the shield-maidens achieve excellence, they engage one another in single combat and participate in contests of strength and skill, such as archery, axe throwing, and the hammer toss.

The Shield-Maidens gladly go into battle wherever evil rears its ugly head. Undead are their most hated foes, and many were inspired to join the faction by tales of saints like Sister Adelind, who was martyred defending a southern city against an undead army of ghouls and vampires. The Shield-Maidens also actively oppose the Cult of Ragnarok, the Blood Reckoning, the Storm Reavers, and other villainous factions. They are friendly with the Skaldic Brotherhood, who share tales of their valorous deeds far and wide, and they admire the Fellowship of Wyrm Slayers for their bravery, though many shield-maidens believe their efforts would be better focused on stamping out evil rather than glory-seeking for its own sake.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is entrusted with missions of great importance by the leaders of the Shield-Maidens. Once only, they can call upon the Valkyries for aid if they are in dire need.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is offered the chance to fight alongside the Shield-Maidens in their next battle against the forces of evil. They are charged 50% of the standard cost for healing and other spellcasting.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: The PC is invited to take part in an archery or spear-throwing contest.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC is free to visit the nearest temple of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and watch the shield-maidens practicing their fighting skills.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: Attempts to join the Shield-Maidens are snubbed, and the PC is charged 25% more for healing or other spellcasting at {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s temples.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: The PC is turned away when they visit {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s temples in search of healing or information.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Shield-Maidens regard the PC as a threat to their community and send a war party to bring them to justice.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: Each order of shield-maidens has its own stronghold. Three prominent bases are described here.

items.name: Chapterhouse of Grajava the Shield-Maiden
items.entry: Built into the side of a mountain just outside the capital city of Stannasgard, the Chapterhouse of Grajava is the headquarters of the Shield-Maidens of Grajava, a dwarven order led by the white-haired, veteran high priest Britta Cragguard (dwarf {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook}). The chapterhouse is home to a splendid golden temple to Grajava, as well as barracks, training facilities, and feast halls. Grajava's priests are renowned for the beer they brew, the delicious Dragon Shield Ale.

entries: The Shield-Maidens of Grajava recently lent their support to their allies in Wolfheim against the vampires and ghouls plaguing that region. Now the order's focus is the Cult of Ragnarok and the shield-maidens are working closely with the Order of the Thunderer based at Thunder Mountain to put a stop to their activities.

items.name: Queen's Hall
items.entry: This longhouse rises above the wetlands in the rambling town of Huldramose. As well as being the seat of Huldramose's two rulers, Queen Thorgerd and Dark Irpa, the Queen's Hall is the headquarters of the Huldra, an order of fierce, female trollkin warriors devoted to {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} who enjoy nothing more than besting arrogant male fighters in combat. The fact that the first Valkyries were chosen by {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} from among the ranks of the Huldra bears testament to their valor and martial prowess.

entries: The Huldra hold regular contests at Queen's Hall, including tests of combat skill and boasting competitions, but the order is best known for its snake handling rituals, designed to test the participant's faith in {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Contestants drink a foul-smelling, hallucinogenic concoction brewed by trollkin witches before handling one or more poisonous snakes to demonstrate their bravery and composure.

items.name: Temple of the Shield-Maiden
items.entry: Newly constructed, the grand temple to {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} rises high in the skyline of Noatun in Trollheim, its roof tiled with burnished bronze and its white banners fluttering in the ocean breeze. Constructed of carved granite and the finest ashwood, the temple is both fortress and training hall. Inside, vaulted halls echo with the chants of the shield-maidens and the clash of practice blades. Hildr Ironbraid (old human {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook}) is a legendary figure among the shield-maidens. She made her name battling giants of Jotunheim before retiring to the role of matron of the temple. However, for three successive Holy Musters, the Valkyries who once appeared to bless the faithful have failed to appear. Whispers among the brethren wonder if Hildr has lost {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s favor. Unknown to the matron, one of her inner circle is secretly a priest of the Cult of Ragnarok and has worked dark runes into the temple's construction to blunt {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s influence.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Shield-Maidens of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} are described below.

items.name: Hafridh Ironeyes
items.entry: A burly and imposing trollkin warrior, gray-eyed Hafridh Ironeyes ({@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook}) is a Huldra commander and sworn protector of the Two Queen's Tree in Huldramose. As well as fighting bravely against the Cult of Ragnarok, who have tried once already to destroy the World Tree, Hafridh leads her shield-maidens in battle against undead raiders from the fallen kingdom of Nordheim to the north. She still mourns her sister Randgrid, who died fighting dwarven reavers, and looks forward to drinking with her in Valhalla when the time comes.

items.name: Hildigunn the Shield-Maiden
items.entry: Hildigunn (human werewolf {@creature Northern Hunter|NorthlandsWorldbook}) is the accidental leader of the Order of the Broken Rune, a chaotic group of female warriors who live far from civilization in Vargrike, where they can enjoy the thrill of the hunt and the occasional violent skirmish with the werewolves of Wargaz the Cruel.

entries: What Hildigunn's followers don't know is that she is herself a werewolf. Once a respected member of the Sisters of Selection, she became afflicted with lycanthropy while searching for a worthy recruit in the wilds. Realizing she couldn't go home until she'd found a cure, Hildigunn decided to stay and make Vargrike a better place. Her fierce charisma has attracted others to her cause, and Sifauga, the Broken Rune's forest stronghold, has even been visited by Valkyries.

items.name: Sister Iselin Fjelde
items.entry: Blond-haired, blue-eyed, and standing over six feet tall, Sister Iselin Fjelde (human {@creature Knight|XMM}) is a high-ranking member of the Spear Maidens of Hope, an itinerant order of knights of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} who take their inspiration from the bravery of Sister Adelind of Yarosbirg. Most of the Spear Maidens wander Krakovar, fighting against the undead occupiers, but Sister Iselin is based at the chapterhouse of Grajava in Stannasgard, where she is attempting to persuade the kingdom's ruler, Beragorn Shipkeeper, to send another, bigger reaver fleet across the Nieder Strait to liberate Krakovar. She is running out of patience fast and is about to take matters into her own hands, plotting to lead several ships full of battle-hungry dwarven shield-maidens in an attack on the City of the Mermaid, against the wishes of Britta Cragguard.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: Cultists of the Doomforgers' Creed (Cult of Ragnarok) have raided a farming village to the south of the Haamu Hills. The village has been burned to the ground, and most of the inhabitants are dead, but the cultists took the priest of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and a handful of shield-maidens alive to be sacrificed in a dark ritual that will fulfill a prophecy heralding Ragnarok. The survivors beg the PCs to mount a rescue attempt, but getting to the cult stronghold involves a perilous path through the mountains or the unknown dangers of a shadow road.

Clues have been found to the location of a fabled magical shield known as Tower of Strength, once borne by the legendary shield-maiden Signy Rimeblade, and the Shield-Bearers order would pay a fortune for its return. Are the PCs brave enough to sneak into Jarnskull, the fortress of the ogre jarl, Enevold Hraundrykkir, and steal the shield from his treasury?

Sister Alfeid of the Sisters of Selection has gone missing in Vargrike while on a quest to find a novice warrior worthy of joining the order. Her last known location was close to Sifauga Keep, but Sister Hildigunn reports that she never arrived. The PCs are asked to determine the fate of the missing shield-maiden.

entries.name: Skaldic Brotherhood

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Great deeds earn eternal glory!"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Art—compose and perform poetry celebrating heroic deeds. Knowledge—gather knowledge and secrets and solve the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. Teaching—teach others the poetic arts and preserve important knowledge and ideas by sharing stories and songs.

entries: The Northlands are renowned for their skalds—talented bards and poets who compose and perform poems to honor their kings and jarls, and act as teachers, historians, and advisors to their patrons and the populace through the tales they tell. The Skaldic Brotherhood is a guild of skalds based in the Northlands that is devoted to poetry, songs, and stories.

Skalds learn their trade at skaldic schools, where they are taught by a maestro, each of whom insists their distinct poetic style is the greatest. Skaldholm is home to the best known of these schools, but there is a handful of other, less prestigious colleges elsewhere in the Northlands. Although each school is run independently, they all belong to the Skaldic Brotherhood.

The Brotherhood is led by the Master of Thyles, who is also the monarch of the island of Skaldholm. Every nine years, this position is bestowed on the greatest skald, an honor decided by a lengthy contest of poetry, storytelling, and flyting (insult-swapping). As the skalds of the Brotherhood travel across the Northlands, performing poems and songs, they gather rumors and secrets from spies and informants in every town and city. All this information gets passed back to the Master of Thyles at the heart of the skald network, where it is recorded and studied by the Brotherhood's scholars.

entries.name: Skaldic Brotherhood in Your Campaign

items.name: Most Common Classes
items.entry: Bard, Cleric, Rogue, Wizard

entries: Bards of all genders make up most of the membership of the Skaldic Brotherhood. Anyone who has studied at one of the skaldic schools in the Northlands is automatically considered a member, while bards from colleges from farther flung lands who wish to join the faction must first become affiliated with a skaldic school. This involves demonstrating that their poetic or musical skills meet the required standard in a performance to the maestro and payment of the 50 GP joining fee.

Clerics of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, wizards, and scholars can also become members of the Brotherhood and are typically based in the faction's colleges and libraries. The Brotherhood has rogues and spies among its ranks too, charged with gathering information from across the Northlands and keeping tabs on villainous groups and cults. Prospective members who are not skalds must provide three interesting secrets along with their joining fee to be admitted into the Brotherhood.

Publicly, the Brotherhood's goals are to celebrate the heroic deeds of kings and others through poetry and song, and to preserve these stories for future generations through the oral tradition, but the Master of Thyles and many skalds are currently focused on another undisclosed objective—solving the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. Brotherhood members were among the first to hear the false rumors that Ragnarok would soon be upon the world, which were spread by the Cult of Ragnarok. When the Master of Thyles discovered the truth, {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} took this knowledge from him as payment for a past bargain, and the Master now only knows that he has forgotten something.

The Master of Thyles has devoted considerable resources to solving the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing before the end of his nine-year term, creating a secret group within the Brotherhood known as the Shadowsingers that reports solely to him. These skalds are skillful spies and masterful manipulators, traveling to the far corners of the Northlands in an effort to uncover what was lost. Ruthlessly focused on pursuing their goals, the Shadowsingers do not shy away from deception, thievery, or even murder in their efforts to discover the truth.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC meets with the Master of Thyles and is offered a mission to uncover information that may solve the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. They have full access to the Brotherhood's oral historians and libraries.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is invited to a local jarl's court and offered the chance to perform a poem praising the lord's deeds. They are given access to the Brotherhood's oral historians or library to research a particular topic.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: A skald invites the PC to watch their next performance and shares useful information related to the PCs' current quest.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC is free to watch public performances by local skalds or watch a student poetry contest at a nearby skaldic school.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: The PC is singled out by the skald at any performances they attend and ribaldly mocked to much laughter from the crowd.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: The PC is refused entry at any location where a skald is performing.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Brotherhood spreads tales of the PC's nefarious deeds far and wide. Whether true or false, the starting attitude of NPCs who have heard these stories worsens by one step, and their reputation (see {@book Chapter 7|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}) may suffer.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: Although headquartered on the island of Skaldholm, the Skaldic Brotherhood has lodges and feasthalls all over the Northlands. Here are two of the Brotherhood's notable bases.

items.name: College of Feathers
items.entry: Located in Hrafnheim, this skaldic school trains mostly huginn bards, as well as a handful of ratatosk and folk of other heritages. The college's hall is a somewhat ramshackle, multi-story structure built into the branches of Hrafnheim's World Tree, and it is a very noisy place, full of croaking ravenfolk and chittering ratatosk competing in poetry and storytelling contests. A temple dedicated to {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} at the heart of the building offers respite from the cacophony. Here, maestro and Shadowsinger Margit Gracekenning (ravenfolk doom croaker) collects reports from Brotherhood spies, which she passes on to the Master of Thyles.

items.name: Hall of the Sagas
items.entry: The Skaldic Brotherhood's primary headquarters is the Hall of the Great Sagas, a magnificent longhouse in the center of Skaldholm town. The hall's roof, gables, grand entrance, and interior are ornately carved with depictions of legendary heroes and monsters, and the sounds of poetry and song fill the air from dawn until the early hours.

entries: The Master of Thyles is in attendance most days along with Sylvoll, his herald and longtime confidant. The Master sits on a great wooden throne to the side of the hall's raised stage, watching bardic performances, presiding over Brotherhood gatherings, or listening to reports from traveling skalds and spies.

The hall is home to the Skaldic Brotherhood's library and is curated by Randulfr Shield-Wolf. While this large chamber contains numerous books and scrolls, including the {@i Bard's Chronology}, a history and timeline of the world, and many important genealogical records, most of the Brotherhood's collection is not written down. Instead, it is entrusted to its oral historians, a group of scholars charged with memorizing the sagas and poems of the skalds so they can be passed down to future generations.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Skaldic Brotherhood are described below.

items.name: Master of Thyles
items.entry: The master bard Eirik Ellefsen (human {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook}) ascended to the role of Master of Thyles seven and a half years ago. During his tenure, he has leveraged the Skaldic Brotherhood's influence to oppose followers of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} trying to bring about an endless winter, as well as the werewolves of Vargrike, and to lend support to the dwarves of Wolfheim against their recent vampire scourge. His overriding concern, however, is the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. Until this puzzle is solved, the Master can think of little else.

items.name: Jenner Mirin
items.entry: Jenner Mirin (tiefling spy) is a Shadowsinger, a thespian, and an expert at lies and subterfuge. They use their charm and wiles to weasel their way into the confidences—and beds—of commoners and nobles alike. Jenner's desire to find the answer to the Riddle is motivated purely by self-interest, and they happily claim any perks that come with being a beloved skald, accepting gifts of coin, ale, and adoration in equal measure. Jenner lacks any altruism; their every action is calculated to reap the greatest reward, though occasionally that means doing "selfless" good deeds in order to make the right impression on the right person.

items.name: Nalgar the Sailor Skald
items.entry: A bold explorer and skilled sailor as well as a talented wordsmith, Nalgar (human {@creature Merchant Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook} [see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|8|NPCs}]) is one of the Master of Thyles's most trusted allies. Nalgar has sailed far into southern lands and into the Uttermost Sea in search of answers to the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. Walking with a swagger and flashing a winning smile as he strums his lyre, the eccentric sailor skald picks up new stories and songs everywhere he goes, making him a valuable source of obscure Northlands lore.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: Randulfr the Shield-Wolf (human {@creature Mage|XMM}), one of the Skaldic Brotherhood's best-known wizards, recently traveled to far-flung planes in search of the answer to the Riddle. On his return, he is being pursued by terrifying shadow creatures and needs the PCs' help getting them off his tail.

Ottar Haukvik, a young warrior desperate to impress his jarl father, enlists a skald to compose an epic poem describing his heroic deeds as he braves the ruins of Issedon. When Ottar's ill-advised expedition fails to return, the Brotherhood asks the PCs to travel there and determine the fate of their comrade.

A skald due to compete in a prestigious poetry competition in the Hall of the Great Sagas is in desperate need of some suitably heroic material. She offers to share the location of a fearsome dragon's lair with the PCs if she can tag along when they go to slay the beast.

entries.name: Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers

items.name: Motto
items.entry: "Dedicated and dependable, by land and by sea"

items.name: Values and Goals
items.entry: Boldness—transport goods and people to any destination in the Northlands, however dangerous or remote. Community—establish a network of trade routes and increase cooperation between kingdoms and cultures. Trust—deliver consignments safely, discreetly, and on time.

entries: Traversing the frozen wastes and icy seas of the Northlands is a daunting task, so wily merchants and wise travelers enlist the help of professionals, which is where the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers comes in. This trusted organization of dwarven transportation experts conveys trade goods, small packages, and people safely and discreetly to almost any destination in the Northlands.

The Steadfast Company was founded ten years ago by an unlucky dwarven merchant named Birgir Silverhorn, furious at losing yet another shipload of trade goods to trollkin sea reavers. Trade can thrive and grow in the Northlands, he argued, if a reliable transportation network could be established. Joining forces with several retired dwarven reavers and grizzled ships' captains, Birgir switched from buying and selling goods to forming a new organization offering secure transportation services.

Since then, the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers has grown rapidly. Based in Wolfheim, the organization maintains offices and warehouses in Bjeornheim, Noatun, Skaldholm, Stannasgard, a few major ports in the south, and has local representatives stationed in smaller towns across the Northlands. The Steadfast Company primarily uses knarr for sea transportation, and wagons, dog sleds, and reindeer sleighs on land, but those willing to pay a premium for a faster service may be offered transport on a flying sleigh or (rarely) travel via the planar pathways.
Although somewhat altruistic, the Steadfast Company is nevertheless focused on enriching its members and will take on transportation contracts from almost anyone, with very few questions asked.

entries.name: Steadfast Company in Your Campaign

items.name: Most Common Classes
items.entry: Druid, Fighter, Ranger, Rogue

entries: The Mile-Steppers attracts adventurers and mercenaries who enjoy long trips through untamed wilderness or across stormy seas, and relish the thrill of battling monsters and pirates to ensure the people or goods they are escorting reach their destination in one piece. The Steadfast Company is always on the lookout for new members and is often hiring guards, sailors, and animal handlers on a one-off basis.

Joining the Mile-Steppers requires the sponsorship of an existing member in good standing. Although the founding members were all dwarves, anyone with suitable skills and a strong work ethic is welcome.

The Mile-Steppers maintain friendly relations with the Lodge of the Dancing Bear, hiring their guides when a delivery job will take them into unknown territory. The Steadfast Company regularly exchanges stories of the road and other information with the Skaldic Brotherhood and sometimes works with the Glorious Order of Giant Killers. Birgir Silverthorn thinks there is something off about the Glorious Order's leadership, but their declared aim to rid the Northlands of warlike giants seems to align with the Company's goal to establish secure trade routes, so the two factions have cooperated on recent occasions.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is invited to meet Birgir Silverthorn and other high-ranking members of the Company. In exchange for helping the faction pursue its goals, they are given access to special travel methods, such as flying vehicles and shadow roads, allowing them to cover vast distances in a much shorter time.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is offered regular, well-paid delivery or escort jobs. They benefit from discounted travel costs and have access to detailed, annotated maps of the Northlands compiled by well-traveled Mile-Steppers.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: The PC is offered a well-paid delivery or escort job.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The PC is free to apply for positions that the Steadfast Company is advertising on its job boards.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: The PC is rejected when they apply for a Steadfast Company job.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: Steadfast Company representatives refuse to conduct any business with the PC.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Steadfast Company spreads tales of the PC's nefarious deeds far and wide. The starting attitude of NPC faction allies who hear these stories worsens by one step. This may affect the PC's wider reputation (see {@book Chapter 7|NorthlandsWorldbook|7})

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: The Steadfast Company maintains longhouses and wayposts across the Northlands. Three of these sites are described below.

items.name: Frostwolf Hall
items.entry: The Company is headquartered in the rowdy dwarf hold of Wolfheim, an unlikely location given its reaving traditions, but Wolfheim is where Birgir washed up and founded the organization, proclaiming that even Wolfheim would benefit from strong trade links. Frostwolf Hall is a well-fortified wooden compound on the city's harbor, with its own docks, warehouse, kennels, and reindeer corral. A large longhouse at the center of the compound is where deliveries are planned and allocated. Detailed, large-scale maps of the Northlands cover every inch of its walls. Fearsome winter wolves and devious traps protect the warehouse holding trade goods waiting to be shipped.

items.name: Sweet Honey Longhouse
items.entry: Located in the town of Bjeornheim, the Sweet Honey Longhouse serves as the base of the Mile-Steppers on the Bjornrike coast. As well as the longhouse itself, which is used as a meeting place and drinking hall for members, the stronghold has docks for the Steadfast Company's knarr and a large warehouse guarded by a hive of ferocious bees, a gift to the Mile-Steppers from Queen Yohanna Honeyhair after they saved last year's salmon harvest from a hungry bukavac. Merchants purchasing goods here can find wares from the south and even eastern realms, and these traders often hire the Steadfast Company to transport their cargo onward to their destination, so there is plenty of work on offer for adventurers.

items.name: Blizzard Creek Waypost
items.entry: The Steadfast Company builds wayposts along its trade routes where its couriers and their dogs or reindeer can take shelter for the night before moving on the next morning. This remote waypost on the borders of Jotunheim came under attack by undead from the nearby vaettir barrows while a Mile-Stepper named Herman (human {@creature Berserker|XMM}) was sheltering here. He narrowly survived a terrifying night, but his dogs were killed, leaving him stranded, and several days of isolation have caused him to lose his mind. Anyone who turns up there is likely to be attacked in a murderous rage.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three prominent members of the Steadfast Company are described below.

items.name: Birgir Silverhorn
items.entry: The founder and leader of the Steadfast Company is Birgir Silverhorn (dwarf {@creature Merchant Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook}), a dwarf with an immaculately braided grey beard and a jeweled eyepatch, purchased after he lost his eye to a trollkin reaver's blade on his ill-fated final voyage as a merchant. Wily and persuasive, Birgir is welcome in the halls of kings and jarls across the Northlands. Based in the Company's Wolfheim headquarters, he insists on accompanying several expeditions each season to ensure the organization's meticulous standards are being upheld. This practice frustrates other Mile-Steppers, not least because Birgir is incredibly unfortunate, and things have a habit of going awry when he's around.

items.name: Radulfr Grousebeard
items.entry: When one of the Steadfast Company's clients needs something delivered fast, the job is often assigned to Radulfr Grousebeard ({@creature Dwarven Ringmage|ToB1-2023}), a cantankerous, bald dwarf with an unkempt, bushy beard, dressed from head to foot in thick furs. Raised in the desolate wilds of the Northlands, Radulfr prefers the company of animals to people and either transports goods alone or accompanied by the Goreaxe Sisters, a trio of nonverbal trollkin reavers, if the trip is particularly dangerous. He drives a magical sleigh that empowers his six reindeer with the gift of flight, allowing them to travel nearly 100 miles in a single day.

items.name: Shivertail
items.entry: Sometimes the Company is contracted to deliver a package—or person—with the utmost secrecy. The Mile-Steppers can often hide such things inside a larger consignment and transport it openly, but if this isn't possible, the faction turns to the extremely overconfident Shivertail (ravenfolk {@creature Spy|XMM}), an expert at traveling through the wilderness without being detected. Her infamous exploits include the time she sneaked into Vargrike's Moon Palace to deliver a threatening message to Wargaz the Cruel from Uffi Toothless, and the occasion when she made it safely across a gorge by walking over the giant Kettil Buckbridge's expansive (and unstable) belly after she made him laugh with an uproarious joke. Shivertail has bright blue eyes and pure white feathers, allowing her to blend in against a snow drift. She loves shiny things and insists on payment in gemstones.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The Mile-Steppers are looking for extra muscle willing to help escort a mysterious traveler across the Lung of the Sea to the Isle of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

A frost giant jarl wants the Steadfast Company to deliver a beautiful diamond necklace to the Snow Queen in her palace at Grokeheim. Getting there means avoiding the ice maidens that wander the frozen plains surrounding her castle.

A Mile-Stepper charged with transporting a wagonload of golden acorns to the ratatosk city of Grenstad on Yggdrasil has gone missing. The PCs are sent to {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Tree in Trollheim—the place she was last seen—to investigate.

A merchant hires the Steadfast Company to transport valuable cargo from Bjeornheim to Stannasgard. Unfortunately, the merchant's treacherous apprentice has tipped off nearby reavers, and the knarr is heading into a deadly ambush.

entries.name: Storm Reavers
entries: Motto. "Leave no survivors! Burn it all!"

Values and Goals. Boldness—show no fear when you face death and become a scourge to the Northlands. Destruction—spread death and destruction in {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s name. Wealth—seize plunder from ships, and pillage coastal settlements.

Reaving has long been a tradition in the Northlands among dwarves, humans, and trollkin alike, but no other raiders match the monstrous violence of the Storm Reavers, a band of sea reavers and cultists of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the North Wind. Based in hidden coves and on small islands along the western coast of the Swive, the Storm Reavers attack merchant vessels and other ships crossing the Nieder Strait, and pillage farmsteads and fishing villages in both Northern and southern lands, inflicting untold misery on their inhabitants.

Unlike other pirates and raiders, the Storm Reavers cannot be bought off with bribes or offers of tribute. They are despicable outlaws who lack any code of honor and show no mercy to their victims. Once everything of value has been seized, survivors of a raid are either brutally murdered on the spot, taken as captives to be sacrificed to {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, or used as thralls. Only corpses, blood-soaked earth, and smoldering ruins remain after Storm Reavers raid.

entries.name: Storm Reavers in Your Campaign
entries: While the leaders of the Storm Reavers and most of their members are trollkin, the promise of violence draws evil-hearted human mercenaries and cultists of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, as well as tundra gnolls and hobgoblins, to their ranks. Since the dwarven reaver kingdoms are a dangerous threat to the existence of the Storm Reavers, dwarves are forbidden from joining the faction. The Storm Reavers take great pleasure in murdering any dwarves foolish enough to seek membership.

Members of the Storm Reavers live in separate communities called clans, though most are not related by blood. The clans are scattered along the Trollheim Frontier, on the western shores of the Swive, often hidden from their enemies in secluded coves or sea caves. Each clan has a single longhouse, a shrine to {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and one or two longships, and is typically led by a {@creature Trollkin Raider|NorthlandsWorldbook}. {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s shrines are simple affairs, usually a cairn on top of a windswept hill or in a small cavern with one or more wooden posts. Sacrificial victims are stripped naked and chained to these posts to die slowly from exposure to the elements.

Clan leaders use trained seagulls to send messages to each other so they can coordinate raids. Large-scale attacks on a well-guarded merchant fleet or a larger port, such as Amberhall, might involve a dozen or more longships from different clans under the overall command of a fearsome {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook} (see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|8|Trollkin}), so communication between ships is vital.

The Storm Reavers are bitter foes of the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers, who protect merchant vessels from pirate attacks. Kings and jarls across the Northlands hate the Storm Reavers. The rulers of Stannasgard, Trollheim, Wolfheim and others are dedicated to stamping out the pirates and have offered their own reavers a sizeable bounty for each Storm Reaver head they take.

rows.name: Welcoming
entries: The PC is invited to meet Drinks Dwarf-Blood at Wavesquall Caverns and take part in a murderous raid on a coastal settlement by the Storm Reavers.

rows.name: Friendly
entries: The PC is invited onboard a Storm Reaver longship to join in an attack on a merchant ship.

rows.name: Intrigued
entries: The PC is welcomed on board a Storm Reaver longship to meet its captain.

rows.name: Indifferent
entries: The Storm Reavers take no interest in the PC unless they happen to be traveling on a merchant ship or other potential prize.

rows.name: Vexed
entries: The Storm Reavers grow suspicious of the PC and send a longship to shadow them.

rows.name: Unfriendly
entries: The Storm Reavers send a longship to attack the PC as soon as they leave port.

rows.name: Hostile
entries: The Storm Reavers conduct a bloody vendetta against the PC and anyone they hold dear, raiding their home and attacking their allies.

entries.name: Key Locations
entries: Two important strongholds of the Storm Reavers are described below.

Wavesquall Caverns. Located on a small island in the Swive, one hundred miles south of Skaldholm, Wavesquall Caverns are home to the headquarters of the leadership of the Storm Reavers. The caverns are a large sea cave complex accessed via a sheltered bay on the western side of the island. The main entrance is large enough for longships to row into but is disguised by a powerful and permanent illusion to appear as a blank rock wall. Inside is a vast cave with a dock big enough to hold a dozen vessels. Several passageways lead deeper into the caves to chambers where the reavers drink, eat, and sleep, as well as the personal quarters of Drinks Dwarf-Blood, which are furnished with stolen tapestries and art objects. Stone steps lead down to a well-guarded and trapped treasure vault, piled high with plunder.

entries.name: Winterchill Hall
entries: This longhouse is built overlooking a bay some fifty miles to the south of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Tree and is home to one of the most fearsome Storm Reaver clans. The wooden walls of Winterchill Hall are covered with winter magic runes, and the building is rimed with frost even at the height of summer.

Every member of the Winterchill clan is a cultist of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and many have undertaken a series of deadly trials to become one of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}'s Chosen. Having survived by winning the god's favor, these reavers have been transformed, taking on some of the characteristics of their patron, so icy blood flows through their veins, and their weapons are always coated in frost. The Winterchill reavers conduct bloody raids up and down the Swive, honoring their god by slaughtering as many foes as they can. They believe that each soul claimed brings an endless winter one step closer.

entries.name: Key Characters
entries: Three infamous Storm Reaver leaders are described below.

entries.name: Drinks Dwarf-Blood
entries: The position of overall leader of the Storm Reavers is a precarious one. Any clan leader or ship's captain has the right to challenge for the leadership at the Great Mustering, the gathering of longships that takes place every Midwinter on a different remote island somewhere in the icy Northlands seas. The challenge is a fight to the death. Drinks Dwarf-Blood, a wily {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook}, has won six challenges so convincingly that he hasn't faced a challenge for the past three years. However, resentment is building among the other leaders at how much loot ends up in the Wavesquall Caverns vault, and a challenge is likely to come soon.
Drinks Dwarf-blood stands over 7 feet tall with moss green stone-like skin and a bulbous nose. His right ear is torn, a souvenir from his last unsuccessful challenge.

entries.name: Screaming Tempest
entries: An influential figure in the leadership of the Storm Reavers and a trusted ally of Drinks Dwarf-Blood, Screaming Tempest (trollkin {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook} [see {@book Chapter 8|NorthlandsWorldbook|8|Trollkin}]) is a fanatical follower of {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} who wields powerful elemental magic, a dark blessing from her god. Tempest has olive green skin and beautiful fey features, which twist into those of an angry hag when she casts spells. She dresses in thick, white furs decorated with bear's teeth and wears a headdress of elk horns.

entries.name: Keelhaul Vott
entries: Captain of the longship Demon's Blood, Keelhaul Vott (tundra gnoll {@creature Pirate Captain|XMM}) is a ruthless pirate leader who enjoys killing his enemies as gruesomely as possible. He wears a gold-winged helmet and a long leather coat over his leather armor. Vott always keeps a couple of live weasels in his pockets as handy snacks; he prefers to eat them fresh.
Adored by his crew of violent cutthroats, Keelhaul Vott has seized enough prizes this year to think about challenging Drinks Dwarf-Blood for leadership of the Storm Reavers at Midwinter.

entries.name: Adventure Hooks
entries: The PCs find a treasure map showing the location of a golden hall purported to hold great riches. The hall sunk to the bottom of the Swive when Mara the witch queen bedded the sea god Aegir, but it can still be found when the sun strikes the surface of the water at certain times of day. Unfortunately, the sunken ruin lies very close to the hidden base of a clan of bloodthirsty Storm Reavers.

The tiny fishing village of Kvarnmark is under threat from the Storm Reavers, and the desperate jarl appeals to the PCs for aid. Can they evacuate the villagers to safety in the nearby caves and then ambush the raiders when they land?

A friend of the PCs has survived a raid by the Storm Reavers but has been taken captive. When the PCs mount their rescue attempt, they discover that their ally has joined the pirates and is due to take part in their next raid. Can the PCs win him back to the light?

data.name: Chapter 4: Heroes of the Sagas
entries: Creating a PC involves making choices that define who they are and what they're good at. Northlands heroes are epic figures striving for glory and renown in a harsh environment. This chapter contains options to help create your PCs, such as subclasses and feats, but also elements to help define their history and personality, such as backgrounds and character threads.

entries.name: Subclasses
entries: Character class provides a character's most exciting abilities. This section offers subclasses for many of the core classes.

entries.name: Species
entries: When you choose your character's species, you determine whether your character is a human or a member of a fantastical species, such as giantkin or ratatosk.

The peoples of the Northlands hail from a variety of lands and include many kinds of sapient life forms. A player character's species is the set of game traits that an adventurer gains from being one of those life forms. Members of most species live for about 80 years, with exceptions noted in the text about the species in this chapter. Regardless of life span, members of all species reach physical maturity at about the same age. Your character can be any age that isn't beyond the normal life span for their species.

entries.name: Parts of a Species
entries: A species includes the following parts.

entries.name: Creature Type
entries: A character's species determines the character's creature type. Every species in this chapter is Humanoid.

entries.name: Size
entries: Your character's size is determined by their species. Individuals within a species may cover a wide range of heights, and some species give you the option to choose your character's size.

entries.name: Speed
entries: Your character's Speed is determined by their species.

entries.name: Special Traits
entries: Your character's species gives them special traits—unique characteristics based on their physiology or magical nature. When you choose a species, your character gets all the special traits listed for it. Some traits involve making a choice from a handful of options.

entries.name: Species Descriptions
entries: Presented here in alphabetical order are the description of seven species: {@race Bearfolk|ToB1-2023}, {@race Beastkin|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@race Giantkin|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@race Ratatosk|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@race Ravenfolk|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@race Trollkin|NorthlandsWorldbook} and {@race Werekin|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Species Variants
entries: What follows are a few variants derived from more familiar fantasy species. You can choose either the more common species or its variant when you create your character.

entries.name: Dwarven
entries: Dwarves are one of the most prolific humanoid species of the Northlands, perhaps second only to humans themselves. Dwarves in the Northlands take on many roles, from hard-working wheat farmers to outstanding metal and leather crafters. Environment and circumstance have subtly transformed dwarves over the centuries and grant them different traits.

entries.name: Elven
entries: Millennia ago, elves were created in the Vanir War between the gods. Most were driven out of their original Northlands territories by the dwarves, forced to move south and join their kin before the Great Retreat. The elven communities remaining in the Northlands are generally isolationist, choosing to inhabit the farthest reaches of the Bleak Expanse or to hide themselves away from view with powerful magic. Ages of seclusion have subtly influenced the native elven populations of the North, granting them certain kinds of magic.

entries.name: Backgrounds
entries: A character's background is a collection of characteristics that represent the place or occupation that was most formative before they began their life as an adventurer. Each background includes a brief narrative of what the character's past might have been like. Players are free to alter these narrative details to better fit their character.

entries.name: Parts of a Background
entries: A background includes the following parts.

entries.name: Ability Scores
entries: A background lists three of your character's ability scores. Increase one by 2 and another one by 1, or increase all three by 1. None of these increases can raise a score above 20.

entries.name: Feat
entries: A background gives your character a specified Origin feat.

entries.name: Skill Proficiencies
entries: A background gives your character proficiency in two specified skills.

entries.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: Each background gives a character proficiency with one tool—either a specific tool or one chosen from the {@filter Artisan's Tools|items|source=xphb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} category.

entries.name: Equipment
entries: Each background offers a choice between a package of equipment and 50 GP.

entries.name: Character Threads
entries: Normally, backgrounds reflect a character's training before they became adventurers and provide various bonuses, such as skills, proficiencies, and equipment. For many characters, a background remains an element of their past. It occasionally impacts a campaign, but it mostly serves an important function as roleplaying fodder and thematic color. For example, a character might sometimes use their nobility as an adventurer, but this background doesn't change or grow.
On the other hand, what if an element similar to a background could continue to develop and even change over the course of a character's adventuring career?

Character threads are positions, occupations, and situations a character might pursue while they continue to go on quests or battle foes. Though threads are similar to backgrounds, they are less about what your character did before becoming an adventurer and more about what your character does in the "background" while they are adventuring.

Perhaps the PC is appointed as an ambassador to a neighboring country or elevated to the position of minister in a royal court. Or perhaps a character with a noble background learns their family has been cheated out of their fortune and is now impoverished.

Threads are aspects added to characters at any time during their career that have a specific short or long-term goal. They reward characters with news and abilities as they advance along milestones toward that goal. Once that endpoint of a thread is achieved, new threads can be applied as they occur during the course of the campaign. You can add threads to your character by choosing one of the ones presented below, or you can use the options presented in this section to create your own tiered threads.

entries.name: Elements of a Character Thread
entries: All character threads establish a specific goal as well as thematic milestones that the character must reach in order to achieve that goal, and each new milestone unlocks a new benefit or. When the specific goal is ultimately accomplished, the character can change their thread to a new one {@b (see Adding or Abandoning New Threads)}. A character can have only one thread at a time.

The use of Threads in your campaign can lead to a balancing issue between characters taking on threads and those who do not. The easiest way to handle this is to just acknowledge that threads may make some characters slightly more powerful than others. GMs uncomfortable with this can also hand out some magic items or other rewards to non-thread using characters.

When adopting a thread, a certain amount of personalization is required to fit the milestones to the goal at hand and to the overall direction of the campaign. Players should work with their GMs to adjust the goal and milestones for their thread as described below.

entries.name: Goal
entries: All threads begin with a goal determined by the player. The goal helps to guide the creation of the thread's milestones and should thematically fit with the character and with the nature of the campaign.

More importantly, the goal should be a specific, achievable objective, something the character hopes to accomplish in the future. The more specific this goal, the better, for this will ease the creation of its milestones. For example, a character picking up the Bloodsworn thread might choose a goal of defeating the giants who destroyed their village.

entries.name: Milestones
entries: With the goal in hand, the milestones must be decided. These are events of personal achievement or significance. They act as obstacles or thresholds on the path to reaching the thread's goal. A thread isn't restricted in its number of milestones, but four is recommended. On achieving each milestone, a benefit is unlocked, depending on its ranking—least, lesser, greater, or superior (see {@b Milestone Benefits}).

While the goal or motivation of a thread is specific, milestones usually are not. This allows the GM some flexibility in applying them to individual campaigns. Each thread description includes a few example milestones, but there are no strict rules about what a milestone might be or when it can occur.

Milestones can even change as the path toward the character's goal shifts. The player and GM might even retroactively determine that an unexpected event counts as a milestone to that thread's goal. Ideally, the player should work this out with the GM, agreeing on applicable milestones and determining how (and when) they are achieved.

entries.name: Spacing Milestones
entries: When creating or adding a thread to a character, decide with the GM how long (in theory) it should take to reach the goal. This might depend on the scope or length of the campaign and on the nature of the thread. An Impoverished Noble thread, for example, might be quite short, ending when a certain wealth threshold is reached. Conversely, the Illegitimate Scion thread might only end when the character is adopted into a new family, an event which could take 20 levels.
Once the length of the thread is determined, add in the milestones, spacing them out evenly in terms of levels.

entries.name: Milestone Benefits
entries: The four ranks of milestones—least, lesser, greater, superior—have recommended level ranges that serve as guides for determining the types of benefits a character receives. These correspond to the level range the character is expected to be within when they reach that milestone. Threads can have multiple milestones of the same rank. Sample benefits are listed in the Milestone Recommended Levels table.
Characters should generally earn only one benefit for each milestone unlocked, but GMs can always choose to reward additional benefits.

entries.name: A Sample Thread Progression
entries: Halbera Gap-Tooth, a bearfolk Viking Fighter, begins her career with the Northlands Reaver background and the Bloodsworn thread. Halbera's player chooses "I must defeat the storm giant who slew my jarl" as a goal.

Working with the GM, the player determines that this thread should only go to 10th level, or thereabouts, because after that the campaign might shift away from the area where the storm giant operates. They create four milestones that can lead Halbera to that final confrontation with her foe, plus benefits for each of those milestones.

items: Uncover the identity of the storm giant. (Least: Cunning)
Learn the location of the storm giant's hidden lair. (Least: a seeking charm usable once per day.)
Defeat one of the storm giant's minions who has important information. (Lesser: Wrath.)
Defeat the storm giant. (Lesser: Gain the lair as a new base of operations.)

entries: This progression assumes a 10-level arc, but threads can be as long or as short as the GM wishes. Shorter-range goals merely require fewer milestones.

entries.name: Adding or Abandoning New Threads
entries: Threads give characters another way to show how they change and grow over the course of a campaign. When a thread is completed, or even abandoned, a character can adopt a new thread to reflect the altering events of the story. Having proven themselves to their estranged parent, for example, a character with the Illegitimate Scion thread now looks to rebuild the family fortune.
